author: David Swanson
title: Art of Peace: Art and Dialogue as Tools for Peace in Nigeria
content:
Africa, Africa Projects, Chapters, Culture of Peace, Nigeria Chapter

By Obi Jane, World BEYOND War Nigeria Chapter Coordinator, November 1, 2026

In Nigerian communities facing insecurity, social tensions, and polarization, young people are often exposed to hostile rhetoric and confrontational messages that can fuel violent behavior. However, the lack of accessible spaces where they can express themselves and explore nonviolent alternatives to conflict is a barrier to their participation in peacebuilding. It is in this context that the Nigerian chapter of World BEYOND War organized the event “Art of Peace: Transforming Conflict through Dialogue, Art, and Nonviolent Action” in the town of Goni-Gora, in Kaduna State, Nigeria. This initiative brought together 30 participants (15 women and 15 men) including young people, peace advocates, representatives of the Nigerian police, the Kaduna State Vigilance Service, civil society organizations, and traditional authorities. The goal was to address the identified need by prioritizing an approach that uses art, dialogue, personal stories, and popular peace education as creative tools to enable young people and community members to explore concrete alternatives to violent conflict.

The event combined several interactive approaches, including a peace education session on the street, facilitated discussions, creative presentations, and a hands-on exercise in nonviolent action. These various activities allowed participants to express themselves and share their experiences in the face of rising violence in their communities. The discussions focused on ways to develop narratives that promote peace, strengthen empathy among people from different backgrounds, and counter hate speech. Participants discussed the impact of violent conflicts on livelihoods and economic activities, noting that insecurity affects both people’s physical safety and their living conditions. They also reflected on how young people can help promote dialogue and mutual understanding in their communities. As the discussions progressed, the Nigeria chapter recognized the need to scale up community-based initiatives aimed at improving public safety. The “Art of Peace” initiative will be replicated, as the program has demonstrated that artistic expression can help young people and other community members challenge violent rhetoric and envision peaceful responses to conflict.

author: Unknown
title: Iain Mckay - Michael Bakunin, Anarchist & Syndicalist
content:
Author

: Iain Mckay

Title

: Michael Bakunin, Anarchist & Syndicalist

Date

: 2026, Fall

Notes

: Publication information is available online at

https://syndicalist.us/

Source

: Scanned from Anarcho-Syndicalist Review #95, Fall, 2026, page 40


 This year marks the 150th anniversary of the death of Michael Bakunin (May 30, 1814, to July 1, 1876). While best known for his struggle against Marx in the (First) International and his correct prediction that the so-called workers' state would generate a new ruling class, there is much more to Bakunin than that. He wrote on a wide range of subjects which activists today will find of interest—the nature of a social revolution, union organizing, nationalism and national liberation, atheism, the need for a specific anarchist organization, amongst others.


 It is important to stress that the conflict within the International was not a personal one. Bakunin championed a tendency that had existed within the International since the start, one which could be termed (to use a later word) syndicalist—that argued for struggle on the economic terrain and favored federalist socio-economic organization which prefigured the socialist world desired. This inevitably brought the federalist wing of the International into conflict with Marx who favored political action (electioneering) and centralized political organization (parties). Bakunin championed this tendency (which was supported by the majority of the International) and became its best-known advocate.


 As is clear from the writings included in this issue, Bakunin advocated syndicalist tactics and specific anarchist organization. However, this is often ignored by commentators upon him and anarchism. Instead, Bakunin's constructive ideas are replaced with suggestions that he was an advocate of pan-destruction and terrorism. Suffice to say, comparing hostile accounts of Bakunin to anarchist ones and the reader would not be condemned if they concluded that there were about two different people with the same name.


 Often this criticism is based on works for which any actual evidence of Bakunin's authorship is lacking or, at best, limited, superficial or dubious. These date from his short association—and infatuation—with the Russian Nihilist Sergei Nechaev and many of the commentators seem blissfully unaware of any research conducted since Marx and Engels first made the assertion, research which shows that Bakunin had no role in the infamous works written during that short period and that Nechaev was their author. This explains why their content is so at odds with Bakunin's other writings, whether public or private.


 Bakunin's advocacy of syndicalism can be seen from his public writings, his letters to comrades and his posthumously published works. Thus we see him argue for economic organization and struggle, reject electioneering and correctly predict it would lead to reformism, see the general strike as a means of commencing the social revolution (although not rejecting the need for insurrection) and a host of other ideas which are associated with the later syndicalism which is all too often claimed to be different to revolutionary anarchism or a new development produced by the failure of "propaganda by the deed" (again, wrongly all too often proclaimed the anarchist tactic).


 Yet we find Bakunin arguing that the "International, by thus placing the proletariat outside the politics of states and the bourgeois world, constitutes a new world, the world of proletarian solidarity across all countries. This world is that of the future... it is the organisation of international solidarity for the economic struggle of labor against capital." Likewise, he indicated that the organs formed to fight capitalism (unions, councils) would be what replaced it:


 This completely practical, completely vital study of social science undertaken and constantly pursued by the workers themselves, both in their respective trade sections and in these trades councils, will necessarily lead and has already led to a large extent to produce in them this unanimous and fully considered conviction, demonstrable both in theory and in practice, that the serious, final, complete emancipation of the workers is possible only on one condition, and that this condition is the appropriation of capital, that is to say the raw materials and all the instruments of labor, including land, by the workers collectively....The economic question considered in this extent …

title: [“In a world that constantly shames us for our bodies, genders, or sexualities, we can trick…
content:
gatheringbones

:

[“In a world that constantly shames us for our bodies, genders, or sexualities, we can trick ourselves into thinking that we are “taking control” and that achieving a certain body ideal is liberation. It is far from that.

For those of us who face multiple forms of oppression, developing eating disorders is not simply wanting our bodies to meet the impossible aesthetic ideal associated with people in dominant culture. Queer and trans people don’t develop disordered eating simply because we want to assimilate to cisgender, heteronormative culture. Of course, appearances can be and often are part of the picture. But when we attribute eating disorders solely to the desire for our bodies to look a certain way, the conversation stops. And we miss out on opportunities for crucial conversations about the connections between eating disorders, trauma, and survival.

Eating disorders help us to survive trauma and oppression.

 For queer and trans folks, the way we both conceptualize and heal from eating disorders must account for the ways we are harmed by systems of power. Eating disorders help us to cope with everyday microaggressions and macroaggressions. They help us to get by in the face of food insecurity. They can keep us safe in a world in which being read as queer or trans can mean life or death.

For many people, disordered eating or behaviours are attempts at shape control, which are attempts to blend in and not become a target. For many of us, eating disorder “treatment” that aims to strip us of the very armour that has allowed us to stay alive, can actually cause more harm if there isn’t an adequate substitute or systemic change to help us to safely exist in the world. Treatment cannot simply be aimed at challenging our “distorted thoughts” or symptom reduction or cheerleading body positivity. Treatment approaches that aim at skills training (e.g., dialectical behaviour therapy) and challenging unhelpful thought patterns that fuel an eating disorder (e.g., cognitive behavioural therapy) are often crucial, but they are not enough for a true sense of feeling safe and at home in one’s body.

Most mainstream treatment approaches perpetuate white supremacist, capitalist systems of harm. Fat people are told that they are holding on to their fat as protection and that if they worked through their trauma, the weight would fall away. Thin people are told they need to restore their weight but they are not to go beyond an established “upper limit.” When we demonize “emotional eating,” there is an inherent assumption that the individual can get to a calm, neutral state at all times when their body needs or wants to be fed. Sometimes “emotional eating” is harm reduction.

Our disorders and symptoms, the things that we feel shame about, were once what helped us to get through the night. We might still be in survival mode. Or, we might have a hard time recognizing that we no longer need to be in survival mode. But before we move on, we might have to pay respect and allow ourselves to grieve how we have been called to protect ourselves in ways that are simultaneously brilliant and destructive.”]

sand c. chang, from dreaming bigger: body liberation and weight inclusivity in health care, from The Care We Dream Of: Liberatory & Transformative Justice Approaches to LGBTQ+ Health, edited by Zena Sharman, 2021

author: CNT Madrid
title: Los teatros de Madrid vulneran el derecho a la huelga
content:
La convocatoria de Huelga General para el 11 de noviembre ya se está haciendo notar en determinados espacios escénicos de la Comunidad de Madrid. Algunos espectáculos programados para ese día están siendo cancelados o desplazados a otras fecha diferentes. Esto, según denuncian los sindicatos CNT y CGT, implica una vulneración del derecho a secundar la Huelga General a numerosas personas trabajadoras de estos espacios escénicos madrileños.


Estas situaciones se están produciendo por ejemplo en Stage Entertainment, la empresa que programa el musical El Rey León en el teatro Lope de Vega y El Alma Al Aire en el Coliseum. En ambos casos, la empresa desplazó ambas funciones del miércoles 11 al lunes 9, poniendo el día 11 como el día de libranza del personal, tal como se informó mediante comunicación interna hecha a las jefaturas de los departamentos técnicos. Lo mismo ha sucedido en el músical Six, en el teatro Gran Vía, gestionado por el grupo Smedia, y en otros teatros de este mismo grupo, como el Alcázar (Un Dios salvaje) o el Fígaro (Victoria).


Un caso similar se ha dado en los teatros Luchana, donde se ha cancelado toda la programación, dando también el día libre al personal y vulnerando así su derecho a secundar la huelga.


Se han producido también irregularidades en el musical Los Miserables, representado en el teatro Nuevo Apolo, donde ATG Entertainment ha actualizado su calendario para mover la función del día 11 al domingo 8. La plantilla de ATG fue informada del cambio mediante comunicación interna. Otros espectáculos de esta misma productora han sido cancelados ese día, como es el caso de los musicales Querido Evan Hansen en el teatro Rialto, Wicked en el Nuevo Teatro Alcalá y La función que sale mal en el Amaya.


Además se han aplazado los conciertos programados para el 11 de noviembre en el Auditorio Nacional de Música, dependiente del Ministerio de Cultura, siendo reprogramados otros días de esa misma semana.


Para los sindicatos mencionados estos son hechos muy graves que el público asistente a esos espectáculos debe conocer. Por esa razón, tanto CNT como CGT avanzan la realización de piquetes informativos en diferentes teatros madrileños. Ambas centrales anarcosindicales también hacen un llamamiento al público madrileño que hubiera adquirido entradas para el día de Huelga General, el 11 de noviembre: rechazad el cambio de fecha y solicitad la devolución de los importes abonados.

author: Maverick Avila
title: ‘Long fight ahead after ethanol spill in Tañon Strait’ – lawyer in landmark case
content:
Wastewater from an ethanol spill discolors Bais Bay, the Philippines’ Negros Oriental province, on Oct. 28, 2025, days after ethanol wastewater spilled into the bay, causing significant damage to coastal and marine ecosystems. Image courtesy of MarGale Bancairen.

Despite the somewhat funny concept, they were serious about their goal: Stop the oil exploration in the Tañon Strait by Japan Petroleum Exploration (JAPEX).

In 2007, Philippine environmental lawyer Rose Liza Eisma-Osorio and four other law professors in Cebu City sat around laughing at an idea: representing marine mammals in court.

Despite the somewhat funny concept, they were serious about their goal: Stop the oil exploration in the Tañon Strait by Japan Petroleum Exploration (JAPEX). The protected seascape between the islands of Cebu and Negros is home to 14 whale and dolphin species, as well as coral reefs and mangrove forests. The Japanese energy company performed seismic surveys and drilled an exploration well, which drove away dolphins and whales from the strait.

It was an ambitious plan, as animals had never been named as petitioners. Eisma-Osorio and fellow lawyer Golly Estenzo Ramos filed the first petition representing the resident marine mammals in December 2007. Their colleagues filed a second petition on behalf of fishing communities directly affected by the exploration activities.

The case, Resident Marine Mammals of the Protected Seascape Tañon Strait v. Secretary Angelo Reyes, went on for several years. In April 2015, the Philippine Supreme Court ruled to void the contract that allowed the exploration, development, and exploitation of petroleum resources within the Tañon Strait.

Eisma-Osorio joined Oceana Philippines as a consultant in 2015, a year after the NGO was established. At 56, she now leads the campaign and legal department as senior director of Oceana Philippines.

On October 24, 2025, a major ethanol wastewater spill hit Bais Bay, part of the Tañon Strait Protected Seascape (TSPS). Oceana Philippines collaborated with marine scientists to assess the severity of the spill. Their research, with the latest report in July this year, found that Universal Robina Corporation’s (URC) ethanol plant continued to leak wastewater, killing fish, corals and seagrass. The NGO is also consulting with fishing communities to build a court case against the company.

With more than 25 years of experience in natural resources law and policy, Eisma-Osorio believes it’s her personal responsibility to ensure there is legal accountability. In an interview with Mongabay via video call, she talked about representing marine mammals, the reaction from the community, and her current legal fight.

Mongabay: What was your thought process in deciding to represent the marine mammals in such a landmark case?

Rose Liza Eisma-Osorio: It was an ambitious undertaking. We wanted to challenge the thinking that only humans can file cases in court. And we knew there were two ways it could go: the court would throw out the case or decide to hear it. So we wanted to be sure, and we had Attorney Ramos and myself to act as stewards representing the marine mammals.

If you look at the case caption, the marine mammals were joined and represented by us, meaning they were also signing as individuals while being represented by us, because if the court did not allow them to join as litigants, it could still allow us to represent the dolphins and whales.

Mongabay: How was the case received back then, by communities, environmental groups, and even the court?

Eisma-Osorio: Around that time, what was refreshing about the campaign was that there was already an organic movement, especially the Save Tañon Strait Movement. There were very active Cebuanos, individuals, and students who helped raise awareness. The fisherfolk we represented were part of it too, so there was community engagement, because we knew they were the injured party in a way.

That was also the strategy behind two petitions. In the Philippines, you have to suffer an injury for the court to say you’re entitled to the remedy. We wanted the fisherfolk to prove their reduced catch and be heard, in the event that the court did not listen to the resident marine mammals case, since proof of injury was still a big question mark at that time.

Mongabay: At what point did you say, ‘This case is winnable?’ What was the turning point in lobbying to represent the resident marine mammals, especially with court updates? …

author: rezgar2
title: The Dark Side of the “Machine God”: 5 Unsettling Truths About Big Tech’s AI Obsession
content:
Silicon Valley routinely promises a sparkling utopia where artificial intelligence will cure complex diseases, optimize global labor, and render the very concept of money obsolete. Yet behind the polished keynotes and corporate public relations, a far more unsettling reality is taking shape. A small handful of ultra-wealthy tech oligarchs, the heads of Meta, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, are making unilateral decisions about the collective future of humanity, operating entirely outside democratic oversight or public accountability.

Silicon Valley routinely promises a sparkling utopia where artificial intelligence will cure complex diseases, optimize global labor, and render the very concept of money obsolete. Yet behind the polished keynotes and corporate public relations, a far more unsettling reality is taking shape. A small handful of ultra-wealthy tech oligarchs, the heads of Meta, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI, are making unilateral decisions about the collective future of humanity, operating entirely outside democratic oversight or public accountability.

This concentration of power exposes a jarring central paradox: the exact same tech CEOs who claim AI will solve humanity’s greatest challenges simultaneously warn that the technology could trigger civilizational extinction, openly describing their pursuit as “summoning the demon.” Rather than pausing development, these executives have accelerated an apocalyptic arms race to build ultra-powerful systems, framing themselves as indispensable guardians of human survival.

To understand where artificial intelligence is truly taking society, we must look past corporate marketing and examine the underlying worldviews, historical lineages, and material harms driving the tech elite. Moving beyond superficial consumer hype reveals how a toxic mix of fringe ideologies, extractive labor practices, and authoritarian state alliances is steering Silicon Valley toward what critical theorists and legal scholars call “techno-fascism.”

To make sense of Silicon Valley’s relentless drive toward Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) and Artificial Superintelligence (ASI), one must understand the bizarre ideological framework shaping its leaders. Coined by philosopher Emile Torres and computer scientist Timnit Gebru, the acronym TESCREAL encapsulates a bundle of tightly interwoven worldviews: Transhumanism, Extropianism, Singularitarianism, Cosmism, Rationalism, Effective Altruism, and Longtermism.

Dr. Emile Torres highlights a critical historical truth at the heart of this ideology: transhumanism is fundamentally “eugenics on steroids.” Unlike nineteenth-century eugenics, which sought merely to optimize the existing human species through selective breeding, transhumanism seeks to use radical technology to completely replace and transcend humanity, engineering an entirely new posthuman species. Within Silicon Valley AI circles, this hypothetical superintelligence is explicitly referred to as a “Machine God.” Tech CEOs effectively act as high priests, competing to bring an all-knowing digital deity into physical existence.

This radical ideology shapes corporate roadmaps in concrete, disturbing ways:

Sam Altman (OpenAI): In a blog post titled “The Merge,” Altman argued that AI surpassing human intellect is inevitable, framing un-merged human beings as a temporary “biological bootloader” for digital intelligence that will ultimately fade into an evolutionary side-branch. Altman notably paid $10,000 to join a brain-uploading waitlist with Nectome and co-founded a brain-computer interface venture to facilitate digital integration.

Ray Kurzweil & Demis Hassabis (DeepMind): Representing Extropianism and Singularitarianism, Kurzweil champions the doctrine of living long enough to achieve digital immortality, targeting a self-improving “singularity” by 2032. Hassabis, DeepMind’s co-founder, operates under a similar singularitarian impulse to engineer self-evolving intellect.

Eliezer Yudkowsky (Rationalism): A foundational figure in modern rationalist thought who famously posited a utilitarian moral calculation arguing that forcing a single person to endure 50 years of relentless torture is ethically preferable to an unfathomable number of people experiencing the mild inconvenience of a speck of dust in their eye.

Elon Musk (xAI/SpaceX): Demonstrating classic Longtermism, Musk explicitly cites the expansion of the Sun billions of years in the future to justify prioritizing …

author: labor4pal
title: Dockworkers Global Strike to Halt Militarization of Ports (Countercurrents)
content:
Dockworkers on this International Day of Action, October 30 objecting to the “militarization” of European and Mediterranean ports today held strikes across the region bringing cargo handling to a halt at 111 ports. Striking workers, activists along with several hundred students shut down the Port of Trieste for more than an hour while rallying on numerous issues. Across Europe 40 other port blockades halted operations as workers protested in France, Greece, the Basque Country, Turkey, and Morocco in North Africa under the rubric “Ports for Peace – Jobs with Dignity.”

The port blockades, described as one of the largest coordinated international strikes in history is intended to send the message that workers refuse to participate in warfare and genocide by disrupting the military logistics networks and to end the use of commercial ports as “instruments of the military machine.” In compliance with the May 2026 Istanbul Declaration published by unions at over 35 European ports, they are demanding “that port facilities not be used to transport weapons destined for war zones nor be transformed into military bases serving NATO, the United States, or the European Union” with a special focus on “the genocide against the Palestinian people and the US-Israeli war of aggression in the Middle East and against Iran.”

In Italy, the grassroots 100,000-member strong Unione Sindacale di Base (USB) along with four other unions organized the general strike and called for all sectors of the country to participate in support of their blocking military shipments to Israel for its genocide in Gaza.

The unions have declared bluntly that “We do not load death. We do not transport bullets, bombs, and missiles so children can be killed. Workers will not pay for the war economy, inflation, armaments, and the profits of the monopolies.” They have also expressed “Full solidarity with the peoples of Cuba, Venezuela and Sudan.”

Other issues to be resolved revolve around worker safety, cargo transparency, decent wages, reduced working hours, fair pension provisions, and a stop to the implementation of the “highly automated port.” This concept is being promoted by internation shipping and container transport companies, which would require fewer union workers in favor of “semi-automated crane systems, driverless transport vehicles and automated container storage planning to increase efficiency and simplify processes.”

The morning blockade at the Port of Trieste saw operations come to a halt as 5,000 people flooded into the main entry point of the normally busy port as a heavy police presence stood nearby. Before departing on a march across the city, the crowd heard from several speakers on a variety of issues, including “housing expenses and soaring rents – increases in energy costs and household utility bills,” along with the inflationary impact of escalating fuel prices. All issues which resonate with working-class people from across Europe and around the world.

Other topics broached by speakers were the continual erosion of public worker’s salaries due to high inflation and increased energy costs and the government’s preference, in claiming that there are no available funds, while spending public funds on “armaments rather than essential services.” Additionally, there were calls for an end to fossil fuels and in ending military propaganda in school curriculum.

To illustrate the issue of misplaced spending the Unione Sindacale Italiana (USI) handed out a broadsheet showing the cost of various military armament and how many new schools and hospitals could be constructed instead, for the equivalent of the billions of Euros being spent by the government. As an example, one Eurofighter jet aircraft could fully fund 25 schools and two hospitals. An obscene misuse of public funds that was reflected in numerous handmade signs carried by protesters.

After rallying, the crowd marched across the city carrying signs along with Palestinian and union flags while chanting loudly and clapping to, “Siamo tutti antifascisti” (we are all anti-fascists) and in calling for an end to the Genocide in Gaza.

author: Unknown
title: Народная Самооборона - Имеет ли марксизм научную основу? Анархистская критика диалектики
content:
Автор

: Народная Самооборона

Название

: Имеет ли марксизм научную основу? Анархистская критика диалектики

Дата

: 2010е

Дополнительная информация

: НС признана террористами/экстремистами и так далее

Источник

: веб архив


 Примечание публикатора:


Статья была откопана из веб-архива одной анархистской организации 2010-х годов. Содержание ее кажется весьма глубоким. Видно, что автор хорошо разбирается в марксизме и в философии. Автор ее, очевидно, анархист. Цель работы – не оставить камня на камне от одного из столпов марксизма – диалектическом методе. Несмотря на критический тон всей статьи, автор предлагает, что особенно ценно, некоторые ориентиры при построении настоящей современной революционной теории.


Приятного чтения!


 Первая статья из нашего цикла о марксизме, посвящена диалектическому материализму. Каждая политическая теория основана на каких-либо философских, социологических или экономических теориях. Основа марксизма – диалектика. Диалектика является ключевой теорией в марксизме – именно её зовут “научным методом”, и именно на ней построена вся система марксизма, включая экономическую и политическую теорию. Поскольку марксисты агрессивно-навязчиво рекламируют диалектику как “научную теорию”, противопоставляя её “ненаучному анархизму”, мы написали большую статью с разбором диалектики, действительного научного метода, применяемого в научном сообществе (как ни странно, ничего общего с диалектикой не имеющего) и метода, применяемого основоположником анархо-коммунизма Петром Кропоткиным.


1. Диалектический материализм.


 Философская основа марксизма представляет из себя критическое развитие Марксом и Энгельсом идей немецких философов – диалектики Гегеля и материализма Фейербаха. Соединив диалектику и материализм и критически развив их, марксисты назвали свою теорию диалектическим материализмом.


2. Диалектика


 Диалектика – это философская система, выдвигающая несколько “всеобщих законов развития”, применимых абсолютно ко всему – к природе и социуму, к истории и математике, к литературе и экономике, к живой природе и неживой… Диалектика в современном виде была разработана в начале XIX века немецким философом Гегелем. Гегель, являясь страстным сторонником идеалистического подхода полагал, что весь мир является лишь сознанием. Доказать эту точку зрения при помощи логики представлялось абсолютно невозможным, а потому Гегель был вынужден отказаться от обычной логики, и создать собственный метод, с помощью которого было бы можно обосновать, что наш мир является Абсолютным Разумом. Сама логика, говорит Гегель, является идеальным способом познания мира… но он доступен только Абсолютному Разуму, обладающему всей полнотой знания. Субъективному человеческому разуму, однако, в деле познания вселенной логика не поможет, мы не сможем понять вселенную посредством обычной логики. Потому Гегель применяет для познания Абсолютного Разума диалектику. При этом он предупреждает, что диалектический метод не должен применяться в обычной жизни, где подходят правила логики. Диалектический метод применяется им для познания вопросов основ бытия в его идеалистической манере. Марксизм, однако, переняв диалектику, перевернул это положение, и объявил о применимости диалектики во всех сферах бытия и сознания. То есть, по сути, инструмент, который самим создателем предполагался не для реальной жизни, но для абстрактных изолированных размышлений о некоем Абсолютном Разуме, охватывающем всё сущее, был перенят марксистами с отрицанием идеалистических выводов диалектики, и применим к реальной жизни. Это подобно тому, как некий теолог использовал бы Библию для познания бога, но атеисты, отрицающие само существования бога переняли бы Библию для познания сущности бутерброда с колбасой.


 То есть с самого начала диалектика являлась антинаучным инструментом. В науке, если факты не соответствуют теории, отвергается теория. Гегель же поступил наоборот, и когда теория не сошлась с фактами, он изобрёл такой метод, который бы доказал, что его теория сходится с фактами. Это подобно тому, как если бы Гегель утверждал, что огонь является жидкостью. Однако это утверждение противоречит фактам. И вместо того, чтобы отказаться от своего утверждения, Гегель отказывается от научных методов, от общеупотребительных терминов, и заменяет их такими методами, так изменяет термины, и так произвольно подбирает их, что на выходе в рамках его рассуждения огонь становится жидким. В реальной жизни огонь от этого жидким не становится, но если в рассуждениях …

author: Unknown
title: Madenciler yine yollarda
content:
Manisa - Soma’da İmbat Madencilik şirketinin işçileri bir yıllık ücretlerinin ödenmemesi üzerine haklarını alamadıkları için Ankara’ya yürüme kararı aldı. Bu, madencilerin ilk yola çıkmaları değil. 1991 yılında Zonguldak maden işçileri, 100 bin kişiyi de yanlarına alarak tarih yazdılar. Toplu iş sözleşmesi (TİS) görüşmelerinde yaşanan anlaşmazlıklar, düşük ücretler, ödenmeyen maaşlar, özelleştirme girişimleri ve hükümetin uzlaşmaz tutumu ayağa kaldırmıştı madencileri.

Son yıllarda; Uyar Madencilik, Fernas Madencilik ve Doruk Madencilik işçileri de benzer gerekçelerle Ankara’nın yolunu tuttular. Güvenlik güçleri tarafından yolları kesildi gaz yediler, gözaltılar, tutuklamalar oldu ancak hiçbir şey yollarından döndüremedi onları. Ankara’da Kurtuluş parkını mesken tuttular, direndiler ve kısmen de olsa kazandılar.

O madenciler, yerin metrelerce altında zifiri karanlıklarda daracık dehlizlerde, havasız bacalarda ölümüne çalıştırılıp analarının ak sütü gibi helal olan hakları için yollara düşüyor. İnsanlık tarihi boyunca verilen mücadelelerle alınan en temel haklarını talep ediyor. İş, güvencesi, iş güvenliği ve çalışma koşullarının iyileştirilmesini istiyor. Kısaca insanca yaşam istiyor. Ancak karşılarında her sefer kolluk güçlerini buluyorlar. Eylemler uzayınca devletin üst düzey yetkilileriyle görüştürülüyor ve tutulmayan sözler verilerek geri çevriliyorlar. Sıcacık koltuklarında devletin her türlü olanağını kullananlar madencinin çalışma koşullarını, yaşadıklarını bilmedikleri için çözüm için adım atamamakta sadece aldıkları emirleri uygulamaktalar.

Madenciler, ekmekleri için sadece alın teri akıtmayıp canlarını da feda etmekteler. Son yirmi yılda binlerce maden emekçisi hayatlarının baharında yaşama veda ettiler. Soma’da 301 işçi zehirli gazdan nefessiz kalarak öldü. Tarihteki gaz odalarının vahşetini hatırlatan manzaralar yaşandı, bir damla kan akmadan can verdi gençlerimiz. Görünen kan, bir suçlu arar. Görünen kan, unutulmaz. Soma'da da kan görülmedi ve unutuldu yaşanan vahşet.

Ermenek’te maden ocağında kirli sularda nefessiz kaldı, boğuldu madenciler. ‘Benim oğlum yüzme bilmezdi’ diyen bir ananın feryatları kayboldu katı vicdanların labirentlerinde. Elbistan’da milyonlarca ton toprağın altında kaldı canlı bedenler, hala oradalar, çıkarılamadılar. Amasra’da, Karadon’da, Dursunbey’de grizu patlamasıyla iki bin derece sıcaklıkta yandı, kavruldu taze bedenler. Bunlara benzer onlarca olayda yüzlerce hayat söndü, hikayeler çok acı bitti.

Neyin bedeliydi bu acılar, yıkımlar. Egemenlerin, sermayedarların rahat yaşaması için birilerinin bedel ödemesi gerekiyordu. İşçi sağlığı ve iş güvenliği önlemlerini almak pahalı, yaşam ucuzdu bu ülkede. Cezasızlık ve hesap vermeme de alışkanlık olmuştu nasılsa.

Şimdi, bu acıları tekrar yaşamamak için yollara düşen madencilere müesses nizamın kurallarını uymadıkları için engel olunacaktır. “Aynı gemideyiz, ülkenin gerçekleri” gerekçeleriyle talepler ötelenecek ve sistem devam ettirilecektir. Ancak, asıl gerçekler madencilerin yaşadıklarıdır. Çözüm, o gerçekler üzerinden aranmalıdır. Madencilerin zor çalışma koşullarından kaynaklı direngenlikleri, zorlukları aşma becerileri ve mücadele azmi her türlü engeli aşacak, başarıyı getirecektir.

İşçilerin, emekçilerin sorunlarının çözümü için birlikte mücadele hayati önemdedir. Tarihte madenci direnişleri, ağır çalışma koşulları ve hayati riskler barındıran bir sektör olmasından dolayı işçi sınıfı mücadelesinin en sert ve kararlı eylemleri arasında yer almıştır.

Dünyada ve Türkiye'de bu direnişler, toplumsal yapılarda ve çalışma hukukunda köklü dönüşümler yaratmıştır. Küçük bir kıvılcım düşünceleri ve duyguları harekete geçiren büyük bir güç olabilir.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Başka olanın hayali: Feminist tahayyül
content:
Feminist Tahayyül Dergisi şimdilerde feminist bilgi üreten ve bu bilgiyi erişilebilir kılan hakemli bir akademik dergi olmanın ötesine geçerek konferanslar ve seminerler de düzenliyor. 


Dergi, Ekim ayında başlayan güz dönemi seminerlerini ve 29-30 Mayıs 2027’de gerçekleşecek 3. konferansını yakın zamanda duyurdu. 


Derginin editörleri Demet Gülçiçek ve Emine Erdoğan geçtiğimiz Nisan ayında düzenledikleri konferanslarının sunuşuna şu

sözlerle

başlıyor:


“Feminist Tahayyül’ün başka türlüsü mümkün değilmiş gibi görüneni sorgulamakta inat ederek ve tüm sınırlara rağmen kendinden ödün vermemeye çalışan pratiklerde ısrarcı olarak, neşesi öfkesini azaltmadan yoluna devam etmesini diliyoruz.”


“Nedir bu Feminist Tahayyül?” sorusu üzerine bianet’e konuşan Demet ve Emine, “Feminist Tahayyül” fikrinin 2018’de, doktoralarını yaptıkları yıllarda feminist birikim üzerine kafa yorarken, feminist düşünce alanlarını çoğaltma arzusuyla ortaya çıktığını söylüyor:


“

Akademik üretim süreçlerinde feminist yaklaşımların artması, çeşitlenmesi gerektiğini düşündüğümüz için bir dergi oluşturma fikri bizi çok heyecanlandırdı.”


Dergi, ismini feminist düşüncenin akademide “eril pratiklerden” farklı biçimde var olabileceği fikrinden, “başka olanın” hayalinden alıyor. Hayal etmenin politik bir eylem olduğunu ifade eden Demet ve Emine, bu yaklaşımı derginin adına yansıtmak istediklerini belirtiyor.


Ayrıca, derginin akademik üretimdeki unvana dayalı hiyerarşiden ve  “nicelleştirilmiş puan” sistemlerinden uzak durmaya çalıştığını,  tüm editoryal süreçlerin gönüllülüğe dayalı yürütüldüğünü ve derginin açık erişimli olduğunu ekliyorlar.


Feminist Tahayyül ne yapıyor? 


2020’den bu yana yılda iki kez (Şubat ve Ağustos) olmak üzere çevrimiçi formatta, pedogoji, beden, duygulanım gibi farklı temalarda 14 sayı yayımladılar. 


2024’ten bu yana ise iki konferans ve her akademik yılda dört ila altı tane olmak üzere çeşitli alanlarda seminerler düzenlediler. Önümüzdeki dönemde Ankara’da düzenlenecek etkinliklerin takvimi şöyle: 


3 Ekim 2026 -  Erkekliğin Dönüş(eme)me Çabaları: Beden, Gençlik ve İnceller


7 Kasım 2026 – Üniversitelerde Şiddet ve Cinsel Taciz


19 Aralık 2026 – “Tuhaf” Akrabalıklar: Feminizm ve İnsansonrası Çalışmalar


29-30 Mayıs 2027 – III. Feminist Tahayyül Dergisi Konferansı


Demet ve Emine, etkinlikleri birlikte düşünmeyi ve bir araya gelmeyi mümkün kılacak önemli araçlar olarak görüyorlar: 


“

Feminizmi ‘akademi’ ve ‘sokak’ olarak keskin sınırlarla ayırmanın pek mümkün olmadığını düşünüyoruz. Bu ayrım üzerine ciddi bir tartışma olsa da feminist bilgi üretimi bir şekilde iki alandan da besleniyor… Feminist Tahayyül buluşmalarında çalışmalarını paylaşan kişiler için feminist bilgi üretiminin kolektif bir düşünme pratiği olduğu fikriyle, üniversitenin kurumsal denetim mekanizmalarından olabildiğince azade, bağımsız bir ortam oluşturmaya çalışıyoruz.” 


Feminist bilgi üretimi


Derginin web sitesini ziyaret ettiğimizde hedeflerinin, “üretilecek olan feminist bilginin erişilebilirliğini ve arşivlenmesini kolaylaştırmak, aynı zamanda Türkiye’de feminist bilginin pratik ve kuramsal yönelimlerini görünür kılmak” olduğunu görüyoruz. 


Editörler bu amacın olanaklarını ve sınırlarını şöyle ifade ediyor: 


“Feminizmin sadece “feminizm çalışanları” ilgilendirmediğini düşündüğümüz için, feminizmi ayrı bir tema olarak değil, sosyal bilimler, beşerî bilimler ve doğa bilimleri dahil herhangi bir bilimsel çalışmada olması gereken bir yaklaşım olarak görüyoruz. Fakat feminist bilginin statüsünde bazı sistematik problemler var: marjinalleştirilme, ciddiye alınmama, tehdit haline getirilme, içinin boşaltılması gibi. Bunlara rağmen, ulusaşırı feminist bilgi üretme pratiklerinin inanılmaz etkileyici bir ısrarı var. Temel kavramlara dair teorik tartışmalardan kıyafet ceplerinin cinsiyetlendirilmiş kullanımına kadar geniş bir yelpazeden bahsediyoruz.”


Feminist hafıza 


Demet ve Emine, ürettikleri çalışmaların gelecekte farklı bir zaman ve bağlam üzerinden değerlendirilecek olmasının hem romantik hem de endişe verici boyutları olduğuna dikkat çekiyor. 


Feminist yayıncılık pratiklerinin tarihsel süreçte birbirinin birikimine dayanmasını meselenin “romantik” ve politik açıdan umut verici yönü olarak tanımlarken, feminist hafızanın bu şekilde inşa edildiğini belirtiyor. 


Bu tarihsel bağın, farklı dönemler ve bağlamlar arasındaki mesafeyi kısaltarak yalnızlık hissini ortadan kaldırdığını ifade ediyorlar. 


Demet ve Emine, Feminist …

title: Συγκεντρώσεις αλληλεγγύης, Δευτέρα 2/11
content:
>Κάλεσμα στο δικαστήριο για την υπόθεση της εκκένωσης Ya Basta, 9:00 δικαστικό μέγαρο Ιωαννίνων


>Καμιά ποινή στις συναδέλφισσες του 3ου Δ.Σ. Ραφήνας, 13:00 Πειθαρχικό Συμβούλιο ανθρώπινου δυναμικού δημόσιου τομέα


Κάλεσμα στο δικαστήριο για την υπόθεση της εκκένωσης Ya Basta


ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗ ΣΤΑ 2 ΔΙΩΚΟΜΕΝΑ ΣΥΝΤΡΟΦΙΑ ΓΙΑ ΤΗΝ ΕΚΚΕΝΩΣΗ ΤΗΣ ΚΑΤΑΛΗΨΗΣ YA BASTA


Στις 23 Σεπτεμβρίου του 2024 εκκενώνεται η Κατάληψη Ya Basta στο Πανεπιστήμιο Ιωαννίνων μετά από επιχείρηση της τεχνικής υπηρεσίας μαζί με ομάδες της ΟΠΚΕ και της κρατικής ασφάλειας. Ο χώρος σφραγίστηκε προσωρινά, έγινε κατάσχεση αντικειμένων και συλλογή δαχτυλικών αποτυπωμάτων και DNA. Στο σήμερα 2 συντρόφια μας διώκονται για παρακώλυση δημόσιας υπηρεσίας και διατάραξη οικιακής ειρήνης (καθώς η κατάληψη στεγαζόταν στο κτίριο των Ά Εστιών) με μοναδικά αποδεικτικά στοιχεία δαχτυλικά αποτυπώματα πάνω σε κινητά αντικείμενα.


Χρειάζεται αρχικά να πούμε ότι η Κατάληψη Ya Basta ήταν ένα ακόμα λιθαράκι στην καταληψιακή – κινηματική ιστορία της πόλης. Δεν θα επιτρέψουμε επομένως σε κανένα καθίκι, είτε θεσμικό είτε με την προβιά του αγωνιστή, να λασπολογεί απέναντι σε καταλήψεις και στέκια, εκκενώντας χώρους και στοχοποιώντας συντρόφια, στο βωμό της πολιτικής καριέρας. Η Ya Basta ήταν ένας απελευθερωμένος χώρος από το 2011 και είχε ενεργή παρουσία μέχρι και το 2013. Με την αυτοδιάλυσή της, ο χώρος παρέμεινε έρμαιο στα χέρια ενός τυχοδιώκτη που παρασιτούσε εκεί για προσωπικό του όφελος. Το Δεκέμβρη του 2023 ομάδα συντροφιών αποφάσισε να ανακαταλάβει τον χώρο προσδίδοντας του ξανά πολιτικά χαρακτηριστικά και ανοίγοντας τις πόρτες του. (

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1628942/

). Από το 2024 και με την επανοικειοποίηση της κατάληψης ο χώρος απέκτησε ξανά ζωή με συνελεύσεις και δομές, προϋπάρχουσες στην κατάληψη, παίρνοντας την σκυτάλη από την πολιτική παρακαταθήκη του χώρου και με τακτικά ανοίγματα επιτρέποντας την ελεύθερη αλληλεπίδραση και επικοινωνία ατόμων αντιιεραρχικά και αυτοοργανωμένα (

https://yabastasquat.espivblogs.net/

). Παράλληλα, υπήρχαν καταλήψεις εστιών που πρόσεθεταν μια διάχυτη αυτοοργανωμένη λογική και μια κοινοτική κάλυψη των βασικών αναγκών αλληλοτροφοδοτώντας την αυτοπραγμάτωση του καταληψιακού αξιακού.

Ενάντια στην αποστειρωμένη και αποξενωμένη πραγματικότητα που επιβάλλει το σύγχρονο ελληνικό πανεπιστήμιο οι καταλήψεις και συλλογικές διαδικασίες είναι αγκάθι και αντιπρόταση στην ζοφερή αυτή πραγματικότητα.


Ξετυλίγοντας, λοιπόν το νήμα της καταστολής του Σεπτέμβρη του 2024, οι πρωτοστάτες στην επιβολή του νόμου και της τάξης δεν είναι όπως θα περιμέναμε μπάτσοι ή ρουφιάνοι της Άννας Μπατιστάτου (πρύτανης του Πανεπιστημίου Ιωαννίνων), αλλά οι πεμπτοφαλαγγίτες της αριστεράς αυτή τη φορά με το προσωπείο της Τετάρτης Διεθνούς. Το οργανωτικό σχήμα ΟΚΔΕ/ΣΣΠ με πλήρη και χρόνια εργαλειοποίηση του Συλλόγου Εστιακών Φοιτητών επιτέθηκε κυκλωτικά και υπεράριθμα σε σώμα συντρόφων μετά την κατάληψη φοιτητικής εστίας.(

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1631698/

 ,

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1631724/

)


Την επόμενη μέρα κι ενώ αλληλέγγυος κόσμος βρισκόταν στην κατάληψη για συνέλευση ενάντια στους ηγεμονισμούς και τραμπουκισμούς των παρακρατικών της ΟΚΔΕ η ασφάλεια του Πανεπιστήμιου Ιωαννίνων χτυπάει την πόρτα και ανακοινώνει την άμεση εκκένωση του χώρου μέχρι το βράδυ της ίδιας μέρας. (

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1631706/

) Ακολουθεί ένα 10ήμερο κινητοποιήσεων στο Πανεπιστήμιο με μικροφωνικές, αφισοκολλήσεις, παρεμβάσεις και ανοιχτές διαδικασίες για την υπεράσπιση της κατάληψης. Τα ξημερώματα στις 23 Σεπτέμβρη μπάτσοι και υπάλληλοι της τεχνικής υπηρεσίας εισβάλλουν στον χώρο και μέσα σε λίγες ώρες τον αδειάζουν και κατάσχουν όσα αντικείμενα υπάρχουν μέσα προκειμένου να μεταφερθούν για αποτυπώματα και DNA (

https://athens.indymedia.org/post/1631858/

). Μέτα από 5 μήνες γίνεται επιχείρηση “σκούπα” από μπάτσους στις εστίες του πανεπιστημίου κάνοντας ντου στα κατειλλημένα δωμάτια με ασφαλίτες να ρωτάνε για τον κόσμο που συμμετείχε στην Κατάληψη Ya Basta.


Ερχόμενα στο τώρα, μετά από 2 χρόνια έρχεται δικογραφία σε 2 συντρόφια μας, διωκόμενα από την Πρύτανη Α. Μπατιστάτου για παρακώλυση δημόσιας υπηρεσίας και διατάραξη οικιακής ειρήνης με μόνο αποδεικτικό στοιχείο τα δαχτυλικά αποτυπώματα σε 3 κινητά αντικείμενα (2 βάζα και 1 ετικέτα από μπουκάλι νερού). Τα δαχτυλικά αποτυπώματα είναι πρωτοφανής μέθοδος δίωξης για τα δεδομένα της πόλης, αλλά εννοείται ότι δεν μας εκπλήσσει, καθώς ξέρουμε πολύ καλά ότι οι κατασταλτικοί μηχανισμοί …

author: ACG
title: Labour and the budget: same old same old (with a side of pickles)
content:
When Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey presented his budget on Wednesday October 28

th

 he said: “This is a Budget for the working people of Britain. For British businesses, big and small.”  Well, no. It offered little to working people, and plenty to businesses, to the military and to the defence industry.


We were offered the pittance of 86p a week off of electricity bills. In addition, there will be a £100 one-off winter fuel payment for 20 million households in council tax bands A to D. This will almost immediately be wiped out by a predicted rise by £276 in January, to just under £2,000 a year. Another forecast from the EDF energy company, predicted that it might rise higher than this.


Healey introduced a £2 cap on single bus fares in England from January 2027. But, for example, many workers and students in London cannot afford to live in inner London and must make long journeys by bus to get to work and study, because they cannot afford the rail and tube fares.


He also announced the end of gas standing charges, which will save a mere £45 a year, and then only for 60% of households. Healey had already announced that an extra £432 million would be spent on a programme to get rough sleepers in England off the streets. Unpaid carers would no longer lose all of their Carer’s Allowance if they earnt more than 1p over the £204 allowed and instead there would be a tapered payment.


On the other hand, Healey reassured the boss class by stating that he was committed to “prevent regulation from holding back investment by removing regulation and tariffs worth £800m to business.” The banks feared that the corporation tax surcharge would be raised by as much as 8 per cent. In fact, Healey only raised it by six per cent, and smarmed the banks by saying,” I celebrate and am grateful for the role you play”. In fact, this surcharge will only last for 15 months from January. As a result, share prices of the main UK banks increased, after the budget announcement.


The Financial Times, the bosses’ voice, enthusiastically noted that Healey and Burnham wanted to reassure business and the banks.


He promised an increase of £10 billion on economic and military support for Ukraine, in addition to the £25 billion already committed by previous Tory and Labour administrations. He would also make cuts in the budgets of various government departments by 1%to further fund defence spending. As a result, the Warm Homes Plan, would suffer a £1 billion cut. He promised a maximum amount of private investment in defence, including through public private partnerships.


Labour had promised to end discriminatory age bands and to increase the minimum wage for 18- to 20-year-olds to be the same as those over 21 years old. Healey broke this promise with the 18 to 20 years olds earning nearly £2 an hour less. scrapping “discriminatory” age bands, and to increasing the minimum wages for 18- to 20-year-olds so young workers are paid the same as those over 21. Healey broke this promise—18- to 20-year-olds will still earn nearly £2 an hour less. The rate for both age levels will rise by 3.9% but this will be cancelled out by rising inflation.


Labour will use these young workers as a cheap labour force, and is already pushing an unpaid work experience scheme at Sainsbury’s.


Labour is preparing for further attacks on welfare, and Healey promised, “As the Prime Minister and I have both said, we will bring down the welfare bill.” They are eying up attacking the Personal Independence Payment, the major disability benefit. All of this is in the pipeline.


Healey did not remove the Triple Lock on pensions, and this will not happen before the 2030 election, but made the menacing statement that Labour would adjust the Triple Lock after that.


All in all, the budget was low key, with a series of minor announcements. In addition to the above, there was the removal of import tax on some 100 products, meaning cheaper prices for things like, baked beans, gherkins, garlic and marmalade. This was derided widely in the media, as this would save around £21 a year, or £1.75 a month! Parental pay would be extended, so that 150,000 parents will receive two weeks of support of up to £194 a week. Again, this will be wiped out by rising inflation.


So, no real challenge to big business and a massive increase in defence spending, with looming attacks on pensioners, young workers and the disabled. But we never expected anything else from the Burnham …

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Tolstoycu Köylülerin Kısa Tarihi
content:
Yazan: Cory Bushman


Çeviren: Gorthim


Çevirilen Asıl Metin


PDF Linki


“Özgür Hıristiyanlar” olarak da bilinen Tolstoycular, Rus edebiyat dehası Lev Tolstoy’un sadık takipçileriydi. Rus Ortodoks Kilisesi’nin yolsuzluk yaptığına dair algıları ve çarlık rejimiyle olan ilişkileri nedeniyle bu kiliseye karşı çıkmışlardı. Tolstoycular, Rus Ortodoksluğunu uygulamak yerine, Tolstoy’un “vahiy” yoluyla ortaya koyduğu “saf” bir dini izlediler. Tolstoy, organize bir din kurmadı; ancak “şu anda hüküm süren uyumsuzluk, aldatma ve şiddet”in yerine “özgür uzlaşma, hakikat ve kardeşçe sevgi”yi getirecek bir yaşam felsefesi geliştirdi.

1


Tolstoy’un hakikat ve kardeşçe sevgi felsefesi, tam anlamıyla şiddetsizlik, vejetaryenlik, komünal yaşam ve alkol, tütün ve küfürden uzak durmayı içeren bir ahlak kuralları üzerine dayanıyordu.


Tolstoycuların üye sayısı, 1917’de yaklaşık altı bin iken 1931’de binin altına düştü. 1940’larda, Bolşeviklerin şiddetli zulmünün bir sonucu olarak, sayıları neredeyse yok olma noktasına kadar azaldı. Sovyet Rusya’daki Bolşevik yönetimi sırasında Tolstoycular gibi dini mezheplerin sistematik olarak ortadan kaldırılması, iktidarı kaybetme korkusuyla sürekli yaşayan istikrarsız ve militarist bir hükümetin doğrudan bir sonucuydu.


1870’lerin ortalarında Lev Nikolayeviç Tolstoy, şiddetli bir depresyon dönemine girdi. İntihar düşünceleri giderek artan Tolstoy, zihnindeki yükü hafifletmek için Buda ve Schopenhauer gibi filozoflara yöneldi. Bu karanlık dönemde yaşamın anlamını arayışı, onu Hristiyanlığa kişisel bir dönüşüme götürdü. Daha sonra bu deneyimiyle ilgili şöyle yazdı: “Şimdi anlıyorum ki, kendimi öldürmemiş olmam, düşüncelerimin geçersizliğine dair içimde var olan belirsiz bir farkındalığın sonucuydu.”

2

 Hristiyanlığa dönüşünün kendisini ölümden kurtardığını defalarca ifade etti.


Tolstoy’un din değiştirmesi, onu daha sonra “gerçek” Hıristiyanlık olarak ilan edeceği şeyi aramaya yöneltti. Rus köylülerinin yalın inancını, peşinden gitmesi gereken bir şey olarak gördü. Tolstoy, Rus Ortodoks Kilisesi’nin dini gerçekleri çarpıtarak ve insanları felç eden batıl inançlar yaratarak köylüleri yozlaştırdığını düşünüyordu. Buna karşılık Rus Ortodoks Kilisesi, Leo Tolstoy’dan hoşnut değildi ve 24 Şubat 1901’de onu resmen aforoz etti. Kilise bu karara sadık kaldı; Tolstoy’un 1910’daki ölümünün ardından, onu bir heretik olarak nitelendirerek kilise cenazesi düzenlemeyi reddetti.


Zamanla Tolstoy’un felsefeleri yaygınlaştı ve öncelikle entelijansiya üyeleri ile Tolstoy’un yakın olduğu köylülerden oluşan küçük gruplar tarafından hayata geçirildi. Tolstoy’un dini felsefelerinin popülaritesi arttıkça, Çar tarafından eserlerine uygulanan sansür de şiddetlendi. Tolstoy’un eserlerinin çoğu, el yazısı ve hektografla çoğaltılmış kopyaların zamanında hazırlanması sayesinde dolaşımda kalabildi. 1893’te Tolstoy’un sekreteri Vladimir Chertkov, Tolstoy’un bazı yazıları korumak amacıyla İngiltere’ye gitti, ancak dönüşünde sürgüne gönderildi.


Tolstoy’un dini ve toplumsal değişim çağrısına yanıt veren bilinen ilk gruplardan biri Dukhoborlar’dı. Dukhoborlar sadece askerlik hizmetini reddetmekle kalmadılar, aynı zamanda silahlarını imha ettiler ve organize ayaklanmalar düzenlediler. En ünlü ayaklanmaları 1895 yılının Paskalya Günü’nde gerçekleşti. Ayaklanmanın gerekçesi olarak şu beş ilkeyi öne sürdüler:


“1. Çara karşı çıkma, 2. Askerlik hizmetine karşı çıkma, 3. Özel mülkiyete karşı çıkma, 4. Et yemeye karşı çıkma ve 5. Cinsel ilişkiye karşı çıkma.”

3


Paskalya Günü ayaklanmasından üç yıl sonra, Dukhoborlar Tolstoy’un maddi yardımıyla baskıcı çarlık yönetiminden kurtulup Kanada’ya göç edebildiler. Tolstoycular ise Dukhoborların aksine, yasaları tamamen reddetmeye daha meyilliydi ve eylemlerinin sonuçlarından kaçma lüksüne sahip değillerdi.


Tolstoycular, Tolstoy’un pasifizm felsefesini sadakatle takip ediyorlardı ve inançları uğruna fedakârlık yapmaya hazırdılar. Tolstoycu Vasya Kirin, ailesine askere gitmeyi reddettiğini açıkladığında, karısı “Seni öldüreceklerini biliyorsun” diye cevap verdi. O ise cesurca şöyle dedi: “Bırakın beni öldürsünler, yeter ki ben kimseyi öldürmeyeyim.”

4


Tolstoycuların vicdani retçi olarak üstlendikleri rol, yalnızca askerlik hizmetini reddetmekle kalmayıp, askeri vergileri ödemeyi ve okullarda verilen askeri eğitimi de reddetmeyi içeriyordu. Sıkı bir pasifist inanca sahip olsalar da, Tolstoycular her bireyin kendi vicdanına göre hareket etmesi gerektiğine inanıyorlardı. Tolstoycu …

title: 100 mila in piazza solo a Torino
content:
Ripubblichiamo il comunicato di

Torino è contro il riarmo.


Anche in occasione dello sciopero generale, chiamato grazie all’Unione Sindacale di Base, Torino ha saputo dare un segnale forte. 


Tutta la città bloccata, dal centro – così tanto al centro del dibattito pubblico in quanto rappresentazione della città vetrina da preservare – sino all’imbocco della tangenziale Nord, per dire no al riarmo e basta al carovita causato dalle scelte politiche di questo governo. 


Le strade sono state inondate da giovani e meno giovani, da studenti delle scuole e dell’università (che rimane tutt’ora occupata nella sede del Campus Einaudi) ai lavoratori della scuola ai precari della ricerca, ma anche da pensionati, disoccupati, famiglie, cittadini, lavoratori e lavoratrici che hanno deciso di fermarsi per un giorno e bloccare la produzione, la circolazione e il consumo delle merci. 


Anche la serata di Torino è stata vivacizzata da un corteo che è riuscito a rimarcare la necessità di prendere le strade centrali della città con una partecipazione importante che man mano è andata ingrossandosi. 


C’è bisogno di continuare a confrontarsi, a ritrovarsi negli spazi liberati e nelle strade, perchè questo è soltanto l’inizio di una lunga lotta che ha l’obiettivo di cambiare il corso della storia. 


Ci uniamo all’invito di ItaliainPiazza17 per una nuova mobilitazione che si terrà sabato 7 novembre alle ore 15 in piazza Castello!

author: Carine Kaneza Nantulya
title: Kenya’s 2027 Election: Time to Address the Warning Signs
content:
On August 16, 2026, hundreds of people armed with machetes, guns, and sticks

attacked

 a convoy carrying opposition politicians and supporters of the Linda Mwananchi movement in Homa Bay county, western Kenya. The attackers killed at least three people and beat and robbed journalists covering the violence. Witnesses said police officers were present but failed to contain the attacks. The incident was among

a series of violent attacks targeting civil society events and opposition gatherings

 in the months leading up to Kenya’s August 10, 2027, general elections. At least six people have reportedly been killed and dozens injured in these attacks, raising serious concerns about the safety of political participation as the campaign season gathers pace.


I returned to Nairobi, Kenya’s capital, where my colleagues and I have been speaking with people from different walks of life to understand how they view the political and human rights environment ahead of the 2027 elections for president and the National Assembly. President William Ruto is expected to seek a second term, while opposition parties and candidates have already begun mobilizing supporters at rallies across the country.


One conversation, with a 28-year-old woman, stayed with me.


“I will not vote in next year’s elections.”


Her words were clear and definitive. I asked her why.


“It is always the same. Our votes do not change anything.”


Another young woman sitting nearby offered a different perspective. We need to look beyond elections, she said, and ask what elections are supposed to achieve: ensuring that every vote counts, that people can participate freely, and that everyone—including women—can participate without fear.


Our conversations revealed a growing sense of anxiety about the elections, and a troubling lack of confidence that the institutions responsible for protecting people’s rights will be able to prevent violence and ensure accountability.


First, there is a palpable fear that the 2027 elections could be violent. Several people we met—including civil society actors, opposition members, grassroots organizers, and youth mobilizers—pointed

to recent violence at political rallies

 as early warning signs.


The violence in Homa Bay was repeatedly described as a turning point. For many, it signaled a deterioration in the political environment and raised concerns about what could lie ahead as campaigning intensifies.


Then there are the so-called “goons”—gangs, allegedly

mobilized or paid

 by politicians to disrupt political rallies, intimidate opponents, and engage in violence. I repeatedly asked interlocutors how best to describe this phenomenon.


Some drew parallels with the

Mungiki,

 an ethnic-based militia and criminal gang that has historically been mobilized for political violence and was entangled in Kenya’s electoral cycles. Opposition and civil society members described young people being mobilized or allegedly paid to disrupt rallies, intimidate political opponents, and influence political gatherings. Some alleged links to senior officials but provided no evidence. The consistency with which these allegations were raised points to a serious concern: the blurring of the lines between political violence, organized criminality, and the government security apparatus, underscoring the need for independent, impartial, and transparent investigations.


At the heart of these concerns is impunity. The

lack of accountability for past abuses

 has left many questioning whether state institutions will protect them or hold those responsible for the abuse accountable.


Some people we met questioned the role of the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights. Young people expressed doubts about the effectiveness of its statements and said it should do more. When we raised these concerns with commissioners, they cited constraints including inadequate funding and other significant capacity and resource limitations.


People also raised concerns about the

independence and effectiveness

 of other institutions responsible for protecting rights and ensuring electoral integrity, including the judiciary, the electoral commission and the Independent Policing Oversight Authority.


A young Gen Z leader described the contradiction between increased youth political engagement and growing fear. Despite young people mobilizing through protests and registering to vote, she told us: “We are all scared

.”

author: Ahmed Ismat Ahmed
title: El Fasher, a year later
content:
Nasr City, October 26, 2026

Today is the anniversary, and I still don’t know what that word is supposed to do for anyone.

I was in Cairo when the city fell. I disappeared there — not in any way a person standing outside me could have seen — and I am not leaving that out, as if the one doing the remembering were a pane of glass. But El Fasher sits on an older arithmetic, and the arithmetic is where I have to start.

The old arithmetic

I was in the street in Omdurman on International Women’s Day in 2019, a month before they finally put Omar al-Bashir out of the palace he had occupied for 30 years. Three out of every four people in that crowd were women. The proportion mattered because NISS — the National Intelligence and Security Service, Sudan’s secret police, who have spent decades learning exactly where a society keeps its weight — knew where to look. They find it. Then they go after it.

So they started arresting the women.

There was nothing accidental in this, and nothing hidden. They were not ashamed, because shame requires believing someone is watching who matters, and they did not believe that. If the police took a man that day, it cost almost nothing to get him back: a friend, a cousin, anyone his age from his own street could walk into that station the same afternoon and walk him out again, because a man’s word, in that system, was still worth something on its own. A woman could not do this. A woman arrested had to produce a man — a father, a brother, a husband, some uncle twice removed — because the state had built itself, brick by brick, on the conviction that a woman’s name, standing alone, was not collateral enough to release a woman’s body.

I watched it work. I watched women I knew go quiet in the weeks after, not because they themselves had been taken, but because they understood, suddenly and completely, that the price had changed shape under their feet. It was no longer only her own body in the cell. It was her family’s name, dragged into a police station because she had been standing in a square where the government had decided women should not stand.

That is the oldest trick this state has ever run. I have come to call the thing that runs it a machine — not a government with occasional failures, but an arrangement built to find whatever a population has left, and take it. The war now being fought in Darfur did not invent the trick. The Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary formed from the Janjaweed — the militias the state itself armed in Darfur two decades ago — inherited it, and scaled it, until a tactic became the way a siege was built.

The city

The siege had an address. Most people who will read this have only ever met it as a dateline, and a dateline doesn’t let you feel what was emptied.

Darfur is the west of Sudan. It is about the size of Spain, pressed up against Chad, Libya, and the Central African Republic, far enough from the Nile and from Khartoum that the center has always been able to treat the distance as a kind of ownership. Farmers and herders live there — Fur, Zaghawa, Masalit, Berti, Borgo, Rizeigat, and more peoples than a briefing ever bothers to list — Arab and non-Arab, in categories the last century hardened and this one found useful. They have shared land, and they have fought over land, and since 2003 they have done both inside a counterinsurgency. The rebellion started the way rebellions in that region usually start. The center took men for its wars and sent almost nothing back. Bashir’s government answered by arming militias, the ones the world learned to call the Janjaweed, and aiming them at the communities the rebels came from. Hundreds of thousands died. The world said genocide, and then largely changed the channel. The militias were not disbanded. They were paid, given rank, and renamed. The Rapid Support Forces are that renaming. Their commander is Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, Hemedti, and he is at war with the army that made the renaming official. El Fasher is where that arrangement came back to the ground it was built on.

The city is older than any of these men. It was the capital of the Fur sultanate, the place Darfur governed itself from, until that was broken from the outside in 1874. Ali Dinar put a sultanate back together in what was left and held it until 1916, when the British killed him and took Darfur into Sudan. After that El Fasher was no longer a capital in the old sense. It was the town where the new state proved it could still reach the …

author: Alf Gunvald Nilsen
title: Southern Authoritarian Populism
content:
The early twenty-first century is a time of monsters in the Global South. 


What do these monsters look like? 


Let me begin with those at work closest to home, namely in post-apartheid South Africa, where I live and work. 


On 30 June 2026, the country’s streets were awash with hate. In cities like Johannesburg, Durban, and Pretoria, as well as in smaller towns, tens of thousands of people – mostly poor and working-class Black South Africans – marched behind slogans blaming undocumented migrants from other African countries for unemployment, crime, failing public services, and drug addiction. Their rallying cry was simple:

Abahambe!

 – They Must Go! The day itself – 30 June – was the “deadline” that xenophobic organizations had set for undocumented migrants to leave the country. In the months leading up to this date, these organizations mobilized popular support for the idea of expulsion across the country. As the deadline approached, thousands of African foreigners flocked to their diplomatic missions to seek emergency repatriation. At least four people were killed before the marches took place, and countless others lost their livelihoods or fled their communities in fear.


Much about this moment was uniquely South African. Above all, the fact that the targets of hate, violence, and murder are Black African migrants, not White migrants from the Global North like me, has been a constant across similar upsurges in 2008, 2015, and 2019. This has led the Cameroonian scholar Achille Mbembe to speak of Afrophobia – a fear and hatred specifically of the Black African Other – as a distinctive predicament of South Africa’s post-apartheid order.  


Yet it was also something more. Across the Global South, we have witnessed the rise of a monstrous far-right politics that rallies majoritarian people-nations against ominous Others while normalizing increasingly authoritarian political orders. This far right takes multiple forms: in some cases, such as Erdogan’s Turkey or Narendra Modi’s India, it manifests as

entrenched

 far-right regimes with a firm grip on political power; in other cases, such as Brazil and the Philippines, it has found expression in

emergent

 formations that have won power electorally without succeeding in consolidating durable regimes but still maintain a strong presence in politics and society. In yet other cases, such as South Africa, the far right is present in more embryonic forms, as reactionary social movements and parties that have begun to make their sway felt in the political domain and throughout the social fabric.


I refer to these political monstrosities as Southern authoritarian populism, and the purpose of this essay is to provide a politically enabling diagnosis of it. My argument is not simply that authoritarian populism has appeared in different countries across the Global South. It is that these diverse trajectories are part of an interconnected turn toward the far right across the Global South. Rather than looking at these regimes, parties, and movements in ways that make despair convincing, I want to present a reading that makes hope possible.


This begs an obvious question: where do we find the critical intellectual resources that enable us to untangle the politics of the new far right in the Global South? My search for an answer to this question has led me to two major conclusions. The first of these is that standard academic perspectives on autocratization and far-right populism have little to offer us. Studies of autocratization show us how strongman leaders eviscerate democratic institutions, procedures, and norms. Populism studies have painted vivid portraits of how these leaders perform far-right politics as a distinctive political style. However, neither of these perspectives can tell us much about the real questions we should be asking if we want to understand Southern authoritarian populism from a progressive and radical perspective and in a way that allows us to counteract it. 


So what are the questions that we have to ask? They are questions about the political economy that has generated the precarious working classes that align with the far right; about the structures of feeling, simultaneously aspirational and anxious, that the far right has been capable of harnessing within this political economy; and they are questions about the ideological work that articulates diverse social forces into revanchist people-nations and produces consent from below to projects …

author: Abahlali_3
title: We mourn the loss of Des D’sa
content:
30 October 2026 Abahlali baseMjondolo press statement

We mourn the loss of Des D’Sa, father, uncle, grandfather, and a comrade to many

The death of Desmond D’Sa has plunged many people on the left in Durban and beyond, across numerous organisations, into shock and despair. Siyakhala ngo Des.

Comrade Des was a stalwart in the struggle against apartheid and was a well-known organiser who formed the South Durban Community Environmental Alliance (SDCEA), an environmental organisation that raised the concerns of families living in the oil- and gas-affected areas of Wentworth and the Bluff.

His activism and the fight against injustices did not end with environmental issues and it definitely did not end in Wentworth and the Bluff. Comrade Des fought against all forms of oppression and injustice, including gangsterism and the mining companies in rural areas, and supported everyone from fisherfolk to migrants and poor people, whether living in flats, hostels or shacks. He did not back down when struggle became dangerous. Comrade Des spoke fluent isiZulu and engaged everyone with the same respect.

He joined the first march against ANC councillor Yacoob Baig organised from Kennedy Road in 2005, which became part of the process towards the formation of our movement. He stood with our movement from the beginning, and was one of the few who never wavered in his support even when we were under severe attack and isolated.

Comrade Des was one of the founders of the Right to Know Campaign that fought fought against secrecy while promoting the right to information. He was also one of the founders of The Durban Coalition, which was first formed in response to the devastating floods of 2022. The Coalition, which unites community organisations across the city in a united front, is thriving today and is an important formation in the city.

We will miss Comrade Des so much. He was always on the side of the people. He was always so warm and kind. We always laughed when he was around.

We wish to thank his family for him. And wish to express our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and comrades.

It is so sad and devastating that you have left us. Till we meet again.

Hamba kahle Comrade Des D’Sa. Ubuyiqhawe.

author: Anele Mbi
title: Buffalo City’s broken houses and decades of empty promises
content:
A housing rectification project in Braelyn Extension 10 in Buffalo City Municipality (BCM) has left residents frustrated with the municipality’s failure to address severe structural faults.


Serious defects in the RD houses include cracked walls and roofs, leaking roofs, and inadequate foundations. Braelyn residents say they have repeatedly complained to the municipality, which has promised to rebuild the houses since 2004, but has taken no action until today, except for a laydown yard constructed by the sitting, ANC ward councillor, Mendi Wetsetse.


The stalled housing project intersects with service-delivery defects across the ward, including unpaved and potholed roads, poor refuse collection, and electricity shortages brought about by the growing Inkandla informal settlement.


Recently, President Cyril Ramaphosa authorised the Special Investigating Unit (SIU) to probe allegations of extensive corruption and maladministration of major BCM tenders.


According to Braelyn residents, talks about rectifying Braelyn Ext 10 RDP houses began before 2010. The then ward councillor, Thabo Myira, who served as a councillor between 2005 and 2010, confirmed the claim.


Media reports also indicate that in 2009, the then minister of human settlements, Tokyo Sexwale promised people living in faulty RDP houses in East London that their houses would be rebuilt. Today, councillor Wetsetse, who is campaigning for a third term in the upcoming local government election, promised to rectify the situation.


Housing defects


Ntombizanele Mabala, an 80-year-old pensioner, said since residents arrived in Braelyn in 1997, they have complained to councillors and the municipality about the poor condition of their houses, but their pleas were ignored. “These are not houses but hokkies. We have children and a family of six. Rain comes in from every direction – through the roof, the walls and underneath – because these houses have no foundations,” she said. “The councillor promised that the housing rectification process would begin before 4 November, but there are still no signs of work apart from a laydown-yard fence erected two years ago.”


Another pensioner, Nothembile Mqhayi, whose house was built below ground level, said her house floods when it rains. She showed

Elitsha

 a hole she had made at the bottom of a wall to let water that entered the house drain out.


The Mqhayi family had to make a hole in the wall to drain out water when the house floods.


Ziyanda Mpakantsho (42), who recently joined an EPWP project and earns R3,000 a month, said rectification is urgently needed because she lives with a sick and disabled person. “I grew up hearing that the cracks in the walls would be repaired, but many years have passed. These Braelyn houses have no proper foundations, so water leaks in when it rains. The houses have not been rectified because the money is being squandered,” she said.


Zama Thutha (70) said the government had not fixed the RDP houses because it was corrupt and unaccountable to voters. “Even the EPWP jobs created recently will end after the elections. Our system of government is capitalism, which puts profit before the needs of ordinary people,” he said.


Recurring delays and more promises


Responses from both the BCM and the Eastern Cape department of human settlements (DHS) are not only conflicting but also suggest the rectification process remains a false hope for Braelyn residents. When asked whether the municipality or its ward councillor has made any promises of rectification, the municipality said the provincial government is responsible for the rectification process.


“The Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality wishes to clarify that it does not currently run a municipal housing rectification programme; this falls outside local government funding allocations. What we can say is that the laydown yard established on-site remains a site-securing measure for future development once capital is allocated.”


The laydown yard is overgrown

.


The provincial DHS said that, despite the constitutional principle of cooperative governance that compels the various spheres of government to share information and support each other, implementation requires compliance with the necessary technical, administrative, planning, and budgetary processes. The department has not denied the fact that rectification has been recognised for several years.
