author: Lance Selfa
title: What to expect in the US midterm elections
content:
The Republican Party, also known as the GOP or Grand Old Party, controls both chambers of the US Congress, allowing President Donald Trump to pursue his far-right agenda with little legislative resistance. But that may soon change.

In the United States, federal elections occur every two years. The congressional midterms, so named because they occur in the middle of a president’s term, will be held on Tuesday. Polling suggests Republicans will be trounced. Voters will elect all 435 members of the House of Representatives, who serve fixed two-year terms, and about one-third of the 100 Senators, who serve six-year terms. A range of state-level races, including for governors in California, Michigan and Florida, will also take place.

The Democratic Party is expected to win back control of the House and possibly even the Senate. But just how much difference will that make?

Lance Selfa

, author of

The Democrats: A Critical History

 and editor of

US Politics in an Age of Uncertainty

, previews the elections and what might come after them.

Multiple indicators point to a Democratic victory in the midterm elections. Trump is an historically unpopular president. Gasoline and diesel prices are at their highest in years because of Trump’s war in Iran.

Consumer confidence is at a 73-year low

, and

74 percent of Americans

 tell pollsters that the country is moving in the wrong direction.

So it’s no surprise that Democrats are favoured to win the House. In fact, Republicans have given up trying to forestall that.

Data-driven forecasters like G. Elliott Morris

 and Nate Silver place the probability of a Democratic House higher than 90 percent, and the probability of the Democrats winning the Senate at 70 percent or higher.

The well-regarded

New York Times

 poll

, published 21 October, estimated that, were the election held then, Democrats would receive 52 percent of the vote, compared to 41 percent for the Republicans. If that holds, it will be the biggest Democrat popular-vote margin in a midterm election since the Watergate scandal brought down the Republicans in 1974.

That result wouldn’t represent an endorsement for the Democratic Party, which remains as unpopular as the Republicans. But US midterm elections are classically “throw the bums out” elections. And the Republicans, who control all parts of the national government, are the bums this year.

Trump and his toadies declare the polls “fake” and promise a Republican victory. But their behaviour—Trump, Vice President Vance and other administration figures are campaigning almost exclusively in “red” conservative areas—suggests they know they are in deep trouble. Polls currently show that the Senate race in Kansas, where Democrats haven’t won since 1932, is a toss-up. And Democrat James Talarico is slightly favoured to win a Senate seat in Texas, where a Democrat hasn’t won statewide since the 1990s.

The last-minute campaign blitz and the truly obscene amount of money billionaires are spending to shore up Republican candidates may limit GOP losses. It seems clear, however, that the Democrats are headed for victory next week. The real question will be how high the Democratic wave will crest.

What will Trump do?

All the above assumes that 3 November will unfold as a “normal” midterm election. But Trump and his minions are talking openly about challenging or overturning the results. Given Trump’s attempts to overturn the 2020 presidential election, nothing is “off the table”.

Trump, his captive Supreme Court, and Republicans at all levels of government have conducted a years-long campaign to disenfranchise sections of the population and undermine democracy. This includes the Supreme Court’s evisceration of the Voting Rights Act, gerrymandering to lock in GOP majorities, and Trump’s so-far failed attempt to use the US Postal Service to make mail-in voting more difficult.

Trump and his Justice Department have continued to act on the lie that non-US citizens are voting illegally. The DOJ has tried to force state governments, constitutionally responsible for running US elections, to hand over their voter rolls. With voting data in hand, the Trump government says it can purge non-citizens from the rolls. So far, no state has complied, and the courts have ruled against Trump and the DOJ.

However, the DOJ has persisted. In late October, it indicted 28 individuals in California whom it claims voted illegally. Moreover, it sent lists of supposed non-citizen voters …

author: Ben Radford
title: UN General Assembly votes to end US blockade of Cuba — again
content:
The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) has overwhelmingly voted to end the United States government’s cruel and illegal economic blockade of Cuba. One-hundred-and-thirty countries voted in favour of the resolution on the “Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba” on October 28, with 17 against and 25 abstentions.

Every year since 1992, the UNGA has overwhelmingly voted to end the blockade. However, this year, there was a rise in votes against and abstentions, likely reflective of new far-right governments — for example, in Colombia, Chile and Honduras — coming to power since last year’s vote. The US has also ramped up its international efforts to isolate Cuba through sanctions and threats of sanctions against countries that trade with Cuba.

This year’s vote took place as escalating US economic warfare against Cuba is causing a devastating humanitarian crisis. The blockade’s impacts have been characterised as a “silent genocide”, severely restricting Cubans’ access to food, medicine, equipment and fuel, and impacting every aspect of daily life.

The Cuban government submitted its annual report to the UNGA in September, detailing last year’s impacts of the US blockade. Between March last year and February this year, the blockade inflicted more than US$8 billion worth of damages.

The economic cost of just four days of the blockade amounts to the cost of all fuel imports needed to meet Cuba’s demand.

On top of existing strangulation mechanisms, the US government imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in January, claiming that the country posed an “unusual and extraordinary threat” to US national security.

The US announced tariffs on goods from countries that, directly or indirectly, sold or provided oil to Cuba. Following the US’s January 3 attacks on Venezuela, it also blocked all Venezuelan oil shipments to the country.

The energy blockade is the reason for widespread blackouts, as well as disruptions to water supply, waste collection and transport.

The fuel shortages are severely impacting hospital operations, including treatments that require a steady energy supply, such as haemodialysis. There are harrowing reports of surgeons having to perform operations by mobile phone lights, due to the blackouts.

The US blockade has affected Cubans’ access to vital treatment and medicine. One example is Cuba’s cancer survival rates, which, while still higher than many low- and middle-income countries, have dropped from 85% to 65%.

Cuba’s infant mortality has risen from 4 out of 1000 live births in 2018 to 9.9 last year — a 148% rise.

Cuban authorities say that the current transport crisis is more acute than during the “Special Period” in the 1990s following the collapse of the Soviet Union, which plunged Cuba into a prolonged economic crisis. Fuel shortages have affected refrigerated transport, preventing more than 30,000 children from receiving vaccines.

In May, the US imposed a regime of secondary sanctions against governments and companies that invest in or trade with Cuba.

For example, the US Office of Foreign Assets Control has imposed fines on US companies for handling cargo shipments bound for Cuba and providing services for people living in the country.

Over the past year, 34 international banking institutions suspended or declined to conduct operations with Cuba, citing risks of secondary sanctions.

Several airlines have ceased operations in Cuba and many international hotel chains also abandoned management agreements for hotels, citing the risks posed by the secondary sanctions regime. These sanctions — along with other US measures — have contributed to the collapse in Cuba’s tourism industry.

“The application of these measures has produced a sophisticated mechanism of asphyxiation directed at the Cuban population, exceeding by far the levels of pressure historically imposed over decades,” the annual report said.

It also notes that the blockade has caused US$3.9 trillion worth of damages since it was imposed. However, it said the impacts go far beyond economic losses, causing suffering, illness and death.

The US blockade of Cuba violates not just international law, but any semblance of humanity.

The US government has made its intention of achieving “regime change” in Cuba by the end of the year very clear; it is openly considering the possibility of military attacks. This has been the US’s policy since Cubans overthrew the …

author: Robert Narai
title: Days of hope and rage in France
content:
At the centre of Paris, the Monument à la République looms over a square that has hosted every great mobilisation of the French left in modern history. The bronze statue of Marianne, symbol of the Republic, holds an olive branch above the words: 

Liberté. Égalité. Fraternité.

 During mass demonstrations on 17 October, dozens of young people scaled the monument while tens of thousands looked on. Some flew Palestinian and red flags. On the statue of 

Egalité

, someone had scrawled “jeunesse dorée” (“gilded youth”, an old term for the idle rich). Marianne herself was draped in a giant yellow vest bearing the words: “The police mutilate high school students”.

For almost a month now, a mass student revolt has been rocking France, in one of the deepest political crises seen in the country in decades. The state that claims to embody liberty, equality and fraternity has answered 

lycéens

 (high schoolers aged 15 to 18) demanding better conditions in schools with tear gas, rubber bullets and mass arrests. That the Republic’s police are maiming young people in the streets is an indictment of the capitalist system the Republic protects.

Days of rage

In response to a national day of action on 17 October, in which an estimated 800,000 people protested across France, the government of Emmanuel Macron unleashed a flurry of violence.

Police fired tear gas into the crowd gathering at Place de la République before the march had formed. Riot police armed with batons, shields and armoured vehicles charged into crowds in Paris, Lyons, Bordeaux and a string of provincial cities, attacking protesters and bystanders alike. According to the Interior Ministry, almost 1,800 people were arrested and more than 500 police were injured, with 855 arrests in Paris alone. A teenager lost a hand in Saint-Étienne and another lost an eye in Mulhouse. Street medics were dragged along the ground by police.

The new element on 17 October was the return of the Yellow Vests, the leaderless movement of rural and provincial workers against fuel taxes and the high cost of living that erupted in 2018, until it was crushed with brute force by the state. After weeks of watching 

lycéens

 face down riot police, the Yellow Vests called their own day of action protesting the cost of living. The Yellow Vests blocked roundabouts and fuel depots from the morning and declared their support for the student revolt. Among them was Pierre, a retiree from Bandol: “I’ve been gassed five times since this morning”, he told 

La Provence

. “[Macron’s government] is declaring war on the people.” The return of the Yellow Vests raises the possibility of the student revolt becoming a rallying point for broader working-class grievances.

Nurses, teachers and firefighters joined the Yellow Vests demonstration. In Lille, 20 rail workers marched together in their SNCF vests. Most of the working class support the movement (55 percent of the French population support the student-led protest movement, according to an Elabe poll) but are not yet part of it.

Whose Republic?

The Macron government’s strategy has been to paint the victims of violence as its perpetrators. Prime Minister Lecornu blamed “far-left groups”, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez targeted “ultra-left individuals”, while Macron declared that “nothing can explain, nothing can excuse” the violence. They pointed to a handful of burnt buildings, such as the town hall in Limoges, to paint a movement of hundreds of thousands as a mindless mob. “The perpetrators directly targeted the institutions of the Republic and the authority of the State”, wrote Bordeaux mayor Thomas Cazenave.

It is worth asking what sort of Republic the mayor of Bordeaux is defending: one in which a burnt town hall causes enormous outrage, but a sixteen-year-old losing an eye to a police grenade prompts hysteria about the need for more law and order.

The ruling class never calls the conditions that produced this revolt violence. Students in France’s poorest schools sit in classrooms infested with cockroaches and rats, in classes of up to 35. Outside school, the police stop, search and arrest young Black and Arab men from the 

banlieues

 (working-class suburbs) for the colour of their skin and the estate they live on, and their operations now cause more than one death per week. Fuel and food prices keep rising, while, according to Oxfam, 53 billionaires own as much as the poorest 48 percent of the population. This is the systematic violence …

author: Binoy Kampark
title: Unmasked agendas: Macron, youth protests and blocking social media
content:
Finally, the ill-fitting mask on the ugly face of government policy comes off. In the sunset of his administration, French President Emmanuel Macron is facing a boiling, indignant movement that began with the protests of disgruntled students and has burgeoned into something much more significant.

Teachers at the Antoine de Saint-Exupéry High School in the southeastern Parisian suburb of Créteil went on strike over severe staff shortages, on September 17. Students and parents added themselves to the strike. The school entrance was blocked, videos taken and social media platforms used to disseminate the message.

A blooming followed through to October, drawing in some 3700 schools and hundreds and thousands of protesters. Social, economic and political angst had been stirred, with grievances focused on inadequate provision of teaching, packed classrooms, overburdened schedules and the dilapidation of school infrastructure. The university admissions platform Parcoursup also came in for criticism.

As part of the response to the protests, Macron has, as is traditional with a smug incumbent caught off guard, identified an aggravating, foreign influence steering matters. Conveniently for him, the fault seems to lie with the progenitors of the social media world, those United States Big Tech beasts and platforms that have turned users into anything from bovine consumers to adept, resourceful users of technology. It’s the resourceful aspect of the technology that is proving particularly troubling for government officialdom.

As one of the last acts of his administration, France’s desperate leader has attempted to impose age-restrictions on users of social media platforms ostensibly as a therapeutic exercise.

In doing so, he has joined a wide tent of invigilating governments keen to use the alleged malignancies of social media as an alibi for controlling access to certain online platforms, a mood captured by the efforts of the European Union to advance the all suppressing EU Kids Act. (Australia was the first to bolt out of the stables last December with its Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024, paraded as a noble effort to limit the use of social platforms by those under 16 years of age. Unsurprisingly, it is showing itself to be a foolish legislative bauble, weak and circumvented.)

On July 21, the French parliament adopted the “Loi visant à protéger les mineurs face aux risques associés à l’usage des réseaux sociaux” (Law aiming to protect minors from the risks associated with social media usage), an alleged palliative for the ills (examples include anxiety, depression and sleep disorders) of using social media for those under 15. This exaggerated sense of moral success did not last long.

In August, France’s Constitutional Council poured cold water on the government’s grand strategy, striking down the legislation as needlessly broad and hopelessly excessive. The access to the platforms, for instance, was “not subject to any condition relating to the functionalities or content offered, the dangers they expose users, and the inadequacy of the safeguards with which they are provided.”

Saliently, the Council noted that the ban encumbered the rights of young people to access information and engage in the democratic system. This meant retarding the useful instruction of children to meaningfully engage the political process on ceasing to be minors. Social networking platforms were not inherently wicked things; they could also serve as educational tools, promote civic engagement and aid in building communities.

A chastened Macron proceeded to direct Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu to make the necessary adjustments in line with the Council’s decision.

The response from Macron to these youth-inspired protests, in light of his stuttering efforts against the corruptions of social media, is a more candid reflection on why governments seek to restrict any platform that adds vim to dissent and disagreement.

In remarks made to members of law enforcement during his October 26 visit to Marseille City Hall, the president scorned social media sites for “damaging our democracies” and being “tools for mobilising the worst impulses”. They had brought “young and not-so-young people to places where criminal acts, attacks and looting were taking place.”

This imprecise, misleading assessment proved most telling.

In the week leading up to October 24, recent reports reveal that the French interior ministry was putting …

author: April Holcombe
title: China’s forgotten miracle makers
content:
History has no parallel for modern China’s economic transformation. To what do we owe the China “miracle”, in which annual GDP growth averaged 9 percent over 40 years, wages up roughly tenfold in 30 years, and more high-speed rail built in ten years than the rest of the world in all time?

In the heyday of globalisation, people said China proved the magic of free markets and free trade. These days, people are more likely to attribute the country’s success to some special Chinese characteristic, such as its state-directed investment or its “Communist” dictatorship. 

These perspectives share in common a wilful or ignorant blindness to capitalism’s real wealth creators. Economic value comes neither from the market’s “invisible hand” nor the state’s “guiding hand”, but plain old everyday hands. The secret to China’s “miracle” is the not-so-miraculous condition of its working class.

Beginning in the 1990s, the greatest ever number of wage labourers was assembled through the collusion of profit-hungry foreign capital with millions of venal bureaucrats and their repressive state machine. Three hundred million people decamped from rural poverty to seek better lives in China’s cities, while urban compatriots in state-owned mines and mills lost their livelihoods through merciless privatisation.

China’s working class is legally stratified into “migrant” and “resident”, subject to the severest dictatorship of their bosses, and deprived of political rights to speak out or unionise. Apply hundreds of billions in Western and Taiwanese investments, lather, rinse, repeat for decades, and voilà! You have the most “miraculous” economic growth in capitalist history. 

China’s migrant workforce

We are used to hearing about how important migrants are to Western economies, but migration—the internal kind from village to city, not country-to-country—has been even more critical to China’s boom. In the 1990s, the government enticed young villagers with the prospect of independence, new experiences and better pay in newly established, deregulated Special Economic Zones with low wages and low taxes.

Lu Qingmin first left her family’s half-acre farm and came to Dongguan, a burgeoning megacity in the southern manufacturing heartland of the Pearl River Delta, in the early 2000s. Bosses preferred migrant women like her, considering them doubly docile. Writer Leslie Chang, in her 2008 book

Factory Girls

, described Lu’s experiences at her first job in a Hong Kong-owned alarm clock factory:

“A day on the assembly line stretched from eight in the morning until midnight—thirteen hours on the job plus two breaks for meals—and workers labored every day for weeks on end. From the moment she entered the factory she wanted to leave.”

The Pearl River Delta opened wide to investment in such sweatshops, and American-style hyper-individualism flowed in with it. Self-help books, life-coaching gurus, pyramid schemes, talent markets, unregulated colleges: each refracted through the false prism of empowerment what migrant workers already felt in their bones:

you are on your own

.

Hukou

: China’s internal visa system

Every migrant who left for the cities took the same thing with them: their rural

hukou

(户口), a residential registration that acts like an internal passport. Originally designed under Mao Zedong in 1958 to prohibit rural-to-urban movement altogether, the

hukou

household registration system was repurposed to create a pliant, defenceless workforce with second-class citizenship wherever it went.

Out-of-town

hukou

holders, also called the “floating population”, now represent just under half of the country’s workforce. Registered to villages far away, they are denied health insurance and pensions by the local government where they actually live. Many cities bar them from buying property, and local schools charge significant sums to teach their children. 

Think of them like the United States’ undocumented immigrants, who can get driver’s licences but not Social Security, who work in practically every key industry, but technically are not supposed to be there at all. Except there are now as many in China as the entire US population.

China does not offer the equivalent of America’s birthright citizenship: children inherit their parents’

hukou

 wherever they are born. Locked out by the prohibitive cost of urban schooling, tens of millions of “left behind” children grow up in the countryside with their grandparents, only seeing their …

author: Mat Ward
title: 10 new underrated protest albums that should be topping the charts
content:
Do you think there’s no good protest music these days? So did I, until I started looking for it. Every month, I listen to it all, then select the best that relates to that month’s political news. Here’s the round-up for October.

New South Wales' Labor government backed Queensland's ban on Palestine freedom slogans on October 1. The move came as Jewish US protest singer David Rovics released probably his catchiest album yet, containing songs "all about the US-Israeli Epstein Empire", before touring Australia. On album opener "The Holocaust Is Now", featuring backing vocals from Green Left writer Kamala Emanuel, he sings: "Can you spend two hundred dollars to buy a loaf of bread? Neither can the Palestinians, they’re dying instead." The LP was released while donkey prices in Gaza surged from $US1000 to $US30,000 "due to the virtual elimination of motorised private transport". As Israel's election loomed on October 28, the album's title track, "Rise", called for Israelis to rise up against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was being endorsed by US President Donald Trump as a "great warrior" who must be re-elected so they could "finish the job" in their disastrous war on Iran. "Overthrow your theocratic state, before it is too late," sings Rovics. "Reject your leaders and their lies. Rise, Israelis, rise!" LISTEN>>>

One of the seemingly few Israelis rising up is pop-rock musician Regev Baruch, with his scathing new album, Super Sparta. Its title is a phrase coined by Netanyahu last year to describe his commitment to eternal war. Discussing the LP, which likens Israelis to Nazis, Baruch said: “There’s this graffiti that says, ‘Grandma, what were you doing during the genocide?’ I was looking for a good answer to that — something I could do to prove I wasn’t part of the silent majority... In the end, I said, ‘OK, there are journalists; they’re investigating. There are lawyers; they’re fighting a legal battle. You’re a musician — just make music.’ That’s the most powerful thing I can do.” Of course, Baruch is far from the only Jewish person publicly condemning Israel's genocide against Palestinians, as shown by the countless Jews who attended vigils marking three years of the war on October 7. Meanwhile, pro-Palestine punks Amyl and the Sniffers, whose new live LP blasts fascistic leaders, said they were donating proceeds from an upcoming Bondi gig to "extend our love" to Jews affected by the Bondi attack. LISTEN>>>

English feminist rage musician Delilah Bon, who paints her body with slogans such as "Free Palestine", also released a new live album on October 16 as her Australian tour loomed. The LP documents a show she played to reach out to American fans after she had to cancel a US tour due to fears about the country's Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. The event, which raised £8,000 for organisations supporting people affected by ICE, opens with the apt "Illegal Aliens" and powers through fan favourites such as "Dead Men Don't Rape", "War On Women" and "Princeless Princess". On the excoriating "Not The President", she sings: "That's not the president, that's just some man, who has abused so many women and children... There's so much love in this world, I'm holding hands with every girl that cries alone in her room, that fears this world is so fucking doomed." She then gets her British fans to chant "fuck Trump" for their peers in the US. The explosive power of her dayglo-daubed live show, in which she goes from pitch-perfect singing to razor-sharp rapping and searing screaming, is inspiring. LISTEN>>>

Also condemning ICE is the new LP from Grammy-winning folk musician Mary Gauthier, released days before an agent in New York shot into a car with a child inside. On "Soldier Of Fortune" she cites ICE victims Renée Good and Alex Pretti as she sings: "You're nothing but a gun for hire, hiding behind a mask. You didn't care if she was somebody's mother, when you shot her in the face through the window glass. A VA nurse on a city street, full of the courage you lack. An angel of mercy, helping a stranger and you fired 10 bullets into his back." That preceded the October 16 LP from Heavens To Betsy, the kind of riot grrrl pioneers who paved the way for the likes of Delilah Bon. The LP, a long-lost 1992 demo released to mark their reformation, centres on "My Secret" in which singer Corin Tucker blasts an abuser. "It turned the tables on everything, and it let go of everything, and it also freaked everyone out," …

author: Unknown
title: Özçelik-İş’te yolsuzluk iddialarını işçiler değerlendirdi: ‘Bizden alınan yevmiyelerle sefa sürüyorlar’
content:
İzel Gözde Meydan [email protected]

Kocaeli – Özçelik-İş Genel Merkezi hakkında belgeleriyle gündeme gelen yolsuzluk iddialarını, sendikanın Kocaeli’de örgütlü olduğu Tezcan Galvaniz ve Bekaert fabrikalarının işçilerine sorduk. İşçiler, sendikalardaki yolsuzlukların normalleştirilmesine tepki gösterdi. Bir yandan işten atmalar ve ağırlaşan çalışma koşullarıyla mücadele ederken diğer yandan sendika genel merkezine ilişkin yolsuzluk haberleriyle karşı karşıya kaldıklarını dile getirdi.

Son bir yılda yaşanan işten çıkarmalarda Bekaert Kartepe fabrikasından atılan bir işçi, yolsuzluk iddialarına şaşırmadığını belirterek “Ben bu habere şaşırmıyorum çünkü önceki sözleşmelerde mevcut sendika şube başkanının, genel sekreterinin ve Kartepe fabrikasının mevcut ikinci temsilcisinin temsilci oldukları dönemde iki üç daire aldıklarını duyduk. Soranlara biri borsadan, diğeri de kaynanamdan kaldı diye söylediler. Yani şimdi bunu temsilci yapabiliyorken, işçiden ayda bir yevmiye alan ve binlerce üyesi olan bir sendikada olması şaşırtıcı değil. Hele ki genel başkanların işçi kökenli, sendikacılıktan gelmeleri; tahsili olmayan, Türkçeyi bile zor konuşan adamların hangi kanunu, hangi hukuku bilerek neyi savunduğunu söyleyebiliriz? Bir de hükümet yanlısı bir sendikaysan bunun daha fazla, daha büyük rakamlar üzerinden yapılması gayet normal. Allah, ‘Her şeyle gelin, kul hakkıyla gelmeyin’ dediği yerde bunların sözde muhafazakâr olup Allah’ın adını kişilikleri, karakterleri, ahlakları gibi kirli ağızlarından düşürmemeleri, sadece din sömürüsü yapmalarından ileri gitmez. Emekçinin ne kadar hakkını yediyse bunlar, yedirdikleri herkes dâhil hepsinden çıksın inşallah” diye konuştu.

Başka bir Bekaert işçisi ise sendikalardaki yolsuzlukların normalleştirilmesine tepki göstererek “Sendikalardaki yolsuzluklar o kadar basite indiriliyor ki çok doğal, normalmiş gibi geliyor. Diğer işçi arkadaşlarda da aynı düşünce var; insanlar normal karşılıyor. Ve en kötüsü, bu duruma işçilerin neredeyse tamamı kulak dahi asmıyor. Sendikalar Kanunu’nu sil baştan düzenlemek gerek. Denetim ise kesinlikle bağımsız olmalı. Son dönemlerde bağımsız sendikaların başardıkları ortada. Denetimin de bağımsız olması gerektiğini düşünüyorum.” dedi.

Tezcan Galvaniz işçisi ise toplu iş sözleşmesi (TİS) sürecini, grev sonrasında yaşanan işten çıkarmaları ve fabrikadaki çalışma koşullarını anlatarak, “Biz bunlarla boğuşurken sendikamız nerede? Bizden alınan yevmiyelerle sefa sürüyorlar” diye tepki gösterdi:

"TİS görüşmeleri altı ay önce başlamıştı. Şu an son sürece doğru hızla ilerliyor, zaman daralıyor. Herkes endişe içinde. Grevden sonra işçi kıyımı yaşandı. Bir süre, kısa süreliğine de olsa fabrikada işi durdurmuşlardı, çalışma sürecinde durgunluk yaşandı. Sonrasında bir anda fabrikada işler yoğunlaştı. İşten çıkarılan, hakkını alamayan ya da zorbalık ve mobbing yoluyla tazminatsız veya çok gülünç rakamlarla tazminata imza attırılarak işinden edilenler oldu. Örneğin, ‘Bu tutara imza atmazsan mahkemeye başvur, iki sene beklersin’ gibi tehditlerle herkesi işinden ettiler. Akabinde iş fazlasıyla yoğunlaştı. Bundan dolayı işçi alımı da hâlâ mevcut değil. Sadece taşeron ambalaj ekibi oluşturuldu ama yalnızca ambalaj ve paketleme işçileri alındı. Onlar 45-50 bin civarında maaş alıyor. Galvanizde yoğunluk varsa haddehaneleri durdurup işçileri geçici olarak galvanize gönderiyorlar. Galvaniz duruyor, boya süreci hep böyle devam ediyor. Kısır bir döngü içinde çalışılıyor. Bakıma alınan hatların bakımındaki yoğunluk, o hatta çalışan işçilere yaptırılıyor. Temizlik işçisi de iki üç kişi kaldı. Onlar da sıkıntı ve yoğunluk çekiyor. Birimlere damacana içme suyunu temizlik işçileri temin ediyordu. Şimdi ara ara kendimiz yemekhanelerden alıp ihtiyacımızı gideriyoruz. Bazen su gelmiyor, susuzluk yaşıyoruz. Kışlık iş elbiseleri henüz temin edilmedi. Bir yazı dizisi yazarken önce giriş, sonra geniş bir gelişme bölümüyle durumlar ele alınır. En son, olayların bilindiği gibi sonuç kısmı ele alınır. Ama bizim hikâyemiz sadece girişe endeksli. Hiç gelişme durumlarını göremez olduk. Birçoğunun, hatta çoğunluğunun iş akdine grevden hemen sonra tazminatsız son verildi. Biz bunlarla boğuşurken sendikamızın genel merkezine ilişkin yolsuzluk haberleri geliyor. Bizden alınanlarla sefa sürüyorlar."

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Empresarios aplauden al presidente cuando pide una hoguera para quemar periodistas
content:
Sólo una Cámara empresaria salió a criticar los dichos del presidente Javier Milei.


Milei en la Fundación Faro


Por Mario Hernandez


Luego de que el viernes 23 de octubre, ante empresarios, el Presidente pidiera una hoguera para quemar a los periodistas, sólo una Cámara emitió un comunicado para alertar sobre el avance del mandatario sobre la democracia, y además lo hizo sin siquiera citar a Milei.


El resto, en tanto, se mantvo en una absoluta negación. La que se expresó sobre el tema fue IDEA. Las que no lo hicieron fueron la Unión Industrial Argentina (UIA), la Asociación Empresaria Argentina (AEA), AMCHAM (la Cámara de empresas estadounidenses en Argentina, el Grupo de los Seis (Sociedad Rural, UIA, Cámara de Comercio y Construcción, ADEBA, la Bolsa) y el campo en general.


Hace una semana, todos ellos emitieron un documento opinando contra un fallo de la Justicia sobre un bloqueo de camioneros a una empresa pyme. Fue una acción como ya ha ocurrido, años previos, con decisiones de política de Estado, discusiones del PJ con la Corte Suprema, críticas del kirchnerismo a los medios y cualquier otra cosa que ameritara marcar la cancha. En los años del macrismo, de hecho, se creó el Foro de Convergencia Empresarial, con el fin de tener una institución que defendiera al PRO y cuestionara a los opositores. Lo integraban dirigentes de todas las Cámaras.


El alineamiento de los privados con Milei, para conservar reformas de fondo, acumular poder y tener negocios, es prioridad sobre cualquier ataque al sistema democrático.


IDEA, el instituto que organiza el coloquio empresario en Mar del Plata, es un polo afín a las ideas liberales. Históricamente reacio a posiciones donde el Estado tiene más poder. Aún así, fue la única entidad que se expresó sobre los desbordes presidenciales.


En un comunicado, precisaron que “la libertad de prensa y el respeto por las ideas, aun cuando existan diferencias, son pilares fundamentales de la convivencia democrática. Desde IDEA consideramos que el debate público debe desarrollarse en un marco de pluralidad de opiniones, diálogo y respeto, sin agravios ni descalificaciones”.


En esa línea, evitaron pronunciar la palabra Milei al aseverar que “quienes fueron elegidos para gobernar deben actuar con responsabilidad y contribuir a un debate público respetuoso. Los agravios a periodistas en el ejercicio de su función contradicen ese deber”.


IDEA concluye que, “en un contexto en el que la ciudadanía realiza un esfuerzo colectivo para alcanzar la estabilidad y el desarrollo del país, desde IDEA insistimos en la necesidad de promover y respetar la libertad de prensa y de expresión, y de sostener un debate público basado en el respeto, la tolerancia y la responsabilidad”.


Los concurrentes al evento de la Fundación Faro aceptaron pagar 25 mil dólares por cabeza o 300.000 pesos por una mesa en el Yacht Club de Puerto Madero a los anfitriones, los Neuss, el grupo que se está quedando con buena parte de los negocios en la era libertaria. También estuvieron José Luis Manzano, Hugo Eurnekian, Bettina Bulgheroni (CICYP y PAE), Marcelo Mindlin, el dueño de Swiss Medical, Claudio Belocopitt y líneas medias de Techint. Se hizo ver, además, el hombre fuerte de Marcos Galperín en Mercado Libre, Juan Martín de la Serna. Todos ganadores y pocos “perdedores” del modelo, entre ellos Gustavo Weiss, titular de la Cámara Argentina de la Construcción.


Rubén Tchernaskovsky


Uno por uno los empresarios aplaudidores


Entre los primeros nombres mencionados apareció Rubén Tchernaskovsky, principal accionista de Newsan y con vínculos en el sector energético.


Damián Pozzoli


También Damián Pozzoli, propietario de Havanna. Además, se mencionó la asociación de Tchernaskovsky y los Neuss en Edison Energía y su participación en operaciones vinculadas con privatizaciones energéticas, entre ellas Transener.


Juan y Patricio Neuss


Otro de los empresarios fue Marcelo Mindlin, presidente de Pampa Energía y del Museo del Holocausto de Buenos Aires.


Marcelo Mindlin (Pampa Energía)


La periodista Natalia Volosin, quien dijo tener un vínculo personal con él, cuestionó su presencia en el evento: “Yo me pregunto qué hubieras hecho y si hubieras aplaudido si hubieran llamado a quemar judíos”. Más adelante, insistió: “Sería importante que cuando llaman a quemar periodistas tampoco te pares a aplaudir”.


Hugo Sigman

title: ‘Labor struggle against capitalism and exploitation’ discussed at women’s conference in Ankara
content:
The second session of the “Women Discuss the Future Side by Side” conference, held at the Chamber of Civil Engineers (İMO) of the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB) in Ankara featured discussions under the theme “Labor struggle against capitalism and exploitation.”


The conference is organized at the initiative of 80 women, including journalists, writers, academics, politicians, and activists.


Ayfer Koçak, Co-Chair of the Confederation of Public Employees’ Trade Unions (KESK), said, “If we are to organize against exploitation, we must create a society in which workers can receive what they are entitled to, a society we call a ‘democratic society.’”


Sabahat Tuncel, an activist with the Free Women’s Movement (Tevgera Jinên Azad – TJA), stated that exploitation could not be eliminated without abolishing the capitalist system. “Because this system itself generates inequality and labor exploitation. Consequently, it exploits women’s labor even further. What we really need to focus on is how to eliminate this system.”


Tuncel continued: “As Marx said, ‘Workers are free only insofar as they can sell their labor,’ but even those conditions have now changed. Workers can no longer even sell their labor freely. Wage increases should not be the sole concern of workers and laborers. Today, the working class is taking to the streets despite the trade unions. We can build democratic socialism through the liberation of labor. If we are not free, if labor is not free, we cannot build a new system. Let us change this system. We can replace it with democratic socialism. We can organize both elderly care and childcare communally. We can find ways to collectivize our labor.”


Emine Teğin, who became known for her speech at a public gathering organized by the DEM Party in Siirt, also addressed the conference, saying: “Why are our young girls and women being killed? Why can we not send our children to university? Why was Rojin Kabaiş killed? Why were Gülistan Doku and İpek Er driven to their deaths? As women, we demand answers to these questions. We want a life of justice, equality, and dignity.”


The conference will continue with its final session, titled “The struggle for gender equality and freedom.”


Women’s conference in Ankara: There can be no peace without justice

author: Black Freighter
title: Anarchism and the Australian Labour Movement: Jean De Lisle's Letter from Newcastle, 25 June 1937
content:
Image: BHP at Port Waratah, Newcastle (University of Newcastle [Australia] Library)

This letter, dated 25 June 1937 and written by Jean De Lisle of Newcastle, NSW describes his involvement in Australian anarchist circles. It is unclear who the recipient was. He discusses the difficulties facing the labour movement, criticising the influence of the Santamaria Catholic faction in the Australian Labor Party and its support for Franco during the Spanish Civil War. He also describes the Communist Party's political compromises and intimidation and harassment by communist militants, whom he calls the 'Knuckle Duster Brigade'. A steelworker at BHP's Port Waratah works, De Lisle mentions his subscriptions to Italian and American publications and expresses interest in forming an anarchist group in Sydney.

The original document can be found attached, and was sourced from the Kate Sharpley Library.

168 King St Newcastle New South Wales Australia June 25 – 1937

I have received word from Fellow Worker A. Westbrook of Sydney that she received a letter from you. I am an anarchist and have been connected with a small Italian group in the North of Queensland. One of the comrades (whose name I will refrain from mentioning owing to the possibility of deportation to Fascisti Italy) is now residing near here, and the last time I called on him he gave me a copy of the paper "Spain and the World" which I gave to Fellow Worker Westbrook and she said she would write to you, and I can assure you we are very pleased to hear from you.

I only receive one Anarchist paper and that is in the Italian language which I am able to read write and speak, but I would prefer the English papers. The paper I receive is called "Il Risveglio Anarchico" printed in Geneva.

I also receive the I.W.W. Industrial Worker from Chicago U.S.A. I am a steel worker employed at the B.H.P. steel works Port Waratah, and I hope you will excuse my writing as my hand is cramped and sore.

The Labour Movement in Australia is in a very bad way, a number of the leaders openly support Franco in Spain.

This is due to the Roman Catholic Church, having gained nearly all leading positions in the Labor Party. The Communist Party will not expose them because it would break the unity of the Party; but instead plead mournfully for a People's Front. One of the Communist Party leaders died here recently and it said the Central Committee ordered them to get a parson to read the burial service which was done (a classic example of the "United Front").

The Comrades as we call here have the sight of us and me in particular and have tried to molest me on several occasions generally 5 or 6 together like a pack of wolves, but never one at a time.

We call them the Knuckle Duster Brigade; but they are losing ground and continue to go more to the right, many of their pamphlets would interest you particularly on the defence of Australia against the Japanese and I will send some the next time I go to Sydney and you no doubt would think they were issued by a capitalist class group.

We will most probably form a small group in Sydney in the near future and will be able to keep contact with you.

Anarchist Greetings Yours fraternally,

168 King St Newcastle N.S.W. Australia.

Reply Aug. 18/37 Papers + Lists

Enclosed cutting from the Communist Party Worker Weekly which has been damaged, but I think you can manage to read it - also photo of Comrade Oliver (capitalist press)

P.S. I am an Australian born Frenchman J.D.L.

I will give Fellow Worker Westbrook some money to forward for literature as soon as possible.

title: Muş'un Xwarik köylüleri mera savunmasında: JES projesine direnişin 180. günü
content:
Muş'un Varto/Gimgim ilçesine bağlı Çalıdere/Xwarik köyünde, ABD şirketi IGNIS H2 Enerji Üretim AŞ'nin jeotermal kaynak arama projesine karşı çadır nöbeti, Jinnews'ın haberine göre 180. gününe girdi. 


3 Mayıs'ta başlatılan direnişte köylüler, projenin su kaynaklarına, meralara, hayvancılığa ve doğal yaşama zarar vermemesi için sondaj faaliyetlerinin durdurulmasını istiyor.


Varto Ekoloji Platformu Gençlik Meclisi öncülüğünde sürdürülen nöbeti cuma günü Segiran, Dapak ve Muzuran köylüleri devraldı. Nöbet alanında "Varto halkı jeotermal enerji santrali istemiyor. Suyuma, toprağıma dokunma" pankartı taşındı.


2 Kasım'da gerçekleştirilecek bilirkişi keşfi öncesinde direnişin 180'inci gününe ulaşması, bölgedeki hareketliliği artırdı. Köylüler ve ekoloji örgütleri, Bingöl İdare Mahkemesi'nin yaptıracağı incelemede bölgenin doğal ve toplumsal özelliklerinin dikkate alınmasını istiyor.


Bakanlık: Jeolojik ve hidrojeolojik veriler eksik


Köylülerin su kaynaklarına yönelik kaygıları, Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığının 21 Ekim'de TBMM'ye gönderdiği resmî yanıtta yer alan eksikliklerle de gündeme geldi.


DEM Parti Muş Milletvekili Sümeyye Boz Çakı'nın 27 Şubat tarihli yazılı soru önergesine sekiz ay sonra yanıt veren Bakanlık, jeotermal arama projesinin tanıtım dosyasında bölgeye ait ayrıntılı jeolojik ve hidrojeolojik verilerin bulunmadığını bildirdi.


Bakanlık, yeraltı su kaynakları ve içme suyu rezervleri üzerindeki olası etkileri değerlendiren hidrojeolojik raporun da sunulmadığını belirterek eksikliklerin giderilmesini ve su temini ile çevre mevzuatına ilişkin gerekli taahhütlerin dosyaya eklenmesini istediğini açıkladı.


Yanıtta, proje alanının Güllüce Regülatörü ve Hidroelektrik Enerji Santrali'nin iletim hattı güzergâhıyla doğrudan etkileşim içinde bulunduğu da belirtildi. Bakanlık, çalışmaların ilgili iletim hattını etkilemeyecek biçimde sınırlandırılması ve sondaj sonrasında Devlet Su İşleri'nden yeniden görüş alınması gerektiğini bildirdi.


Bakanlık, mera tahsislerinde çiftçilerin görüşlerinin dikkate alındığını ve faaliyetlerin çevresel etkilerinin mevzuat çerçevesinde değerlendirildiğini savundu.


Köylüler ise karar süreçlerine yeterince katılamadıklarını ileri sürüyor.


4 bin hektarlık sahada 10 sondaj kuyusu


Şirketin Güzelkent sahası için hazırladığı projede, yaklaşık 4 bin 38 hektarlık ruhsat alanında toplam 10 jeotermal arama kuyusu açılması öngörülüyor. Sondajlar için belirlenen ÇED alanı ise 8 hektar.


2025 tarihli proje bilgilerine göre yaklaşık 95 milyon lira yatırım bedeli öngörülen arama çalışmalarının 20 ay sürmesi, 30 kişinin istihdam edilmesi planlanıyor.


Proje dosyasından aktarılan verilere göre bir sondaj noktası Küçüktepe köyündeki bir konuta yaklaşık 160 metre, bir diğeri Mengeneç Çayı'na 103 metre uzaklıkta bulunuyor. Bazı sondaj noktaları orman alanları içinde yer alıyor.


IGNIS, kendi internet sitesinde Güzelkent sahasının Kuzey Anadolu ve Doğu Anadolu faylarının kesişimine yakın bir bölgede bulunduğunu belirtiyor. Şirket, jeolojik ve jeofizik araştırmalar yürüttüğünü, rezervuar özelliklerini belirlemek amacıyla yeni sondajlar planladığını açıklıyor.


Henüz faaliyette bir elektrik üretim santrali bulunmuyor. Tartışma, ileride santral yatırımına dönüşebilecek jeotermal kaynak arama ve sondaj aşamasında yoğunlaşıyor.


Köylüler jeotermale neden karşı çıkıyor?


Bölgenin başlıca geçim kaynakları hayvancılık, küçük ölçekli tarım ve arıcılık. Köylüler sondaj sahalarının yalnızca kapladıkları alanla değil, su dolaşımı, otlaklar ve doğal yaşam üzerindeki olası etkileriyle değerlendirilmesini istiyor.


Jeotermal enerji, fosil yakıtlara alternatif yenilenebilir bir kaynak olmakla birlikte, çıkarılan sıcak ve mineralli akışkanların yönetimi özel önlemler gerektiriyor. Kuyuların sızdırmazlığının sağlanamaması, sondaj atıklarının uygunsuz depolanması veya kullanılmış jeotermal akışkanın güvenli biçimde yeniden yeraltına basılamaması halinde su ve toprak kirliliği riski doğabiliyor.


Jeotermal akışkanların kimyasal bileşimi sahadan sahaya değişiyor. Bazı alanlarda bor, arsenik ve çözünmüş başka minerallerin çevreye yayılması tarımsal üretim açısından sorun oluşturabiliyor. Bu risklerin Varto'da gerçekleşip gerçekleşmeyeceği ise saha ölçümleri ve bağımsız bilimsel incelemelerle belirlenmek zorunda.


Sondaj ve akışkan enjeksiyonunun fay sistemleri üzerindeki olası etkileri de bölge halkının itirazları arasında. Jeofizik uzmanları, deprem tehlikesi bulunan alanlarda doğal sismik hareketliliğin …

title: Διεθνής απεργιακή ημέρα δράσης σε 110 λιμάνια σ’ όλο τον κόσμο: Δεν δουλεύουμε για τον πόλεμό τους!
content:
Σε όλες τις ηπείρους και πάνω από 110 λιμάνια ανά τον κόσμο κινητοποιήθηκαν στην απεργία των λιμενεργατών και τη διεθνή ημέρα αντιπολεμικής δράσης φωνάζοντας ότι δεν δουλεύουν για τη μεταφορά όπλων. Λιμάνια των λαών και της ειρήνης και όχι ορμητήρια των ιμπεριαλιστών. Στη Γαλλία 90% ακινητοποίηση, στην Ιταλία πάνω από ένα εκατομμύριο στους δρόμους 70 πόλεων. Στην ελληνική γεωγραφία, μεγάλη παμπειραϊκή απεργία και συμμετοχή, στη Θεσσαλονίκη μπλοκαρίστηκαν εμπρευματοκιβώτια και φορτηγά, κινητοποιήσεις σε πολλές πόλεις και λιμάνια.


Χαρακτηριστικά του έντονου αντιπολεμικού και αντιϊμπεριαλιστικού παλμού των διαδηλώσεων είναι και τα συνθήματα στα πανό: Καμιά θυσία για τα κέρδη και τους πολέμους τους. Καμιά συμμετοχή στα ιμπεριαλιστικά σχέδια ΗΠΑ, ΝΑΤΟ, ΕΕ, Ισραήλ. Δώστε λεφτά για μισθούς, υγεία και παιδεία και όχι στου πολέμου τα σφαγεία. Κρίση, πόλεμος, ξερηζωμός, αυτός είναι ο καπιταλισμός. Κανένας ναυτεργάτης στις εμπόλεμες θάλασσες, καμία θυσία για τα κέρδη των εφοπλιστών. Κάτω η κυβέρνηση του πολέμου. Λευτεριά στην Παλαιστίνη. Έρευνα για τις κοινωνικές ανάγκες κι όχι για τον πόλεμο. Καμιά εμπλοκή των πανεπιστημίων στην πολεμική προετοιμασία. Μπλόκο στην πολεμική μηχανή.

title: Tuncay Yılmaz: We want to build a united front of resistance in Europe - Part Two
content:
ANF spoke to Tuncay Yılmaz, founding co-chair of the Socialist Refoundation Party (SYKP), about the outcomes of the Cologne meeting, the need for a common struggle, the situation of left-wing and democratic forces in the face of the rising far right in Europe, and the roadmap for the proposed alliance.


The first part of this interview can be read

here

. 


On 17 October, 25 organisations from different political traditions came together in Cologne. Similar attempts to build alliances have been made in Europe before. Why has the need to establish a common platform for struggle emerged again today? What distinguishes this meeting from previous initiatives?


Organisations from different political traditions and social groups in Europe have come together at various times. Previously, there was the European Assembly for Peace and Democracy (ABDEM). We then extended the organisation of the Peoples' Democratic Congress (HDK) in Turkey to Europe, establishing a broad organisation under the name HDK Europe. This organisation later became the European Democratic Forces Union (ADGB) and continued its activities under that name. Most recently, ahead of the NATO summit, a joint initiative called PANEV was established against imperialist aggression, wars and NATO.


All these initiatives emerged from efforts to find ways for the forces of democracy, peace, equality and freedom to become better organised in Europe and pursue more effective political action against the enormous aggressive power confronting us.


The alliances we established at different times sometimes lost their effectiveness, both because of changes in the objective conditions in which they were formed and, to speak frankly, because of our own shortcomings. This is a reality, and we are aware of it. Indeed, this was one of the issues on the agenda of our meeting. We want to learn from our previous experiences.


However, the mistakes we made in the past or the changes we have experienced should not prevent us from bringing democratic forces together again and carrying out a common struggle. And indeed, they are not preventing us. One of the main motivations that brought us together at this meeting was the growing hostility towards migrants in the European countries where we live, the rise of the right, fascist movements coming to power and increasing state violence. The fact that laws targeting asylum seekers have reached almost inhumane proportions is also deeply concerning to all of us. We want to build a united front of resistance against all of this.


At the same time, however, all our attention, thoughts and concerns are focused on developments in Turkey. Looking at Turkey, we see a totalitarian regime being built step by step. Everyone who opposes it becomes a target. Presidential candidates are arrested. Selahattin Demirtaş has been imprisoned for years, as has Figen Yüksekdağ. Ekrem İmamoğlu was subsequently arrested. The Republican People's Party (CHP), which prides itself on being the founding party of the state, is also under serious pressure. Attempts are being made to divide the party, and many of its representatives have been arrested.


Alongside all this, a negotiation process has begun. It has not yet reached the stage of a peace process. However, this negotiation process has the potential to generate a collective strength capable of pushing back attacks on democracy through the positive developments it could bring to the country's political life. Despite this, we see that the political authorities are acting with appalling arbitrariness in this process as well.


To speak frankly, this process has been made possible by the determination and goodwill of Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. After all, decisions were taken to lay down arms and dissolve the organisation. These decisions represent a profound transformation in the movement's historical existence.


Despite this, the state continues to display an extremely indifferent and unserious attitude towards taking steps on these issues, potentially jeopardising the process. Its actions could allow the anti-democratic practices it maintains throughout the country to continue in different forms in this area as well. We can all see that, for months, instead of implementing the legal arrangements brought onto Parliament's agenda with broad support, the authorities have merely continued saying, "We want this as well, and we want that too."


Frankly, they are acting entirely with …

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: How The Proud Boys Lost Their Name
content:
West Palm Beach, FL – On Sept. 26, the film “American Martyrs” premiered at the Kravis Center’s Cohen Pavilion in West Palm Beach, Florida. 


The subject of the film, presented by the far-right media outlet Gateway Pundit, was the Proud Boys – specifically the “seditious five,” whom a federal jury found guilty of seditious conspiracy to stop the presidential transfer of power for their role in the Jan. 6, 2021 storming of the U.S. Capitol.


The official poster for the film, promoted by Enrique Tarrio and Gateway Pundit on X ahead of its premiere. Note that Zachary Rehl, first on the left in the lineup, is AI-generated.


The five Proud Boys presenting the film were chairman Henry “Enrique” Tarrio, Ethan Nordean, Joe Biggs, Zachary Rehl and Dominic Pezzola. In reality, the actual fifth member of the “seditious five” is Jeremy Bertino, not Pezzola, who pleaded guilty and testified against the others during their trial. 


In August 2025, Bertino appeared on an episode of Tarrio’s Substack podcast titled “Kiss of Judas,” where the “government star witness” allowed the permanently sunglasses-clad chairman to humiliate him for the twelve people who liked the post. Despite this entreaty to re-enter the flock, Bertino did not make the cut as an “American martyr.”


Besides Tarrio, who received a full pardon, the others had the sentences commuted by executive order during President Donald Trump’s first day back in office on Jan. 20, 2025. 


The film premiere, held less than four miles from Trump’s Mar-a-Lago Club, was graced by numerous right-wing characters, including leading “Stop the Steal” figure and former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani,

QAnon digital warrior

 and former U.S. Army general Michael Flynn and convicted fraudster George Santos.


Led by right-wing media figure Lara Logan, the event opened at 7 p.m. with an open bar that overlapped with a 10-minute window set aside for “prayer, national anthem and pledge.”


After the 80-minute film concluded, the Gateway Pundit presented Tarrio with a Gateway Pundit-branded award created specifically for the occasion recognizing him “as an American Martyr and Hero.”


“It’s not an Emmy,” Tarrio wrote on X two days later. “But it’s so much better.”


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Despite the obvious connections to the Proud Boys organization, the premiere lacked any of the recognizable branding belonging to what it depicted as a persecuted “drinking fraternity.”


Even on Tarrio’s person, the golden cock and abbreviated name have given way to the branding for his streaming outfit, “War Boys,” which has gained a whopping 700 followers on Rumble since the channel was created in April last year.


And on Tarrio’s merch website – where the Afro-Cuban now in his 40s markets just about any idea as apparel, including a t-shirt reading “Enrique Tarrio Eats Cream Pies” with an AI illustration of Tarrio licking an over-sized cream pie – reveals a distinct absence of Proud Boys related merchandise.


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Tarrio’s ability to capitalize on Proud Boys merchandising, which once characterized his merch store, hit a setback last year when a D.C. Superior Court judge awarded the brand to a historically-Black church following a years-long legal battle set in the wake of the 2020 Presidential election.


At the beginning of 2025, the Metropolitan African Methodist Episcopal (MAME) church was the only place one could purchase official Proud Boys merchandise, re-branded to signify Black pride, with proceeds going toward the church’s community justice fund.


In April 2025, the church’s hold on the brand was tested on the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, who were sued in the Southern District Court of New York for their continued usage of the Proud Boys branding and merchandising.


The court reached a default judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, a chapter associated with Tarrio, earlier this year on April 8, awarding MAME $75,000 for trademark infringement and nearly $200,000 in attorney’s fees.


The judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys is only a small part of the church’s pursuit to be fully compensated in the amount awarded by the court, which continues to be a major struggle to this day and sees all related parties continue to be wrapped up in the ongoing court battle.

author: paradox-a
title: Die falsche Welt des Gute-Laune-Faschismus
content:
Zum Posterboy des Gute-Laune-Faschismus wurde Ulrich Siegmund gekürt, der AfD-Ministerpräsident in spe aus Sachsen-Anhalt. Die AfD fuhr hier mit 43,8% ihr bislang bestes Ergebnis ein. Je strukturschwächer, gottverlassener und migrationsärmer die Gegenden sind, desto stärker ist der Zuspruch zum nationalistischen Autoritarismus. So bereisen die ewig grinsenden Rattenfänger das Land und punkten unter Deutschen, die die Überwindung ihrer eigenen bürgerlichen Existenz herbeisehnen und hoffen dies auf dem Weg der Zerstörung der liberalen Demokratie zu erreichen.


Der Wohlfühl-Faschismus ist ein Phänomen, das vor zwanzigdreißig Jahren noch völlig unvorstellbar gewesen wäre. Und in zweidrei Jahrzehnten werden wir uns ebenfalls fragen, was in dieser Phase eigentlich passiert ist. Wer sie verstehen will, muss sich dazu nicht nur die Wahlkampf-Strategien der AfD anschauen, sondern auch kultur- und medienwissenschaftlich vorgehen. So ist es kein Zufall, das seit Anfang des Jahres 2026 massenhaft KI-generierte Songs bei Youtube erscheinen. Aufgrund ihrer hohen Klickzahlen landen diese wiederum durch die Algorithmen sehr schnell in der Vorschlagleiste.


Die extrem rechte Propaganda-Maschinerie bedient sich somit nahezu perfekt abgestimmt der Mittel, die der Plattform-Kapitalismus entwickelt hat. Und sie greift auf eine künstlich-sentimentale Popkultur zurück, die unterm Strich meistens schon sehr schlicht und beschränkt war. Ob volkstümelnd wie Heino, oder neu-deutsch-hart wie Rammstein, sülzig wie Julia Juls, Runa&Rebellin oder pop-rockig wie Weimar, Sleipnir und andere – Vorbilder für die extrem rechte Computermusik gibt es genug…


Sicher könnte man auch dagegen halten und sagen, dass die Generierung von Musik und Video-Material durch technische Sprechapparate von allen möglichen Leute mit kommerziellen Absichten, um Aufmerksamkeit zu erhalten oder einfach nur aus Langeweile generiert wird. Und das stimmt auch. Bedenkt man, wie durchproduziert und geglättet kommerziell erfolgreiche Musik heute ist, scheint der Schritt zur sogenannten KI klein zu sein. Dennoch gibt es eine spezielle Affinität von faschistischem Denken zur offensichtlich künstlichen Kultur, die den Anschein von menschlicher Kreativität verlässt und damit post-human ist. Laut Jason Stanley wird damit auf die Herstellung von „Unwirklichkeit“ abgezielt.


Um ein paar Beispiele von viralen KI-generierten Songs und „Künstler“ zu nennen, sind da beispielsweise:


– „Spätestens HIER wacht jeder auf! Der Sound des Wandels“ („Aufbruch Deutschland“, 501.537 Aufrufe)


– „Steh auf, wenn du Deutscher bist | Stolz auf Heimat und Kultur“ („Ottilie“, 339.081 Aufrufe)


– „Was ist aus unserem Land geworden? | Ein Lied über den Verlust der Heimat“ („Fenja“, 338.697 Aufrufe)


– „Dorfmarie – So war es, so soll es wieder sein“ („Dorfmarie“, 160.534 Aufrufe)


– „DIE WACHT AM RHEIN (LIVE) | Rock-Version eines historischen Gedichts“ („Julia im Exil“; 113.198 Aufrufe)


– „Kein schöner Land… WO DIE EICHEN STEH’N“ („Freya“; 18.974 Aufrufe)


– „Thüringen Ein Land Eine Geschichte Ein Herz“ („Der Heimatklang“, 4334 Aufrufe)


– „Heimweh nach Deutschland“ („Liv Eisen“, 2067 Aufrufe)


Die Titel verraten schon das Wesentliche. Wenn man die Textzeilen hört oder liest, wird deutlich, dass die immer gleichen Narrative, endlos wiederholt werden. Stets geht es um den Verlust einer imaginären „Heimat“ oder glorreichen „Nation“, um eine angebliche „Überfremdung“, anknüpfend an den Verschwörungsmythos eines „großen Austauschs“. Der Gute-Laune-Faschismus lebt in der ewigen Wiederholung von Mustern immer gleicher Opfer-Inszenierungen, dem Streicheln narzisstischer Kränkungen, sowie der Vorstellung einer zukünftigen Größe, die nur durch die Erniedrigung der ausgemachten Feinde erreicht werden kann. All dies sind Produkte einer staatlich-kapitalistischen Gesellschaftsform, die mit Patriarchat, Rassismus und Naturbeherrschung verknüpft ist. Zusammengefasst ist die Computer-produzierte Lyrik in ihrem billigen Abklatsch armselig – und faschistisch.


Dabei darf man nicht vergessen, dass auch der historische Nationalismus keine naturwüchsige Volksbewegung war, sondern ein Elitenprojekt, das eine Nation und eine darin angeblich ursprünglich vorhandene Kultur verordnete, anerzog und drillte.


Hört man die künstlich erzeugten Lieder und ihre Texte an, greifen Form und Inhalt ineinander. Bekanntlich ist den Fans derartiger wohlfühlfaschistischer Erzeugnisse vollkommen egal, ob sie ein KI-generiertes Lied …

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Rosa Amorim: "Hablar de reforma agraria en Brasil es hablar de un proyecto de dignidad de vida"
content:
“Com a barriga vazia não consigo dormir,

E com o bucho mais cheio, comecei a pensar.

Que eu me organizando posso desorganizar

Que eu desorganizando posso me organizar

Que eu me organizando posso desorganizar”.

Da lama ao caos, Nação Zumbi - Chico Science


“Con la panza vacía no puedo dormir,

Con el buche más lleno, empecé a pensar.

Que desorganizándome puedo organizar

Que organizando me puedo desorganizar

Que desorganizándome puedo organizar”


Por Mariángeles Guerrero y Carla Perelló

Desde Brasil


Rosa Amorim es la primera mujer del Movimiento de los Trabajadores Rurales sin Tierra (MST) en ser electa diputada nacional en Brasil. Es negra, lesbiana, oriunda de Pernambuco, nordeste del país, y tiene 29 años. Integra el Partido de los Trabajadores (PT). Durante la pandemia, mientras gobernaba Jair Bolsonaro, fue una de las impulsoras de la red de cocinas solidarias que enfrentaron el hambre en los barrios populares de las ciudades. La reelección de Lula da Silva significa una victoria popular y una esperanza, pero la conformación de un Congreso con mayoría de la extrema derecha plantea sus propios desafíos. En ese escenario, sostiene que la “lucha parlamentaria” será vital. “Queremos que Brasil deje de ser uno de los países que más venenos y agrotóxicos consume”, afirma.


Hija de la lucha por la reforma agraria, Amorim creció en las filas del MST y también fue dirigente estudiantil. Desde sus orígenes, el movimiento campesino mantuvo su autonomía aunque apoyó candidaturas del PT. Pero, en 2022, tras el retroceso en materia de derechos que significó el gobierno de Jair Bolsonario, presentó sus propios candidatos. Ese año, ella fue electa diputada del estado de Pernambuco.

El pasado 5 de octubre fue electa diputada nacional; una de lxs 38 legisladorxs LGBT+ que obtuvieron un escaño y una de los cuatro integrantes del MST que estarán en el Congreso brasileño

.


En el histórico proceso electoral que consolidó a Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva como presidente por los próximos cuatro años, Amorim fue una de las jóvenes que acompañó la campaña para revertir la derrota que el PT obtuvo en la primera vuelta.

Llevará las banderas de la reforma agraria y la soberanía alimentaria al Poder Legislativo. Allí el agronegocio presiona, de la mano de la bancada ruralista, para obtener beneficios y seguir extendiendo la frontera agropecuaria

, causando deforestación y contaminación.


En contraste, el MST lleva cuatro décadas de lucha por la tierra para la producción de alimentos sanos.

“Alimentamos al pueblo porque con comida en la panza podemos tener mentes pensantes y con mentes pensantes podemos organizarnos”

, sostuvo en entrevista con Tierra Viva, haciendo honor a la histórica banda nordestina Nação Zumbi liderada por Chico Science.


Foto: Prensa PT


Las cocinas solidarias, que define como “una tecnología social para organizar al pueblo”, se convirtieron en política pública en 2023, durante el gobierno de Da Silva. Su objetivo es vincular el campo con la ciudad, llevando alimentos sanos a espacios comunitarios de los barrios populares. En esos ámbitos se brinda un plato de comida pero también escucha, alfabetización, contención y cuidados. Para la diputada, comer es el primer paso para cuestionar por qué existe el hambre y la pobreza.


—¿En qué situación está hoy la soberanía alimentaria en Brasil?

—Hablar del hambre no es solamente hablar de si el pueblo come por la mañana, por la tarde y por la noche. Es más profundo. Combatir el hambre también significa hablar de la calidad de lo que se come. Y para eso vamos a tener que librar una lucha muy grande. Ya la estamos librando, pero va a ser todavía mayor: la lucha contra el agronegocio, contra el modelo de producción vigente que hace que las personas se enfermen por lo que consumen todos los días. Queremos que Brasil deje de ser uno de los países que más venenos y agrotóxicos consume. Y esto tiene una relación directa con la lucha parlamentaria. Vamos a tener que librar una enorme disputa contra el agronegocio en el Congreso para reducir la cantidad de agrotóxicos que se autorizan en Brasil. También vamos a tener que poner en la agenda la ampliación de las tierras cultivables destinadas a la agricultura familiar y campesina.

Llego al Congreso Nacional para conformar y construir la bancada de la tierra, de la agricultura familiar y de la agricultura campesina. Queremos debatir cómo combatir el hambre y qué estamos consumiendo en Brasil.

Tenemos que debatir la …
