author: rezgar2
title: The Brazilian Victory: Left Unity and Digital Autonomy
content:
Rezgar Akrawi : Lula's victory offers an experience worth studying and learning from. It demonstrates the possibility of cooperation among left-wing forces despite their differences, while recognizing the other factors that contributed to the result.


The left does not need to erase its diversity in order to unite. It needs to turn that diversity into an organized and effective force, strengthen its independence across all five pillars, and pursue the struggle for freedom, equality, and social justice while developing democratic, humanist socialist alternatives to capitalism.


Author


Rezgar Akrawi


رزكار عقراوي


    Submitted by

rezgar2

 on October 29, 2026


Rezgar Akrawi


The leftist leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic victory in Brazil’s presidential election on October 25, 2026. The result came amid intense political and social polarization and the growing influence of the far right in Brazil and across Latin America, backed by the American far right led by Donald Trump.


The significance of this electoral victory extends beyond Lula securing a fourth term. It also lies in the political and organizational experience that helped make it possible, above all the ability of diverse left-wing and progressive forces, with different programs and ideological outlooks, to forge a broad electoral alliance around common ground in confronting the far right.


A Broad Left-Wing and Progressive Alliance Despite Differences


Lula contested the election with the support of the ‘Brazil Ready for More’ alliance, comprising seven left-wing and progressive parties organized into two party federations and two separate parties. The ‘Brazil of Hope’ federation brought together Lula’s Workers’ Party, the Communist Party of Brazil, and the Green Party. The second federation united the Socialism and Liberty Party, which includes socialist and radical-left currents, with the Sustainability Network. The Brazilian Socialist Party and the Democratic Labour Party also joined the alliance, alongside supportive social movements and trade unions. Lula ran with Geraldo Alckmin of the Brazilian Socialist Party as his vice-presidential candidate.


The importance of this alliance lies in its ability to bring together communists, socialists, the radical left, social democrats, and Greens despite their disagreements over capitalism, the role of the state, and the limits of social reform. These forces agreed on common electoral objectives while preserving their identities and organizational autonomy.


This is one of the most important lessons of the Brazilian experience. Left unity does not require ideological or organizational uniformity. It means being able to work together on common ground while respecting pluralism and differences.

 Disagreements over Lula’s economic and social policies will naturally persist, including among the forces that supported him at the ballot box.


Unity Does Not Mean Abandoning Criticism or Autonomy


The Brazilian experience raises an important question for left-wing forces around the world. Why do ideological and organizational differences become barriers to cooperation, despite so much common ground, even when these forces face shared political and class challenges?


Pluralism among communists, social democrats, the radical left, environmentalist and feminist currents, and independent leftists can be a source of strength and intellectual and political richness, provided it is managed democratically and constructively, without monopolization, exclusion, or claims to possess the absolute truth.

 Unity does not require abandoning criticism or offering unconditional acceptance of the policies of governments led by left-wing and progressive alliances.


Confronting Capitalism and the Far Right Requires a Broad Social Front


The victory demonstrated the importance of connecting the defense of democracy, rights, and freedoms with the economic and social demands of working classes and poor and marginalized communities.


Lula drew broad support from lower-income groups and proposed expanding social assistance, improving living conditions, and defending democratic institutions.


Confronting capitalism and the far right therefore cannot be confined to elections and party alliances. It requires sustained mass organizations in workplaces, neighborhoods, universities, trade unions, and social movements, together with policies that tackle class inequality and improve the lives of the majority …

author: Mary Stuart
title: How the Far-Right Uses Climate Disasters to Build Political Power
content:
Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s

End Times Fascism and the Fight for the Living World

 is critical reading for anyone seeking to understand and push back against the far-right coalitions wielding considerable state and corporate power around the world.


Klein and Taylor posit that today’s fascists believe that end times have arrived, and have made it their mission to profit from cascading global crises, while hunkering down and protecting themselves as the world burns around them.


The book details three factions of end times fascists, united by their shared apocalypticism. The religious fundamentalists believe end times are upon us, but they will be saved by their messiah. The Silicon Valley technologists are building technologies they say could be world-ending, that in the meantime are killing jobs, consuming vast resources, and polluting communities. The ethno-nationalists espouse conspiratorial ideas about cultural replacement and treat immigration as an existential threat.


DeSmog Canada editor/reporter Mary Stuart spoke with Astra Taylor about how climate change fits into end times fascism, the importance of AI data centre fights, and how we can understand Canadian Prime Minister Carney’s neoliberal moves in response to U.S. President Donald Trump.


Taylor is a writer, documentarian, and activist. She co-founded the

Debt Collective

, a membership-based union for debtors, and is the author of several books, including

The Age of Insecurity

 and

Democracy May Not Exist But We’ll Miss It When It is Gone

.


This interview was conducted by phone and has been edited for length and clarity.


Mary Stuart:

 

I


want to start by


asking how your book can help us understand some recent elections. Jair Bolsonaro’s son Flávio won the first round of voting in Brazil’s election and


nearly


became president. The far-right AfD recently won in Saxony-Anhalt.


How do these wins fit into your analysis of end times fascism?


Astra Taylor:

 One phenomena we describe in End Times Fascism relevant here is the role of Pentecostal religious communities in turning out the vote. To paraphrase reporting from Brazil, a voter said “my heart’s with Lula, but my pastor told me to vote for Flávio”.


The incredibly difficult conditions that we’re living under created fertile terrain for prophecy and religion, for kinds of pentecostalism, a faith that is focused on prosperity, individual advancement and banking on the idea that life is suffering here on earth, but you will be rewarded in the afterlife.


There’s also interference from Tech oligarchs. We don’t know the half of it at this moment, but the way the platform [Meta] refused to run ads for Lula’s party and beyond is certainly a factor. And the Trump regime [is playing a role] as well.


AfD is a similar. Naomi and I wrote a piece in the

Financial Times

 and we open with the images that went viral this summer of the Danube River drying, and Nazi warships emerging. Hundreds of Nazi warships sank during WWII, and as the river receded, this paraphernalia was coming out of the mud. We thought it was a powerful metaphor for today. What’s really striking is the riverbed— the fact that it’s drying because of climate change. Our point is that fascism always emerges from crises. And we cannot separate the ecological and economic crises people are facing.


People are really struggling with affordability. People are feeling that they don’t have a future. And actually quite strikingly, rates of immigration are quite low, right? So [Saxony-Anhalt is] one of the places with the least immigration, but [the AfD] step in and say “the problem is the immigrants, it’s not a larger economic system.” This is a classic fascist move that we describe throughout the book.


MS:


What role do climate change and climate denial play in end times fascism?


AT:

 Naomi and I are insistent that the planet is a player in our politics. Fascism always surges in moments of crisis.


We are in a world that is being roiled by disasters and shocks. We’ve reached a point where the consequences [of climate change] are undeniable. You cannot deny a heat dome when you’re inside it. You cannot deny a hurricane when it’s blowing the roof off your house. Of course, you can still deny why the storm is coming. You can embrace a Marjorie Taylor Greene perspective and say that it’s due to space lasers or you can say “the climate has always chained, this is nothing new, we don’t know if it’s human causing it.” …

author: nodes of resistance
title: Rechenzentren, „KI“ und Strategien für emanzipatorischen Widerstand
content:
Im Vorfeld der bundesweiten Konferenz zur Vernetzung von Widerstand gegen „KI“ und Rechenzentren. am 7.11.26 in Berlin veröffentlichen wir folgendes Diskussionspapier


Es regt sich Widerstand gegen Rechenzentren und das, wofür sie stehen. Damit dieser Widerstand möglichst weit trägt, halten wir eine Diskussion zu drei Themen für wichtig:


1) Der enge Zusammenhang von Rechenzentren und „KI“


2) Gemeinsam kämpfen für Klima- und soziale Gerechtigkeit, gegen Faschismus und Militarisierung


3) Wirksamer Widerstand durch Vielfalt und Unberechenbarkeit


1) Der enge Zusammenhang von Rechenzentren und „KI“


Der massive Ausbau von Rechenzentren und der Hype um „KI“ hängen unmittelbar zusammen. Denn: Der Hype um „KI“ mobilisiert die finanziellen Ressourcen und die politisch einstimmige Unterstützung für einen in Geschwindigkeit und Umfang beispiellosen Ausbau materieller Infrastruktur. Der Zusammenhang umfasst die technische, ökonomische und politische Dimension.


• Der technische Zusammenhang: Rechenzentren sind gewissermaßen die Fabriken von „KI“. Während es schon länger Rechenzentren gibt (seit dem Aufkommen von „Cloud“ als zentral verwaltete Rechenkapazitäten), macht „KI“ noch viel mehr und größere Rechenzentren erforderlich: Manche Rechenzentren dienen primär dem Training von „KI“-Modellen (diese brauchen besonders teure Halbleiter-Chips und liegen oft eher ländlich), andere primär der Inferenz, also dem Errechnen von „KI“-Outputs basierend auf trainierten Modellen (diese liegen meist möglichst nah an Internetknotenpunkten, oft urban). Rechenzentren liegen am Ende einer komplexen globalen Lieferkette: Besonders deutlich ist die erhöhte Nachfrage nach seltenen Erden und Metallen sowie nach Wasser und (fossiler) Energie, die an vielen Stellen dieser Lieferkette benötigt werden: Bei der Herstellung der Lithografiemaschinen, die wiederum nötig sind, um Chips zu produzieren zu können, die wiederum nötig sind, um ein Rechenzentrum zu betreiben. Die Infrastruktur rund um Rechenzentren und „KI“ ist seit einigen Jahren in erheblichem Aufbau und schließt zunehmend auch Endgeräte ein, deren Funktionieren an eine kontinuierliche Anbindung nicht nur an Internetkonnektivität, sondern auch an „KI“ und Cloud gebunden ist (von Heimgeräten über industrielle Produktion hin zu Kampfjets).


• Der finanzielle Zusammenhang: Der Finanzierung von Rechenzentren liegt ein quasi-religiöser Glaube an die Unausweichlichkeit und die Spekulation auf zukünftige Profitabilität von „KI“ zugrunde. „KI“-Unternehmen fahren jährlich Milliardenverluste ein, weil ihre Ausgaben in Form von Kosten von Rechenkapazitäten, Energie und Löhnen über den Einnahmen liegen. Rechenzentren sind dabei der Knotenpunkt für finanzielle Risiken: Die Chipherstellung ist (bisher) profitabel (siehe Bilanzen von Nvidia, TSMC, SK Hynix), das gleiche gilt für die Bereitstellung von Rechenkapazitäten als Dienstleistung, die vor allem die drei Hyperscaler-Unternehmen Amazon, Microsoft und Google anbieten. Rechenzentren sitzen zwischen der Chipherstellung und der Bereitstellung von Rechenkapazitäten und werden häufig nur angemietet von denjenigen, die dann wiederum Rechenleistung nutzen oder verkaufen. Rechenzentren sind extrem kapitalintensiv (bis zu mehreren Milliarden Euro pro Rechenzentrum) und hochspekulativ, sodass auch Menschen aus der Rechenzentrumsbranche (anonym/vertraulich) sagen: „Wer das Risiko versteht, wird nicht investieren.“ Das Risiko (also die Wahrscheinlichkeit von Verlusten) ergibt sich u.a. aus einer kurzen Lebensdauer von Chips (je nach Quelle ein, zwei oder max. sieben Jahre), der langfristigen Finanzierung von Rechenzentrumsbau (oft 15-20 Jahre), einer hohen Unsicherheit über die Verfügbarkeit und den Preis von Chips, Energie und Wasser und einer ebenfalls hohen Unsicherheit über die Nachfrage nach „KI“-Rechenkapazitäten. Diese Risiken werden aktuell immer neu verschachtelt durch komplexe Zirkelkäufe zwischen „KI“-Unternehmen, Chipherstellern und Rechenzentrumsbetreibern, was selbst Finanzanalyst*innen kritisch bewerten. Bereits seit mehreren Jahren attestieren u.a. Analyst*innen von Goldman Sachs das Vorliegen einer „Blase“.


• Der politische Zusammenhang: Die vermeintliche Unausweichlichkeit von „KI“ wird politisch verknüpft mit einem Wettbewerb um geopolitische Vorherrschaft (v.a. zwischen USA und China), einem Streben nach „Souveränität“ (z.B. durch Chipherstellung und Rechenzentren in Europa) und dem (Un-)Heilsversprechen immer mächtigerer …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Anarquistas pela anarquia sobre as eleições no Brasil/ Anarquistas por la anarquía sobre las elecciones en Brasil
content:
Enviado a La Zarzamora/ *Traducción al español al final.

Contra o fascismo todas as ações são úteis! Encontra teu lugar na luta. Revolte-se!

São os dizeres de um cartaz que apareceu nas ruas de Porto Alegre em 2019, e que são dizeres vigentes, antes de 2019, depois de 2019, nestes dias e que serão vigente ainda muito depois.

Nestes tempos em que o apelo anti fascista tende a afunilar-se no voto diante de um contexto em que o resultado das eleições no Brasil podem consolidar o neo fascismo a nível continental, nos é importante compartilhar um olhar anárquico que nos possibilite sair do pânico e construir antagonismos aos fascismos atuais, apesar de que nada seja tão simples assim. Para isso inicialmente vamos a entender que enquanto anárquicos e anarquistas, fazemos parte de coletividades, redes, e grupos dentro da sociedade que não compartilham nossa posição política, para depois apontar e precisar que nossas posições políticas não são sinônimos de pertencimentos ou identidades.

Cientes de que habitamos territórios felizmente diversos e com pessoas que tem maior ou menor apego à autonomia e a auto determinação, pensarmos nos diferentes lugares de luta contra o fascismo, consiste precisamente em aceitarmos dentro dessa diversidade, mutuamente, o que quer dizer horizontalmente, longe das tentativas uniformizadoras. Então podemos respeitar e entender que os cidadãos votantes “lutem” por não ter um presidente fascista, mediante o voto. Ao final é uma vergonha andar pelo mundo com a imposição majoritária de governantes misóginos, racistas, e aquele longo etc que bem sabemos sobre as famílias com tendência monarquista e miliciana. E mais profundamente, é respeitável o ódio que sentem por um personagem desse naipe. Quando trata-se de pessoas que não compartilham o local ácrata de luta contra o sistema, seu lugar na “luta” é nas urnas e é entendível.

Agora quando falamos de pessoas que escolhem a anarquia como posição política, e seus locais de luta é que nos debruçamos com um debate que a cada eleição nos faz perder companheiros e que a cada eleição nos joga diante de acusações de supostos purismos, falta de tática, falta de solidariedade, indiferença e outro longo etc. No entanto, o que no fundo incomoda a cada eleição é o fato de que os mesmos anarquistas chamem a fazer campanha por um candidato e façam apelo ao chamado “voto tático”.

Independentemente dos argumentos, isso incomoda não apenas quem escuta esses apelos e decide que sendo anarquista não tem como votar, mas acredito que incomoda também a quem vai na campanha, faz o apelo e tem que pensar, argumentar, escrever, fazer vídeo ou responder que apesar de… segue sendo anarquista. É nessa mesma justificativa que pode ser percebido que votar não forma parte do repertório das práticas anarquistas.

Ao nos perguntarmos sobre nosso lugar na luta contra o fascismo o que evidencia que somos anarquistas? Qual é a diferença com os demais? O apelo ao voto anarquista já nos indica que somos reconhecidos por não votar. Então pedem-nos, diante do desespero, o favor de abdicar de uma de nossas práticas e isso não é pouca coisa.

Um dos nossos fundamentos, enquanto anárquicos e anarquistas, é o rechaço ao Estado. Odiamos ele porque enxergamos nele a cristalização de todos os processos opressivos, mas mesmo odiando o Estado ele nos afeta, e as pautas que possam resultar do circo dos horrores que foi eleito, vão nos afetar com politicas que procuram devolver forças para o patriarcado, ao militarismo, ao extrativismo, a moralidade religiosa, ao conservadorismo. De fato é por isso que odiamos o Estado, porque ele nos afeta, porque nos impõe.

Para além desse fundamento, o que do anarquismo fez com que nosso coração batesse e escolhêssemos esse caminho? Se há algo que fazemos sem nenhuma obrigação é ser parte das agitações e movimentos anarquistas, então sendo uma escolha tão livre, o que dessa proposta nos tocou o coração?

A autonomia, a autogestão, a horizontalidade, o apoio mútuo, a solidariedade, são práticas anarquistas que também são fundamentais e que, inegavelmente, são também incompatíveis com a existência dos Estados, porque cada Estado pretende anular essas práticas. Se sustenta no discurso de que as pessoas não sobreviveríamos sem o Estado, apesar de que catástrofes já demonstraram a efetividade da organização horizontal, apesar de que a história social e coletiva tem se desenvolvido majoritariamente sem Estado se pensamos nela historicamente e fora do eurocentrismo …

Résultat : on vient de quitter l'époque contemporaine et, depuis, Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres. Mais ces ténèbres, elles sont super drôles.


Jamais autant de créatures multiformes n'avaient déferlé dans nos insurrections. Il nous a fallu analyser cet étrange phénomène. Alors on a invité deux experts des ténèbres joyeuses : le philosophe Norman Ajari et l'essayiste Pacôme Thiellement. La brèche entre les mondes vient de s'ouvrir, elle n'est pas près de se refermer.  La police mutile les lycéen-s!

 Unterdrückung, Polizeistaat und Faschismus, so sichbar wie schon lange nicht mehr.


An diesen Punkt sind wir nicht ohne Grund gekommen. Denn die Herrschenden nutzen ihre Macht, um die Ressourcen dieser Welt nach ihrem Kalkül einzusetzen. Das heisst, das Geld geht ins Militär, anstatt in die Schulen. Das heisst das Geld geht in KI, anstatt in den Klimaschutz. Das heisst offene Grenzen für Kapital und geschlossene Grenzen für all diejenigen, die durch die Kriege des Kapitals ihre Lebenswelt verlieren. Kurz, der Status Quo ist nicht einfach so passiert.

Reparation

 vorgezogen haben. Hervorheben wollen wir dabei auch, dass die genannten Probleme nicht isoliert betrachtet werden können. Die Herrschenden finanzieren ihre Kriege und Genozide mit dem Geld, dass dann anderswo fehlt.

Es ist ein und dieselbe Rechnung.

 Und aus eigener Tasche bezahlen sie es sicher NIE! Aka, wir alle bezahlen es. In der heilen Schweiz immerhin (noch) nicht mit unserem Leben. Und die Verantwortlichen sitzen tagtäglich vor unseren Nasen. Was eine Gesamtscheisse! Zum Glück findet der Kampf dagegen gerade wieder Wege in die Festung Europa.

The kids are alright after all!


Wir lehne dabei das Narrativ ab, es handle sich einach um Schüler*innenproteste. Erstens geht es schon lange nicht mehr um "Protest" es geht um Konfrontation und die Weigerung, sich zu unterwerfen.

Der Geist des Aufstands geht um in Europa.

 Zweitens waren es von Beginn an nicht einfach Schüler*innenproteste, sondern eine viel breitere Bewegung, die ihre Lebensrealität nicht mehr akzeptieren wollte. Und die Poteste waren von Beginn an militant. Wehe all denen, die Denken, die

Casseurs

Casseurs

Ein kleines bisschen Gerechtigkeit blitzt auf in jeder zerbrochenen Scheibe der sonst für uns unbezahlbaren Innenstädte. Solidarität mit allen

Zerbrecher*innen

 dieser Welt!

Wir haben euch lieb.

Denn niemand ist frei, sind wir nicht alle frei!

On en a marre - en Suisse aussi!

title: İpek Er’s mother: My daughter was killed a second time
content:
“My daughter was killed a second time today.” With these words, Hikmet Kılınç, the mother of Kurdish woman İpek Er, who died in 2020, protested the recent acquittal of former gendarmerie officer Musa Orhan at a women’s conference in Ankara. Six years after her daughter’s death, she has leveled serious accusations against state officials and announced her determination to continue her fight for justice all the way to the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR).


The protest follows a ruling issued on October 22 by a criminal court in Batman. Musa Orhan, who was sentenced to ten years in prison in 2021 for a serious sexual assault against İpek Er, was acquitted of the charge of incitement to suicide in a separate trial. According to Kılınç, the decision represents another setback in her years-long struggle to secure legal accountability for her daughter’s death.


Addressing more than 500 participants at the “Women Discuss the Future Side by Side” conference, Kılınç recounted her experiences since her daughter’s death. She accused state authorities of exploiting her hopes for justice and attempting to exert political pressure on her. “For six years, they told me: If you stay away from the Kurdish parties, we will ensure justice for your daughter. After six years, they acquitted him,” Kılınç said. She explained that she had sold all her possessions and moved to Batman. “Under the pretext of defending my daughter’s rights, they deceived me.”


The mother also directed her criticism at former Turkish Interior Minister Süleyman Soylu, accusing him of protecting Orhan and facilitating his acquittal. At the same time, she appealed to Kurdish members of parliament not to lose sight of the case. “My daughter’s blood must not go unavenged. As long as I live, I will fight for her rights. I will pursue this case all the way to the ECtHR,” Kılınç said. “My daughter was killed by someone who wielded state power. As long as the perpetrator walks free, there can be no talk of justice.”


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/b62c3f26_20261031121003_2026-10-31-ankara-hikmet-kilinc-ipek-er-annesi-kadinlar-yan-yana-gelecegi-konusuyor-konferansi-cagri-1.mp4


Allegations of threats and abuse


In her speech, Kılınç also described the violence and intimidation her daughter had endured. According to her mother, İpek had been manipulated and subjected to pressure. She had been threatened with the killing of her father and brother, and there had even been an attempt to sell her. “İpek’s hair is evidence of the torture she suffered. I still have my daughter’s bloodstained clothes,” Kılınç said. She said she continues to preserve her daughter’s personal belongings to this day.


Kılınç made these statements at the two-day women’s conference held at the Chamber of Civil Engineers in Ankara. Since Saturday, journalists, academics, politicians, and activists have been discussing peace, justice, equal citizenship, and the struggle against patriarchal violence.


Six years of legal proceedings


On July 7, 2020, İpek Er filed a criminal complaint against Musa Orhan with the public prosecutor’s office in Siirt. Orhan was serving as a professional soldier in the district of Beşiri at the time. Er stated that he had been raped by him. On July 16, she attempted suicide after leaving a farewell letter. After spending 34 days in hospital, she died on August 18, 2020.


Orhan was initially detained but subsequently released under judicial supervision. Following public protests, he was remanded in custody on August 19, 2020, but was released just one week later after an appeal. He was later dismissed from the gendarmerie.


In December 2021, a criminal court in Siirt sentenced Orhan to ten years in prison for sexual assault, applying mitigating circumstances. Despite his conviction, he remained free. A separate criminal case was also brought against him in Batman on charges of incitement to suicide. That trial ended in an acquittal on October 22. The ruling concerns only this second charge and does not overturn his earlier conviction for sexual violence.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Alegatos en el juicio por el triple lesbicidio de Barracas: “El crimen fue motivado por odio a las víctimas”
content:
El juicio por el triple lesbicidio de Barracas del que fueron víctimas Pamela Cobbas, Roxana Figueroa y Andrea Amarante, y que dejó con graves secuelas a Sofía Riglos Castro, la única sobreviviente del ataque, está en su recta final. Esta semana las querellas de todas ellas y la fiscalía coincidieron en pedir que se considere fue un lesbicidio y femicidio, solicitando la pena máxima de prisión perpetua para Justo Fernando Barrientos, el único acusado. El hombre de 69 años vivía en la misma pensión que las cuatro mujeres lesbianas y la noche del 5 de mayo de 2024 las atacó arrojando un artefacto explosivo a la habitación donde ellas dormían.


Las audiencias de alegatos fueron el 26 y el 28 de octubre. Las protagonizaron las querellas y la fiscalía, reconstruyendo paso a paso cómo fue el feroz ataque y también sus antecedentes. A partir de eso y considerando la jurisprudencia en Argentina y el sistema internacional de derechos humanos, pidieron al tribunal que considere para Barrientos la pena máxima y que el delito se encuadre como mediado por violencia de género y como un crimen de odio, motivado por la orientación sexual de las víctimas. Algo que al principio de la investigación,

el juzgado de instrucción se negaba a admitir

. Pero gracias al trabajo persistente de abogados y activistas se reconoció el encuadre jurídico como crimen de odio, tal como prevé el artículo 80 inciso 4 del Código Penal en Argentina.


“El crimen estuvo motivado por el odio a las víctimas”


El miércoles 28, el fiscal general Manuel Fernández Buzzi  aseguró a los jueces del Tribunal Oral en lo Criminal y Correccional (TOCC) Nº5 que

existen suficientes pruebas para considerar que “el crimen estuvo motivado en un sentimiento muy profundo y visceral: el odio que sentía hacía las víctimas. No solo las quemó vivas sino que lo hizo de noche, adentro de su habitación, donde convivían

”. Y destacó que Barrientos sentía “desprecio y aversión” hacia ellas por ser lesbianas. A partir de lo que se escuchó en la sala en las audiencias, la fiscalía -así como las querellas- consideró probado que el odio de Barrientos no nació el día que atacó a sus víctimas, sino que existía una historia previa de hostigamiento, tal como

contamos en esta agencia

 en mayo de 2024.


El fiscal general Manuel Fernández Buzzi expuso su alegato por el triple lesbicidio y ataque de Barracas. Foto: Matías Pellón/Fiscales.gob.ar


Las víctimas “vivían acosadas y discriminadas por Barrientos por ser lesbianas y por ser mujeres”, dijo el fiscal. Y agregó que aprovechó la situación de vulnerabilidad de ellas para atacarlas. “Él se creía superior, se permitía discriminar y despreciar a estas mujeres porque no cumplían con el estereotipo que la sociedad les asigna. El motivo del crimen fue el odio. No fue un homicidio cualquiera: las prendió fuego de una manera deliberada, con el objetivo de quemarlas vivas, de que sufrieran y agonizaran”.


El fiscal pidió que la sentencia tenga en cuenta que se trató de un homicidio agravado por ensañamiento, por mediar violencia de género y odio a la orientación sexual en los casos de Pamela, Roxana y Andrea, y en grado de tentativa en relación a Sofía, de modo que abordó los crímenes como femicidios y lesbicidios. La fiscalía también dejó en claro que “este crimen expresa lo peor de la interacción social: el sexismo, la intolerancia, la discriminación y el odio”.


“Necesitamos que el Estado nos cuide”


Antes de la fiscalía, expuso su alegato la querella colectiva de la Federación Argentina de Lesbianas, Gays, Bisexuales y Trans. El equipo jurídico lo integran las abogadas Samanta Pedrozo y Flavia Massenzio, y Sofía Saavedra Chávez, asistente letrada.


Pedrozo abrió la audiencia 18 con una introducción: “Solemos decir que somos una querella colectiva, si bien me escuchan a mi, soy parte de un colectivo que está expectante de este juicio”. Pedrozo recordó que en reiteradas oportunidades se les negó a la FALGBT la posibilidad de ser querellantes. “Y seguimos insistiendo hasta que en diciembre de 2024 llegamos a Casación Penal. A partir de ese momento pudimos formar parte de este proceso y es histórico estar acá. Lo que les pasó a Andrea, a Pamela, a Roxana y a Sofía no les pasó solo a ellas, nos pasó a todas las personas que desde que nacemos tenemos que aprender a vivir con el odio y la discriminación”.


Así quedó la habitación del hotel donde vivían las cuatro víctimas. Foto: Ariel Gutraich/Agencia Presentes

author: Amy Goodman
title: Remembering Legendary Farmworker Organizer and Activist Dolores Huerta
content:
Huerta wasn’t just an organizer — she also loved life, says journalist Maria Hinojosa.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Immigrant rights and labor icon Dolores Huerta died Wednesday at the age of 96. Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America, working with Cesar Chavez. From 1965 to 1970, the union organized the historic Delano grape strike, which ended in major gains for farmworkers’ labor rights.

In the years that followed, Huerta became heavily involved in the women’s liberation and immigrant rights movements and became a major supporter of the Democratic Party. In March, The New York Times published an investigation into Cesar Chavez’s history of sexual abuse of women and girls in the farmworkers’ movement, prompting Huerta to reveal that she, too, had been raped by Chavez. Huerta said the assaults led to the births of two of her children.

Dolores Huerta appeared on Democracy Now! many times over the years. We remember her legacy with Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Maria Hinojosa, who says, “Dolores was not only a labor organizer, a civil rights organizer, a feminist, committed, always optimistic about the possibilities of this country, but she loved life, and I want people to remember that.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman.

The legendary labor organizer, feminist and civil rights activist Dolores Huerta has died at the age of 96. She was co-founder of the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America. She worked with Cesar Chavez at both groups. The United Farm Workers grew out of a merger between the National Farm Workers Association and the Filipino-led Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee.

Dolores Huerta coined the phrase ”¡Sí se puede!,” “Yes, we can!” It became a rallying cry for farmworkers, a lasting slogan for social justice movements.

Dolores Huerta appeared on Democracy Now! many times. We’ll hear her in her own words later in the broadcast, but first let’s turn to the trailer of the 2017 documentary Dolores, which featured interviews with Angela Davis, Gloria Steinem, Hillary Clinton and Nancy Pelosi.

title: «Nos falta una maestra»: paro nacional de docentes y auxiliares por justicia para Nanci Godoy y condiciones laborales dignas
content:
Foto: redes sociales.


La CTERA convocó a un paro nacional docente para hoy, jueves 29 de octubre, tras el hallazgo sin vida de Nanci Estela Godoy, la maestra rural de Corrientes desaparecida desde el 7 de octubre. La medida reúne al Frente de Unidad Docente Bonaerense (FUDB), la Asociación Trabajadores del Estado (ATE), la Asociación de Maestrxs de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, la Unión Docentes Argentinos (UDA), el Sindicato de Obreros y Empleados de Minoridad y Educación (SOEME) y la Unión del Personal Civil de la Nación (UPCN), además del frente de SUTEBA Multicolor y gremios universitarios como CONADU, CONADU Histórica, AGD-UBA y FAGDUT, cuyas medidas de fuerza ya estaban previstas. La jornada de duelo, paro y movilizaciones reclama justicia por el femicidio y una investigación que determine las responsabilidades penales y estatales. Pero el reclamo también se inscribe en un escenario de conflictos salariales, precarización laboral y desfinanciamiento educativo: mientras en Buenos Aires las seccionales de SUTEBA Multicolor acaban de realizar nuevas jornadas de paro y protesta contra el acuerdo paritario del 6%, en Corrientes el sindicato provincial SUTECO denuncia las condiciones de aislamiento, inestabilidad y desprotección en las que Godoy cumplía su tarea.

title: The Cornell Case and the Left's Betrayal of Itself
content:
Here's an article about the feminist reaction to the "Cornell 7" case that has been in the news recently (October 2026). A version of it was published in "Compact." (The hyperlinks have been deleted, unfortunately.) The general point is that contemporary feminism has become an albatross for the left, and is also contributing to destructive social and cultural trends.

In the 1960s, feminists demanded that women and men have legal equality, that women be treated as mature adults who are free to make their own choices be it with regard to sex or their careers, that patriarchal paternalism be dismantled. In the 2020s, feminists demand that women be constantly protected against men, that patriarchal paternalism be resurrected, that women be legally treated as not responsible for decisions they’ve made because, in certain contexts, only men have agency. And men, they argue, are inveterate misogynists, abusers, and rapists, so the agency they manifest is almost invariably malign.

The reaction to the “Cornell 7” case is the latest example. A remarkable wave of hysteria has swept liberal and left culture, from mass media and social media to university campuses. Misandry is drenching the discourse; mobs are going after anyone who questions the dominant narrative; the guilt of the accused is automatically assumed, because the accused are men and men are by definition guilty. Is it any wonder that millions of men in recent years have turned away from the left—which seems to hate them—and fallen into the clutches of the far-right and the “manosphere”?

Consider what has transpired. Far from condemning the wildly irresponsible comments of public figures like Governor Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James, which treat as established fact accusations made in a civil lawsuit, leftists themselves, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Zohran Mamdani, have talked as though the case has already been decided. This is despite the highly ambiguous evidence that has been presented, much of which tends to exonerate the alleged perpetrators of the “gang-rape.” Not only is presumption of innocence thrown out the window; it is obvious that even if the accused end up being found innocent, most liberals and leftists will remain sure of their guilt.

Lynch mobs have been out for blood. A few weeks ago, it was easy to find thousands of people “liking” public demands to kill the accused. Even innocent bystanders were victimized. The campaign of overwhelming harassment to which the journalist Michael Tracey has been subjected for questioning the “guilty until proven innocent” narrative led to his father receiving “thousands of nonstop crazed texts/calls/voicemails” threatening him with brutal violence. The current owners of Tracey’s childhood home were “inundated” with “crazed threats,” and received suspicious packages at their house. Friends and family of the accused men were harassed by thousands. So was the family of an innocent man who happens to have the same name as one of the accused.

Since liberals and leftists are refusing to stand up for decency and the rule of law, it is left to conservatives to do so—which enables them to claim the moral high ground against “lunatic” leftists and thereby score political points. It turns out that many conservatives take women more seriously as (potentially) responsible adults and moral agents than most leftists do.

Feminist moral panics may seem well-intentioned in that they’re allegedly motivated by concern for the safety of women, but these episodes illustrate the extent to which the (so-called) “left” has been corrupted and co-opted by neoliberal dynamics, particularly in the era of social media. The atomized, polarized, siloed, anti-intellectual, narcissistic soundbite culture of social media—itself a reflection of capitalist tendencies—has helped produce a liberal-left that dehumanizes others, reflexively assumes the worst of men, exploits controversies for social media clout, and contributes to the very social breakdown that leftists rightly attack neoliberalism for engendering. After all, a feminism that teaches women to hate and fear men, and to view themselves as being on a higher moral plane, doesn’t exactly promote healthy relationships. It exacerbates gender wars and culture wars, thus, again, gifting the right wing with talking points and grievances to rally around.

author: Sara Fayyazi
title: Making Women’s History Part of the Curriculum
content:
Two teachers from Sacred Heart Preparatory School in California, Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams, have proposed an Advanced Placement U.S. Women’s History course in response to the issue of students not learning about women’s history. The courses would allow studying women’s experiences and contributions in greater depth. Establishing this course would create a better understanding of American history as it includes the diverse experiences of women and would help students connect the historical struggles for equality to gender issues today.

Women have contributed to shaping the nation’s politics, economy, and social movements, yet their participation is often overlooked by traditional history classes. From fighting for the right to vote, challenging discrimination, and advocating for female autonomy, women have had a significant role in building the foundation of the United States today.

One of the main arguments for WAPUSH is that women’s experiences are not explored in the classroom. In the article Educational Activism: Creating an AP U.S. Women’s History Course, Serene Williams, Kristen Kelly, and Clara Robinson explain that topics such as women’s suffrage and reproductive rights receive limited attention in the current AP U.S. History curriculum. The women’s suffrage movement involved decades of organizing, political campaigning, and resistance. However, teachers may not introduce this topic to students or have enough time to examine its strategies and leaders in detail. A dedicated course would allow students to study these movements more thoroughly and understand how women helped shape American democracy.

Women’s history is much broader than the fight for voting rights. The proposed WAPUSH curriculum includes women’s labor, politics, religion, culture, war, and violence against women. It also examines how race, class, sexuality, religion, and other identities shaped women’s experiences. This approach is important because women throughout the years have never shared one universal experience. Indigenous women, Black women, Immigrant women, etc., have faced different opportunities and forms of discrimination. Studying these differences would help students develop a greater understanding of American history and that America was not built on just our founding fathers, but by women who paved the path for opportunity and development through blood, sweat, and tears.

An AP course would also help students recognize the connection between historical events and current issues. The debate over reproductive rights and other feminist struggles today cannot be fully understood without examining the laws and political movements that shaped access to contraceptives, abortion, and female economic support. Studying topics from the suffrage movement to the Equal Rights Amendment can help students understand the political equality that has developed through activism and engage in feminist discussion. Learning this history would give students the context needed to evaluate debates instead of viewing them as different events.

Establishing this course would show that women’s history is worthy of advanced academic study. The WAPUSH campaign began in 2022, and according to its website, the campaign gathered more than 4,000 petition signatures and received encouragement from College Board leadership as it worked toward launching this course. Its proposal has also received university support, while the campaign continues seeking letters from high schools willing to offer the course. This continued support brings women closer to bringing light to women’s history and giving women a space in school systems and curricula. This petition is one step closer every day to its goal to educate and inform people all across America of women’s contributions.

An AP U.S. Women’s History course would make education more comprehensive, inform students even more about the history of the U.S., and connect past struggles to present issues. Women have influenced American politics, economics, culture, and social movements, yet their experiences are not always given sufficient attention in existing courses. By offering students an opportunity to examine these experiences, the College Board could help create a more inclusive and accurate understanding of the nation’s past. Women’s history is not separate from American history but instead an essential part of it.

author: Tam Saavedra
title: The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality are Here!
content:
Ver versión en español


The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality Just Changed the Game for Disability Rights—Here’s What You Need to Know 


Big news for women with disabilities and all feminist disabled advocates, allies, and organizations worldwide!

 


During its 35th Session in August 2026, the

UN Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

 (UN CRPD)

 officially adopted the historic

Guidelines on Identifying and Addressing Intersectional Discrimination Against Girls, Adolescents, Women, and Older Women with Disabilities

.

 


This milestone represents a monumental step forward for disability rights. For the first time, States have explicit, actionable guidance to support their obligations at the intersection of gender and disability.

 


Read the official CRPD Guidelines here

 


What Are the CRPD Guidelines on Intersectional Discrimination?


The Guidelines serve as an authoritative framework developed by the UN


CRPD Committee to help States better prevent, monitor, and address intersectional discrimination.

 


Throughout years of UN CRPD country review processes, the Committee identified a persistent, critical gap:

the specific rights of women with disabilities and the complex, intersectional discrimination they experience are rarely understood or adequately addressed by governments.

 


As the UN CRPD celebrates its 20th anniversary, these Guidelines were issued to bridge that gap—ensuring the convention is implemented to benefit

all

 women, girls, and gender-diverse people with disabilities across their lifespans.

 


Why Are These Guidelines a Game


–

Changer?

 


International documents rarely explicitly focus on the detailed, lived experiences and rights of women with disabilities. These Guidelines clearly name and elaborate on the systemic barriers

 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities face daily across the globe, including:

 


Sexual & Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR):

 Addressing and preventing enforced sterilization, forced contraception, lack of accessible healthcare, restrictions on abortion, and lack of perinatal, menstrual, and menopause care.

 


Gender-Based & Disability-Based Violence:

 Exposing institutional violence, digital/online abuse, and the widespread lack of support services for victims.

 


Caregiving Recognition:

 Validating women with disabilities as active caregivers and mothers, rather than only recipients of care.

 


Economic & Educational Exclusion:

 Highlighting barriers in the labor market, economic and exclusion from education during puberty.

 


Crisis & Climate Response:

 Tackling compounded exclusion during environmental disasters, climate emergencies, and humanitarian relief efforts.

 


…just to name a few.

 


7 Key Breakthroughs in the Framing of the Guidelines 

 


What makes this document uniquely transformative is its progressive, structural approach:

 


Explicit Inclusion of Gender Diversity:

 The Guidelines explicitly encompass the rights of transgender, intersex, non-binary, and other gender-diverse people with disabilities and ask for gender diversity – inclusive interpretation of all obligations described.

 


Recognition of Historical Root Causes:

 The Committee explicitly addresses the legacy and ongoing impacts of

colonialism and enslavement

, establishing that States benefiting from these historical systems bear a particular responsibility to remedy their ongoing effects.

 


An Open Catalogue of Diversity:

 The text recognizes that women with disabilities belong to multi-marginalized communities—including Indigenous, Black, Dalit, Adivasi, refugee, asylum-seeking, religious minority, and pastoralist groups or people living in informal settings, among others —while leaving space for all intersecting identities.

 


Structural & Preventive Approach:

 Moving beyond a strictly punitive, reactive model, the Guidelines demand the dismantling of systemic oppression (such as ableism, audism, racism, and patriarchy) through early intervention, education, and public policy reform. 

 


Decriminalization

 is also a disability issue:

The guidelines recognize impacts of criminalization of abortion, homosexuality, gender identity and expression as well as

restricting marriage or consensual relationships as an important intersectional disability rights issue.

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Nunavik school board to pilot sex-education program
content:
Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, Nunavik’s school board, will test a sexuality education program in Kuujjuaq and Umiujaq in November.


The pilot program was developed with the Nunavik Regional Board of Health and Social Services and is intended to help children understand personal boundaries and how to stay safe in sexual situations, said Sarah Aloupa, president of Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, in an interview.


“It’s important for parents to take this very seriously. This program is for the students’ well being,” she said.


Aloupa said the initiative responds to a need raised by Nunavik residents and parents. The school board’s council of commissioners heard a presentation from the health board about the proposed program in June.


The program will cover students from kindergarten to Grade 11, with information packages for different age groups.


Aloupa declined to share the teaching material.


The pilot is scheduled to run Nov. 2 to 6 at Jaanimmarik School and Pitakallak School in Kuujjuaq and Nov. 16 to 20 at Kiluutaq School in Umiujaq. The schools were chosen in part because they were ready to take part and have staff with relevant experience, said Jade Duchesneau-Bernier, spokesperson for the school board.


During those weeks, staff will participate in training and parents can review material and ask questions at evening information sessions.


Their feedback will help shape the final program. While the board has not yet clarified how parents can do so, they can opt their children out, Aloupa said.


Information about the sessions is being sent to parents through school letters and posted on Facebook.


Aloupa pointed to sexual abuse cases in the region as part of the broader need for education on the subject.


In February 2025, Nicolas Cyr, a physical education teacher at Jaanimmarik School, was

charged

 with sexual assault of a minor, sexual interference of a minor and assault.


The pilot is intended to help the Nunavik school board and the region’s health board assess the program before considering whether to expand it to the other 18 schools Kativik Ilisarniliriniq operates, Aloupa said.


The organizations have not yet set a timeline for a region-wide rollout.

author: TGEU
title: Trans activists and stakeholders gather at TGEU’s Pre-Council to advance trans rights in Eastern Europe and Central Asia
content:
On 9-10 September in Ljubljana, Slovenia, 27 trans activists from Eastern Europe and Central Asia (EECA) and international stakeholders came together to ask one question: how do we protect trans people in a region where democracy and human rights are deteriorating?


The second TGEU Pre-Council Strategic Meeting on Trans Rights in EECA took place ahead of TGEU’s 10th European and Central Asian Trans Council. Over two days, participants analysed the rapidly changing political and legal environment, exchanged lessons learned, and explored ways to strengthen cooperation, joint advocacy and coordinated action.

 


The Strategic Meeting brought together three groups with different but complementary types of expertise and mandates: 


EECA trans activists with direct experience working with communities and conducting national advocacy


International stakeholders working on human rights and the rule of law


Allied movement leaders engaged in human rights protection.


Together, they aimed to build a shared understanding of key challenges and possible responses, identify political and legal leverage points for 2026–2027, and strengthen trust and cooperation.


Key takeaways


Participants shared strategies for responding to anti-trans policies.


They explored practical approaches to depathologisation and healthcare, and how strategic litigation can drive wider legal and social change.


TGEU will follow up on the priorities, requests and commitments that emerged, including by connecting participants with international organisations.


The Pre-Council was intended not as a stand-alone meeting, but as a point for continued exchange and action.


A region under pressure 


Across EECA,  trans people are being used as scapegoats to reinforce authoritarian power and control. Trans people are portrayed as a threat to ‘national identity and values’ or ‘women and children’ within a broader and increasingly coordinated anti-gender discourse. 


Pressure from authoritarian states and anti-gender forces is growing alongside:


Laws and policies that increasingly target civil society


War and armed conflict


Cuts to funding for civil society programmes


Increasingly unsafe conditions for trans human rights defenders


Limited opportunities to protect rights through national and international human rights mechanisms


Transforming exchange into action 


Rather than simply sharing information, the meeting focused on turning shared experiences into action.


Participants discussed specific examples from different countries, exchanged tried-and-tested strategies, and learned more about the work of the Council of Europe, the OHCHR, the UN Human Rights Committee, and international human rights organisations. They examined examples of solidarity with other civil society movements and explored practical approaches to improving healthcare for trans people and strengthening their autonomy, including the role of ICD-11 and WPATH standards.


They also mapped alliances, explored the potential of strategic litigation, identified concrete opportunities for collaboration, and had a forum where various actors could ask questions and get practical answers.


The discussions strengthened a sense of regional solidarity and created a space for new partnerships and commitments to emerge. 


What happens next 


In the coming months, TGEU will stay in contact with participants and support follow-up on the priorities, requests and commitments that emerged during the discussions. 


This will include facilitating connections between participants and relevant branches of international organisations interested in further collaboration, including opportunities for strategic litigation. 


TGEU will also continue to monitor cross-sectoral and international health-related initiatives and processes to identify relevant developments early and connect EECA activists with stakeholders in advance, so they can engage strategically and contribute their perspectives. 


Your support makes change possible


We work across Europe and Central Asia to advance trans rights, build strong communities, and drive change through research, advocacy, and community-building.


Your donation helps us continue this vital work — defending trans lives, amplifying trans voices, and advocating for justice every day.

author: Pinko Collective
title: Letter in Support of the Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá and Trans and Queer People Facing State Repression Worldwide
content:
We reprint the open letter below in support of the Dolls of Berlin. To add your name as a signatory, follow the link at the bottom of the page.

On the afternoon of Sunday 18 October a large police squad forcibly entered Casa Kuá, a queer community center in Berlin, Germany, where at that point The Dolls of Berlin, a transfem social collective, was gathering. Police detained several women for hours while ransacking Casa Kuá. We, the undersigned, stand in support with The Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá, and queer and trans people facing state violence, repression and erasure everywhere. We are demanding that the German State drop the case and immediately stop the criminalization of trans spaces and solidarities. We are urging everyone to contribute to the fundraiser, to help our comrades continue their essential work and activities, and keep

nourishing much needed survival spaces for the most vulnerable communities

. 

The attack against the Berlin Dolls comes at a time of unprecedented rise of state fascism, both in Germany where the AfD recently won local elections in Saxony-Anhalt, in neighbouring European countries, and in India, Brazil, Argentina, the United States and elsewhere. This rise of the far right has been accompanied by a massive increase on attacks on queer and trans people. In Turkey between 12-14 September, in coordinated overnight raids across five cities, Turkish police targeted seven LGBTQI+ rights organizations, two groups supporting people living with HIV, and 13 bars and clubs where queer people gather. Board members of some of the country’s oldest LGBTQI+ associations, including Kaos GL and Lambda Istanbul, were

taken from their homes

. Human Rights Watch reports that at least

112 people were arrested and that 82 remain in detention

 by court order. On 3/4 October Taiwan police

raided a Taipei queer bar

 detaining 51 persons and abusing disabled customers.

At the same time, increasingly authoritarian states, including Germany, are seeking to erase trans existence through administrative violence, putting barriers in front of access to trans healthcare. As European governments divert public spending to remilitarisation efforts, access to housing, welfare, jobs and education become circumscribed. In the UK, the drastically curtailed access to trans healthcare in recent years has led to trans suicides on an

unprecedented scale

. Recent government guidelines on so-called 'single sex spaces' are likely to cause more deaths such as that of trans woman, Joelle, who died after being

denied cancer care for 16 days

. A stark example of the hypocrisy on the part of the ruling elite came on 21 October when openly gay Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jette and his partner celebrated the expected arrival of their child, while his government

denies queer refugees the right to family reunification

. The attacks on queer and trans people are accompanied by attacks on, and further marginalisation of the disabled, migrants and refugees, precarious workers, poor Black, Brown and Indigenous communities, the unhoused and incarcerated, compounded for those in multiple of these categories. It is a tell-tale sign of fascism when particular communities are rendered vulnerable, disposable and presented as scapegoats for the various harmful effects of racialised capitalism. 

That the relatively small community of queer and trans people, and racialised trans femmes in particular, has become a target for (proto-)fascist and authoritarian regimes globally is no surprise. Transness especially stands out as a visible transgression of cis hetero patriarchal norms on which fascist authority is built. It forms a thorn in the eye of regimes dependent on popular internalisation of its structural "truths". Transness thus becomes a powerful wedge issue that allows states to whip up fear and distrust of trans people which is consolidated through state carceral and administrative violence. It is also no surprise that state attacks on queer and trans people are on the rise globally at a time when Gen Z, along with older social movements are rising up in France, Albania, Brazil, India, Argentina, Indonesia, Greece and across the planet. Time and again, queer and trans people have stood at the helm of

social movements and popular struggles for liberation

.


The 18 October attack on The Dolls of Berlin at Casa Kuá is historic. Coming at this conjuncture in history, it is signaling the moment that demands we all stand up not only …

Κάλεσμα/Αφίσα από

Βιβλιοπαρουσίαση και συζήτηση “Οι μαχήτριες του Δημοκρατικού Στρατού 1946-1949” της Τασούλας Βερβενιώτη

Η παρουσίαση του βιβλίου της Τασούλας Βερβενιώτη, «Οι μαχήτριες του Δημοκρατικού Στρατού 1946-1949», θα διεξαχθεί ως συζήτηση μεταξύ των:


Τασούλα Βερβενιώτη, Πέγκυ Ζάλη, Δέσποινα Ζευκιλή, Penny, Γυναικεία Δομή της Κοινότητας των Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


Από το οπισθόφυλλο του βιβλίου:


Η τόσο μεγάλη συμμετοχή των γυναικών στον Δημοκρατικό Στρατο αποτέλεσε ένα ανατρεπτικό γεγονός για όλη την ελληνική κοινωνία, το οποίο ήταν δύσκολο να το κατανοήσει, να το ερμηνεύσει και να το εντάξει -ακόμα και σήμερα- στη συλλογιστική της. Ο στόχος αυτού του βιβλίου δεν είναι να εξιδανικεύσει τη δράση των μαχητριών του Δημοκρατικού Στρατού, αλλά να την καταγράψει, ώστε να την καταστήσει ορατή. Η ιστοριογραφία δεν διαθέτει πολλές αναπαραστάσεις γυναικών που συμμετείχαν σε ένοπλες εμφύλιες συγκρούσεις, γι΄ αυτό το εγχείρημα ήταν δύσκολο. Το 2000, μετά το Ψήφισμα 1325 του Συμβουλίου Ασφαλείας του ΟΗΕ, η έρευνα για τον ρόλο των γυναικών στους πολέμους έχει αρχίσει να αναπτύσεται. Ως γενικό συμπέρασμα θα μπορούσαμε να πούμε ότι οι γυναίκες δεν είναι απλώς θύματα των πολέμων αλλά και φορείς κοινωνικής αλλαγής.

author: Andrea DiP
title: Um beijo em uma mulher trans
content:
A cena toda deve ter durado cerca de três segundos: A deputada federal Erika Hilton (Psol-SP) faz um vídeo comemorando a eleição de Lula após a contagem das urnas, no dia 25 de outubro. Ele passa por ela, pega seu rosto, tasca um beijo carinhoso em sua bochecha e sai do quadro. Um gesto simples, espontâneo, terno, um carinho. 


Eu não sei se Lula tem noção do tamanho da declaração que fez pro mundo.

 O presidente de um país, que acaba de ser reeleito em um processo histórico e inédito em tantos níveis – com participação popular e engajamento sociais sem igual, em uma virada épica que acontece apesar de todo tipo de sabotagem das

Big Techs

 ao governo Trump, de tentativas de boicote ao

transporte público

 para que as pessoas não chegassem às urnas a uma grande imprensa tacanha jogando contra –

um homem de 81 anos, que tem os olhos do mundo virados para si, mostra publicamente afeto a uma mulher trans. 


Trecho de vídeo publicado por Erika Hilton


Essa cena me emociona por diferentes motivos. Tenho passado os últimos anos me infiltrando em eventos da extrema direita pelo mundo e entrevistando essas figuras. Posso afirmar que não houve um desses congressos sequer, nenhuma dessas conversas, que não passou por discursos ultraviolentos contra pessoas trans. 


Já escrevi bastante sobre isso, inclusive sobre como no governo Trump essa violência levou a resoluções e políticas públicas desde seu primeiro dia de mandato. Não vou me repetir aqui sobre a maneira como essas narrativas são construídas com base no pânico moral e na ideia da destruição da família e de valores sagrados. O que quero ressaltar é que

a demonização de pessoas trans está hoje no epicentro político da extrema direita. É um tema de consenso entre eles, usado para mobilizar o medo, o ressentimento e o ódio e que tem efeitos concretos na vida de milhares de pessoas. 


E a mobilização desses afetos não é exclusiva da extrema direita, também é importante dizer. Não sei dizer quantas vezes eu mesma fui perseguida, ameaçada e exposta por mulheres que se dizem feministas radicais trans excludentes ou quantas vezes o Pauta Pública foi alvo de ódio quando apontamos nosso microfone para pessoas trans. Tudo bem. Como me disse Judith Butler, ser perseguida por essas pessoas é um distintivo de coragem. 


Um outro ponto importante é que

o Brasil é um dos países que mais mata transexuais no mundo

. Quando Lula faz esse gesto, que mensagem ele manda para o povo? E que mensagem ele manda para as pessoas trans?


A cena me lembrou o relato de Suzanne Hommel, uma alemã nascida em 1938 que falou no documentário “Encontro com Lacan” sobre o tempo em que foi paciente do psicanalista francês. Ela carregava traumas profundos de sua vivência durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial, mas, em uma de suas sessões com Lacan, contou de um sonho recorrente que a acordava sob forte angústia todos os dias pontualmente às 5h da manhã. Acrescentou o contexto histórico de sua infância: “Era às 5h da manhã que a Gestapo vinha buscar os judeus em suas casas”. Ao ouvir a palavra “Gestapo” (polícia secreta oficial da Alemanha Nazista) o psicanalista levantou-se rapidamente da poltrona e fez um carinho suave em seu rosto. Quando ela conta isso no documentário, imediatamente leva a mão ao rosto imitando o gesto. 


Através desse ato físico e verbal, Lacan transformou a palavra “Gestapo” em “geste à peau”, que em francês significa “gesto na pele”, e introduziu ternura onde antes habitava apenas o horror e o trauma. No documentário, ela se emociona ao dizer que isso não apagou seu sofrimento mas o modificou de forma definitiva e que mesmo décadas depois, ela ainda sentia aquele toque que mudou a forma como olhava para a própria história e sua própria dor. 


O “geste à peau” de Lula em Erika Hilton neste momento da nossa história, me parece muito poderoso, simbólico, um marco de posição diante do mundo, que pode ressignificar um monte de afetos pra muita gente. E ao mesmo tempo é tão bonito precisamente porque foi um afago espontâneo em um país que está ressignificando sua relação com a política, que ainda sofre com o trauma dos quatro anos sob o governo genocida de Bolsonaro – e que escolheu neste domingo apostar na ternura ao invés do horror.


Aliás, que fique marcado aqui: Erika Hilton foi reeleita como a mulher mais votada da história para a Câmara dos Deputados e, com 1,5 milhão de votos conquistados em São Paulo, é a segunda parlamentar no país a romper a barreira de 1 milhão de votos …

Queer/Feminist Alternatives to Both Historical Anarchism and State Systems

Benevolent State Control vs. Community Care

Cindy Barukh Milstein. 2024. Constellations of Care: Anarcha-Feminism in Practice. London: Pluto Press.

Constellations of Care is an anthology of answers to a fundamental question: what do people do to survive and thrive from the margins of society? According to the volume’s editor, Cindy Barukh Milstein, the goal of state-based systems is not to provide prosperity and security for all. Rather, they strategically reserve material and political protections for those who conform to a masculine and heteronormative model of the ‘good citizen’. The various authors of this anthology, all members of various anarcha-feminist collectives, employ the praxis of anarcha-feminism to suggest that resistance to state-based exclusion depends first and foremost on the practice of care, sustaining and building relationships that give life to those without political and economic power or opportunities, who unwittingly or willingly do not conform to the standards desired by the state. Empowerment and social transformation are not driven by massive state projects, but by interpersonal and highly specific interventions managed by those who share the ontological experience of exclusion through inhabiting queer or feminine bodies.

What follows is a collection of histories, reflections, conversations, and artwork that reflect collective, anti-hierarchical, and locally organized efforts to care for a global network of the excluded. Whether written by underground abortion care providers in Poland, communal kitchen collectives that sustained anti-government protests in Colombia, or unhoused and precarious sex workers in Philadelphia who hold weekly needle exchanges, each of its thirty-seven entries offers an approach to creating communities by and for the marginalized.

In some ways, Milstein’s work sits at odds with a strictly academic style of writing. One of the first entries in the book, written by members of the Nightshade collective in Philadelphia, actively denounces the ability of formal academia to understand and advance anarchist theory, suggesting that academia is inherently hierarchical, focuses on creating grand universalist theory rather than accepting theoretical plurality, and gatekeeps legitimacy through economically restricting access to academic credentials (p. 24). Constellations of Care is based on the idea that theory is created, interpreted, and used not by researchers, but by the everyday stakeholders in the political processes that it analyzes. The book emphasizes alternatives to academic style in some of its editorial choices. For example, each section’s author biography veers away from listing degrees or institutional affiliations, and rather briefly chronicles the author’s skill sets and political positions, as well as their close relationships to both communities and geographies, often defined by a city or an Indigenous land designation, rather than a nationality …

author: Paul Gregoire
title: Allega Spender pushes to remove religious exemptions against LGBTIQ students, teachers
content:
The Sex Discrimination and Fair Work Amendment (Equality in Treatment in Religious Schools) Bill 2026, introduced on October 12, seeks to repeal the offending exemptions in federal sex discrimination law as well as removing the related provisions in federal workplace relations law. It also extends protections to associates of those who are captured under the current exemptions.

Section 38 of the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 (SDA) makes it lawful for religious education institutions to discriminate against a teacher, student or contract worker due to their “sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital or relationship status or pregnancy”.

The proposal took centre stage in 2018, as the national religious freedoms debate took off prior to then-Coalition Prime Minister Scott Morrison shooting it down.

Morrison’s push to establish a religious freedoms regime in 2018 uncovered their existence. His years-long religious crusade was defeated after debate on these exemptions.

Labor PM Anthony Albanese promised to progress the reform in 2022, but changed his mind.

Spender, independent MP for Wentworth, is pushing popular reforms, despite far-right commentators claiming it as an attack on religious freedom.

“These exemptions have already been removed in state and territory law, to varying degrees, but there are no national standards,” Spender told NSW Parliament on October 12.

“The Australian Law Reform Commission’s 2024 review found that religious schools could still maintain their ethos without this exemption.

“At its heart, section 38 of the Sex Discrimination Act is repealed in its entirety and replaced with a far narrower provision,” Spender said in her second reading speech on her private member’s bill.

“Protections are also extended to a person’s associates ... This means a child cannot be treated differently just because she has two mums.”

The bill repeals the current provisions affecting students, teachers and contract workers in section 38, replacing it with a provision that allows institutions to preference staff based on faith in two ways — at their initial employment and in the promotion of senior leadership roles such as “principal, vice-principal, religious education teacher, chaplain” or any other comparable role.

The bill inserts section 7AAA into the SDA, which makes it unlawful to discriminate against an associate, such as a spouse or relative, of a person protected under the Act. It removes provisions that permitted discrimination based on sex, sexuality or gender.

It also repeals provisions in the Fair Work Act 2009 that extend discrimination into workplace agreements.

“But preferencing is not a licence to discriminate,” Spender said. “A school can choose a candidate because of their faith. It cannot fire someone because of their sexuality. Many students have wonderful, formative experiences at religious schools. Many LGBTQIA+ students come out to their friends and teachers in these schools and are accepted. But … this is not everyone’s experience.”

The exemptions in section 38 of the SDA relating to sexual orientation and gender identity, were inserted into the Act when a 2013 bill added anti-discrimination provisions into the law that related to sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex characteristics. The exemptions in respect of gay and transgender individuals joined pre-existing ones that permitted discrimination based on sex.

The October 2018 Ruddock review into religious freedoms recommended tightening these exemptions in federal law, which drew attention to and then condemnation of the laws.

While Morrison initially tried to downplay the outcry, he reversed course and promised to repeal the discriminatory measures targeting students. But Morrison, a Pentecostal, attempted to progress three versions of the Religious Freedoms Bill — two in 2019 and one in 2022 — and the removal of any exemptions was forgotten.

Each version of the religious freedoms legislation was increasingly watered down.

Three years of debate on these laws made it clear that his measures sought religious privileges.

The public debate over religious concerns is different to the present, with the conservative push to insert the controversial International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition of antisemitism into all levels of government to curb criticism of Israel and its genocide.
