author: Jillian Kestler-D’Amours
title: Masked White Supremacists Are Stoking Residential School Denialism in Canada
content:
“We have endured fear, and we will not be intimidated,” one Indigenous leader said.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

It was 3:00 am when Doug George-Kanentiio first arrived at the Mohawk Institute Residential School in Brantford, Ontario, in 1967.

He was 11 years old, and he would go on to spend 18 months at the abusive institution, which was Canada’s longest-running residential school. The notorious school operated for more than 140 years before it closed in 1970.

“They weren’t places of learning, they were places of confinement,” George-Kanentiio said.

Decades later, he still remembers the hunger, fear, and brutality that he and the other Indigenous children who were forced to attend the Mohawk Institute endured there every day.

“Anything you could imagine [being done] to a child, when it comes to abuse, that’s what these individuals did,” said George-Kanentiio, who is from Akwesasne, a Kanien’kehá:ka (Mohawk) community on the U.S.-Canada border, between New York state and the provinces of Ontario and Quebec.

“It was physically painful and extraordinarily cruel,” he told Truthout.

More than 150,000 First Nations, Metis, and Inuit children were separated from their families and forced to attend residential schools across Canada between the 1870s and the mid-1990s.

The institutions — which aimed to forcibly assimilate Indigenous children into the country’s predominantly white European culture — were rife with physical, sexual, and psychological abuse.

The children were barred from speaking their languages, and thousands are believed to have died while in attendance due to abuse, malnutrition, and rampant disease that resulted from squalid conditions. In 2015, a federal commission of inquiry said the system amounted to “cultural genocide.”

Yet while George-Kanentiio and other survivors have spoken about their abuse for years, efforts to downplay, minimize, and distort facts about the residential school system are getting louder in Canada.

The rising wave of residential school denialism has drawn widespread alarm as Indigenous community leaders and other experts say right-wing figures are trying to derail truth and reconciliation — the process of investigating and redressing the devastating impacts of Canada’s colonial policies, including its residential school system — while harming survivors in the process.

Niigaanwewidam Sinclair, an Indigenous studies professor at the University of Manitoba, likened residential school denialism to Holocaust denialism.

“They’ll say, ‘We’re just asking questions, it’s free speech, we’re trying to just tell the other side,’” he told Truthout.

“They weren’t places of learning, they were places of confinement.”

But he emphasized that residential school denialists are not really interested in a “good-faith conversation.” Instead, Sinclair said, they have two main goals: to “monetize ignorance” and to gain public attention.

“They’re trying to profit off of the fact that for 150 years Canadians were miseducated about Indigenous peoples and residential schools in particular,” he explained.

The issue came to a very public head last month when a group of about two dozen masked men affiliated with white nationalist group Second Sons Canada gathered on the lands of Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc, an Indigenous (First Nation) community in the province of British Columbia.

Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc has faced years of pressure from denialists since it announced in 2021 that a preliminary radar search of the grounds of the former Kamloops Indian Residential School had uncovered the potential remains of more than 200 children.

The discovery sparked a reckoning across Canada as people demanded justice for the myriad crimes committed at residential schools, which were funded by the government but run by various churches.

But the findings in Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc also fueled denialism, with far right activists and politicians seizing on early reporting errors to accuse the community and media outlets of lying.

“The entire country is motivated and moving towards implementing truth and reconciliation,” whereas denialists are “trying to slow things down, and they’re trying to profit,” said Sinclair.

The men who entered Tk̓emlúps te Secwépemc in late September hung a banner on an overpass that day reading, “Got bones?” — a reference to the 2021 discovery of possible remains …

author: Unknown
title: Fransa'da ırkçılık ve İslamofobi karşıtı gösteriler düzenlendi
content:
Fransa'da farklı sendika, dernek ve kitle örgütü kuruluşlarının çağrısıyla Paris, Strazburg, Roubaix, Stains, Nanterre, La Courneuve dahil farklı kentlerde ırkçılık karşıtları bir araya geldi.

Ülkede artan ırkçılığa ve İslamofobiye tepki verilen gösterilerde, 23 Ekim'de Yvelines ilinde düzenlenen terör saldırısında hayatını kaybeden Kongo asıllı Fransız Pengo Bossio Wangi anıldı.

Gösterilerde, söz konusu ırkçı saldırıda yaralanan 1'i çocuk olmak üzere 5 kişiye yönelik destek mesajları da dile getirildi.

Başkent Paris'te Stalingrad Muharebesi Meydanı'nda yerel saatle 19.00'da başlayan gösteriye yüzlerce kişi katıldı.

Göstericiler, "Irkçılık bir görüş değil, hayatları paramparça eden bir suçtur", "Paramparça olan hayatlardan ziyade kırılan vitrinlere şefkat gösteriyorlar" ve "Irkçılık öldürür" yazılı pankartlar taşıdı.

Göstericiler, ırkçı söylemleri yaymakla suçlanan CNews kanalında çalışan bir gazetecinin gösteriye katılmasına "CNews dışarı" ve "CNews katil, (Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel) Macron suç ortağı" sloganları atarak tepki gösterdi.

Irkçılıkla mücadele derneği SOS Racisme'in Başkanı Dominique Sopo, burada yaptığı konuşmada, birkaç yıldır ülkede ırkçı saikli suçların yeniden işlenmeye başlandığını söyledi.

Sopo, bazı medya organlarının bünyelerinde ırkçı söylemlerin sarf edilmesine izin verdiğini belirterek, bu söylemin son derece "ciddi" olduğuna dikkati çekti.

Yvelines'e bağlı Trappes kentindeki saldırıyı yapan teröristin "siyahilere ve Araplara saldırarak 17 Ekim'deki gösterilerinde, dükkanı yağmalanan esnafın öcünü almak istediğini" dile getirdiğini aktaran Sopo, terör saldırısından birkaç gün önce Fransız televizyon kanallarında eylemlerdeki yağma olaylarıyla ilgili ırkçı bir çerçeve kullanıldığını belirtti.

Trappes Belediye Başkanı Ali Rabeh ise Ulusal Birlik (RN) Partisi Başkanı Jordan Bardella'nın daha önce Trappes kentini "Paris'e 30 dakika mesafedeki Kabil'e" benzettiğini hatırlattı.

Rabeh, Trappes'a yönelik damgalayıcı sözler kullananları terör saldırısının failine silah vermekle suçlayarak, "Kanallarda durmaksızın aktarılan yabancılara, göçmenlere, Müslümanlara karşı sarf edilen nefret söylemleri, Fransızların bir kısmının insanlıktan çıkarılmasına neden oldu." dedi.

Bu durumun, bu kişilerin "iç düşmanlar" gibi gösterilmesine sebebiyet verdiğini kaydeden Rabeh, ırkçılık zehrinin tüm ülkeye bulaştığını dile getirdi.

Irkçılık Karşıtı Koalisyon'dan yapılan açıklamaya göre, Paris'te Cumhuriyet Meydanı'nda düzenlenmesi planlanan bir diğer gösteri, Paris Emniyet Müdürlüğünce yasaklandı.

Sosyal medyaya yansıyan görüntülere göre, bazı göstericiler, yasağa rağmen Cumhuriyet Meydanı yakınlarında toplandı.

Sokakta yere oturan göstericiler, Fransa'nın ulusal marşı La Marseillaise'i okudu.

Polis, eylemi dağıtmak için kalkanlarıyla göstericileri iterek bölgeden uzaklaştırmaya çalıştı.

Yvelines ilinde 23 Ekim'de bir kişi, bulunduğu araçtan etraftakilere ateş açmıştı. Saldırıda 1 kişi hayatını kaybetmiş, 5 kişi ağır yaralanmıştı.

39 yaşındaki saldırgan Kevin T, olay yerinde gözaltına alınmıştı.

Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Emmanuel Macron, saldırının ırkçı nitelikte bir terör saldırısı olduğunu duyurmuştu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: anonerror
title: [Valladolid] Apertura de nuevo local de CNT
content:
Antifascistas, antirracistas, anticapitalistas, transfeministas e internacionalistas. En medio de una convocatoria de huelga general por la vivienda y contra todos los poderes que viven de desangrar a la clase trabajadora, CNT Valladolid inaugura un nuevo local en calle Merced, 6, de Valladolid, entre las plazas de Santa Cruz y Circular.


Hace más de dos años empezamos un proyecto muy ilusionante. Nuestro local se quedaba pequeño y teníamos que buscar otro. Hicimos un proceso de reflexión colectiva, para tener claras nuestras necesidades presentes y futuras. Una tienda de fontanería se ha convertido en un sindicato como el nuestro, con más salas donde reunirse, un salón amplio en el que convocar actos… Un nuevo espacio en Valladolid a disposición de todas las personas trabajadoras.


A pesar de que quedan retoques, el pasado 17 de octubre nos decidimos a abrir puertas en un acto en el que nos reunimos la afiliacIón con personas afines del presente y del futuro. Contamos con las actuaciones de Jesús Puebla Mimo, de Rubén Ruiz, Rosa Vicente y José Luis Alonso, de Chusma y de Juguillos, de Astrolabio, y tuvimos ocasión de mover el esqueleto con las aportaciones de Eva DJ. No faltaron el recorrido por el nuevo local, el picoteo hecho a mano en comida y bebida, y sobre todo las ganas de llenar de vida esta nueva casa para la rebeldía y la defensa frente a empresaurios y politicastros de todos nuestros derechos actuales y los que nos inventemos en el futuro. Para todo ello y más, contad con CNT, vuestra herramienta de lucha, vuestro sindicato de clase, vuestra alternativa sindical.

Porque si el sistema utiliza esas diferencias para dividirnos y para colocar a unas personas en posiciones de mayor vulnerabilidad, el sindicalismo tiene que hacer justamente lo contrario:

reconocernos como parte de una misma clase y organizarnos juntas.


Por eso abrimos este espacio.


Para que haya más gente, más organización y más lucha.


Porque somos CNT.


CNT tiene una historia profundamente ligada a la organización de la clase trabajadora y a la lucha por los derechos laborales y sociales.


Antes que este local, CNT tuvo varios, cada uno con su historia: desahucios, asaltos policiales, atentados… Desde la calle Francisco Zarandona multiplicó por diez su afiliación en tiempos de la segunda republica; desde los pactos de la moncloa, superando multiples dificultades, hemos crecido en varios locales en Valladolid que han ido abriendo cada vez más brecha en la provincia y en la ciudad. Hasta llegar a este en el que nos encontramos

Tenemos una memoria sindical fuerte y combativa. Pero no queremos convertir esa memoria en una fotografía, ni mirar hacia atrás únicamente para recordar lo que fuimos.

Nuestra memoria nos obliga a mirar hacia delante.

lucha antifascista

L'attentat raciste du 23 octobre, qui a tué Pengo Bossio Wangi et blessé cinq autres personnes dont une enfant de 12 ans, on aurait pu le prévoir, et on aurait dû l'empêcher. Malgré la violence et le harcèlement auxquels leurs luttes les exposent, c'est contre une telle actualisation de la violence raciste que se mobilisent chaque jour les militant.es antiracistes. Par son abjection monstrueuse, l'assassinat déchire la réalité mais il n'est pas moins le produit de cette réalité, et de tout ce qui en elle relève, jusque dans l'apparente normalité des discours quotidiens, de la mécanique organisée du racisme.


Que le racisme soit en cours d'intensification en France, et qu'il tue, on le savait. Que tous les discours, politiques, intellectuels, médiatiques, qui relativisent ou nient l'existence du racisme - allant même jusqu'à remettre en question le terme d'

islamophobie

 - partagent la responsabilité dans cet assassinat, on le sait. On savait aussi que le racisme ne s'arrête pas aux portes de l'extrême droite, qu'il structure le

contrat racial

, non seulement comme un crime originel, mais comme une domination perpétuée et amplifiée par des discours qui sursaturent l'espace public et social, des négligences organisées, des lois, telles que la proposition de destitution de la nationalité (inextirpable d'un ancrage fasciste), ou par les différentes juridictions qui étendent la laïcité pour en faire un régime de disciplinarisation raciale. Que ce soit à Trappes, précisément dans la ville qui n'a cessé d'être visée par l'extrême droite, que l'assassinat raciste ait été perpétré, expose on ne plus clairement que le racisme fonctionne comme une chaîne de concaténation entre les discours qui désignent une population, l'assignent à une sauvagerie extérieure à la politique, au monde commun, à l'humanité même, et le passage à l'acte. L'extension de la brutalité policière et étatique prend également une autre forme. Depuis au moins les répressions contre les Gilets jaunes, les « forces de l'ordre » étendent leur capacité à violenter les corps pour exposer un peu plus clairement à chaque mouvement social la violence meurtrière qui les fonde, et que le gouvernement a encore confirmée et explicitée par la proposition, cette année, d'une loi sur « la présomption de légitime défense pour les forces de l'ordre », c'est-à-dire d'un

droit de tuer

 (adopté par l'Assemblée nationale, et en cours d'examen au Sénat).


Ainsi, la violence aujourd'hui en France, c'est les vies tuées, les mains arrachées, les yeux explosés, les gaz contre la foule rassemblée, les nasses, les gardes à vue

La violence, ce sont toutes les raisons éminemment politiques qui ont mené les gens dans les rues : lycéen.nes, étudiant.es, gilets jaunes, parents, minorités, précaires, retraité.es, militant.es. Parce que la violence, c'est que dans ce régime capitaliste, hier mais spécifiquement aujourd'hui, la vie bonne n'est pas possible.


La violence, aujourd'hui, c'est que Pengo Bossio Wangi n'est …

author: Elliot Downes
title: NT government closes Darwin’s largest homelessness shelter
content:
Residents of Darwin’s largest homelessness shelter were evicted by the Northern Territory government on 12 October, and relocated to Batchelor, a town 100 kilometres away.

Yilli Short Stay Accommodation (YiSSA), which is run by Yilli Rreung Housing Aboriginal Corporation, was home to hundreds of people, mostly Aboriginal. Many have experienced domestic violence and are living with serious health conditions, including kidney conditions requiring dialysis. 

Residents from communities across the territory would stay at YiSSA while accessing medical care or other services in Darwin. Nearly 400 people were directly affected by the closure of the facility, including 160 children.

YiSSA’s closure will place more pressure on remaining homelessness services in Darwin. Meanwhile, the minority of residents transferred to the smaller facility in Batchelor will not have the same access to support networks, food, healthcare and education. Batchelor is a town with a population of around 500, a small health clinic and no public transport. 

The closure of a key homelessness service is particularly egregious given the Northern Territory has the highest rate of homelessness in the country. According to data released last year by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, 

one in every 25 Territorians requires homelessness assistance

, and Aboriginal people make up 89 percent of those accessing homelessness services in the Northern Territory.

As the biggest landlord in the territory, the Northern Territory government is largely to blame for this situation. Territorians on the emergency public housing waiting list can expect to 

wait up to a decade for a roof over their head

. The government is also responsible for the apartheid-like conditions in Aboriginal town camps on the outskirts of places like Darwin and Alice Springs, as well as the overcrowding in remote communities.

The closure of YiSSA was announced by the ruling Country Liberal Party (CLP) in July. Ostensibly, it was due to a failure to secure a deal with Ausco, the owner of the buildings and other infrastructure on the Crown land site. But in reality, it was a political decision. 

After years of renting the demountable buildings, the government offered to buy them for $3 million—the equivalent of just one year’s rent. When this offer was rejected by Ausco, the federal government proposed to cover the cost of the purchase on the condition that Yilli Rreung continue running the service.

The CLP rejected the offer of federal funding, with Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro calling it a 

“waste of taxpayers’ hard-earned money”

. Yet it has cost 

$16.25 million to establish and fund the Batchelor facility

, run by Mission Australia.

The announcement of YiSSA’s closure sparked a campaign by the activist group, Justice Not Jails (JNJ). It culminated in a 200-strong rally outside of the Australian Homelessness Conference in Darwin just days before residents were to be evicted. 

Anna, an activist with JNJ, told 

Red Flag

 that the decision doesn’t make sense “unless you approach it from an ideological viewpoint. Some of the YiSSA residents have said that [the government] just don’t want Aboriginal people to have a nice, secure place to live.”

The YiSSA closure is symptomatic of a Trumpian government that has targeted Aboriginal people in particular. Since coming to power in 2024, the CLP have lowered the age of criminal responsibility to 10, reintroduced spit hoods in detention, and made it easier for Aboriginal children to be removed from their families and placed into long-term state care.

This has involved a significant expansion in the carceral state, with the prison population 

increasing by 24 percent between 2024 and 2025

, and the Finocchiaro government announcing earlier this year the construction of a new private prison in Darwin. 

The Northern Territory is one of the most incarcerated places in the world, 

second only to El Salvador

, with more than 1 percent of the entire population behind bars. Increasingly, this includes people on remand, who are awaiting trial or sentencing.

According to Anna, the next phase of the campaign will involve putting pressure on the federal Labor government. “There’s been a lot of disagreement between the CLP and Labor about what was actually promised. It’s all really immature and I think disrespectful to the people whose lives are actually being affected,” she told 

Red Flag.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Suggests Ilhan Omar, a US Citizen, Doesn’t Have Constitutional Rights
content:
“She goes, ‘I have constitutional rights.’ The arrogance,” Trump said at a rally in Texas.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

President Donald Trump suggested that Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota), a U.S. citizen, should not have constitutional rights because of where she’s from in racist remarks at a rally this week.

“She was from Somalia and she came over and right away she started opening her mouth, ‘I have constitutional rights,’” Trump said mockingly, in the middle of a three-and-a-half minute rant about Omar in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday night. “She comes from a country with no government, no counsel, no police, no anything. It’s not even a country. It’s just a piece of land.”

“She goes, ‘I have constitutional rights.’ The arrogance,” Trump said. He then transitioned into making Islamophobic comments about Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

Trump has consistently targeted Omar with racist remarks, and has previously called Somalia a “garbage country.”

Trump’s comments on Tuesday suggest that he believes Omar should not be afforded basic rights laid out in the U.S. Constitution, like freedom of speech and religion or the right to a fair trial. Notably, these protections are supposed to apply to everyone within the United States, not just citizens.

Trump has repeatedly remarked on Omar’s right to constitutional protections. He has said some iteration of these comments at many rallies this midterm cycle — including just after Homeland Security Investigations’ pre-dawn raid on her house earlier this month. However, Tuesday’s version is the clearest he’s been about suggesting that Omar doesn’t deserve such rights.

The president’s rant comes as his administration is attempting to denaturalize and deport Omar — part of a mass deportation campaign that critics say has already drastically eroded or is directly violating numerous constitutional liberties.

This is a remarkable rebuke of the Constitution coming from the leader of the party that is attacking people like Omar and El-Sayed as un-American.

Indeed, Republicans in Congress and in Trump’s orbit have repeatedly made comments suggesting that only Christians should be allowed to be in Congress, and that Muslims specifically should be barred from holding office.

At a rally in Ohio on Wednesday night, for instance, Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) said that El-Sayed, who was born in Michigan, is an “affront to me as a naturalized citizen of this country” and “can be nowhere near D.C.” His reasoning was that El-Sayed doesn’t understand “that our rights come from God Almighty” and that “Jesus came here for our salvation.”

The GOP’s racist and Islamophobic remarks have become increasingly incendiary as the election has neared. On Wednesday, Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) said that, if El-Sayed were to gain access to classified information, “there is a very real risk that Americans will die as a result” — a remark that critics noted was open incitement to violence.

Just days before the raid on Omar’s house, Trump called for a race war against Somalis in Omar’s home state of Minnesota. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said “The people of Minnesota must fight back” against Somali immigrants in the state.

title: Eskişehir’de göçmen ve mülteci işçiler güvencesizliğe mahkûm ediliyor
content:
Berivan Özkara [email protected]

Eskişehir’de tarımdan hayvancılığa, sanayiden otomotiv atölyelerine, ev içi bakım işlerinden farklı hizmet alanlarına kadar pek çok sektörde göçmen ve mülteci işçiler çalışıyor. Düşük ücret, sigortasız çalışma, ödenmeyen alacaklar, işten çıkarılma ya da sınır dışı edilme korkusu, göçmen ve mülteci işçilerin karşı karşıya kaldığı başlıca sorunlar arasında. Patronlar, göçmenlerin güvencesiz koşullarını emek maliyetini azaltmanın bir aracı olarak kullanıyor. Avukat Şahap Arpacı ile Eskişehir’deki örnekler üzerinden göçmen ve mülteci işçilerin çalışma koşullarını, yaşadıkları hak ihlallerini ve bu tablonun işçi sınıfının bütünü açısından ne anlama geldiğini konuştuk.

Eskişehir’de mülteci işçilerin yoğun olarak çalıştığı alanların başında tarım ve hayvancılık geliyor. Özellikle kırsal bölgelerde mevsimlik işlerde çalışan Afgan ve Suriyeli işçiler, ağır çalışma koşullarına ve düşük ücretlere rağmen geçimlerini sağlamaya çalışıyor. Alpu, Beylikova, İnönü, Mihalıççık ve Seyitgazi çevresindeki tarımsal üretimde mülteci emeğinin yaygın biçimde kullanıldığını belirten Şahap Arpacı, “Eskişehir’in köylerinde tarımla uğraşacak bir genç nüfus kalmadığı için bu bölümü Afganlar ve Suriyeliler doldurdu. Şu anda patates sökeceksek, domates toplayacaksak, pancar sökeceksek Eskişehir köylerinde bu işi büyük oranda Afganlar ve Suriyeliler yapıyor” diyor.

Bu işlerde çalışan mülteci işçiler, yerli işçilere kıyasla çok daha düşük ücretlerle çalıştırılabiliyor. Arpacı, kayıt dışılığın iş kazası ve hastalık durumlarında da işçileri savunmasız bıraktığını vurguluyor: “Herhangi bir iş kazası geçirmeleri halinde, bu tarlada da olabilir fabrikada da olabilir, hastaneye, adliyeye gidip hukuki anlamda başvurabilecek bir mekanizmadan da yoksunlar.”

Eskişehir’de mülteci işçilerin çalıştığı bir diğer alan sanayi. Avukat Şahap Arpacı, Teksan ve Baksan Sanayi Sitelerinde, otomotiv tamirhanelerinde, boya ve mobilya sektöründe çalışan Iraklı ve Suriyeli işçiler bulunduğunu; organize sanayi bölgesinde ana fabrikalara üretim yapan yan sanayi işletmelerinde de mülteci emeğinin kullanıldığını anlattı.

Bu alanlarda da kayıt dışılık, düşük ücret ve güvencesizlik öne çıkıyor. Göçmen ve mülteci işçilerin çalışma izinlerinin ya da sigorta kayıtlarının bulunmaması, ücret alacaklarını kanıtlamalarını da zorlaştırıyor. Arpacı, işçilerin aylarca ücret alamadığı durumlarla karşılaştıklarını belirterek, kayıt dışı çalışmanın hukuki süreçlerde yarattığı güçlüğü şöyle anlatıyor:

“En büyük sorunlardan bir tanesi, çok düşük ücretlere çalışmış olmalarına rağmen maaşlarını zamanında alamamaları. Sigorta girişleri yok, çalışma izinleri yok. Hangi hukuki yolla alamadığı üç aylık maaşı alacak? Avukat tutsa, iş mahkemesine, ara bulucuya başvuracak olsa bunu kanıtlayamayacağız. İş mahkemeleri SGK girişine ve çalışma izinlerine bakıyor.”

Patron ücreti eksik ödendiğinde ya da ödemeyi geciktirdiğinde işçi işten çıkarılma tehdidiyle karşılaşabiliyor. Mülteci ve göçmen işçiler bakımından bu baskıya, sınır dışı edilme korkusu da ekleniyor. İşçilerin çalışma ve oturma durumlarına ilişkin belirsizlikler, patronların elini güçlendirirken işçinin emeğinin karşılığını istemesini dahi zorlaştırıyor. Böylece ücretin ödenmemesi yalnızca iş yeri içinde yaşanan bir sorun olarak kalmıyor; işçinin ülkede kalma ve yaşamını sürdürme kaygısıyla birleşerek daha ağır bir baskıya dönüşüyor.

Arpacı’nın aktardığı Filistinli bir işçinin yaşadıkları, bu baskının nasıl işlediğini gösteriyor. Boya ve kimyasallarla çalıştığı iş yerinde işçinin fazla mesai ve diğer ücret alacaklarıyla birlikte 200 bin liranın üzerinde alacağı olduğunu belirten Arpacı, bu alacağın tahsili için hukuki sürecin başlatılmak istendiğini ancak patronun diğer işçileri tehdit ederek tanıklığı engellediğini anlattı:

“Şahit var; kendisi gibi Iraklı, Filistinli birçok işçi var, aynı problemleri yaşıyorlar. Ama hepsi bırakın şahitlik yapmayı, korktukları için müvekkilimizin telefonlarına çıkmamaya başladı. İşveren, ‘Sizi deport ederim, sizi göç idaresine şikayet ederim’ diyerek işçileri korkutuyor. Göç idaresinde tanıdıkları olduğunu söylüyor. Böyle bir şey olmasa bile ‘Göç idaresi müdürü benim akrabam, orada çalışan memur benim amcamın oğlu’ diyerek işçi üzerinde idari, işveren kaynaklı ve sosyal bir baskı kuruyor.” Arpacı, işçinin alacağının sonunda çok daha düşük bir tutar üzerinden anlaşmaya bağlandığını dile getirdi: “Biz en son 200 küsur bin liralık alacaktan vazgeçtik. Ara bulucuda 80 bin …

author: Unknown
title: Turkish soldiers torture three women from Rojava at the border
content:
Turkish soldiers reportedly detained and assaulted three women at the border between Rojava and Northern Kurdistan, confiscating their money and personal belongings. According to the ANHA news agency, the incident occurred near the village of Qereman in Dirbêsiyê as the women attempted to cross the border from Rojava into Northern Kurdistan.


According to ANHA, the three women were stopped and tortured by Turkish border guards. No information is currently available about their whereabouts or state of health. No further details about the incident have been released so far.


Reports of mistreatment, violent pushbacks, and assaults by Turkish border forces continue to emerge along the Turkish-Syrian border. Human rights organizations have documented cases for years in which people attempting to cross the border have been beaten, shot at, or robbed of their personal belongings. Those particularly affected are people trying to cross the border due to war, persecution, or economic hardship.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: 98 Percent of Trump’s Refugee Admissions Have Been White South Africans
content:
The openly white supremacist policy is poised to continue through 2027, the administration has said.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The Trump administration is blocking admissions for nearly every type of refugee — except for white South Africans, who make up nearly all of those admitted under President Donald Trump’s second term so far, data shows.

According to State Department data compiled by economist Steve Rattner, white South Africans make up 98 percent of refugee admissions between February 2025 and July 2026. Of 10,764 refugees admitted in that time, 10,597 originated from South Africa, while only 167 were from other countries.

Most of those from other countries were approved prior to Trump’s executive order last year to prioritize admissions of Afrikaners, per Rattner. Trump and his allies falsely claim the group is being subject to persecution and “white genocide,” which has been repeatedly debunked by experts. In fact, Afrikaners are largely faring fine in the country, owning the vast majority of land in South Africa despite making up only roughly 7 percent of the population.

The State Department’s raw data is even more stark. According to the State Department’s Bureau of Population, Refugees, and Migration, only five refugees out of 16,292 total arrived from Afghanistan, while South Africans made up the remainder in fiscal year 2026, which ranges from October 2025 to September 2026.

Meanwhile, Trump is barring admissions from nearly every other country. Trump capped refugee admissions for fiscal year 2026 at 17,500, near record lows that were previously set during his first term.

By contrast, as Rattner noted, 100,034 refugees were admitted in fiscal year 2024 under President Joe Biden. Roughly a third were from Africa, while 30 percent were from the Near East or South Asia, and another 25 percent were from Latin America or the Caribbean.

The Trump administration is poised to continue this openly white supremacist policy next year. The administration notified Congress last month that it is intending to cap refugee admissions to 17,500 once again in 2027, limited to mostly white South Africans. The notification says that white South Africans are facing land seizures and persecution, while noting that they would be likely to assimilate in the U.S.

The policy comes as the Trump administration has openly embraced racist rhetoric and carried out a mass deportation campaign in which immigration agents are racially profiling their targets. Those originating from Latin American countries have been targeted the most with deportation orders in fiscal year 2026.

Last month, the White House bragged in a post on X that it had cut legal immigration and refugee admissions from majority-Muslim countries by 96 percent between December 2024 and February 2026. Meanwhile, Republicans and Trump administration officials have openly and repeatedly spewed vile Islamophobic rhetoric, including against Somali Muslim Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota), who the administration is reportedly attempting to denaturalize and deport.

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

author: By Dan Feidt, Unicorn Riot
title: ‘Icepick’ Leak Exposes Thousands of Homeland Security Personnel, Groups and More
content:
Washington, DC — There’s been yet another major security breach among federal agencies. The Department of Homeland Security’s ‘single sign-on’ (SSO) login system was reportedly subverted by a hacker going by “Department of Peace” (DoP), which has revealed thousands upon thousands of federal employee records. Around one-fifth of Homeland Security’s personnel have been exposed. Offices and locations are identified in great detail, from Canadian airports to agents in U.S. embassies around the world. Groups assigned within the SSO system, going back at least to 2011, are also exposed, showing the names of globe-spanning activities, and management personnel handling undercover operations.


Thousands of personnel records include supervisors and subordinates, which enabled generating gigantic organizational charts automatically across these agencies. Combine this with the groups (some officials tagged in dozens) and one can easily browse around the highest levels of activities, including thousands of groups dealing with surveillance, special operations, finance, social media, and much, much more. Additional

updates are at the end of this post

author: Wini Omer
title: It’s not the refugees, it’s the austerity measures!
content:
A Sudanese journalist, with whom I worked for two years at the same newspaper, told me when I contacted him to check on his situation after the last wave of attacks against refugees in Libya: “We are trapped in our homes. We can’t leave. I didn’t send my kids to school since the beginning of this wave of violence. The situation is difficult beyond imagination.”

The Sudanese who left Sudan seeking refuge in Libya, amid very violent clashes that started in April 2023 and continue to this moment, are facing violence, danger, and hatred in what was supposed to be a safe refuge. But this reality is not exclusive to Sudanese refugees, and the violence is indifferent to other nationalities who are fleeing conflicts, war, and instability at home: Ethiopians, Eritreans, and refugees from the Central African Republic.

In Libya, African refugees faced waves of violence, the latest in June this year. Despite competing for power, Libya’s rival authorities in the east and west have united in stoking anti-migrant rhetoric and launching a violent campaign of mass detention and expulsions against migrants and refugees, as a recent

Human Rights Watch report

 has indicated.

In Egypt, a

crackdown campaign

 led by security forces, accompanied by social media hate speech against Sudanese and Syrian refugees, intensified on the ground, blaming them for the rise in living costs, mainly rents, groceries, and basic life needs. As a result of systematic brutality, between January and June 2026,

12 Sudanese passed away in Egyptian detention centers

 and police cells, including a child of 17. Refugees processed for deportation are forced to sign voluntary return declarations.

Sudan hosts one of the largest refugee and asylum-seeker populations in Africa, mainly South Sudanese, Ethiopians, and Eritreans, who currently face detention and

forced deportation

 from the capital, Khartoum, to refugee camps close to the borders with their countries of origin, after the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) regained control of the capital. This step was taken following a growing political rhetoric that profiled them as criminals and blamed them for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) controlling Khartoum. Accordingly, they were deported to refugee camps in White Nile State, Al-Gadarif State, and Kassala State, camps that lack all basic human needs and restrict freedom of movement and the right to work. Many South Sudanese mothers were deported while their children were not allowed to accompany them, leaving them in limbo.

Such rhetoric, mainly produced and shared by pro-SAF individuals and platforms, provides the military establishment with a popular cover to reproduce its symbolic authority. It is also used by some actors within the army as a tool to bolster its legitimacy against the Rapid Support Forces, portraying it as the guardian of national sovereignty and the representative of the “authentic Sudanese” against the “foreign threat.” This reflects a deeper attempt to regain control over the state and society at a moment of total collapse of political and legal frameworks.

For many of these refugees, especially the Eritreans, returning is not an option, considering the human rights situation in Eritrea. But according to media reports, both Eritrea and Sudan are

complicit in the repatriation of civilians from Sudan

 back to Eritrea.

Whether it is the systematic violence against Sudanese refugees on the continent, or the deliberate violence against African refugees in Sudan, these incidents reflect one broader reality in which violence is used and reproduced either by state actors or by the citizens of the host countries to whom the refugees sought safety within the African continent. This reality raises a critical question about how to understand such incidents, the politics behind them, and why we are seeing them now.

Shifting the blame

Have the refugees led to the economic crises in Egypt, Libya, or Tunisia? Or are these crises a direct result of the state’s social and economic policies?

In Egypt, the last ten years have witnessed a high level of dependence on debt; Egypt has become one of the IMF’s largest borrowers, while social expenditure, including social protection, health, and education, has shrunk, accompanied by political oppression. Those debts have been invested in projects lacking a developmental dimension, such as

the new administrative capital

 project, which is expected to cost up to $300 billion by the time it’s finalized …

author: Amina Khan
title: EU transforms Frontex into a high-tech deportation command centre
content:
Yesterday, 27 October 2026, the European Commission tabled a new Regulation for Frontex, the EU’s border agency, expanding its powers and refocusing its mandate on deportations, preventing arrivals, and surveillance beyond EU territories and into social media. This would effectively turn Frontex into the EU’s deportation agency, equivalent of ICE in the United States.

At the centre of this reform is a budget that would almost double to nearly €12 billion for 2028–2034, leading to a massive expansion of the EU security and surveillance industrial complex. Frontex will test and deploy new technology to repress migrants, funnelling billions of taxpayer money to surveillance, security and defence contractors. EU’s hostile border security regime has for years produced systemic and massive human rights violations of migrants, refugees and racialised people, and those who stand in solidarity with them. This proposal will accelerate that.

Frontex as an ICE-style deportation enforcement agency

The proposal operationalises the recently adopted Deportations Regulation and deepens Frontex’s position as the central actor of a Europe-wide deportation machine. This will make the agency responsible for collecting and analysing data from Member States in order to “predict” deportation needs, and allocating resources to them. Frontex will now have a “Deportation Coordination Centre” that is expected to act at all stages of the deportation procedure, from detecting and identifying people that may be expulsed, booking or arranging flights and escorts, to monitoring their “reintegration” in the destination country.

Alarmingly, it expands Frontex’s powers to deport outside of the EU’s borders. Based on a simple status agreement, Frontex will be able to deport people from one third country to another, with the aim of preventing people from even reaching the EU. This will likely mean sharing sensitive data with third countries and countries of origin, where individuals may be at risk of persecution or harm.

The Frontex mandate reform comes in a package with a proposal to digitalise the management of deportation cases. The border control agency is given a key role in the harmonised technical design of EU and national digital systems, to exchange data on deportations, including sensitive data transfers to third countries (biometric data, travel documents and history, grounds for deportation, health data, etc.), and automate certain steps of the procedure, such as adding deportation orders in the Schengen Information System (SIS) to detect people.

Increased data processing and content policing

With this reform, Frontex’s practice of “debriefing interviews” is codified, particularly during the screening procedure introduced by the Migration Pact. The agency conducts these covert “voluntary” interrogations of people immediately after they disembark or cross the border. During these interviews, the agency extracts data from migrants deemed to be “suspects” of “cross-border crime”, without the possibility for migrants to seek legal counsel. Debriefing interviews have been rightfully criticised for their absence of fundamental rights monitoring and their unfairness as they take place when a person is detained and lacks privacy.

A new “Online Monitoring and Response Centre” will also surveil social media platforms to identify “suspicious behaviours or trends” in people’s movements at the EU borders, and before that, in the countries of origin and transit. Aggregated data collected online will be fed into Frontex’s “risk analysis” to guide border forces’ deployment and reaction. Social media monitoring was already declared as carrying high-risk for violating the fundamental rights of people affected, and was banned by the European Data Protection Supervisor in 2019 when first implemented by the EU Agency for Asylum.

Frontex will also seek designation as a trusted flagger under the Digital Services Act (DSA), allowing the agency to report pieces of online content to platforms for removal, effectively giving the agency extrajudicial powers to police the internet. It may also recommend national authorities to issue binding take-down notices. Frontex depriving people from finding legal support, sharing their stories or expressing solidarity is undoubtedly a serious infringement of freedom of expression.

All information collected during debriefings and online monitoring activities will contribute to Frontex’s border surveillance intelligence …

author: TGEU
title: Join the HIV Awareness Week in Berlin to establish the Emergency Support Network
content:
We are organising two free-of-charge parallel training programmes for queer and trans people that will come together on Friday, 20 November, to establish the Emergency Support Network.


This network should help people navigate services, identify realistic pathways to HIV prevention and care, and receive support without having to navigate complex systems alone. We also want to recognise that Ballroom houses, queer and trans collectives, and migrant communities already provide essential care infrastructure. We intend to strengthen these existing relationships, rather than create a parallel system disconnected from the communities themselves.


The initiative is particularly focused on two target audience groups:


Queer and trans people living with HIV who face barriers to accessing healthcare, especially those without health insurance, appropriate documentation, or access to HIV treatment and other essential services.


Queer and trans people on the move, including migrants, refugees, asylum seekers and undocumented people, who face difficulties accessing healthcare, HIV prevention, testing, PrEP, PEP and treatment.


Community HIV Training — 16, 18 and 20 November


This programme is intended for queer and trans adults, particularly queer and trans youth aged 18 and over, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, undocumented people and other people on the move.


It is especially relevant to queer and trans people who are living with HIV and face difficulties accessing treatment or healthcare, as well as those who need access to HIV prevention, testing, PrEP, PEP and other sexual health services.


The sessions will be interactive and community-led, covering HIV prevention and care, PrEP, PEP, testing, treatment, U=U, sexual health, pleasure, harm reduction and navigating healthcare systems.


An important feature is that registration for this programme is anonymous.

 Participants are not asked to provide their names, email addresses or HIV status. Anyone who wants to receive practical information or reminders can voluntarily register their email address through a separate form, which is not linked to their anonymous demographic responses.


This distinction is particularly important for people who may be reluctant to engage with services or activities because of concerns about confidentiality, stigma or their migration status.


register here


Health Champions Training — 17, 19 and 20 November


This programme is designed for trans and queer community leaders, particularly people involved in Ballroom houses, collectives and grassroots networks.


The training follows a train-the-trainer approach and will cover HIV, STIs and other infectious diseases prevention, treatment and sexual and reproductive health knowledge, and other topics like U=U, harm reduction, structural barriers to healthcare, peer education and safe healthcare navigation.


Participants will work through practical exercises such as community mapping, HIV knowledge games, real-life scenarios, role-play and referral mapping. The objective is to equip them to become trusted points of connection between their communities and healthcare services, while recognising that Health Champions are not expected to act as clinicians, legal experts or crisis responders.


On the final day, Health Champions will meet healthcare professionals, service providers and participants from the other training programme to help establish practical referral pathways and community-based support structures.


register here


Building the Emergency Support Network

—


20 November


On Friday, participants from both programmes will come together with healthcare professionals, community organisations and service providers.


The aim is to establish direct connections between people who need support, trusted community leaders and organisations capable of providing services. Participants will learn what support is available, who can access it, what barriers remain and how to make safe referrals.


The week will culminate in

Under the Jellicle Moon Kiki Ball on Saturday, 21 November

, celebrating Ballroom culture, community leadership and the relationships developed throughout the initiative.


Note:

All workshop participants must be 18 or older and attend all three days of their respective training. Snacks and dinner will be provided each day.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Denunciaron ante la CIDH la política migratoria de Milei: restricciones para pobres y privilegios para el poder económico
content:
La Comisión Argentina para personas Refugiadas y Migrantes (CAREF), la Red Nacional de Migrantes y Refugiados, el Movimiento de Trabajadores Excluidos (MTE/UTEP) y el Centro de Estudios Legales y Sociales (CELS) expusieron ante la la Comisión Interamericana de Derechos Humanos (CIDH) sobre las reformas migratorias impulsadas por el gobierno argentino de ultraderecha, que dificultan la regularización, aumentan las restricciones y estigmatizan a migrantes pobres, mientras habilita mecanismos extraordinarios de naturalización para el poder económico buscando facilitar la extranjerización de la tierra y los bienes comunes.


Compartimos el comunicado del CELS:


Política migratoria: la Argentina ante la CIDH


CAREF, la Red Nacional de Migrantes y Refugiados, el MTE/UTEP y el CELS expusimos ante la CIDH sobre las reformas migratorias impulsadas por el gobierno argentino. Advertimos sobre las dificultades para la regularización, las restricciones para acceder a la salud -mujeres embarazadas sin atención, niñas, niños y adolescentes con atención discontinua- y una política de control migratorio estigmatizante.


Hoy participamos del 197° Período de Sesiones de la Comisión Interamericana de Derechos Humanos (CIDH) en una audiencia sobre el impacto de las reformas en las políticas de regularización, acceso a la salud y control migratorio en la Argentina. CAREF, la Red Nacional de Migrantes y Refugiados, el MTE/UTEP y el CELS expusimos sobre las consecuencias de una serie de reformas que están desarticulando una política migratoria construida durante más de veinte años basada en el reconocimiento de la migración como un derecho humano. Desde 2024, y especialmente a partir del DNU 366/2025, el Gobierno dificultó el acceso a la residencia regular, restringió derechos, modificó las condiciones de expulsión y trasladó la gestión migratoria y de protección de refugiados a la órbita del Ministerio de Seguridad. Estas medidas fueron adoptadas sin debate en el Congreso y acompañadas por un discurso oficial que asocia la migración con la inseguridad y la criminalidad.


Uno de los principales efectos de las reformas que denunciamos ante las y los comisionados es que la regularización se volvió más difícil para quienes tienen menos recursos. El DNU 366 incorporó como requisito para acceder a la residencia permanente -y renovar la temporaria- la acreditación de medios económicos suficientes, mediante formas de prueba vinculadas fundamentalmente al trabajo registrado. Desde su entrada en vigencia, las residencias permanentes otorgadas cayeron de 24 mil a 8 mil por semestre. Al mismo tiempo, se eliminó el acceso a la residencia permanente que correspondía por tener hijos, hijas o cónyuges argentinos. El resultado es que miles de personas con trabajo, familia y años de arraigo en el país pueden ser empujadas a la irregularidad. Mientras se endurecen estas condiciones, el Gobierno habilita mecanismos extraordinarios de naturalización para quienes realizan grandes inversiones: una política migratoria cada vez más restrictiva para los sectores de menores ingresos y privilegiada para quienes tienen recursos económicos.


Las organizaciones también advertimos sobre las consecuencias que este proceso ya tiene en el acceso a la salud, al trabajo y a otros derechos básicos. El DNU 366 dejó de garantizar el acceso gratuito al sistema público nacional de salud -excepto en emergencias- para quienes no tengan residencia permanente. Pudimos registrar interrupciones de tratamientos y estudios, solicitantes de asilo que no fueron atendidos, mujeres embarazadas sin atención oportuna y niñas, niños y adolescentes con atención discontinua. La irregularidad migratoria repercute además sobre el trabajo: quienes integran la economía popular difícilmente pueden acreditar ingresos mediante un recibo de sueldo y, sin DNI, encuentran todavía más obstáculos para ingresar al trabajo registrado y ejercer otros derechos.


Este retroceso se combina con una política de control y hostigamiento sobre la población migrante. La Red Nacional de Migrantes y Refugiados denunció controles de identidad, requisas y demoras arbitrarias que afectan especialmente a personas de piel morena, con rasgos indígenas o afrodescendientes. Desde la UTEP se señaló que los llamados operativos de “control poblacional”, realizados junto con fuerzas federales y la Dirección Nacional de Migraciones, se concentran en espacios del comercio informal donde trabajan numerosos vendedores ambulantes …

author: Ben Smoke
title: Home Secretary Refuses to Meet Worker Affected by Her ‘Nasty’ Immigration Plans
content:
Home secretary Shabana Mahmood has refused to meet with a migrant care worker who will be affected by her rightwing immigration reforms.


Mahmood was asked to meet the worker as part of a discussion with Unison boss Andrea Egan about plans to make migrants wait up to 15 years to apply for indefinite leave to remain,

the i Paper reported

. 


But the home secretary refused Egan’s request and the meeting, which is part of

a charm offensive by Mahmood

 to stave off a growing rebellion against her reforms, was cancelled.


Unison is officially affiliated with the Labour party and has been at the forefront of opposition to Mahmood’s plans. Egan, who was expelled from Labour amid a purge of leftwing members in 2022, has described the reforms as “dehumanising”. 


Egan

said on X

 on Wednesday: “Shabana Mahmood’s failure to engage with the migrant workers whose lives her nasty proposals will devastate is totally unacceptable. These are brilliant, committed workers who hold our public services together. Unison won’t tolerate them being attacked and ignored.” 


The Home Office

told the i Paper

 the meeting was a private one-on-one talk between Mahmood and Egan that Unison had chosen to cancel.


Former shadow chancellor John McDonnell urged Mahmood to “think again on this decision not to meet” the worker. Writing on

X

, he said “the work visa issue is causing totally unnecessary division in the Labour party.”


In an interview with

 Sky News

 on Thursday, energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh refused five times to back Mahmood’s policy of making people wait 15 years for permanent residency. 


In a now deleted social media post earlier this week,

Fahnbulleh hit out

 at “any attempt to prolong the time people have to wait for settlement.”


In March this year whilst not a member of cabinet, Angela Rayner referred to the reforms as

“un-British”

. She

has since

 attempted to downplay reports of a cabinet split over the policy. 


The government

has delayed

 its official announcement of the policy, the Critic reported, and says it is “considering responses” to a public consultation that closed in February.

title: Αύριο θα είναι η δική σου σειρά… Όταν ο καπιταλισμός κατασκοπεύει (Β’ Μέρος)
content:
Του Ν’ Γκουζότο


Εικοσιτρία χρόνια πριν γίνεται μια δημόσια συζήτηση, στην Ομοσπονδιακή Επιτροπή Εμπορίου των ΗΠΑ, σχετικά με την ανάγκη νομοθέτησης, για την ιδιωτικότητα των πολιτών. Είναι δύο ομάδες που συγκρούονται, μπροστά στα μέλη της επιτροπής που καλούνται να αποφασίσουν, αν θα μπουν κανόνες που θα ορίζουν τι αποτελεί παραβίαση της ιδιωτικότητας. Από την μια μεριά τα στελέχη της τεχνολογικής βιομηχανίας υποστηρίζουν ότι είναι απόλυτα ικανοί να ρυθμίσουν τα πάντα κι ότι κάθε κυβερνητική παρέμβαση θα ήταν εκτός από δαπανηρή και αντιπαραγωγική. Από την άλλη μεριά οι φιλελεύθεροι υποστηρικτές των πολιτικών ελευθεριών ωρύονται προειδοποιώντας ότι, οι δυνατότητες συλλογής και επεξεργασίας προσωπικών δεδομένων από την πλευρά των εταιρειών, αποτελούν μια πρωτοφανή απειλή για τις ατομικές ελευθερίες. Ζητούσαν από την επιτροπή να αποφασίσει

τι συνιστούν τα ανθρώπινα πλάσματα στην νέα ηλεκτρονική εποχή.

 Αν υπάρχει κάποιο όριο ή απλά θεωρούνται σαν δωρεάν πρώτη ύλη για το εμπόριο; Τότε ένα επίτροπος

αναρωτήθηκε

 που πρέπει να τεθεί αυτό το όριο;


Όπως εύκολα γίνεται κατανοητό, διανύοντας την χρυσή δεκαετία του νεοφιλελεύθερου καπιταλισμού όπου η αγορά αυτορυθμίζεται, το όριο που ζητούσαν οι πάντες ποτέ δεν μπήκε.


Η αγορά κέρδισε και έβαλε τα θεμέλια της ανάπτυξης μιας νέας οικονομικής λογικής, την οποία η

 Shoshana Zyboff

, την ονομάτισε

κατασκοπευτικό καπιταλισμό.


Η επιτυχία του βασίζεται στη δημιουργία σχέσεων με την μορφή ενός μονόδρομου καθρέφτη, οι τζαμάδες τους αποκαλούν και spyglass, όπου ενώ παρακολουθείσαι, εν αγνοία σου βαφτίζεσαι σε μια κολυμπήθρα μετα-αλήθειας. Κατόρθωσε να ριζώσει και να ευδοκιμήσει στο διαδίκτυο – που οριζόταν σαν ο μεγαλύτερος ακυβέρνητος χώρος στον κόσμο, και να το ελέγξει απόλυτα.


Όταν πρωτοεμφανίστηκε η Google, όλοι άρχισαν να χρησιμοποιούν τη νέα μηχανή αναζήτησης ψάχνοντας οτιδήποτε μπορούσαν να φανταστούν και μάλιστα δωρεάν. Κανείς δεν κατάλαβε ποτέ, ότι ταυτόχρονα τον έψαχνε και η Google. Το ίδιο έγινε και με το Facebook, όπου όλοι πίστεψαν ότι ήταν ένας πίνακας ανακοινώσεων όπου ο καθένας μπορούσε να καρφιτσώσει ένα σημείωμα. Σήμερα γνωρίζουμε ότι οι ψηφιακές πλατφόρμες είναι ένα μέσον που μπορεί ο καθένας να διασπείρει ψευδείς αλήθειες σαν επικίνδυνους ιούς γιατί γι’ αυτές δεν παράγεται κανένα εμβόλιο.


Όλα αυτά στηρίζονται στην ψευδαίσθηση, ότι η ζωή του καθενός είναι ιδιωτική υπόθεση κι ότι εμείς επιλέγουμε, πιο κομμάτι πληροφορίας ανταλλάσσουμε έναντι μιας επιθυμητής συναλλαγής. Μια παρόμοια συναλλαγή θα εμφανιστεί σύντομα και στην Ελλάδα, θα διαφημιστεί σαν ο πιο ασφαλής τρόπος συναλλαγών. Θα αντικαταστήσει την πιστωτική κάρτα, αυτή άλλωστε χάνεται ή κλέβεται και θα βασίζεται πάνω στην αναγνώριση του προσώπου, μέσω των βιομετρικών χαρακτηριστικών. Σιγά σιγά περνάμε σ’ έναν τρόπο ζωής που το πρόσωπο μετατρέπεται σε κάρτα εισόδου, στην οικονομική αλλά και κοινωνική ζωή, με δικαίωμα πρόσβασης. Είναι το πρώτο σημείο που φαίνεται να συναντιούνται οι δύο κυρίαρχοι τρόποι επιτήρησης στον σημερινό κόσμο, ο Κινεζικός και ο Αμερικανικός ή Δυτικός τρόπος. Το ξεκίνησαν οι Κινέζοι «κομμουνιστές», όταν δημιούργησαν ένα προσωποποιημένο σύστημα κοινωνικής πίστωσης, που βασιζόταν στην αναγνώριση προσώπου, αλλά και συναισθημάτων. Οι περισσότεροι Κινέζοι συμφώνησαν ότι ήταν ένα σύστημα που φυλούσε τους έντιμους.


Αλλά πολλοί και μεταξύ τους κι εγώ, πιστεύουμε, ότι ένα σύστημα που φακελώνει ενώ διαβάζει την συμπεριφορά μας, αποφασίζει αν αποτελούμε ή όχι κοινωνική απειλή αν μη τι άλλο, εκτός από βαθιά ταξικό είναι απόλυτα ολοκληρωτικό. Ήδη τα συστημικά μέσα και site διαφημίζουν τον τρόπο σαν πιο αξιόπιστο, μπορεί να ξεχωρίσει ακόμα και ομοζυγωτικούς διδύμους, διασκεδάζουν τα περί φακελώματος με την λογική ότι το πρόσωπο μας υπάρχει παντού στο Διαδίκτυο. Τα υπόλοιπα, φαντάζουν ψιλά γράμματα για τους ίδιους διότι θεωρούν τους εαυτούς τους, όπως και οι Κινέζοι, εκ των προτέρων αθώους. Άλλωστε είναι γνωστό ότι οι πρώτοι που επικροτούν αυτού του είδους τα συστήματα, δηλώνοντας ότι

οι ίδιοι δεν έχουν να κρύψουν τίποτα

, είναι οι μικροαστοί της μεσαίας τάξης.


Το αποκαλούμενο και

 Big Nine

: Amazon, Google, Facebook, Tencent, Baidu, Alibaba, Microsoft, IBM και Apple, συνεπικουρούμενες από όλες σχεδόν της εταιρείες που εδρεύουν στην Κοιλάδα της Σιλικόνης, δημιούργησε τον κατασκοπευτικό καπιταλισμό. Εκμεταλλευόμενο μια γνωσιακή ανισότητα των χρηστών σε σχέση με το μέσον και τα κενά του νόμου, άρπαξαν τον έλεγχο της πληροφορίας αλλά και της ίδιας της μάθησης. Χειραγωγώντας τον κόσμο …

author: Unknown
title: Murray Bookchin - The Youth Culture
content:
Author

: Murray Bookchin

Title

: The Youth Culture

Subtitle

: An Anarcho-Communist View

Date

: 1970

Notes

: Published in

Hip Culture: 6 Essays on Its Revolutionary Potential; Yippie, Third World, Feminist, Marxist, High School Student, Anarchist

.

Source

: <

https://archive.org/details/HipCulture

>


 The “hip culture”—the word is really the youth culture and I will use it from now on—does not really need any “defenders”.

[1]

 As an elemental phenomenon, its own existence and development must eventually constitute its only “defense”. What the Youth Culture

does

 need, however, is a better interpretation than it has received up to now—and this would be impossible to achieve without dealing with its critics.


 Bourgeois critics may be dismissed out of hand. Generally, criticism of this kind takes the form either of a patronizing psychoanalysis (the classical image of the “rebellious sons” slaying their “fathers”) or simply a brute condemnation directed against the “impudence” of young people. The most serious criticism, or at least the most systematic, comes from the orthodox Marxists, who usually complain that the Youth Culture is not sufficiently “revolutionary”. On close inspection the criticism from this quarter centers around the notion that the Youth Culture is “elitist”, “escapist”, “bourgeois”, “anti-rational” and should all else fail—nonpolitical.


 Here, one comes up against a vexing problem. Polemics with orthodox Marxists usually appear in a false light—and for

both

 sides of the argument. Any revolutionary who attempts to interpret the Youth Culture from a non-marxian viewpoint tends to appear like a spiritualized vapor, or “worse” (horror of horrors!), a “petty bourgeois hedonist” who is far removed from the bread-and-butter issues and oppressions of daily life. The Old Left “critic” of the Youth Culture, in turn, seems to live in an unreality of his/her own, patently ignoring the brute fact that long-hairs and students are far in advance of the workers on all the critical issues of the day. The two sides become polarized into “either... or” positions, as though oppression can be defined in only one of two ways: spiritual

or

 material, psychic

or

 economic, alienative

or

 exploitative. This, or course, is pure bullshit. Both go together. They interpenetrate in varying degrees and assume different degrees of weight, depending upon the situation in question. The crisis of bourgeois society is

universal’,

 it can no longer be boxed into the neat little compartments that the orthodox Marxists have constructed, polished, and labored to preserve for nearly a century. As women and blacks well know, every form of material oppression is marked by spiritual oppression and every form of spiritual oppression by material oppression. In the case of many white young people, material oppression may not have as much

weight

 as spiritual, but it is nonetheless real and particularly visible on campuses, where students are processed by an “educational” system that operates along factory lines.


 The most astonishing thing about the traditional Marxists is their utter inability to see how enormously the terrain of the revolutionary struggle has expanded with the development of capitalism. Marxian orthodoxy is still fighting the battle of “socialism”: a very specific historical terrain, delimited by the old coal-steel technology of the Industrial Revolution, the cry for “justice,” the killing exploitation of the “factory hand,” and a conception of revolution mediated by “transitional stages” (the “proletarian dictatorship” and “socialist state”) designed not only to deal with counterrevolution but, in the words of Marx and Engels, “to increase the total of productive forces as rapidly as possible.” In the century and more since Marx and Engels penned these words, capitalism itself has increased “the total of productive forces” to a point where even toil, not only material scarcity, is being brought into question—and these new “productive forces” could easily be extended to the Third World following a revolution in America and Europe. What the traditional Marxists can’t get into their heads is that capitalism has finally created the material preconditions for

communism (libertarian

 communism, flttflrctocommunism), not “socialism”; for

freedom,

 not “justice” (or what used to be called “social democracy”).


 This enormous change has profoundly affected all the issues and movements of our …

author: Sam Wainwright
title: Reject the AUKUS death machine, join the fight for the future
content:
The nuclear powered submarine USS Colorado docked at the HMAS Stirling naval base on Menadup/Garden Island, five kilometres from Rockingham in Perth’s southern suburbs, on October 27.

The vessel is in port for a month of maintenance exercises in preparation for the Submarine Rotational Force — West program which will start in September next year, being the first of four United States’ and one British nuclear powered submarines based at HMAS Stirling.

Its arrival was an opportunity for Labor to insist that AUKUS is “on track”, without resolving any of the significant cost and time blow-outs associated with the plan to build the SSN-AUKUS class submarines.

It also means that HMAS Stirling has become a de facto US navy base, with its submarines and crew not just visiting, but stationed in Western Australia, allowing the US to qualitatively step up its presence in the Indian Ocean.

When AUKUS was announced five years ago, in the shadow of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, we were told it was necessary in order to uphold a mythical “rules based order”. Since then, Israel has gone on a genocidal rampage with the support of western governments.

Any hope that US President Donald Trump’s violent rejection of international law, in both word and deed, might lead the Anthony Albanese government to have second thoughts about integrating Australia ever more tightly with US military strategy, through AUKUS and the Force Posture Agreement, has been smashed on the rocks.

The opposite is true. Neither Albanese, foreign minister Penny Wong or defence minister Richard Marles have spoken against Trump’s rampage across the world; be it the kidnapping of the Venezuelan president, threats against Greenland and Canada, the criminal blockade of Cuba, bombing of Iran or the the cruelly misnamed "Board of Peace” foisted on Gaza.

When Wong was directly asked by a journalist whether she agreed that the war on Iran was a breach of the United Nations Charter, the best she could manage was this mealy-mouthed response — “It’s up to the US and Israel to explain the legality of their actions”.

While the Albanese government might still cloak its domestic neoliberal economic agenda in some token progressive rhetoric and gestures to mark out some space between it and the Coalition, its foreign policy is now completely subordinate to Trump’s.

Reinforcing this orientation is the long established ambition of both Labor and Liberal to make Australia one of the world's top ten weapons exporters, further tightening integration with both US and Israeli weapons manufacturers.

Trump’s decision to boost US military spending by 50% on 2025 levels by 2027 has turned this push into a stampede as Australian governments, businesses and universities fall over themselves to try to get a slice of the action.

Meanwhile, urgent action to address the real existential threat to humanity posed by runaway global warming is stalled, demonstrated by the approval of new and expanded fossil fuel projects and Labor’s lowering of expectations ahead of the COP31 climate summit.

Capitalism, based on the endless search for profits and growth, is incapable of solving the climate crisis.

Since the industrial revolution, every new source of energy — biomass, coal, oil, nuclear and renewables — has added to energy production, not replaced it. In other words capitalism welcomes renewables, but in addition to fossil fuels, not instead of them.

Both the federal government and senior military strategists are perfectly well aware of this, just as they know that this will lead to climate breakdown, social crisis and war.

Consequently the real long term climate plan of the Albanese government is increased repression at home and war abroad. It’s not an exaggeration to say that militarism is their deadly serious response to the climate crisis.

Confronting and dismantling AUKUS, the Force Posture Agreement and the weapons industry is central to the fight for a safe climate.

A certain amount of catastrophic warming is already baked into the system. Even if we do everything materially possible to halt and reverse warming starting today, we still face massive ecological disruption. But this is no excuse for giving up.

Replacing a society based on greed, that is pushing us to ecological collapse and war, with a society based on human solidarity is necessary to face the climate crisis. But we face serious obstacles in the fight to pull humanity back from the brink.

Modern day capitalists …

title: LIVE Oct 30, in DC! See Aymeric Monville, Jennifer Ponce de León and Gabriel Rockhill, speaking on “Requiem for French Theory”
content:
NYC, on October 29th, at CUNY (25 Broadway) * DC, on October 30th at Busboys and Poets (235 Carol St NW) * (And a couple of days ago in Philly’s Free Library)


APPEARANCES


Coming from Left Field

 (Episode 152)


In this episode of Coming From Left Field, philosopher and cultural critic Gabriel Rockhill joins

Greg Godels & Pat Cummings

 to explore the Ford Foundation, the 1966 Johns Hopkins conference often cited as a launching point for French Theory in the United States, Cold War cultural politics, and the wider political economy of academic knowledge production. Rockhill argues for rebuilding a class-centered, internationalist Marxism and joins a thoughtful exchange on China, Vietnam, socialism, imperialism, inequality, and the challenges of assessing existing socialist projects without demonization or uncritical celebration….


Marx Memorial Library

in London hosted a dual book launch for

Requiem for French Theory

 and

Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism?

with Gabriel Rockhill, Aymeric Monville, and Jennifer Ponce de León, who engaged in a discussion regarding the effects of imperialism on the production and dissemination of knowledge.

Watch here

or below


Far from simply engaging in a critique of the faux radicalism of the prominent discourses within the imperial theory industry, the discussion was grounded in a reasoned defense of the vibrant international tradition of anti-imperialist Marxism. Topics included the imperial promotion of Western Marxism and postmodern French Theory, the international war of ideas, the failed efforts to discredit anti-imperialist Marxism, culturalism and identity politics vs. a materialist analysis of the colonial question, fascism past and present, the dialectics of actually existing socialism, and the current state of global class struggle in theory and practice.


REVIEWS


Marxism-Leninism Today,

 by

Greg Godels

:


“During the 1960s and 1970s, it was an oft-repeated quip that the European left was long on theory and short on practice, while the North American left was strong on action, but allergic to theory. In West Germany, Italy, and France, young leftists would often passionately debate theoretical questions deep into the night, while seldom coming to a common commitment to action the next day. Their youthful U.S. counterparts—revived after the retreat from High McCarthyism–counted on spontaneous action and a firm commitment to common, inherited political values rather than the ideas buried in deep theoretical tracts. But those observations were far from completely true. The often student-driven U.S. New Left developed a thirst for a broader, deeper explanation of the injustices that they were rejecting. Many of those committed to action turned to left classics–quite often a reconsidered Marx–and others favored a wave of West European radical-oriented thinkers….”

Read more…


ZZ’s Blog

, as reviewed by Zigedy:


“During the 1960s and 1970s, it was an oft-repeated quip that the European left was long on theory and short on practice, while the North American left was strong on action, but allergic to theory. In West Germany, Italy, and France, young leftists would often passionately debate theoretical questions deep into the night, while seldom coming to a common commitment to action the next day. Their youthful US counterparts–revived after the retreat from High McCarthyism– counted on spontaneous action and a firm commitment to common, inherited political values rather than the ideas buried in deep theoretical tracts. But those observations were far from completely true. The often student-driven US New Left developed a thirst for a broader, deeper explanation of the injustices that they were rejecting. Many of those committed to action turned to left classics– quite often a reconsidered Marx– and others favored a wave of West European radical-oriented thinkers. It is the rise and importation to the US of one particularly influential “brand” of European theory to which Aymeric Monville and Gabriel Rockhill’s new book is devoted.


In

 Requiem for French Theory: Transatlantic Funeral Dirge in a Marxist Key

 (New York,

Monthly Review Press

, 2026, $22.00, 168 pp.), Monville and Rockhill show that what became known as “French Theory” in the US was both a calculated interruption of the rediscovery and study of Marxism and an intellectual trend hostile to anti-capitalist and socialist currents….”

author: Jonathan Rosenblum
title: Vancouver Is the Next Battleground for Municipal Socialism in North America
content:
Vancouver socialists won big. What comes next?

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Vancouver, British Columbia, is the next battleground for municipal socialism in North America.

On October 17, Vancouver voters decisively evicted their right-wing mayor, replacing him with the Green Party’s candidate. But more consequentially, they also tossed nearly all of the pro-corporate incumbents from all three municipal legislative bodies — city council, the school board, and the parks board — and replaced them with a combination of insurgents from the left-wing party Coalition of Progressive Electors (COPE), the Greens, and an establishment center-left party, OneCity.

A broadly democratic socialist organization, COPE ran on a bold platform demanding full rent control, an end to data center construction, and taxing the rich to fund social housing, schools, parks, and libraries. All 12 COPE candidates swept into office, constituting the single largest party bloc. Now with those dozen seats on the three boards — out of 27 total seats — COPE is poised to advance a bold, socialist-inspired agenda for one of Canada’s major cities.

This is a massive political sea-change from the last municipal election. In 2022, A Better City Vancouver (ABC Vancouver) swept to power, placing businessman Ken Sim in the mayor’s office and winning 7 out of 10 seats on city council; six out of seven on the parks board; and five out of nine on the school board.

Over the following four years, Sim and his allies advanced an unabashedly pro-developer agenda. They froze the city’s Empty Homes Tax; waived developer fees; eliminated the city’s Renters Office; and canceled climate justice programs. The ABC Party-majority school board starved programs for vulnerable students, tried to sell off school properties, and severely restricted public participation at board meetings. Sim also pushed to make Vancouver a bitcoin-friendly city, led a failed effort to abolish the parks board, and rankled many when he set up a private gym for himself in city hall.

Sim embraced the ruling class, collecting maximum individual donations of $1,250 from the likes of Lululemon founder and billionaire Chip Wilson; leaders within major real estate development companies, including Polygon Homes, Westbank, and Onni; and venture capital firm Canaccord Genuity. Sim repaid those favors, declaring October 3 to be “Chip Wilson Day” and honoring Canaccord’s founding chairman with his own day on October 18.

Featuring a huge seaport and international airport, Vancouver is Canada’s Pacific trade gateway. Big tech firms — like Amazon, Microsoft, and Telus — have a prominent presence in the city. Tourism and film production also are big economic drivers. But property development and investment have come to dominate the city’s downtown, with gleaming glass skyscrapers towering over the water and the city’s iconic Stanley Park. In the last 40 years, both domestic and foreign capital have rushed in to snap up Vancouver’s luxury condominiums and business centers. For many owners, these are not places to live or do business in, but rather serve as lucrative tax shelters and investments.

A city of almost 700,000, Vancouver is home to no fewer than seven billionaires, and the contrast between the uber-wealthy and the rest of the population is profound. A majority of Vancouver residents are renters. Rent control — set by provincial authorities — hasn’t stopped Vancouver from clocking median rents of $2,600 per month ($1,850 in U.S. dollars). Rents are 37 percent above the national average in Vancouver, making it the most expensive rental market in Canada. Some 40 percent of Vancouver tenants are rent-burdened — spending more than 30 percent of their income on housing costs and scrimping on other necessities. Nearly three-quarters of the city’s beloved community centers have been deemed to be in poor or very poor condition. School classrooms are overcrowded and understaffed.

Housing, however, is the most animating issue. Talk to any renter in Vancouver and inevitably the problem of “renovictions” and “demovictions” will come up. British Columbia limits how much landlords can raise rents annually. But there’s no prohibition on evicting tenants by claiming that renovations are needed, and then jacking up the rent for the new tenants. Landlords have grabbed onto this statutory loophole …
