Christa Pike, whose twice-botched execution in Tennessee last month has renewed calls for abolishing the death penalty in the United States, spoke out about her experience on Friday, a month after she had “walked into the execution chamber at Riverbend men’s prison prepared to die.”

“I had made my peace,” Pike said in a statement dictated by her legal team. “I had told the people who loved me, supported me, and stood by me through the years I was grateful for them. I had also told the people in the room, and who were there to witness my execution, that I was leaving them in loving kindness. Several days later, I woke up alone in a hospital, confused and in pain.”

Despite an ongoing legal fight stemming from the pervasive abuse the 50-year-old suffered throughout her youth, the US Supreme Court let Tennessee move forward with its plan to kill her on September 30. Pike, who was sentenced to death over the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, survived two injections of pentobarbital from a doctor involved with an earlier botched execution at the maximum security prison in Nashville. She was taken by ambulance to Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

Dr. Mark Fowler knew something was wrong after 45 minutes passed without word from the warden. In most cases, executions take no more than ten minutes. When he was summoned from his waiting room to the chamber next door, he saw Christa Pike, who’d received two lethal doses of… pic.twitter.com/EJ9TcAe8a9

“There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain,” Pike said Friday. “My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn’t just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul. I had not contemplated life beyond that night, and I’m deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position. I continue to think about my victim’s family and the terrible pain and loss they have endured. I am recovering, and I know that I am getting stronger. But healing is not the same as being okay.”

“Since that night, I have been largely isolated in the prison’s medical ward, away from other people and the human connections that mean so much to me,” she continued. “That isolation brings its own kind of pain. I spent 28 years in solitary confinement, and much of what I am experiencing today is a repeat of that condition. I am searching for meaning in what happened to me. One thing that has given me strength is the extraordinary love and support I have received from people around the world. I am overwhelmed by the kindness and prayers of people I have known for years and complete strangers who have never met me.”

“To know that so many people care about me, that they see me as a human being whose life matters, is something I cannot fully put into words,” Pike said. “It is humbling, and it has touched me more deeply than I can explain. I also want to thank the first responders, doctors, nurses, and everyone at the hospital who cared for me. They treated me with compassion, dignity, and respect. I will never forget their kindness. I also want to thank my attorneys and everyone who has fought for me, stood beside me and refused to give up on me.”

She added that “I don’t know why I survived that night. I don’t know what comes next. Some days, finding hope is harder than others. For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time. And I am holding on to the love and kindness of so many people who have reminded me that I am not alone.”

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Thousands of farmlands in Bicol converted to mining, energy, infra projects
content:
Claiming the Land: Kilusang Magbubukid ng Bicol provides assistance to affected farmers and members of the local peasant group in Bula, Camarines Sur. (Photo By Reynard Magtoto/Bulatlat)

Farmers organizations warned that agricultural land conversion and large-scale development projects could displace farming communities, threaten food production and undermine farmers’ access to land.

Farmers organizations in the Bicol region have raised concerns over alleged land grabbing and agricultural land conversion involving haciendas, mining operations, renewable energy developments and infrastructure projects.

The farmers travelled to Manila late in October to call on the Marcos Jr. administration to stop land grabbing and land-use conversion of agricultural lands.

In Camarines Norte, peasant groups identified 25,000 hectares associated with the Mabilo Copper-Gold Project, while another 64,884 hectares were linked to a renewable energy development in Mount Labo.

An additional 321 hectares were identified in connection with mining operations in the province.

In Albay, the organizations identified several disputed landholdings, including 141 hectares at Hacienda Mitra/Illas in Guinobatan, 130 hectares at Hacienda Alsua in Pio Duran, 250 hectares at Hacienda Asistio in Ligao, and 200 hectares at Hacienda Ribaya, also in Ligao.

Another 78 hectares were identified at a Hacienda Alsua property, alongside 34 hectares associated with the expansion of Bicol University.

Agricultural land conversion was also reported in Daraga, including 148 hectares for the core site of Bicol International Airport and another 200 hectares for its expansion site.

An additional 110 hectares were identified for conversion associated with the Cagraray Eco-Park and Misibis Bay development.

In Camarines Sur, peasant organizations identified 817 hectares allegedly affected by land grabbing allegedly involving the Tuazon/Lao family in Bula, 244 hectares at Hacienda Veneracion in Pamplona, and 1,014 hectares in Barangay San Ramon, Siruma.

The groups also cited 309 hectares associated with the Naga Agro-Industrial Complex and between 300 and 500 hectares for an airport extension in Naga City.

In Masbate, peasant groups identified 1,807 hectares at Hacienda Pecson in Cawayan, and 13,000 hectares allegedly affected by land grabbing involving the Wanglo/Belon family in Aroroy.

Meanwhile, 700 hectares at Hacienda Beringer were identified in Sorsogon, alongside other land disputes and conversion projects.

In Catanduanes, the groups reported 111 hectares allegedly affected by land grabbing in Gigmoto.

Farmers organizations warned that agricultural land conversion and large-scale development projects could displace farming communities, threaten food production and undermine farmers’ access to land.

Farmers defending their land are met with state violence, according to the data from human rights organization Karapatan Bicol. The group reported 342 incidents of alleged human rights violations from July 2022 to July 2026 across the region.

The organization documented 28 victims of extrajudicial killings, 297 cases of threats, harassment and intimidation, 146 cases of coercion, 91 cases of red-tagging, and 75 violations of freedom of association.

It also documented 23 political prisoners, and 55 cases involving attacks on or the use of schools, medical facilities, religious institutions and other public places for military purposes.

Camarines Sur recorded the highest number of reported incidents at 212, followed by Albay with 48, Sorsogon with 42, Masbate with 27, Camarines Norte with 11, and Catanduanes with two.

Karapatan Bicol accused state security forces and the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) of involvement in intimidation and other alleged abuses targeting rural communities and peasant organizations.

The organization also raised concerns about military operations in farming communities, alleging that these have contributed to fear and restrictions on organizing. (RVO)

author: Kodao Productions
title: Commercialization of Bilibid land would violate prisoners’ rights, KAPATID warns
content:
Political prisoners’ support group KAPATID asked the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) to protect the rights of persons deprived of liberty (PDL), warning of a Bureau of Corrections’ (BuCor) plan to close and commercialize the New Bilibid Prison (NBP) reservation by 2028.


The group said the plan may escalate into a “dual human rights and land displacement crisis” that would force prisoner transfers and residents’ evictions.


“We are deeply concerned that the impending closure threatens not only prisoners facing forced transfers but also long-time residents facing displacement. Residents have sent distress messages reporting as many as three eviction notices, with proceedings already underway,” KAPATID spokesperson Fides Lim said.


Lim demands a full disclosure of BuCor’s land-use plan on the 366.7-hectare public property as well as a congressional inquiry in PDL conditions at the country’s biggest jail facility.


At the CHR’s civil society consultation on the Human Rights Situationer on Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDLs) on Wednesday, KAPATID urged the CHR to press for a halt to transfers and evictions pending a human rights review.


Protect NBP lands


KAPATID’s also launched its “Protect NBP Lands” campaign, calling for transparency, accountability, and meaningful participation by affected communities and civil society in decisions on the reservation’s future.


“Decongestion must not become a pretext for commercial development at the expense of human rights,” Lim said.


“Transferring prisoners to already overcrowded facilities merely shifts the problem elsewhere, while threatening family ties, access to medical care, and legal counsel,” she added.


KAPATID said it shares CHR’s concern over the need to scrutinize BuCor’s actual land-use plan.


The reservation is 52.79% larger than Bonifacio Global City while BuCor Director General Gregorio Pio Catapang Jr. has cited projected annual revenues of ₱1 billion to ₱2 billion from commercialization.


“People deserve to know how this public property will be used and who stands to benefit,” Lim said.


Bucor plans to transfer NBP


KAPATID also questioned plans to relocate the NBP. “NBP must be retained at its present site because it serves a population overwhelmingly rooted in Luzon,” Lim said.


BuCor data as of September 30, 2026 show that 88.91% or 18,110 of NBP’s 20,369 PDLs come from Luzon, including 62.20% from Metro Manila, CALABARZON, and Central Luzon.


Meanwhile, reported occupancy rates reach 573% at Iwahig Penal Farm, 504% at Leyte Regional Prison, and 399% at San Ramon Prison and Penal Farm.


KAPATID said the planned transfers could constitute cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment under the UN Convention Against Torture, the Nelson Mandela Rules, the Anti-Torture Act, and other applicable laws.


It called on the CHR to investigate whether forced transfers, considering their foreseeable effects on family contact, health care, and conditions in overcrowded receiving facilities.


“Genuine decongestion means reducing the prison population through timely, lawful releases—not simply transferring overcrowding elsewhere,” Lim said.


KAPATID reiterated its calls for expedited processing of prison records and time allowances, swift action for executive clemency, the prompt release of those who have served their sentences, and humanitarian release for the very elderly and seriously ill. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

author: Hayley Tsukayama
title: Why VPNs Are Worth Defending
content:
Developers of virtual private network (VPN) apps are reporting that their products are again being pulled from Apple’s App Store in Russia. This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online.

Why? VPNs give people a way to control their own online activities. When you visit a website through a VPN, that website only sees the VPN server's location (well, IP address) rather than your actual location. It's like sending a letter through a P.O. box so the recipient doesn't know where you really live. It can also disguise where you’re accessing information from, which can make it possible to access information banned by your government.

This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online.

Going after tools that give people the space to communicate and access information freely is a common tactic from the totalitarian playbook. This latest demand comes after several steps the Russian government’s taken to surveil speech specifically on Apple products. In 2024, the Moscow Times reported that Russia’s state media watchdog, Roskomnadzor, went after VPN apps on the Apple App Store, after banning access to Western social media platforms and blacklisting opposition media sites. Russia then blocked Apple’s FaceTime software in 2025, according to Apple Insider.

Bloomberg also recently reported that the Russian government has added Apple and Microsoft to its state surveillance registry. This gives Roskomnadzor access to local users’ correspondence, Apple Insider reported, and puts both companies in a position to turn over customer information to the country’s security services as required.

With government control encroaching on their devices and less access to tools that give them alternate methods, people in Russia are left with shrinking options to communicate online or find information that isn’t state-sanctioned.

While Russia’s actions offer a more extreme vision of what happens when the government tries to enforce speech rules by attacking vital privacy tools, it is far from the only government doing so. Several states in the U.S., bent on making it difficult to circumvent invasive age-gating laws, have suggested banning VPNs—either to access certain content or in some cases to simply ban them outright. EFF has publicly (and loudly) criticized these proposals, because going after VPNs is a dangerous step down the road of censorship.

Attacks on speech and privacy online are deeply troubling, no matter where they happen. What those in power may see as a “loophole” in their invasive laws is actually an expression of user control. We’ll continue to speak out when we see governments going after them to take that control away.

author: EDRi
title: EDRi-gram, 29 October 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Celebrating end-to-end encryption, and the digital justice community in Europe and beyond

We’re still riding the high from October milestones showcasing the strength of our community. We had the pleasure of greeting many of you in person and online for #PrivacyCamp26 two weeks ago to discuss the origins of technology and how to pivot from conversations around “sovereignty” to meaningful, community-led self-determination. If you weren’t able to make it but you’re curious about the conversations, you can rewatch the livestream of some of the panel discussions.

Then, on October 21, we celebrated Global Encryption Day, highlighting end-to-end encryption as a crucial foundation to our right to safe and secure communication online and to life as we know it. Thanks to our members and partners, our message of protecting encryption was visible across several European capitals – from the metro trains of Prague to key landmarks in Berlin, Paris and Dublin with mobile “encryption trucks”. We also worked with European Sex Workers Alliance and Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement to raise awareness on the importance of safe and secure communications for sex workers as well as womens’ rights. You can read more about the action in this edition, and stay tuned for more updates coming soon on our social platforms.

Yet another win for digital rights this month came with the news of Norway’s data protection authority imposing a fine of 92 million Norwegian crowns (roughly EUR 8.8 million) on Microsoft’s adtech unit Xandr for unlawfully sharing ​Grindr users’ sensitive data with thousands of advertisers.

While we’re bolstered from the wins and community spirit, there’s a lot more to resist and much work to be done. We are still reeling from the EU governments’ final position on the Digital Omnibus on Data, which amongst other unsavoury things, will to allow companies to use our data to develop or use their AI systems if it serves a ‘legitimate interest’ – without us knowing or accepting. This is a blank cheque for tech corporations to indulge in outrageous data grabs and exploit potentially sensitive information about us.

Earlier this week, the European Commission also announced a revamp of Frontex, EU’s border agency, that is set to double its budget and expand its role in deportations and surveillance. Not only will this turn Frontex into EU’s ICE equivalent, the new Regulation also wants to allow Frontex to be able to monitor social media for information that may forecast people’s movements at EU borders. Let alone leading with solidarity and care, the EU seems intent on violating people’s freedom to move and to express themselves. author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Cyberlibel complaints vs journalists strengthen calls to decriminalize libel
content:
The criminal sanction for Philippine libel laws is “excessive” and is in violation of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) to which the Philippines is a signatory.

Libel complaints were recently filed against journalists and media company executives. For a journalists’ group, these validate the previous calls to decriminalize libel.

The GMA chapter of the National Union of Journalists of the Philippines (NUJP) stressed that libel laws silence journalism. “[C]riminalizing speech only undermines the public’s fundamental right to know,” the chapter said in a statement.

Davao City 1st District Rep. Paolo Duterte filed libel and cyberlibel complaints against GMA executives and broadcast journalists which stemmed from the network’s report about alleged cash deliveries to the Dutertes claimed by dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.

Duterte filed the complaint before the Davao City Prosecutor’s Office on October 23, more than two weeks after his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, made a joke about filing a multimillion-peso libel case against GMA Network. Her remarks happened during a press conference on October 6 while reading her affidavit which answers Gracioso’s claims.

Among the respondents were GMA executives Felipe Gozon and Gilberto Duavit, as well as journalists Mel Tiangco, Vicki Morales, Emil Sumangil, Darlene Cay, Marvin Parado, Joel San Luis, and other unidentified individuals.

In a statement released on October 23, the TV network said that they have not yet received the complaints.

Gracioso and National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) director Melvin Matibag were also named as respondents.

Meanwhile, veteran journalist Philip Lustre Jr. was arrested on October 24 over a cyberlibel complaint reportedly filed by Mans Carpio, Sara’s husband. He was unaware of the complaint, according to his legal counsel. He was released on bail on the same day.

NUJP has been campaigning for the decriminalization of libel, echoing the views of the United Nations (UN) Human Rights Committee that the criminal sanction for Philippine libel laws is “excessive” and is in violation of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) to which the Philippines is a signatory.

Right(s) Up: Why journalists and advocates push for decriminalization of libel

On September 18, NUJP released its policy review on libel laws, stating that the high court has already identified the problem of these laws but reform requires legislation. The review, to name a few, cited Justice Marvic Leonen’s opinion in Disini, Jr. v. Secretary of Justice which stated that libel was unconstitutional as penal sanctions impose “an invidious chilling effect.”

It added that removing jail time alone, as proposed by some legislators, is not decriminalization because of limitations of a fine-only regime, saying that if the accused cannot pay, subsidiary imprisonment may follow.

The review cited the data obtained from the Office of Cybercrime of the Department of Justice (DOJ), indicating that 3,770 cyberlibel cases had been filed, as of May 2022, since the enactment of the Cybercrime Prevention Act. More than 2,500 cases remained pending in courts and before the prosecution level. There were already 12 convictions.

In the 2023 study by NUJP, 61.5% of the libel cases against 50 journalists from 2021 to 2023 were filed by politicians.

ML Party-list Rep. Leila de Lima said that filing a libel suit against journalists and media workers for doing their job sends a “chilling message” to other members of the press. Parties being accused can just respond to the allegations, she wrote in a Facebook post.

Under the Journalist’s Code of Ethics approved by media groups, journalists shall recognize the duty to air the other side and the duty to correct substantive errors promptly.

“Contrary to allegations of malice or unverified reporting, the report went through standard, multi-layered editorial and legal verification procedures,” the NUJP GMA Chapter said. “The team conducted due diligence—verifying information through official sources, law enforcement documents, and background checks—and obtained proper clearance from network leadership and legal counsel before airing the story.”

In the subject report, the reporter, Cay, and anchor Tiangco mentioned that they were trying to get the comments of the people implicated by Gracioso, including the Dutertes, but they did not receive a response when the report was aired …

title: La bande à « Balance ton Claude »
content:
Nous avons déjà longuement abordé les ressorts de l'« affaire Thélyson Orélien » dans nos pages (nous renvoyons, entre autres, à

cet excellent texte de Jean Claude Noel

). L'enquête qui suit porte sur ses délateurs, la bande à « Balance ton Claude » du nom du compte X à l'origine de la polémique. On y découvre que l'affaire Thélyson Orélien, est un double écran de fumée qui masque une convergence d'intérêts, financiers, idéologiques et géopolitiques, entre l'industrie de l'IA, les libertariens de la Silicon Valley, les christo-fascistes de l'administration Trump, et leurs imitateurs bien-de-chez-nous.


« Démarche complètement apolitique », « lanceur d'alerte », anonymat nécessaire pour éviter les attaques

ad hominem

… Toutes ces auto-justifications offertes par la bande à « Balance ton Claude », qui est derrière la polémique Thélyson Orélien, servent à ripoliner une opération idéologique, menée par un groupe de jeunes « libéraux-conservateurs » (doux euphémisme), très actifs dans l'espace médiatique, depuis les colonnes du Figaro, et les fabriques à propagande du projet Périclès. En outre, ces alarmes hypocrites s'inscrivent dans les récits

IApocalyptiques

 déployés par l'industrie pour faire gonfler investissements publics et privés. Une bulle profitant surtout aux nouveaux technoligarques, qui sont prêts à jeter la démocratie et l'humanité entière dans le chaudron de la valorisation et de la domination sans partage.


Les problèmes posés par la rédaction

I

A

ssistée

cachent une autre forme d'imposture : les allégations de neutralité politique répétées par la bande à « Balance ton Claude ». Une fine équipe, composée de cinq membres, d'après le premier accusateur anonyme sorti du bois

 [

1

]

, et qui n'a pas eu droit à la même attention que Thélyson Orélien.


«

Notre démarche était complètement apolitique

 [

2

]


 »

, déclarait ainsi Samuel Fitoussi dans

Le Point

, après avoir tombé le masque. Pourtant, le profil de nos Claudettes risque d'affoler votre détecteur à

bullshit

. Pas besoin du logiciel Pangram, vous allez voir, pour confondre ces immenses tartufes, présentés comme des «

lanceurs d'alerte

ayant

 l'amour de la vérité chevillé au coeur

et dénonçant les impostures intellectuelles

 [

3

]

 ».


Samuel Fitoussi


Commençons par vous donner une idée de l'honnêteté intellectuelle de M. Fitoussi. Quelques heures après avoir lancé la polémique sur le livre de Thélyson Orélien depuis le compte X « Balance ton Claude » (encore anonyme à ce moment-là), le chroniqueur du

Figaro

 intervient sur Radio J, où il déclare : «

comme aujourd'hui, le RN n'est pas un parti particulièrement violent ou antisémite ou quoi que ce soit, [renvoyer dos à dos les extrêmes] c'est en fait banaliser la dangerosité de cette gauche pro-Hamas...

 »


La journaliste lui fait alors remarquer que l'extrême-droite est quand même «

très proche de l'AfD, un parti néo-nazi

 ». Réponse de Samuel Fitoussi : «

J'ai beaucoup de critiques à l'égard de ces partis. Pour le RN, par exemple, je les trouve étatistes, socialistes, relativement incompétents

 […]

mais je pense qu'il faut reconnaître que les choses ont évolué, que le RN n'est plus le RN d'il y a 30 ans, et c'est même plus le RN d'il y a dix ans, qui voulait sortir de l'Union européenne, et c'est plus le RN antisémite

 [

4

]

 ».

L

'amour de la vérité chevillé au cœur

, on vous dit.


Par ailleurs, l'intérêt de M. Fitoussi pour les implications de l'IA générative n'est pas pure curiosité, étant donné qu'il travaille pour le fonds d'investissement FRST CAPITAL, spécialisé dans l'industrie naissante du

machine learning

(un des domaines informatiques que l'on trouve derrière la formule générique « IA », et dont les avancées ont notamment permis le développement des « grands modèles de langage » – ou

LLM

 – comme le célèbre ChatGPT).


Incidemment, FRST CAPITAL est une ancienne filiale d'OTIUM CAPITAL, la holding de Pierre-Edouard Stérin, milliardaire christo-libertarien qui utilise ses gains pour financer un projet de conquête politique par l'extrême-droite, baptisé « Périclès » (pour Patriotes, Enracinés, Résistants, Identitaires, Chrétiens, Libéraux, Européens, Souverainistes), et doté d'un budget de 150 millions d'euros

 [

5

]

.


Cerise sur le gâteau : FIRST CAPITAL n'investit pas seulement dans les « laboratoires d'IA », mais également dans la fabrique d'opinion, en produisant des sondages douteux sur la popularité d'Elon Musk ou …

title: Terminal Kadıköy’ün reklam ekranı hack’lendi: “Bu bina kent suçudur”
content:
İstanbul'un Kadıköy Söğütlüçeşme’deki Terminal Kadıköy’de bulunan bir reklam ekranı, “BU BİNA KENT SUÇUDUR” yazısıyla hack’lendi. Kent hakkı savunucuları, deprem toplanma alanı ve yeşil alanın alışveriş merkezine (AVM) dönüştürülmesine tepki göstererek kentlerin her alanının kâr maksimizasyonuna göre planlandığını vurguladı.


ETHA’daki habere göre, Söğütlüçeşme Tren İstasyonu’nun viyadük altındaki alanında kurulan Terminal Kadıköy, Nisan 2025’ten bu yana işletiliyor. Açıldığı günden bu yana onlarca dükkânın faaliyet gösterdiği alan, yeni bir tüketim merkezine dönüştü.


Kent hakkı savunucuları, ekoloji örgütleri ve Kadıköylüler, projeye karşı yıllardır itirazlarını sürdürüyor. Haydarpaşa Dayanışması, projeyi “soylulaştırma merkezi” olarak nitelendirerek “Kamusal alanlar ticarileşiyor, bu bir kent suçudur” açıklamasını yapmıştı.


Savunucular, AVM’ye dönüştürülen alanın geçmişte sokakta yaşayan hayvanların kent sakinleri tarafından beslendiği geniş bir yeşil alan olduğunu belirtiyor. Bölgenin yıllarca “izbe bir alan, güvensiz bir yer” olarak tanımlandığını aktaran kent hakkı savunucuları, bu söylemle projeye toplumsal rıza oluşturulmaya çalışıldığını ifade ediyor.


500’den fazla ağaç kesildi


Proje kapsamında bölgede 500’den fazla ağaç kesildi. Kent hakkı savunucuları, Söğütlüçeşme’deki alanın deprem toplanma alanı niteliği taşıdığını ve projenin bu işlevi fiilen ortadan kaldırdığını belirtiyor.


Savunucular, “Hem bir deprem toplanma alanı hem kentsel bir yeşil alanın tümü, bir avuç AVM’ye kurban edildi” diyerek kamusal alanın sermayeye peşkeş çekilmesine tepki göstermişti.


Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı ise proje için “ÇED Gerekli Değildir” kararı vermişti.


Terminal Kadıköy sonrası Kadıköy’de artan yoğunluk ve trafik baskısı

author: David Swanson
title: It’s Time to Ban Autonomous Weapons
content:
Africa, Cameroon Chapter, Chapters, Demilitarization

By Guy Feugap, World BEYOND War’s Africa Organizer, November 1, 2026

As part of the Stop Killer Robots campaign’s Global Week of Action from October 25 to 31, 2026, the Cameroon chapter of World BEYOND War organized a photo action at the Reunification Monument in Yaoundé. This event, held at this symbolic site representing Cameroonians’ aspirations for peace, aimed to draw public attention to the dangers of autonomous weapons and the need to encourage the country to maintain its position and call on other states to permanently ban autonomous weapons. This event is part of a global campaign leading up to the Seventh Review Conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW), scheduled for November 16–20, 2026, in Geneva.

Through this symbolic action, World BEYOND War members in Cameroon are drawing attention to an issue that has now moved beyond the realm of science fiction: the development of weapons systems capable of autonomously selecting and attacking targets. For the members, it is essential to ensure that technological advances do not compromise human life or the fundamental principles of international law; no technology, even when controlled by a human being, is acceptable if its purpose is to kill human beings. Using campaign posters, the participants helped bring to light a major threat to peace, security, and the protection of human life. Beyond the photography, this event was an opportunity to educate chapter members and raise awareness among passersby about the ethical, legal, and humanitarian issues surrounding autonomous weapons, while emphasizing the importance of civic engagement including through signing the Stop Killer Robots campaign petition.

The urgency of this mobilization is underscored by reports of testing and use of autonomous weapons systems in armed conflicts, particularly in Ukraine. The Stop Killer Robots campaign highlights systems capable of autonomously detecting and killing people. It also highlights the use of military tools based on artificial intelligence to propose targets with minimal human validation, like in the contexts of Gaza. Not all of these tools are necessarily autonomous weapons, but they illustrate the risks associated with the increasing automation of military decision-making. When automated systems are deployed in this way in conflicts, it becomes essential to determine how to ensure that no new weapons are produced and put into circulation. The time for debating the technical possibilities of artificial intelligence in the military sphere is over. It is time to establish legally binding international rules to prevent harm and protect humanity from the consequences of autonomy in weapons systems.

The Seventh Review Conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, to be held November 16–20, 2026, in Geneva, presents an opportunity for States to turn several years of diplomatic discussions into concrete negotiations. The Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems, having completed its latest mandate to develop the elements of an international instrument, has seen more than 70 states, as well as the United Nations Secretary-General and the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross, acknowledge that the work accomplished provides a sufficient basis to begin negotiations. Furthermore, 130 countries have expressed their support for a legally binding instrument on autonomous weapons systems. In this context, Stop Killer Robots calls on States Parties to adopt, at the Review Conference, a mandate to negotiate a new protocol to the Convention in 2027, with the goal of concluding negotiations within one year. If no agreement is reached in Geneva to launch negotiations, the campaign urges states in favor of legally binding regulations to consider other diplomatic avenues to ensure the process is not stalled.

Cameroon’s position is of particular importance in this effort. As a State Party to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons and a member of the African Group and the Non-Aligned Movement, Cameroon supports the negotiation of a legally binding instrument on autonomous weapons systems. During the March 2026 session of the Group of Governmental Experts, Cameroon noted that the work carried out had led to significant progress and that the evolving text constituted an excellent basis for negotiations toward the adoption of a legally binding …

title: SOLIDARITY WITH ALL ANTI-WAR PRISONERS IN RUSSIA & DRAFT DODGERS IN UKRAINE
content:
Beneath is the text of the leaflet distributed outside both the Russian and Ukrainian embassies in London by members of the Anarchist Communist Group and the Network of Anarchist Internationalists (NAI) on Saturday October 31st


For the past five years, the warring states of Ukraine and Russia have been sending the working class to die on the battlefields, killing civilians across the war zone and destroying critical infrastructure with missiles and drones. European states are arming Ukraine, helping to keep the war of the trenches going on indefinitely—a war that has already lasted longer than WWI—in order to lay the groundwork for the revitalisation of their declining industry by shifting it more and more toward a war economy. The endless war, financed by loans from Europe and the USA, allows states to carry out their ideological, bureaucratic and technical “defensive” restructuring, as well as the broader restructuring of production, at a time when the US is pulling back from funding the war in the region and the whole planet is beginning to smell of gunpowder. The loans under the Rearm Europe arms program and the record ‘defence’ budgets being pushed by Europe point with certainty toward war austerity, in other words an even harsher exploitation of the working class, as its future wages are put up as collateral for current spending. In 2025, global military spending reached $2.887 trillion, the highest level ever recorded by SIPRI, while Europe increased its military spending by 14% in a single year. European military spending reached an average of 3.2% of GDP, up from 2.8% in 2024.


The Death Camp that is Ukraine, hemmed in on all sides, built jointly by Russia on the one hand and the USA and Europe on the other, plays a key role in spreading militarisation throughout European societies: expanding the arms industry, increasing military spending, intensifying and generalising conscription, recruiting men and, to

some extent, women into the armed forces with the lure of a career, and repressing those who refuse to take part.


Within this process, desertion and draft resistance movements play an important role in undermining the ideology of national unity and the state’s ability to keep mobilising entire populations for war. This is why the widespread draft resistance and desertion in Ukraine and Russia—300,000 deserters and 2,000,000 draft dodgers in the former, and more than 75,000 deserters and 260,000 draft dodgers as early as September 2022 in the latter—is so significant and deserves the support of the antiwar movement. The stories of violence and imprisonment suffered by those resisting mobilization on both sides of the front show what the militarisation of society means

in practice, and what it costs to refuse to fight for the state and the bosses.


In Russia, which has recently entered a phase of silent mass mobilisation, deserters—most of them forcibly recruited through coercion and blackmail—are being summarily executed on the spot by their own commanders (zeroing out). Along the borders of Ukraine, men trapped inside the country by martial law—which prevents them from leaving for safer countries—are trying to cross frozen mountains and rivers to escape

mobilisation. Some freeze to death; others drown. Those forced to remain in the country are left at the mercy of the TRCs, a special military unit that rounds up men from the streets, their workplaces, public transport stops, cafés and outside schools. They are thrown into vans and taken to the front in a practice that has become known

as busification’. Those who physically resist busification or take part in armed resistance inside training centers end up facing crushing prison sentences. When an army lifer is killed in such an incident, the sentence is life imprisonment.


Bogdan Koshel, 27, was drafted in Kyiv in June 2025. After contemplating suicide, he eventually turned his weapon on the military bastards who were training him and was sentenced to life in prison on June 9, 2026, for the deaths of two of them. Twenty three-year-old Oleg Gavrilov and five others arrested under martial law for

“obstructing mobilization” during the July 8, 2026 uprising in a neighborhood of Lviv against a busification operation are being prosecuted for assault against police officers. Twenty-seven-year-old Ukrainian Trotskyist Bogdan Syrotiuk was sentenced to 15 years in prison not for any physical attack or act of resistance, but simply for expressing antiwar …

title: Pisa: Rivendicazioni della Sapienza Occupata. “Noi la guerra non la paghiamo”
content:
Ripubblichiamo il comunicato del

Collettivo Universitario Autonomo di Pisa

 in merito alle rivendicazioni dell’occupazione avvenuta a conclusione del corteo del 30 ottobre in occasione dello sciopero generale.


Ieri 30 ottobre 2026 siamo scese in piazza per lo sciopero generale chiamato da USB e molti sindacati di base, uno sciopero internazionale contro il carovita e la guerra: più di 100 porti sono stati bloccati per interrompere i flussi della guerra e la sua logistica. Le piazze gremite in tutta Italia hanno detto una cosa molto chiara: noi la guerra non la paghiamo.


Investire sulla guerra è una scelta politica, non solo di questo governo ma di tutta l’oligarchia globale.


La guerra non è solo un’ipotesi futura, la guerra occupa già il nostro presente: la paghiamo con il rincaro dei prezzi al supermercato, sui trasporti, sul carburante, sulle bollette. La paghiamo quando il nostro diritto allo studio viene eroso di giorno in giorno, e quando le nostre università, spolpate di fondi e definanziate, devono convertire la propria ricerca agli interessi delle aziende e dell’industria bellica.


Le tante voci alzatesi in corteo oggi nella nostra città si sono unite nella decisione di occupare il palazzo della Sapienza, sede storica dell’università di Pisa, sempre meno a disposizione dellə studentə e sempre più rifunzionalizzata per essere vetrina dell’istituzione. La Sapienza, però, è anche il luogo dove si sono prodotte nel 1967 le

Tesi

, documento programmatico del movimento studentesco che avrebbe trasformato l’università negli anni successivi. Nelle

Tesi della Sapienza

 dellə studentə in lotta di sessant’anni fa si legge che “l’università appartiene alla base universitaria”. Siamo qui oggi per gridarlo di nuovo a gran voce.


L’università è di chi ci studia e di chi ci lavora. Chiediamo condizioni dignitose per chi le nostre università le tiene aperte, le pulisce e le vive. V ogliamo ribellarci al futuro che ci viene prospettato fatto di precarietà e di saperi svenduti alla guerra e alla devastazione del territorio. Università e conoscenza sono beni pubblici, di cui dobbiamo prenderci cura. L’università deve essere un luogo accessibile a tuttə, che rispetti il nostro tempo e i nostri bisogni, in cui crescere insieme, costruire un futuro collettivo, dove custodire i saperi e metterli a disposizione di un territorio da tutelare.


Immaginiamo un’università che non sia un’autostrada da percorrere per la propria carriera, ma una piazza dove condividere il nostro desiderio di conoscenza e di trasformazione. In tutto il mondo le persone riempiono le strade e dalle università ai porti tutto si può bloccare: l’occupazione della Sapienza è solo una prima pietra lanciata nella nostra città nella nuova ondata di rabbia e desiderio di riscatto che sta animando tutto il Mediterraneo.


Con questa occupazione vogliamo avanzare pretese rivolte al Governo, al Ministero dell’Università e della Ricerca, all’Università di Pisa e all’Azienda Regionale per il Diritto allo Studio (DSU Toscana).


Al governo – contro la finanziaria di guerra, contro il carovita


Chiediamo:


1. Il reinvestimento in istruzione, ricerca e sanità di tutti i fondi aggiuntivi previsti per la difesa nella nuova legge di bilancio del 2027.


2. Il ripristino del taglio delle accise sui carburanti di 24,4 centesimi complessivi.


3. La modifica del Codice degli appalti, affinché ci sia una progressiva internalizzazione dellə lavoratorə, a partire dalle università.


4. Un aumento di 5 miliardi di euro del Fondo di Finanziamento Universitario.


Al Ministero – contro la privatizzazione degli studentati, contro l’università trattata come fosse


un’azienda

Chiediamo inoltre che vengano resi disponibili gli altri 27 mila posti letto promessi dal PNRR e non ancora realizzati.


2. La modifica dei criteri di premialità nella distribuzione dei finanziamenti all’Università.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: No fue una guerra civil: fue un golpe de Estado contra la República española
content:
Una república legítima.


Lo que nos enseñaron como «guerra civil» empezó como un golpe de Estado contra un régimen legítimo. La República había nacido de las urnas en 1931 y, el 16 de febrero de 1936, el pueblo volvió a elegir un Gobierno del Frente Popular. Los militares que se alzaron el 18 de julio habían jurado lealtad a la República y rompieron su palabra para tomar el poder por la fuerza. Eran militares traidores, y su golpe fue ilegítimo: pretendía quebrar la legalidad y acabar con la democracia.


Un golpe fallido, salvado desde el extranjero.


El golpe fracasó en Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia y buena parte del país, porque el pueblo salió a defender su República. Con la flota republicana vigilando el estrecho de Gibraltar, el Ejército de África no podía cruzar. Fueron los aviones alemanes e italianos los que hicieron posible el traslado de las tropas. El propio Hitler lo reconoció años después: dijo que Franco debería erigir un monumento al Junkers Ju 52. Sin esa ayuda, el golpe no habría podido continuar.


Hitler, Mussolini y las tropas coloniales.


Alemania envió la Legión Cóndor, con aviación, artillería, carros de combate e instructores. Italia envió decenas de miles de soldados, una cifra que, según las estimaciones más altas, rondaría los 100.000 efectivos si se cuentan aviadores, marinos y relevos, además de aviones, submarinos y buques de guerra. Las aviaciones alemana e italiana bombardearon a la población civil: Madrid desde noviembre de 1936, Gernika en abril de 1937 y Barcelona en marzo de 1938. Franco, además, trajo de África entre 60.000 y 80.000 soldados marroquíes, integrados en buena parte en las tropas regulares indígenas, los Regulares, que fueron empleados contra el pueblo español. Sin esa ayuda y sin esas tropas, los sublevados no lo habrían tenido tan fácil para doblegar a un pueblo que defendía su libertad, su democracia y su derecho a decidir.


Una República abandonada.


Francia, el Reino Unido y casi todas las democracias europeas le dieron la espalda a la República mediante la política de No Intervención, que Alemania e Italia violaron a la vista de todos. Churchill, que se negó a estrechar la mano del embajador republicano, encarna bien esa actitud: las élites europeas temían más una República con reformas sociales que a Hitler y Mussolini. La Unión Soviética fue el principal apoyo estatal en el envío de armas, mientras que México también prestó ayuda a la República. A ello se sumaron unos 35.000 voluntarios de las Brigadas Internacionales, llegados de decenas de países para defenderla.


Terror y exterminio.


Los sublevados no querían solo ganar: querían exterminar al adversario político. En Badajoz, en agosto de 1936, las columnas del Ejército de África asesinaron a miles de personas; en Málaga, en febrero de 1937, la población civil que huía por la carretera hacia Almería fue ametrallada desde el mar y desde el aire. En Galicia, donde el golpe triunfó de inmediato, miles de personas fueron asesinadas por ser sindicalistas, alcaldes, maestros o, simplemente, por ser de izquierdas. Las mujeres sufrieron violaciones, torturas y rapados de cabeza, prácticas que el general Queipo de Llano alentó desde la radio.


La Iglesia bendijo el golpe como una «cruzada» y siguió legitimando la dictadura. Franco fue presentado como «Caudillo de España por la gracia de Dios». Hoy, más de cien mil desaparecidos siguen en unas 6.000 fosas, y no hay herida que pueda cerrarse sin verdad ni justicia.


La Transición que no hizo justicia


Después de la dictadura no hubo juicio, ni verdad, ni reparación suficientes. La Transición fue un borrón y cuenta nueva: la Ley de Amnistía de 1977 contribuyó a garantizar la impunidad de los responsables de los crímenes del franquismo. Los franquistas no rindieron cuentas por sus crímenes y muchos de ellos se incorporaron a la política. De Alianza Popular, fundada por antiguos ministros de Franco, surgió el Partido Popular, y de ese espacio político nació Vox.


Décadas de silencio permitieron que las mentiras se repitieran y que la historia se prostituyera. Hoy, un partido como Vox se niega a condenar el golpe y la dictadura; hay quien convierte en héroes a los fascistas y hay jóvenes que levantan el brazo y gritan «¡Viva Franco!». Rajoy dejó a cero la partida presupuestaria destinada a la memoria histórica, y el PP ha gobernado de la mano de Vox en comunidades autónomas y ayuntamientos.


Había que hacer justicia, reparar a las víctimas y contar la verdad …

author: Mitchell Plitnick
title: As US and Israel Plot Iran Escalation, Regional Powers Scramble to Avert It
content:
Saudi, Pakistani, and Turkish leaders met with Iranian officials in Tehran, signaling their reticence to renew the war.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The first of two elections that many believe are the final bell before all out war is resumed against Iran is now complete. Although it seems likely that the efforts to cobble together a governing coalition in Israel, if that is even possible, will take weeks, the American midterms are expected to be the last milestone before the United States and Israel launch a massive attack on Iran.

There is no doubt that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is almost bursting with anticipation of the bloodshed to come. Donald Trump, as always, seems unsure of how to proceed, but seems very uncomfortable with the situation as it stands, while also being unwilling to make the concessions necessary to end this futile, destructive war he started for no good reason.

Iran can do little to deter an American attack, if that is what Trump decides to do. But it can retaliate with devastating consequences, which will be felt by its Gulf Arab neighbors, Israel, and the global economy.

That is why the countries of the newly created Mecca Pact — Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Türkiye — took the dramatic step of meeting Iranian officials in Tehran.

Iran trumpeted the meeting as demonstrating the seriousness with which the Sunni Muslim states take the Islamic Republic, meeting in the Iranian capital rather than in a third country.

Saudi Arabia said the meeting was aimed at mediating between the United States and Iran, but there is no evidence the United States had any part in the planning of this meeting. Indeed, the indications are the opposite; one purpose of the confab was to establish regional dialogue specifically on security matters.

Participants included Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff Field Marshall Asim Munir, Saudi Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Turkish Director of National Intelligence Ibrahim Kalin. They met with Iran’s Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei.

The fact that the meeting included leaders of the countries’ respective militaries indicates that the description of the meeting — that it was to deal with regional security — is likely accurate.

And, while little has been made public about the substance of the meeting, it also seems fair to say that there was little progress that could have been made on the major issues—the war with U.S. and the ongoing battles between Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni Ansar Allah.

Regarding Ansar Allah, Saudi Arabia was feeling Iran out to see if they would intervene with the Yemeni fighters whom the Saudis have been unable to defeat.

But Iran doesn’t have much reason to do so. While they could benefit from pulling the Saudis away from the American war effort, the compromises Tehran would have to make are far too great.

Reports out of Israel state that the Saudis offered Ansar Allah $1 billion for a ceasefire. But the Yemeni group will not budge on its understandable demand that Saudi Arabia drop its air blockade of Yemen.

This is not an issue Iran can try to mediate. If they try to get Ansar Allah to compromise on the air blockade, it undermines their argument that the United States must end its sea blockade of Iran.

Iran supports Ansar Allah’s cause, but if they thought they could get concessions from the Saudis on the kingdom’s support for American military efforts, Ansar Allah might find it reasonable to agree to a temporary ceasefire to help their ally.

But they cannot compromise on the air blockade, nor would Iran want them to. As long as Saudi Arabia maintains its efforts to block air traffic in Yemen, they can’t buy their way out of Ansar Allah attacks.

On the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, the Saudis are very worried, as are all the countries of the Gulf and their neighbors. They should be, given that Trump has warned the Gulf states to get ready for a “short, intense military campaign.” Considering that the war started on February 27 was supposed to end in just a few days, or weeks at most, no one is counting on the “short” part. But it is likely to be intense, and that intensity will be felt in Iran and the Gulf Arab states.

The problem for Iran is that its interlocutors can do little to turn Trump’s mind. Even Saudi Arabia, which is in a terrible position …

author: Agenda2029
title: Sabotage gegen Rheinmetall – Niemals Kriegstüchtig!
content:
In Kassel soll das größte Panzerwerk Europas gebaut werden. Wir stellen uns dagegen, zur Rüstungshauptstadt für die kommenden Kriege zu werden. Deshalb haben wir in der Nacht die Baustelle des Logistikzentrums von Rheinmetall in Kassel-Calden sabotiert und mehrere Bagger und Radlager angezündet.


Zeitenwende in Nordhessen


Wer in Nordhessen lebt, spürt was Zeitenwende heißt. Tag für Tag überschlagen sich die Nachrichten von Rüstungsinvestitionen. Fast kein Abend vergeht ohne Panzer in unseren Straßen zu sehen, die in die Kriegsgebiete der Welt exportiert werden. Kaum ein Kommunalpolitiker, mittelständisches Unternehmen oder Forschungsstandort der nicht hofft, etwas von den Milliarden der Zeitenwende abzubekommen.


Wir haben uns dafür entschieden, dabei nicht länger zuzuschauen und ein zentrales Projekt der Aufrüstungskampagne angegriffen: den Defence Hub Nordhessen von Rheinmetall.


Der Defence Hub Nordhessen umfasst den Ausbau des Panzerwerks in Kassel sowie den Bau eines Logistikzentrums auf 30.000 Quadratmetern und eines militärischen Drohnenzentrums am Kassel-Airport. Mit 260 Millionen Euro von Rheinmetall und über 20 Millionen Euro vom Land Hessen soll das Projekt bis Ende 2027 hochgezogen werden.


Für das Pressespektakel zum Auftakt verkündete Rheinmetall Chef Armin Papperger stolz: Kassel wird zukünftig das größte Panzerwerk Europas und „eine neue Drehscheibe“ der Rüstungsindustrie sein. Boris Rhein ergänzte: Der kriselnde Flughafen Kassel-Calden wird „künftig noch stärker als militärische Drehscheibe, für Trainingsflüge der Bundeswehr sowie zur Erforschung und Erprobung neuer Drohnen-Technologie“ dienen.


Während jeden Monat Millionen an Steuergeldern in einen leeren Flughafen versenkt werden, von dem nur die Privatjets von Superreichen starten, soll das Aufrüstungsprogramm nun die Rettung sein: Drohnen, Bundeswehrflüge und Logistik ersetzen die Passagiere und Urlaubsgäste, die partout nicht kommen wollen.


Mit Staatsgeldern in die Krise


Was in Kassel-Calden passiert, ist ein Sinnbild für die Zeitenwende in Deutschland: Der Staat tritt als Auftraggeber auf und versucht mit Milliarden an Rüstungsinvestitionen die schwächelnde Wirtschaft anzukurbeln. Deutschland tritt die Flucht nach vorne an. Wenn die Autoproduktion auf dem Weltmarkt nicht mehr konkurrenzfähig ist, dann immerhin der Leopard-Panzer und vielleicht auch bald wieder das deutsche Heer.


In einer Zeit, die weltweit von imperialistischen Konflikten und Kriegen geprägt ist, will die Bundesrepublik ihre Krise durch militärische Aufrüstung lösen und zukünftig ohne die USA an der Spitze Europas stehen können. Was uns als notwendige Investitionen in die Verteidigungsfähigkeit verkauft wird, ist die Option, die eigenen Interessen wie Zugang zu Ressourcen und Handelsrouten mit militärischen Mitteln außerhalb Deutschlands durchsetzen zu können. Der Bau von eigenen Langstreckenwaffen oder die Befugnisse der Geheimdienste zur Sabotage im Ausland sind offensive Fähigkeiten. Es ist die Möglichkeit, künftig weiter die Konfrontation mit dem russischen Regime um die Vormachtstellung in Osteuropa eingehen zu können.


Von der Drehscheibe …


Wir wissen aus allen Konflikten der Großmächte, dass am Ende die einfachen Menschen, die Frauen und die Jugendlichen am meisten unter den Folgen des Krieges leiden werden. Nicht Armin Papperger und Boris Rhein oder deren Kinder sollen im Schützengraben von der Drohne zerfetzt werden, sondern wir. Wenn wir den Kriegsvorbereitungen nicht international entgegen treten, haben wir bald keine Perspektive für unser Leben mehr.


Je mehr Geld in die Rüstungsprojekte fließt und je weiter der Umbau ziviler Wirtschaft zur Kriegsindustrie voranschreitet, desto größer wird auch hier die wechselseitige Abhängigkeit und die Verflechtung zwischen Rüstungskonzernen und den staatlichen Auftraggebern werden. Gleichzeitig gehen die Panzer, die am Ende von Rheinmetall und Co. durch Staatsgelder produziert werden, nicht wieder produktiv in den Wirtschaftskreislauf ein. Die Aufrüstung wird die Krise der letzten Jahre nicht lösen, sondern höchstens verschieben.


Wenn in ein paar Jahren die Hallen voll mit Panzern und Sprengköpfen sind, werden die Probleme der deutschen Schwerindustrie und der mittelständischen Zulieferer nicht gelöst sein. Für Kassel bedeutet das: Geht die staatliche Nachfrage nach Kriegswaffen in ein paar Jahren wieder zurück, wird auch die davon abhängige Industrie zusammenbrechen und zahlreiche Menschen ihre Arbeit …

author: daniel
title: Ein Tag BRD
content:
Der 30. September 2026 eignet sich exzellent als Tag der deutschen Menschenrechtsverletzungen.

Am frühen Nachmittag des 30. September verlassen rund ein Dutzend Menschen wütend und entsetzt das Landgericht Duisburg, unter ihnen Vater, Mutter und Schwester von Ibrahima Barry. Sie sind schon zu hören, bevor sie zu sehen sind: „Justice for Ibrahima!“, tönt es laut aus dem Inneren des Gebäudes. Wir, die wir draußen warten, stimmen mit ein und nehmen die uns Entgegenkommenden in den Arm und in unsere Kundgebung mit auf. „Ibrahima, das war Mord!“ Und doch sind die neun Polizist*innen, die Ibrahimas Leben an einem Januartag 2024 in Mülheim an der Ruhr beendet haben, soeben frei gesprochen worden. Nicht etwa, weil nicht nachzuweisen gewesen wäre, was sie gemacht haben: den 23-Jährigen mit Elektroschocks malträtieren, zu Boden werfen und das Gesicht nach unten drücken, ihn beleidigen, wie ein Paket verschnüren und Druck auf seinen Oberkörper ausüben, so lange bis ihm der Atem ausgeht und sein junger Körper aufgibt. Die tödlichen Handlungen können auf der Webseite von Forensis (1) in allen erschreckenden Details nachvollzogen werden, sie waren auch dem Gericht bekannt. Die neun Polizist*innen wurden freigesprochen, weil ein deutsches Gericht, diese neun Polizist*innen, ihre Ver-teidiger*innen und mit ihnen ein Großteil der deutschen Bevölkerung der Meinung sind, diese Art einen Menschen zu behandeln, sei gerechtfertigt, sei rechtens, sei so ganz richtig. „Notwehr“ sei das gewesen. Er habe sich schließlich gewehrt in seinem Todeskampf, habe unter den Polizeistiefeln, die ihm die Luft nahmen, nicht ausreichend still gehalten. Er habe schließlich auch gestört mit seinen psychischen Problemen, seinen lauten Schreien, seiner Anwesenheit in diesem Land. Folgerichtig mussten Vertreter*innen des deutschen Staates dem ein Ende setzen und andere Vertre-ter*innen des deutschen Staates mussten es für richtig befinden. Reine Notwehr! „Ihr habt mich umgebracht“, waren Ibrahimas letzte Worte. Wie soll einem angesichts dessen nicht das Herz in tausend Stücke zerspringen? Rest In Power, Ibrahima! Du wirst nicht vergessen.

Parallel dazu saßen an diesem 30. September ein paar hundert Kilometer südlich fünf junge Menschen zum 20. Mal in diesem Jahr hinter Panzerglas im berüchtigten Stuttgart-Stammheimer Hochsicherheitssaal und versuchten, ihrem Strafprozess zu folgen. Staatlicherseits wird das volle Repressionsrepertoire gegen die Ulm 5 aufgefahren. Die Stuttgarter Generalstaatsanwaltschaft macht ihnen unter dem Vorwurf der Bildung einer kriminellen Vereinigung den Prozess (2), weil sie ein Jahr zuvor in die Waffenschmiede von Elbit Systems in Ulm eingestiegen waren und dort einigen Sachschaden angerichtet haben. Die fünf wiederum machen Elbit Systems Deutschland und dem deutschen Staat den Prozess für ihre Komplizenschaft bei der Verübung eines Völkermords in Gaza – für die fortgesetzten Waffenlieferungen, für die Leugnung der Kriegsverbrechen an der palästinensischen Bevölkerung, für das ungestörte Betreiben einer Tochterfirma von Israels Hauptlieferanten von Kriegsgerät in Ulm. Dieses Geschäft mit dem Tod haben die fünf zu stören versucht. Nun zerren sie die Komplizenschaft des deutschen Staats auf die Stammheimer Bühne. Mittlerweile hat die Verteidigung deutlich herausgearbeitet, dass der Ulmer Sitz seit über hundert Jahren Geschäfte mit Völkermord macht und diese Firmenhistorie stolz auf der eigenen Webseite bewirbt. Die Blutspur zieht sich von den deutschen Kolonien des Kaiserreichs über die Beteiligung an Besatzung und Zwangsarbeit in der NS-Zeit bis zur heutigen KI-gesteuerten Kriegsmaschinerie, die Gaza in Schutt und Asche legt. Die 1903 gegründete „Gesellschaft für drahtlose Telegraphie Telefunken mbH“ lieferte mobile Funkstationen, die die deutschen Kolonialtruppen beim Völkermord an den Ova Herero und Nama logistisch-kommunikativ unterstützten. (3) Die Nachfolgefirma Telefunken profitierte zunächst von der Besetzung Polens, eröffnete ein Werk für militärische Komponenten in Lódź und verschleppte im Jahr 1944 etwa 1400 polnische Zwangsarbeiterinnen nach Ulm. (4) Elbit Systems führt seit 2007 die Geschäfte fort und liefert heute aus Ulm die Kommunikationstechnik, die die verschiedenen Kriegsgeräte der israelischen Armee vernetzt und die Zielbestimmung der zu Tötenden erleichtert.

Dies sind nur zwei Schlaglichter eines Tages in der BRD in September 2026. Wie soll einem angesichts dessen nicht das Herz in tausend Stücke zerspringen? …

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Hegseth visit exposes deepening US military intervention in the Philippines
content:
US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth attends a meeting in Cebu on October 28, 2026, together with other defense leaders from other countries. Photo from the Department of National Defense's Facebook page

For ILPS Philippines, these agreements are not merely defense arrangements. They further integrate the country into Washington’s military operations and its First Island Chain strategy against China.

The arrival of US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth in Cebu on October 28 has drawn condemnation from progressive groups, which warned that the Philippines is increasingly being drawn into Washington’s military and economic agenda at the expense of national sovereignty.

The International League of Peoples’ Struggle (ILPS) Philippines said Hegseth’s visit for the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting comes amid the Trump administration’s aggressive expansion of US military power in the Asia-Pacific and its preparations for greater confrontation with China.

The group described Hegseth as a key enforcer of Washington’s war agenda, criticizing Ferdinand Marcos Jr. administration for facilitating the growing US military presence in the country.

Under the Marcos administration, military cooperation between Manila and Washington has expanded through weapons deployments, joint military exercises, intelligence-sharing arrangements, and the increased use of Philippine military facilities.

Read: Missiles, markets, and massacres: Balikatan, ASEAN, and the war logic of US imperial decline*

During Hegseth’s March 2025 visit, the two governments agreed to deploy advanced US weapons, including the Navy Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System (NMESIS), expand high-end military exercises, strengthen defense-industrial cooperation, and launch joint cyber operations.

In October 2025, Hegseth and Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. announced a Task Force-Philippines to strengthen joint military planning and operational coordination. This was followed by a 15-year Communications Interoperability and Security Memorandum of Agreement (CISMOA) in May 2026, further institutionalizing secure military communications and information-sharing between the two countries.

These arrangements build on the General Security of Military Information Agreement (GSOMIA) and the nine Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) sites across the Philippines.

For ILPS Philippines, these agreements are not merely defense arrangements. They further integrate the country into Washington’s military operations and its First Island Chain strategy against China.

The consequences, the group warned, extend beyond military installations. With US forces increasingly capable of operating advanced weapons from Philippine territory, Filipino communities could become vulnerable to retaliation in the event of a regional conflict.

Read: Tacloban fishers slam Balikatan exercises

During the May 2026 Balikatan exercises, the US military reportedly launched a Tomahawk cruise missile from Tacloban Airport, demonstrating its capacity to conduct long-range missile strikes from Philippine soil.

“Our country is being transformed into a forward operating platform for US wars, exposing millions of Filipinos to the grave danger of retaliation, devastation, and death in a regional conflict,” ILPS Philippines said.

The group accused the Marcos administration of sacrificing national independence through its cooperation with Washington, using tensions with China to justify the expanding US military footprint.

While opposing China’s coercion and violations of Philippine sovereign rights, ILPS Philippines stressed that the country cannot defend its sovereignty by allowing another foreign power to use its territory for military operations and war preparations.

Progressive groups also warned that US intervention is not confined to military installations. They said Washington’s economic initiatives are tied to its strategic interests in the Philippines, particularly its access to critical resources and supply chains.

The Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP) condemned Hegseth’s visit, saying the US is pursuing both military access and greater control over resources through initiatives such as Pax Silica.

A US-led initiative seeking to secure supply chains for critical minerals, semiconductors, and other strategic technologies, Pax Silica could further open Philippine resources to foreign corporate interests, the farmers’ group warned.

author: anred
title: BDS reclama a Lula que rompa los vínculos económicos y militares con Israel: «es hora de pasar de las palabras a los hechos”
content:
Imagen: @cois4ruim


La reelección de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en Brasil generó expectativas en el movimiento internacional de solidaridad con Palestina, pero también reabrió el debate sobre la continuidad de los vínculos económicos, comerciales y militares entre Brasil e Israel. Andressa Oliveira Soares, co-coordinadora de políticas para América Latina del Comité Nacional Palestino del movimiento de Boicot, Desinversión y Sanciones (BDS), calificó el resultado electoral como “una pequeña gota de esperanza”, aunque reclamó que el próximo mandato traduzca las declaraciones diplomáticas en medidas concretas contra Israel. “Brasil ha frustrado los planes imperialistas de Estados Unidos en la región. Ahora, Brasil debe poner su peso geopolítico y económico al servicio de la defensa del derecho internacional”, sostuvo. Entre las principales exigencias, planteó interrumpir las exportaciones de petróleo a Israel, terminar los contratos militares, cancelar el tratado de libre comercio entre el Mercosur e Israel y suspender las importaciones de agrotóxicos, además de cortar los vínculos académicos, deportivos y culturales, por el genocidio que lleva adelante el gobierno de Benjamin Netanyahu contra el pueblo palestino en Gaza.

Por ANRed.


La

reelección de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva para su cuarto mandato en Brasil

 abrió nuevas expectativas y también exigencias en el movimiento internacional de solidaridad con Palestina. En un pronunciamiento difundido el lunes 26 de octubre, el

Comité Nacional Palestino del movimiento de Boicot, Desinversión y Sanciones (BDS)

planteó que el nuevo mandato presidencial

debe traducir las posiciones diplomáticas de Brasil contra el genocidio en Gaza en medidas concretas contra Israel

.


“La reelección de Lula en Brasil representa para Palestina una pequeña gota de esperanza para quienes creen en la justicia social y los derechos humanos en Latinoamérica y más allá.

El pueblo brasileño ha rechazado contundentemente a la ultraderecha, que en toda América Latina ha avanzado para fortalecer su alianza con el genocida Israel

. Brasil ha frustrado los planes imperialistas de Estados Unidos en la región. Ahora,

Brasil debe poner su peso geopolítico y económico al servicio de la defensa del derecho internacional

. Esta victoria debe traducirse en acciones decisivas en apoyo del derecho internacional para los pueblos oprimidos, desde Palestina hasta Brasil”, remarca el documento, que lleva la firma de

Andressa Oliveira Soares

, co-coordinadora de políticas para América Latina del movimiento.


El pronunciamiento reconoce las posiciones que Lula y sus anteriores gobiernos sostuvieron respecto de Palestina, pero advierte sobre la distancia entre esas declaraciones y las políticas económicas y comerciales: “

los gobiernos previos de Lula han sido favorables al reconocimiento de algunos derechos del pueblo palestino y se han manifestado contra el genocidio

. Sin embargo,

 aún no han dado pasos concretos para imponer sanciones legales efectivas a Israel, tal como lo estableció la Corte Internacional de Justicia

”, en referencia a las medidas provisionales dictadas en el proceso iniciado por Sudáfrica contra Israel por violaciones de la Convención para la Prevención y la Sanción del Delito de Genocidio.


En su momento,

Lula calificó de genocidio las acciones israelíes contra la población palestina y en septiembre de 2025 anunció que Brasil intervendría en el proceso iniciado por Sudáfrica ante la Corte Internacional de Justicia

. El 17 de septiembre de ese año, el país presentó formalmente una declaración de intervención en virtud del artículo 63 del Estatuto de la Corte, en tanto Estado firmante de la Convención contra el Genocidio. Sin embargo,

estas decisiones no implicaron una ruptura de las relaciones diplomáticas ni la suspensión integral de los vínculos comerciales con Israel

.


Uno de los principales puntos señalados por BDS es la continuidad del intercambio económico

. El tratado de libre comercio entre el Mercosur e Israel, firmado en 2007 y vigente para Brasil desde abril de 2010, continúa en funcionamiento. Según datos del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores brasileño, el intercambio comercial bilateral alcanzó los 1.900 millones de dólares durante 2025: Brasil exportó bienes por 568,6 millones e importó aproximadamente 1.300 millones.

 Entre las principales exportaciones brasileñas se encuentran carne bovina, soja y café, mientras que las importaciones incluyen …

author: PETA-Team
title: Ukraine: Freiwilliger Tierretter und Hund sterben nach Drohnenangriff
content:
Am 27. Oktober 2026 wurde ein Team von PETAs Partnerorganisation

Animal Rescue Kharkiv

 bei einer

Tierrettung in der Ukraine

 angegriffen: Zwei Drohnen trafen das Fahrzeug der Helfer:innen, zerschlugen die Windschutzscheibe und verletzten den 40-jährigen Helfer Jesse Adams und einen der geretteten Hunde tödlich. Wir von PETA Deutschland und unsere internationalen Partnerorganisationen betrauern den Verlust des engagierten Freiwilligen aus Kanada. 


Gleichzeitig zeigt der tödliche Angriff auf unser Partnerteam, wie gefährlich die Lage im ukrainischen Kriegsgebiet weiterhin für alle Lebewesen ist. Erfahren Sie hier mehr zu dem Angriff und wie Sie unseren Partnern und den Tieren vor Ort helfen können.

 

 


Schwerer Angriff auf Tierrettungsteam: Russische Drohnen töten Helfer bei der Rettung von Tieren und setzen Unterkunft in Brand 


Der tödliche Angriff ereignete sich, als Jesse Adams aus dem kanadischen Vancouver Island, und andere zivile Retter:innen unserer Partnerorganisation

Animal Rescue Kharkiv

 (ARK) Tiere in einen Transporter luden – einige von ihnen verletzt, alle vom Krieg tief verängstigt und evakuierungsbedürftig.  


Zwei Drohnen trafen das Fahrzeug, zerschlugen die Windschutzscheibe, verletzten Adams mit einer massiven Splitterexplosion und töteten einen

der geretteten Hunde

. Eine weitere Drohne traf das Haus, in dem die Tiere kurzfristig bis zur Abholung in das Projekt von ARK untergebracht waren, und setzte es in Brand.  


Rettungskräfte eilten herbei, um das Feuer zu löschen, Adams wurde sofort ins Krankenhaus transportiert – doch er verstarb während der Notoperation aufgrund seiner schweren Verletzungen. 


Weiterer Angriff auf vorübergehende Unterkunft der geretteten Tiere 


Währenddessen schlugen erneut zwei weitere Drohnen in das Haus ein, in dem die Tiere kurzfristig untergebracht waren. Die Unterkunft brannte lichterloh – doch alle Tiere konnten in Sicherheit gebracht werden. Dennoch sind alle Beteiligten schwer traumatisiert – das Einsatzteam und die

geretteten Tiere

. 


„Tiere führen keine Kriege, aber sie sind Opfer davon, müssen ohne Nahrung, Wasser oder tierärztliche Versorgung unter schweren Verletzungen leiden, es sei denn, jemand kommt ihnen zu Hilfe. PETA fordert alle auf, an die Tiere zu denken, die von Konflikten betroffen sind, und an die Helden, die ihr eigenes Leben riskieren, um ihnen zu helfen.“  

Ingrid Newkirk, PETA-Gründerin

 


PETA und ARK sind in tiefer Trauer um Jesse Adams  


Adams war Mitbegründer der

RainCoast Dog Rescue Society

 in Kanada und einer von zahlreichen Freiwilligen mit militärischer Grundausbildung und viel Erfahrung in gefährlichen Einsatzgebieten, die ARK-Teams vor Ort unterstützen.  


In einem seiner letzten Instagram-Beiträge vor einigen Tagen schrieb Adams darüber, wie er einer Familie geholfen hatte: Diese hatte sich geweigert, ihr Zuhause in einem Gebiet zu verlassen, das täglich von Drohnen, Bomben und Raketen getroffen wurde, bis sie wussten, dass ihre Tiere sicher evakuiert werden konnten. Adams und das ARK-Team halfen der Familie bei der Evakuierung ihrer mehr als ein Dutzend Tiere und schrieben dann über den Einsatz: 


„Wir sind die großen Risiken eingegangen, weil diese Menschen und Tiere dringend unsere Hilfe brauchten. Wir sind das Risiko eingegangen, weil wir wollten, dass jemand dasselbe für uns tut, wenn wir Hilfe brauchen. Wir sind das Risiko eingegangen, weil es nicht viele gibt, die es getan hätten.“ 


Lebensgefahr für Menschen und Tiere: Angriff zeigt erneut, wie wichtig die Hilfe vor Ort ist 


Seit Beginn des russischen Angriffskrieges im Februar 2022 unterstützen wir von PETA Deutschland gemeinsam mit unseren internationalen Partnerorganisationen durch unseren Global Compassion Fund die lebensrettende, aber auch lebensgefährliche Arbeit des ARK-Teams in der Ukraine. Denn die Retter:innen arbeiten unter der ständigen

Gefahr von Bomben

, Beschuss und Gewalt, um verängstigte, traumatisierte,

verletzte

 und oft stark unterernährte Tiere in der Ukraine zu retten.  


In den vergangenen Jahren wurde ein großes Projekt vor Ort aufgebaut, sodass bisher fast 40.000 Katzen, Hunde, Pferde und andere Tiere gerettet, medizinisch versorgt und liebevoll aufgepäppelt werden konnten.  


Immer wieder lebensgefährliche und tödliche Angriffe auf Helfer:innen

+

author: webadmin
title: No Land, No Hunting
content:
Thank you to West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs for this guest article.


On Thursday 8th October, West Midlands Hunt Sabs (WMHS) held a protest outside The Bower House in Shipston on Stour. The restaurant is owned by Andrew Stephen Bower Knight, who continually allows, not only the Warwickshire Hunt to illegally hunt foxes on his land at Compton Scorpion, but the North Cotswold Hunt too.


The protest caused quite a stir amongst the pro-hunt community prompting the British Hound Sports Association (BHSA) to publish a social media post stating

“Rural businesses are under attack by urban saboteurs.”


Visitors to The Bower House in Shipston on Stour were made aware that business owner, Andrew Stephen Bower Knight, enables illegal fox hunting.


The campaign against the Warwickshire Hunt is one that spans back years and is steeped in controversy, including the fact that Warwickshire Police entered into a “secret deal” with the hunt when they withdrew the Community Protection Notice that they had been issued.


WMHS have always highlighted the importance of holding landowners to account, something which featured heavily in the campaign against the now defunct Atherstone Hunt. The Hunting Act stipulates that should a landowner allow the hunting of a wild mammal with dogs on their land then they are breaking the law.


Demonstrations took place outside businesses that supported the now defunct Atherstone Hunt.

© West Midlands Hunt Sabs


Section 3.1 of the Hunting Act 2004 states;

“A person commits an offence if he knowingly permits land which belongs to him to be entered or used in the course of the commission of an offence under Section 1.”

Section 1 of the Hunting Act states;

“A person commits an offence if he hunts a wild mammal with a dog.”


“Trail” hunting does not exist, a fact which was openly discussed during a 2020

webinar

 held by the then Hunting Office, now the BHSA. It was the hunting community who coined the term “smokescreen” to describe “trail” hunting, as they discussed ways that hunts could continue to break the law. Now they are acting the victim, especially when landowners are reminded of their part in this pantomime.


WMHS work alongside other anti-hunt groups such as Locals Against the Warwickshire Hunt and Warwickshire Hunt Watch to use a varied approach to their campaigning. One of which is writing to landowners to remind them of their responsibilities and to inform them of what the Warwickshire Hunt are capable of.


As well as detailing the contents of the Hunting Act, the letters remind landowners that only last year, Ben Halsall of the Warwickshire Hunt was convicted under the Hunting Act after a fox was killed. The letter also states that the presiding judge at the trial made a statement that there was

“no evidence at all of any trail being laid.”


In 2023 this fox was killed by the Warwickshire Hunt, on land owned by Marcus Dill of Idlicote House Estate. Hunt member Ben Field was found guilty; however, no charges were brought against Marcus.


The letter goes on to say that

“The new huntsman, Jack Weedon has previously been caught on camera blocking an active badger sett in a Site of Special Scientific Interest and has recently been cautioned under a Section 4a Public Order offence.”


The protest held on 8th October took place during a book signing event by Dame Prue Leith. The aim; to make people aware of the fact that the business, through its owner, is linked to illegal fox hunting. However, the pro-hunt community have tried to claim that by protesting, sabs are putting people’s livelihoods at risk, rather than focusing on the fact that the only person putting any livelihood at risk is Andrew, by continuing to break the law and enable an illegal fox hunt.


If people choose to not use an establishment or support a business because they facilitate fox hunting, that’s their prerogative.


The Warwickshire Hunt have already lost a lot of land, some of which is through landowners rescinding their permission due to public outcry. In October 2025 Warwickshire Christmas Tree Farm very publicly withdrew permission for the hunt to use their land, stating that due to the public’s disgust at their affiliation with the Warwickshire Hunt they were left with no choice.
