author: Sara Luterman
title: Nursing Home Residents Have a Right to Vote — Despite What Trump CMS Agency Says
content:
The Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Cindy Napolitan and her daughter Melissa have multiple sclerosis, a degenerative condition in which the immune system attacks the brain, spinal cord and nerves. They have lived together at a nursing home in Mesquite, Texas, for nine years. In previous elections, Cindy and Melissa Napolitan voted by mail, but this year they took an unusual step: They voted in person. They worried their mail-in ballots — and even their in-person votes — may not be counted.

“I’ve never worried like this before. I’ve never worried that I don’t have the proper ID. I’ve never worried that somebody is going to intimidate me. Will I encounter somebody that’s going to threaten me or make me feel less than? So yeah, I’m very worried, and I shouldn’t be,” Cindy Napolitan said. “I shouldn’t have to be worried about stuff like that. This is the 19th Amendment. I’m allowed to vote.”

Nursing home residents are guaranteed the right to vote. Around two-thirds of all nursing home residents in the United States are women, making aging and long-term care gendered issues.

There is no data on how many nursing home residents exercise that right. Cindy, 70, and Melissa Napolitan, 48, at least, feel like they’ve had good experiences with voting at their facility. Cindy Napolitan, in particular, has worked with the activities coordinator to organize rides to the polls for her, her daughter and other interested residents.

“We are scheduled to go on the first day of early voting. So in case there are any issues that we come across, we still have time to rectify the situation and be allowed to vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan are more concerned this year than in previous years about government interference and voter suppression. Their fears are not unfounded: Experts and advocates for the rights of nursing home residents, older adults and people with disabilities are worried too.

In July, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services rescinded previous guidance affirming that nursing home residents have the right to vote.

“The memo does not alter the underlying law. Nursing homes are governed by the Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 and its implementing regulations,” said Nina Kohn, a professor at Syracuse University and expert on elder law. “That law still requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights as Americans.”

The memo also emphasized voter fraud in nursing homes, specifically around mail-in ballots. For years, President Trump has disparaged mail-in ballots, insisting without evidence that fraudulent votes by mail had a role in his loss during the 2020 presidential election. His comments have led to some states restricting who can use a mail-in ballot and in what contexts.

According to experts, including Kohn, there is no evidence that voter fraud is a serious or widespread problem in nursing homes. Instead, Kohn is concerned about the chilling effect that it may have on residents’ rights.

“The language in the memo itself is intimidating, and it may understandably make staff think that they could face criminal prosecution or be in some other form of legal trouble if they help residents vote,” Kohn said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan do everything together — and on Monday, they voted together. They are also roommates at the facility; most people living in nursing homes are assigned roommates who are strangers.

“Unlike other people that have roommates that don’t get along, I’m very lucky and fortunate that I have somebody that loves me and I love her,” Cindy Napolitan said.

This is the second time Cindy and Melissa Napolitan have voted in person since entering a nursing home. The first time was during the 2024 presidential election.

“I’ve been checking my status weekly to make sure that I haven’t been dropped off the voter rolls, making sure my daughter and I don’t have some sort of issue that says that we can’t vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

People living in nursing homes and other long-term care facilities face specific barriers. Some residents may need assistance filling out their ballots because they lack the movement or dexterity to hold a pen or press buttons on a computer screen. People with dexterity or coordination issues may also be unable to produce the same signature twice …

author: Mostafa Hosny
title: ‘Citizens’ health’ session at Egypt Forum 2026 boasts spending success with no mention of declining hospital bed numbers
content:
On Tuesday, the second day of Egypt Forum 2026, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar described the political leadership’s support for the healthcare sector as unprecedented.


Speaking at the “citizen’s health”

session

 of Egypt Forum 2026, he said the approach dated back to the beginning of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s presidency in 2014, when, he

said,

 Egypt faced a massive “disease burden,” with a lack of data and years of inadequate budget allocations that had failed to meet developmental ambitions for the system, particularly as population growth accelerated.


The minister said the state’s development plan had delivered gains in the sector, citing 16 presidential initiatives that had benefited 95 million citizens at a cost of LE44 billion. 


Abdel Ghaffar stressed that success in healthcare should not be measured by spending levels, but by the results citizens ultimately experience.


Mada Masr looked into some of those results, drawing from government

data

 published by the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS).


One clear result over the time period is the notable decline in the number of beds in public hospitals between 2013 and 2024, with a drop from around 98,291 to 84,225. 


Over the same period, the number of beds in private hospitals rose from 26,009 to 36,014. 


Still, the combined total of beds in public and private hospitals fell from 124,300 in 2013 to 120,239 in 2024.


While Abdel Ghaffar portrayed inadequate budget allocations as a problem of the past, the state

has consistently fallen short

 of the constitutionally mandated minimum for healthcare spending.

 Article 18 of the Constitution requires the state to allocate at least three percent of gross national product to public healthcare starting in FY 2016/17 and gradually increase spending over time. The state has not met this threshold since the Constitution was adopted in 2014. Since then, healthcare spending has not exceeded 1.7 percent of GNP in most years.


The government allocated 1.51 percent of GNP to healthcare in the current fiscal year’s budget, half the constitutional minimum. 


Meanwhile, the government has

introduced

 a different method for calculating budget allocations that allows it to claim it is meeting the minimum spending threshold.

 


Rather than using its previous classification, which was based on the Health Ministry’s expenditure, the government now uses a “broader and more comprehensive” definition. Under this new definition, healthcare expenditure also encompasses spending by a number of off-budget economic authorities and companies as well as “any other entities providing healthcare services, such as police and military hospitals, Al-Azhar hospitals, the comprehensive health insurance system and its associated programs,” a Finance Ministry source previously told Mada Masr. Without publicly available data on these entities’ healthcare spending, it is impossible to verify whether they bring total annual healthcare spending to the constitutionally mandated minimum.


The same expansion of what constitutes annual “health spending” also allows the government to include the budgetary allocation for these entities’ debt repayments as investment in the sector, according to the same source.


The president

confessed

 three years ago that the state is not meeting the constitutional requirements, saying in a public address that “the required numbers aren’t available, folks.”

 His comment came days after the government’s assertion that it was meeting the required spending levels.


Aside from its commentary on expenditure, the government’s Egypt Forum 2026 also highlighted the Universal Health Insurance System, one of the leading presidential health initiatives.


Egypt’s Healthcare Authority head, Ahmed al-Sobky,

described

 the system as a comprehensive reform of Egypt’s healthcare sector, capping an “enormous leap forward” under Sisi, following earlier historic transformations under King Fouad I and former President Gamal Abdel Nasser.


Shortly before the forum, the government began promoting the second phase of the Universal Health Insurance System, launching a pilot phase in Minya Governorate. 


The first phase launch in the governorates of Port Said, Ismailia, Suez, South Sinai, Luxor and Aswan began in 2018 and was

completed

 in 2025.

title: Ulus: Healthcare must be free and accessible to all
content:
Structural problems in public hospitals and shortcomings in healthcare services are making it increasingly difficult for citizens to access medical care. People struggling to secure appointments through the Central Physician Appointment System (MHRS) sometimes have to wait at least 15 days just to submit an appointment request. Patients who eventually manage to obtain appointments after considerable effort must then try to explain their health problems within limited consultation times due to overcrowding in hospitals.


Difficulties in securing appointments and restrictions on consultation times are further deepening problems concerning the quality and accessibility of healthcare services.


Mehmet Nuri Ulus, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Health and Social Service Workers’ Union (SES), spoke to ANF about the problems facing public hospitals.


‘Healthcare is not being transformed, it is going backwards’


Ulus recalled that the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government has introduced healthcare reform and transformation programmes since 2002. He said that the policies implemented in recent years have caused serious problems in healthcare services and continued: “The AKP government has announced numerous programmes under the names of healthcare reform and healthcare transformation. However, particularly over the past 10 to 15 years, what has been called healthcare transformation has, from our perspective, meant collapse and regression. We have experienced both the COVID-19 pandemic and the earthquake during this period. These major crises showed us just how inadequate the healthcare system was in responding to the problems that arose.


The healthcare system should have been prepared for these crises and should have had the capacity to meet society's healthcare needs. Healthcare is a service that must be provided within the framework of the social welfare state. Everyone must be able to receive healthcare services equally, accessibly and in their mother tongue.


However, in recent years, we have seen healthcare services increasingly turn into a system in which those who have money can access care more easily. The proliferation of private hospitals is one aspect of this. Another is the emergence of an approach in which even public hospitals link faster access to certain tests, radiological examinations, medical reports and surgical procedures to payment. This undermines the principle that healthcare services should be equal for everyone.”


‘Physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues’


Ulus addressed the appointment crisis in the healthcare system, pointing out that the queues once seen outside hospitals now continue through the Central Physician Appointment System. He said appointment systems should make healthcare more accessible, but many citizens are currently unable to secure appointments.


Ulus said: “The AKP government used to say that people had to go to hospitals early in the morning and wait in queues to see a doctor. Today, physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues. Instead of waiting for hours outside hospitals, people now try to book appointments on their phones or online. However, when you access the system, you cannot find an available appointment. The queues have therefore not disappeared; they have simply changed form. Citizens now find themselves waiting in front of digital systems to access healthcare.


People face serious difficulties securing appointments, particularly in departments such as ear, nose and throat, ophthalmology and dermatology. Citizens who cannot obtain appointments are then forced to turn to private hospitals. However, considering the economic crisis, the struggle to make ends meet and the housing problems in Turkey, not everyone has the financial means to seek treatment at private hospitals.


As a result, the inability to access healthcare has become another dimension of economic hardship. Healthcare should be free and accessible, yet citizens are forced to stretch their financial resources to obtain the medical care they need.”


‘The budget is not allocated to preventive healthcare services’


Ulus said that the problems facing the healthcare system are not limited to difficulties in securing appointments. He drew attention to the following issues: “When we look at the Ministry of Health's budget and healthcare policies, we see that preventive healthcare services are consistently pushed into the background. title: Söke Ekmek ve Gül açıklaması: Her çocuğa okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı yemek istiyoruz
content:
Aydın - Söke'de Belediye Meydanı’nda Söke Ekmek ve Gül "Bir Öğün Ücretsiz Sağlıklı Yemek Güvenli Okul Güvenli Ulaşım İstiyoruz” diyerek basın açıklaması yaptı.

Söke Ekmek ve Gül’ün çağrısıyla yapılan açıklamaya veliler, Söke Kadın Dayanışma Derneği ve Söke Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri de destek verdi. "Bir öğün ücretsiz sağlıklı yemek güvenli okul güvenli ulaşım istiyoruz” pankartının açıldığı basın açıklamasıni Söke Ekmek ve Gül adına öğrenci velisi Huri Abrinç okudu.

Çocukların okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek yiyebilmesi için yıllardır ülkenin dört bir yanında ve Söke’de aralıksız mücadele ettiklerini belirten Abrinç; “Söke Ekmek ve Gül olarak imza kampanyaları düzenledik, stantlar açtık, çocukların beslenme hakkını kararlılıkla savunduk. 2022 yılında Ekmek ve Gül tarafından başlatılan, 2023’te Kocaeli Ekmek ve Gül Kadın Dayanışma Derneği’nin çalışmalarıyla büyüyen, Esenyalı Kadın Dayanışma Derneği üyesi bir kadının hukuki mücadelesine kadar uzanan bu talep; bugün Türkiye’nin her köşesindeki kadınların, velilerin, öğretmenlerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin ortak talebidir. Toplanan binlerce imza, yapılan basın açıklamaları ve dayanışma ağları bu ihtiyacın ne kadar hayati, acil ve vazgeçilmez olduğunu defalarca kanıtlamıştır.

Çünkü biliyoruz ki derinleşen ekonomik kriz ortamında çocukların okula aç gittiği, ailelerin beslenme çantalarını doldurmakta zorlandığı, temel gıda ürünlerinin dahi lüks hâline geldiği bir ülkede; sağlıklı beslenme bir lütuf veya yardım değil, en temel insan hakkıdır. Çocuklar açken eğitimde fırsat eşitliğinden ya da nitelikli bir eğitimden söz edilemez” dedi.

Yürütülen bu haklı mücadeleler ve yükselen kamuoyu baskısı sonucunda Millî Eğitim Bakanlığının 5-19 Ekim tarihleri arasında ücretsiz okul yemeğine ilişkin velilerin görüşlerini almak amacıyla bir anket süreci yürüttüğünü hatırlatan Abrinç: “Yıllardır dile getirilen bu yakıcı ihtiyacı anlamak için çocukların açlığının bu kadar derinleşmesini bekleyen Bakanlığa soruyoruz: Velilerin ve kadınların sesi neden bugüne kadar duyulmadı” sorusunu sordu.

Bakanlığın adım atması önemli olsa da, yürütülen anketin kapsamı, erişilebilirliği ve yöntemi ciddi soru işaretleri doğurduğunu vurgulayan Abrinç anketle ilgili eksiklikleri sıraladı:

İnternet üzerinden yürütülen ankete pek çok veli eşit biçimde katılamamıştır. Veliler ankete ulaşmaya çalıştıklarında "yetkiniz yok" uyarılarıyla, sistemde yaşanan teknik sorunlarla karşılaşmış; internet ve telefon imkânı bulunmayan ya da dijital araçları kullanmakta zorlanan aileler süreçten tamamen izole edilmiştir. Ayrıca anket hakkında velilere yeterli bilgilendirme yapılmamıştır.

Edindiğimiz bilgilere göre ilkokul öğrencileri anket kapsamı dışında tutulmuş, süreç yalnızca ortaokul ve lise düzeyine sıkıştırılmıştır. Oysa en temel gelişim çağındaki ilkokul ve okul öncesi çocukların beslenme hakkı nasıl göz ardı edilebilir?

Servis imkânlarının kaldırılması veya kısıtlanmasıyla mağdur edilen taşımalı eğitim kapsamındaki aileler, bu anket hakkında da yeterince bilgilendirilmemiştir. Çocukların ulaşım ve beslenme ihtiyaçları birlikte değerlendirilmelidir.”

“İnternete erişemeyen, yetki engeline takılan ya da anket kapsamına alınmayan çocukların sağlıklı beslenmeye ihtiyacı yok mu? Çocukların en temel hakkı, teknik aksaklıklarla dolu bir anketin sonucuna ya da hangi eğitim kademesinde olduğuna indirgenebilir mi?” sorularını soran Abrinç, “Bir ankete katılamamış olmak, ücretsiz yemek ihtiyacının olmadığı anlamına gelmez! Çocukların açlığı anket sorularıyla giderilemez; beslenme sorumluluğu yalnızca ailelerin ve kadınların omuzlarına yıkılamaz” ifadelerini kullandı

Mıllî Eğitim Bakanlığına ve yetkililere çağrı yapan Abrinç şu talepleri sıraladı

Eşit ve Koşulsuz Hak: Okul öncesinden liseye kadar, kamu okullarındaki tüm öğrencilere ayrım yapılmaksızın her gün bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek derhal sağlanmalıdır.

Anket Sonucu Beklenmemelidir: Ücretsiz okul yemeği bir anketin sonucuna bağlanmadan, bütçe bahanelerinin arkasına sığınmadan kalıcı bir kamu hizmeti olarak uygulamaya konulmalıdır.

Şeffaflık ve Hesap Verilebilirlik: Yapılan anketin kaç veliye ulaştığı, hangi kademeleri kapsadığı ve sonuçların nasıl değerlendirildiği kamuoyuyla açık ve şeffaf bir şekilde paylaşılmalıdır.

Erişilebilir Katılım Yöntemleri: Dijital araçları kullanamayan veya erişim sorunu yaşayan veliler için yüz yüze görüşmeler, basılı formlar ve okullar aracılığıyla katılım kanalları oluşturulmalıdır.

author: Chandra Bozelko
title: I’m Done With Mental Health Providers
content:
B

ack in the early 2000s, my parents had me involuntarily hospitalized several times. I got the whole psychiatric smorgasbord: strapped to a gurney when I was perfectly able to walk, injected with medications against my will,

spoken slowly and loudly to

 like I was incapacitated. I got the works, except for one hallmark experience of forcible treatment: I was never restrained because I didn’t do anything to endanger anyone. When people ask me why I didn’t kick or punch the nurse administering the shots, I don’t have a good answer. I’m just not good at violence.


The psychiatrists are, though. They never physically struck me — with all the damage they inflicted, they didn’t need to — but I saw one esteemed Yale shrink throw a red-haired woman onto a couch.


Because I criticized the system and I wouldn’t agree to debilitating regimens of medications, I was labeled as having no insight into my own illness. That’s worse than any diagnosis they can muster. To them, I was so ill that even the most severe psychiatric interventions would never help me. One famed Columbia doctor told my parents to abandon me, like leave me stranded there in New York, because I was terminally mentally ill.


He was just one example of psychiatry’s total divorce from the healing arts. One NYU psychiatrist left a message on my parents’ voicemail calling them “pieces of excrement” because they supposedly hadn’t paid his bill, only to call three minutes later to say in a pleasant lilt: “Never mind, I found the check.” Or the Fifth Avenue psychiatrist who wore women’s eyeglass frames (but not in that accidental and ironic way George Costanza did on Seinfeld) and told me I should become a firefighter because I had muscular thighs.


Cross-legged, I sat in front of Barnes and Noble’s psychology rack and picked out books by prominent critics of modern psychiatry whose titles told my story: Peter Breggin’s

Your Drug May Be Your Problem

, and

Antipsychiatry: Quackery Squared, The Manufacture of Madness

, and

Psychiatric Slavery

 by Thomas Szasz.


The books confirmed what I had surmised. We’ve buried trauma with diagnostic codes. We’ve medicalized feeling too much or not enough. We’ve pathologized normal responses to abnormal situations. I refused to see any practitioner who worked within these constructs because they’re contrived, and designed to accomplish several goals that don’t include my health.


I refused, that is, until a jury convicted me of several crimes after a trial that has become a minor legend in the history of criminal justice in Connecticut, and I couldn’t stop crying. I went to a psychiatrist who wore a “Four More for Gore in 2004” political button on his jacket. It was 2007.


He wrote a prescription for Wellbutrin, a pill I had never been prescribed so its novelty intrigued me and goaded me into swallowing it. It didn’t make me less depressed; it gave me tiny seizures. But I did stop crying, and it put my ulcerative colitis into remission, an unexpected bonus.


I continued to take it throughout over six years in prison, meeting every six weeks with a psychiatrist who struggled with English, so conversation was a challenge and abuse either constant or impossible — the language barrier never let me know. When I left, a condition of the four years of probation awaiting me was that I had to get “mental health treatment as required.”


I dutifully surrendered myself to the Midwestern Connecticut Council on Alcoholism. I didn’t have a substance abuse disorder; MCCA treats low-income people, and I had nothing when I came home.


”I’m not doing group therapy or 12-step stuff. So I guess whatever you’re going to have to do to send me back [to prison], get it started now,” I told the intake worker. I was willing to do more time to avoid the psychiatric industrial complex.


Once they realized I was serious, they were floored, but they accommodated me, and found me individual therapists who made me skittish but at least I would only disappoint one person and not an entire room with my contrariness.


First was Cheryl. I really liked her but she was disciplined by the state for going furniture shopping with a client. I couldn’t tell from the licensing order if the furniture was meant for an abode that they would share, which would be a whole different kind of misconduct.


Then it was Rona, who was unproblematic. She winced every time she handed over a urine cup because she knew there was no risk of the sample coming back ‘dirty’ …

title: Émeutes, pillages et état d'urgence
content:
Allons nous enfin quitter l'époque contemporaine ? C'est la question qu'est venue ouvrir avec fracas le soulèvement du 17 octobre. Pour discuter de cette journée, de ce qu'elle enseigne, appelle et peut-être présage, nous allons enchaîner les invitations et les discussions. Pour cette première, nous accueillons Eugénie Mérieau et Samuel Hayat. On discute de ce qui a fait événement et de pourquoi cet événement naît d'une époque, celle-là même que tout le monde veut quitter et pas seulement la GenZ. Comment la police s'est-elle retrouvée à ce point en déroute ? Pourquoi l'état d'urgence n'a-t-il pas encore été décrété ? Sommes-nous à l'aube d'un virage encore plus autoritaire du régime ou de sa dislocation finale ? En quoi le pillage doit-il être défendu contre ceux qui s'en désolidarisent ? Pourquoi faut-il soutenir ce que d'aucuns appellent la « casse » ? Allons-nous enfin devoir choisir entre apocalypse et révolution ?

author: Tam Saavedra
title: ¡Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad están aquí!
content:
Read in English


Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad acaban de cambiar las reglas del juego para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad: Esto es lo que necesitas saber

 


¡Grandes noticias para las mujeres con discapacidad y para todas las personas defensoras, aliadas y organizaciones feministas y con discapacidad en todo el mundo!

 


Durante su 35º Período de Sesiones en agosto de 2026, el

Comité de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad

 (CDPD de la ONU)

 adoptó oficialmente las

Directrices sobre la Identificación y Abordaje de la Discriminación Interseccional Contra las Niñas, Adolescentes, Mujeres y Mujeres Mayores con Discapacidad

.

 


Este hito representa un paso gigante para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad. Por primera vez, los Estados Partes cuentan con orientación explícita y accionable para respaldar sus obligaciones en la intersección entre género y discapacidad.

 


Lee las Directrices oficiales de la CDPD de la ONU aquí

 


¿Qué son las Directrices de la CDPD sobre Discriminación Interseccional?

 


Las Directrices constituyen un marco internacional autorizado, desarrollado por la CDPD de la ONU, para ayudar a los Estados a prevenir, supervisar y abordar de mejor manera la discriminación interseccional.

 


A lo largo de años de procesos de revisión de países por parte de la CDPD de la ONU, el Comité identificó una brecha persistente y crítica:

los derechos humanos específicos de las mujeres con discapacidad y la discriminación interseccional y compleja que experimentan, rara vez son comprendidas o abordadas por los gobiernos.

 


Al celebrar el 20º aniversario de la CDPD de la ONU

, e

stas Directrices fueron emitidas para cerrar esa brecha, garantizando que la convención se aplique a favor de

todas

las mujeres y niñas con discapacidad, y las personas de género diverso con discapacidad a lo largo de sus vidas.

 


¿Por qué estas Directrices cambian las reglas del juego?

 


Los documentos internacionales rara vez se centran de forma explícita en las experiencias de vida y los derechos de las mujeres con discapacidad. Estas Directrices nombran y explican las barreras sistémicas que las mujeres y personas de género diverso con discapacidad enfrentan a diario en todo el mundo, incluyendo:

 


Salud y Derechos Sexuales y Reproductivos (SDSR):

 Abordar y prevenir la esterilización forzada, la anticoncepción forzada, la falta de atención médica accesible, las restricciones al aborto y la falta de atención perinatal, menstrual y menopáusica.

 


Violencia de Género y Basada en la Discapacidad:

 Exponer la violencia institucional, el abuso digital/en línea y la falta generalizada de servicios de apoyo para las víctimas.

 


Reconocimiento de las labores de cuidado:

 Validar a las mujeres con discapacidad como cuidadoras activas y madres, en lugar de tratarlas únicamente como receptoras de cuidados.

 


Exclusión económica y educativa:

 Destacar las barreras en el mercado laboral y la exclusión de la educación durante la pubertad.

 


Respuesta a crisis y cambio climático:

 Combatir la exclusión agravada durante desastres ambientales, emergencias climáticas y esfuerzos de ayuda humanitaria.

 


Por nombrar sólo algunas.

 


7 avances clave en el enfoque de las Directrices

 


Lo que hace que este documento sea un instrumento transformador único es su enfoque estructural y progresista:

 


Inclusión explícita de la diversidad de género:

 Las Directrices abarcan explícitamente los derechos de las personas transgénero, intersexuales, no binarias y de otras diversidades de género con discapacidad, y solicitan una interpretación inclusiva de la diversidad de género de todas las obligaciones descritas.

 


Reconocimiento de las raíces históricas:

 El Comité aborda explícitamente el legado y los impactos continuos del colonialismo y la esclavización, estableciendo que los Estados que se benefician de estos sistemas históricos tienen la responsabilidad particular de reparar sus efectos actuales.

 


Un catálogo abierto de diversidad:

 El texto reconoce que las mujeres con discapacidad pertenecen a comunidades multimarginalizadas —incluidos grupos indígenas, afrodescendientes/negros, dalit, adivasi, refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, minorías religiosas, pastoriles o personas que viven en asentamientos informales, entre otros— dejando espacio para todas las identidades interseccionales.

You may have heard of her: Aradia, daughter of Diana, the Roman moon goddess, and Lucifer, the personification of the morning star. Siblings in this particular tale, they create and birth Aradia with the sole purpose of sending her to earth to help liberate Italian peasants from the crushing weight of the ruling class. The lore says she was meant to teach witchcraft and sorcery to the disempowered resistance, so they could utilize the teachings to rise up and win the class war. To poison the powerful. To bind them and their oppressive deeds from causing further harm.

At least this is what Charles Godfrey Leland relayed in his slim, influential 1899 book, Aradia: Or The Gospel of the Witches.

“And thou shalt be the first witches known;

And thou shalt be the first of all i’ the world:

And thou shalt teach the art of poisoning;

Of poisoning those who are the great lords of all;

Yea, thou shalt make them die in their palaces;

And thou shalt bind the oppressor’s soul (with power)”

The book itself includes invocations, spells, tales of Aradia’s origins, and claims of a secret witch society who had a long, unbroken lineage of practicing folk magic and pre-Christian spiritual and healing traditions throughout Italy. In the book, followers of Aradia are instructed to gather in groups and have monthly naked meetings in forests during the full moon in honor of Diana until “…the last of your oppressors shall be dead.”

“If I were just to look at the book itself without the modern view, I would say Aradia is an initiator, she is someone who elevates people who are really not just disenfranchised, but slaves; enslaved in their souls, enslaved in their bodies,” says Dr. A.D. Manns, cultural historian and author of Aradia's Hidden Hand: The Untold Life of Roma Lister (Hexen Press, 2025). “And through her intervention, she's bringing these subjugated peoples to another level, allowing them to gain a certain degree of mastery.”

It is thrilling to consider; not a savior coming to rescue everyone, but rather a divine ally of sorts arriving with the power of organizing with the people and providing them with more tools to fight.

Poison those in power. Cast spells. Achieve collective freedom.

A woman named Maddalena (sometimes known as Margherita or Maddalena Talenti) was Leland’s paid informant who collected, and provided Leland with, information detailing Aradia’s origin story as the symbol of resistance and uprising she is portrayed as in Aradia. Maddalena herself claimed she was a link in the unbroken lineage Leland described in the book, a Tuscan and Etruscan witch, a role she said was passed down to her through generations.

Reception of the book has been complicated. It has been discussed, critiqued, praised, referenced, evaluated. It even influenced the modern witchcraft and neo-pagan revivals in the mid-1900’s. Wicca has roots in Leland’s Aradia, too; Gerald Gardner was deeply inspired by the book and adopted much of what he read and wove it into spells and rituals for his Gardnerian …

author: Thomas More
title: A Guide to the Study of Marx - Max Beer
content:
A short study-circle syllabus on Marx by the socialist historian Max Beer. It was published in 1924 by the Labour Research Department as part of its workers’ education series. It covers three areas: Marx’s general views (class society, the relativity of economic and ethical concepts, the Hegelian inheritance), historic materialism, and political economy, from surplus value to the falling rate of profit. It also includes a short biographical sketch of Marx and a suggested order for reading Capital. It ends with G. D. H. Cole’s practical hints for students and class leaders, and period adverts from the Plebs League and the Communist Bookshop. It is a good example of how Marxism was taught to British worker-students in the 1920s.

Labour Research Department, LRD

 Сегодня революционная борьба страдает от недостатка способностей на индивидуальном, организационном и социальном уровнях. Нашим крупнейшим социальным движениям, как и нашим самым страстным индивидуальным усилиям необходим милитантский импульс, способный стратегически соединять разрозненные действия. Милитантность позволяет массовым движениям испытывать обоснованную гордость и ощущать свою причастность к наиболее успешным революционным действиям. Она также даёт активному меньшинству чёткую цель и место в формировании социальной силы. Однако стойкая милитантность — это акт свободы, но сегодня большинство людей оказываются «втянуты» в неё не из сознательного выбора, а в силу обстоятельств. Мы, люди, борющиеся за социальную революцию, хотим иметь возможность самим решать, как развивать нашу милитантность. Мы требуем возможности сознательно участвовать в милитантской практике, поскольку так революционный потенциал наших движений будет обеспечен свободой людей.


 И всё же, даже при наличии свободы выбрать милитантскую деятельность остаётся вопрос:


 Куда революционерам направить свои усилия, чтобы их деятельность была связана с той реальностью, в которой в конечном счёте будет жить народ, пробуждала в людях чувство субъектности в Истории и принятие ответственности за этичность своих действий в настоящем?


 Наш ответ следует искать во взрослом образовании, которое представляет собой особенно благоприятную почву для долгосрочного участия в судьбе народных движений. Людям всегда будет необходимо учиться. Поэтому мы предлагаем создать, поддерживать и защищать революционное образовательное направление, которое станет местом встречи и обмена опытом для людей, стремящихся учиться и учить других, — в том числе членов сообщества, активистов, организаторов, диссидентов и милитантов.


 Стремление учиться, которое обычно связывают с молодёжью, новичками, студентами и теми, кому недостаёт опыта, не следует отвергать как стихийную форму организации. Нередко люди, «научившись», переходят к «действиям»: применяют полученные знания, но покидают пространство обучения, в котором они развивали свои способности, не заботясь о том, чтобы сохранить прочную связь с его методами и целями.


 Однако мы настаиваем на том, что это пространство нуждается в целенаправленной защите, если оно должно оказывать долговременное влияние на социальные преобразования. Прежде всего, защита этого пространства со временем будет способствовать коллективному становлению милитантов, которые смогут использовать общий образовательный опыт как основу для единой стратегии и политической программы. Кроме того, сохранение этого пространства будет способствовать пониманию значимости милитантов в социальной борьбе и осознанию того, насколько милитантность необходима для успеха революционных движений.


 Стремление учиться должно выполнять две функции: с одной стороны, служить пространством, где люди получают инструменты и обретают сообщество, необходимые для становления милитантами; с другой — знакомить более широкое сообщество с понятием милитантности и её теорией. Таким образом, наша цель едина, но включает два самостоятельных аспекта, которые необходимо развивать одновременно:


 Мы должны создать образовательное пространство для становления милитантов, а наше регулярное участие в его жизни должно обеспечивать надёжные пути как к милитантской деятельности, так и обратно — к образованию.


 Таким образом, стремление учиться станет пространством, где люди с большим и меньшим опытом смогут встречаться и учиться друг у друга.


 При столь ясных целях нас, несомненно, будут оценивать по нашим же критериям — приверженности делу и стойкости. Ясное определение того, что представляет собой стремление учиться, сможет воплотиться в жизнь лишь благодаря нашей приверженности ему, а его эффективность можно будет оценить лишь по тому, насколько долго оно сохраняется и насколько верно остаётся своим целям.

Ohne Perspektive gibt es mehr zu erleben. Besetze ein Haus, sperre eine Autobahn, errichte ein Zeltlager neben einer Startbahn oder einem AKW, erobere eine Stadt, leg einen Strommasten um, feiere deinen Geburtstag in der Oper, rauche einen Joint im Kinosaal, laß das Schulfest in großartiger Weise außer Kontrolle geraten, entführe einen Touristenbus und beschere den Insassen den aufregendsten Tag ihres Lebens, baue eine Kirche zu einer öffentlichen Toilette um, stell deine Wagenburg in der Einkaufspassage auf. Zwanzig Wachmänner treiben den Konsumterror in absurde Höhen, indem sie ungefragt das komplette Inventar des Kaufhauses verteilen. Die temporäre autonome Zone kommt auf Sie zu!¶

Der Slogan der political correctness lautet: ''Im Zweifelsfall nicht feiern''. Alle möglichen Handlungen könnten patriarchalisch wirken, die Umwelt verwüsten, ausländische Mitmenschen unterdrücken, Neonazis auf dumme Gedanken bringen, den Trikont zum Affen machen, kulturelle Eigenarten verletzen, ein allzu europäisches Urgefühl heraufbeschwören und vor allem: der eigenen Mentalität schaden. Bleiben wir also besser in unseren heiligen vier Wänden, schauen in die Glotze und bewegen uns nur hinaus, wenn wir zu 100% von der Unschuld des sorgfältig geplanten Zusammenseins überzeugt sind. Jedes Objekt, jede Geste, jedes Wort kann falsch sein, so falsch es nur geht, ohne daß wir uns dessen bewußt wären. Die Kollaboration lauert im kleinsten Winkel. ¿QUÉ es el patriotismo? ¿Es el amor por el lugar donde uno nació, el lugar de los recuerdos y las esperanzas de la infancia, de los sueños y las aspiraciones? ¿Es el lugar donde, con ingenuidad infantil, contemplábamos las nubes fugaces y nos preguntábamos por qué nosotros tampoco podíamos correr tan rápido? ¿El lugar donde contábamos los miles de millones de estrellas centelleantes, aterrorizados ante la idea de que cada una de ellas fuera «un ojo» que traspasara lo más profundo de nuestras pequeñas almas? ¿Es el lugar donde escuchábamos el canto de los pájaros y anhelábamos tener alas para volar, como ellos, hacia tierras lejanas? ¿O el lugar donde nos sentábamos a los pies de nuestra madre, embelesados por maravillosos relatos de grandes hazañas y conquistas? En resumen, ¿es el amor por ese lugar, donde cada pulgada representa recuerdos queridos y preciosos de una infancia feliz, alegre y juguetona?

Si eso fuera patriotismo, pocos hombres estadounidenses de hoy en día podrían considerarse patriotas, ya que el lugar de juego se ha convertido en fábrica, molino y mina, mientras que los sonidos ensordecedores de la maquinaria han sustituido a la música de los pájaros. Tampoco podemos ya escuchar las historias de grandes hazañas, pues las que cuentan hoy nuestras madres no son más que historias de dolor, lágrimas y aflicción.

¿Qué es, entonces, el patriotismo? «El patriotismo, señor, es el último recurso de los sinvergüenzas», dijo el Dr. Johnson. León Tolstói, el mayor antipatriota de nuestro tiempo, define el patriotismo como el principio que justifica la formación de asesinos en masa; un oficio que requiere mejor equipamiento para el ejercicio del asesinato que para la fabricación de artículos de primera necesidad como zapatos, ropa y viviendas; un oficio que garantiza mejores beneficios y mayor gloria que el del trabajador medio.

Gustave Hervé [1], otro gran antipatriota, califica acertadamente el patriotismo de superstición —una mucho más perjudicial, brutal e inhumana que la religión—. La superstición de la religión tuvo su origen en la incapacidad del hombre para explicar los fenómenos naturales. Es decir, cuando el hombre primitivo oía un trueno o veía un relámpago, no podía dar una explicación a ninguno de ellos y, por lo tanto, concluía que detrás de ellos debía de haber una fuerza mayor que él mismo. Del mismo modo, veía una fuerza sobrenatural en la lluvia y en los diversos cambios que se producen en la naturaleza. El patriotismo, por el contrario, es una superstición creada artificialmente y mantenida a través de una red de mentiras y falsedades; una superstición que despoja al hombre de su autoestima y dignidad, y aumenta su arrogancia y vanidad.

De hecho, la vanidad, la arrogancia y el egoísmo son los elementos esenciales del patriotismo. Permítanme ilustrarlo. El patriotismo parte de la base de que nuestro planeta está dividido en pequeños rincones, cada uno rodeado por una verja de hierro. Quienes han tenido la suerte de nacer en un rincón concreto se consideran mejores, más nobles, más grandiosos y más inteligentes que los seres vivos que habitan en cualquier otro rincón. Por lo tanto, es deber de todo aquel que vive en ese rincón elegido luchar, matar y morir en el intento de imponer su superioridad sobre todos los demás.

I den ungsocialistiska pressen hade så tidigt som år 1907 agitation förts för syndikalismen. I majnumret år 1910 av den fackliga tidningen Bageriarbetaren gjorde bagarnas förtroendeman, Anders Sjöstedt, som var redaktör för nämnda tidning, ett försök att hindra syndikalismens spridning bland bagarna, vilka i stort antal gripits av den syndikalistiska agitationen. Då skrev undertecknad ett genmäle mot den mäktiga förbundschefens angrepp under rubriken: **.."Man säger... Genmäle på artikeln i majnumret."*

"Man säger, att bagarna skola vara med då det gäller att upplösa förbunden och bilda Lokala Samorganisationer", inledde vår förtroendeman Anders Sjöstedt, och tillade sedan: "Tack för erbjudandet, men skall man då behandla bagarna på samma sätt som man vill göra nu, tycker vi synd om bagarna." På detta sätt vill jag svara att aggressiva kommer arbetsgivarna alltid att vara oavsett vilken organisationsform arbetarna har, tills dess de får så kraftigt mothugg så de lugnar sina rovdjurskänslor. Och då behövs det sannerligen syndikalistiskt försvarskraft. Därför kan inte en förtroendeman, om än med stor vilja, uträtta något ensamt - utan en vaken, handlingsfull och slagkraftig organisation.

Lusten att krossa arbetarnas organisationer har icke saknats av de privata arbetsgivarna - ej ens från styrelser och föreståndare för kooperativa bagerier i södra Sverge. Närmare angivet Skåne. Där har till och med öppna strider utbrutit.

Alla arbetsgivare vill ha utgifterna så små som möjligt. Men inkomsterna så stora som möjligt. Detta får ju främst arbetarna, producenterna, lida för.

Vidare hade Sjöstedt skrivit: "Lyssna på styrelserna för 'Föreningsbagerierna' och och för en del kooperativa bagerier vilka diskutera om bagarna på ett utmanande sätt, när det gäller deras avtal."

För min del tyckte jag att bagarna icke skulle bry sig om vad dessa konservativa styrelsemedlemmar pladdrar om. Och är det någon underhandling de ej vill bry sig om och önskar de icke vara med om någon överenskommelse som vi vet att de kan gå med på, behöver vi icke kompromissa och springa och berusa dessa herrar i all evighet, och tigga om rätt till mänsklig existens. Vi ha förmåga att slå till! Vi äro de starka! Gör slut på fegheten! Det är vi som är producenter!

Därför behöva att omändra organisationerna till kampduglighet och smidig anpassningsförmåga efter de förhållanden som kan uppstå. Vad de Lokala Samorganisationerna angår så äro de mest praktiska, och kan med heder avlösa de gamla tungrodda byråkratiska fackföreningarna, som äro i majoritet i detta land.

Att inte organisationsfrågan är ett aktuellt spörsmål just nu, bland bagarna, är en lögn av stort mått. Den är aktuell och skall bliva det ännu mer när tiden är mogen. Trots vad Sjöstedt skriver! Och hans ångest som så tydligt märks!

Allt sedan de reformistiska organisationernas början har i regel "förts de korslagda armarnas strid", som de gamla ledana är så förtjusta i - till borgardömets fromma!

Detta har visat sig odugligt. Vi har ju bagerier, som är bojkottade ända sedan den tid som "Svenska Bageri- och Konditoriarbetareförbundet" startades. Och det var inte i går!

Vi har exempel på detta i Göteborg och i Uddevalla, ja lite varstans i detta land.

Det skulle taga allt för stort utrymme i anspråk att räkna upp alla. Och när uppgörelse kommer att träffas vet ingen! Och ingen gör något för att ändring skall ske. Ingen delar ut så mycket som en bojkottslapp för att upplysa allmänheten om förhållandet, att konflikt råder. Därför behövs det pigga organisationer i vilka medlemmarna äro socialistiskt skolade och nyktra. Då kan vi marschera framåt och vinna något, trots det att arbetsgivarna göra allt för att slå ned vår frammarsch. Detta få ingen glömma!

Man skriver så ofta och påstår att folk är så egoistiska, att de ej vill betala avgifterna till föreningarna …

Author

: Warzone Distro

Title

: A is for Nihilism

Date

: 2017/09/08 04:28

Source

: Retrieved on 01/17/2026 from https://warzonedistro.noblogs.org/post/2017/09/08/a-is-for-nihilism/


“We’re all animals prescribed medication in the form of artificiality. Moral values, roles and “higher purposes” are socially constructed and assigned to us to reinforce social control. Individualist anarchy contradicts the homogeny of civilized order. Our animality is imprisoned by an institutional society that enforces its order through domesticated membership. Beneath all of the socially constructed identities, roles, conditioning and subservience we crave anarchy-acting and experiencing life out of bounds, above and beyond indoctrinated captivity. When we undress all of these assignments and refuse the medication of civilized order we are naked, wild and unique. Life opens up as a playground, and like within a self-aware dream in which we decide to have fun, it becomes a playground of limitless potential. In a self-aware dream, we know we must hurry and have fun before we awake. Life is a dream in which we must hurry and play before we wake up dead.”


 — Blitz Molotov


Introduction


 Nihilism comes from the Latin nihil, meaning “nothing”. As a philosophical position, nihilism involves rejecting certain existence claims. Two prominent forms of nihilism are existential nihilism, whch rejects claims that human life is meaningful, and moral nihilism, which rejects claims that human actions can be right or wrong. Other forms include epistemological nihilism, mereological nihilism, and political nihilism. As with any other philosophical label, there is diversity within nihilism and disagreement over what counts as nihilism. Labels with some overlap include existentialism, absurdism, fatalism, and pessimism. Some people embrace nihilistic conclusions as a philosophical matter, while other people relate to nihilistic themes more as a matter of intuition, personal experience, or personal expression. With that said, this zine does not represent any “official” definition, nor a new program or political ideology. Instead it merely presents some common anarchist-nihilist ideas which encourage an anti-political critique of all social control and order, in favor of individual empowerment, anarchy and insurrection.


A

 is for Anarchy beyond (the nostalgic captivity of) leftism.


Critiquing the Left


 Critiquing civilization as the logic, institutions, and physical apparatus of domestication, control, and domination.


 A critique of communism, socialism, and all other left ideologies as they merely seek to redistribute the exploitations of the earth more evenly among classes of humans without addressing the destructive relationship between mass society and the earth.


 Understanding that an attack upon capitalism that fails to target civilization can never abolish the institutionalized coercion that fuels society.


 Critiquing the Left as nebulous, anachronistic, distracting, a failure & at key points a counterproductive force historically (“the left wing of capital”).


 Critiquing Reductionism (Only particular aspects of the social struggle are included in leftist organizations. Other aspects are ignored, invalidated or respressed, leading to further and further compartmentalization of the struggle. Which in turn facilitates manipulation by elites and their eventual transformation into purely reformist lobbying societies with all generalized, radical critique emptied out.)


 Critiquing Leftist activists for political careerism, celebrity culture, self-righteousness, privilege politics, vanguardism & martyrdom.


 Critiquing Specialization or Professionalism (Those most involved in the day-to-day operation of the organization are selected — or self-selected — to perform increasingly specialized roles within the organization, often leading to an official division between leaders and led, with gradations of power and influence introduced in the form of intermediary roles in the evolving organizational hierarchy.)


 Critiquing the tendency of Leftists to insulate themselves in academia, scenes & cliques while also attempting to opportunistically manage struggles.

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire—A Commentary on the European Movement Centered on France from September to October 2026
content: From September to October 2026, a movement centered on France provided us with an excellent window for observing the communist cause in the 21st century and also triggered widespread public discussion. Previously, in the form of four separate commentary articles, we published them successively on the libcom platform, unfolding one by one as the movement progressed. These four pieces are not independent theoretical expositions; rather, they develop within the whole theoretical system represented by The Shackles of the Elements, Dance a Dance of Roses on the Land of Rhodes, and The Contemporary Dimensional Ascension of Capital. Now we have found the opportunity to combine them into one volume and add some notes. This is also the first time we have taken theory out of the study and put it to trial on the real field of movement.

title: Эррико Малатеста - Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

: Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"

Дата

: 28 сентября 1920

Источник

: Umanità Nova, год 1-й, №187


НАКОНЕЦ-ТО!

Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"


 Наконец-то появился тот, кто говорит ясно!


 До сих пор, когда мы говорили, что то, что социалисты называют

диктатурой пролетариата

, на самом деле есть не что иное, как диктатура некоторых людей, которые с поддержкой партии становятся над пролетариатом и навязывают себя ему, нас за это называли чуть ли не клеветниками.


 Вопреки всякой вероятности и всем установленным фактам утверждалось, что в России разрешена та квадратура круга, которой было бы правительство, действительно представляющее интересы и волю управляемых.


 Соответственно, Москва стала Меккой пролетариата: оттуда исходил свет, а вместе со светом – и категорические приказы относительно идей, которых должны придерживаться, и линии поведения, которой должны держаться те, кто с разрешения вышестоящих хотел называть себя коммунистами.


 Вследствие этого изумительного открытия, сделанного в России, – правительства, созданного по образу народа и для блага народа (или пролетариата, как угодно называть), – всё, что приходило из России, казалось обладающим чудотворной силой; и достаточно было назвать по-русски

советом

 любое собрание или комитет, чтобы он был возведён в верховный фактор революции.


 Но вот очарование разрушено.


 На этот раз не мы раскрываем секрет: мы, анархисты, злоязычные и непочтительные по убеждению. На этот раз это официальная газета Итальянской социалистической партии, до сих пор наиболее авторитетный орган московского слова.


 Это

Avanti!

 от 20-го числа текущего месяца, которая говорит:


 «....

В России при советском режиме Партия действительно направляет всю политику Государства, и вся общественная деятельность как отдельных лиц, так и коллективов подчинена решениям Партии, так что

 В САМОМ ДЕЛЕ ДИКТАТУРА ПРОЛЕТАРИАТА ЕСТЬ ДИКТАТУРА ПАРТИИ И, СЛЕДОВАТЕЛЬНО, САМОГО ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОГО КОМИТЕТА».


 Итак, теперь мы знаем, чего нам следует ожидать: диктатуры Руководящего органа Социалистической партии, или диктатуры нарождающейся Коммунистической партии, или даже диктатуры Д'Арагона и компании!


 Но руководители Социалистической партии, претендующие ввести Диктатуру, должны понять, что это, по крайней мере в Италии, невозможно: невозможно, потому что есть мы, анархисты и синдикалисты.


 Если бы мы находились в том же соотношении сил с социалистами, в каком, возможно, оказались наши товарищи в России, дело было бы простым: диктаторы избавились бы от нас средствами, дорогими всем диктатурам, – виселицами и тюрьмами, – и шли бы вперёд, пока не были бы свергнуты революцией или реакцией.


 Но мы уже сила, с которой необходимо считаться, и мы быстро развиваемся, чему благоприятствуют обстоятельства и то, что

Avanti!

 называет

необузданным темпераментом трудящихся масс

. И мы твёрдо решили не подчиняться.


 Не то чтобы мы верили, что массы всегда правы и что мы хотим всегда следовать за массами в их изменчивых настроениях. У нас есть программа, идеал, который мы хотим привести к победе, и поэтому мы отличаемся от массы, – мы люди определенного направления. Мы хотим воздействовать на массу, подталкивать её по пути, который считаем лучшим; но поскольку наша цель – освобождение, а не господство, мы хотим приучать массы к свободной инициативе и свободному действию.


 Мы верим, что свобода учит свободе и солидарности, и поэтому питаем отвращение к любому авторитарному устройству – как в обществе в целом, так и в любой отдельной партии или объединении.


 Социалисты хотели бы подготовить народ к свободе посредством власти.


 Но если бы, по предположению, которое мы отвергаем, было верно, что для торжества революции и устройства нового общества необходимо сосредоточить в немногих руках государственную власть, если бы было верно, что кто-то обязательно должен командовать, – тогда, пусть социалисты хорошенько поймут, – командовать хотели бы мы и не подчинились бы, разве что силой, командованию того, кто, по нашему мнению, заблуждается.


 Следствием чего было бы то, что революция, совершённая по авторитарным меркам и с диктаторскими целями, неизбежно привела бы в Италии к войне между одними революционерами и другими.


 Этого не хотели бы мы; этого не должны хотеть социалисты.


 Поэтому, оставив в стороне теории и судя о вещах реалистично, социалистам следовало бы отказаться от всяких диктаторских притязаний и принять либертарную …

“Just as we arm our hands to strengthen our blows, we must also fortify our minds. Our imagination, nourished by memories of resistance that has come before, bolstered by a precise projectuality, sharpened by critical thinking and corrosive insight, proves to be an arsenal of choice. […] Obviously there is no shortage of military and political campaigns against existing powers to inspire those who don’t concern themselves with ethical and practical coherence, dismissed as an excess of purism, but there is also no scarcity of revolts against the long conquest of domination over life. And while the tension towards freedom transcends all “isms,” for anarchists, the two-fold challenge is to both grasp the particularities of our contexts with realism and draw on historical experiences that resonate with our uncompromising ideals.” –History Drowned in Lethe

There was a world in which I was tempted to be charitable to the author of “Good Night Eurocentric Pride“. The article in Tinderbox #9 which it is criticizing certainly had a limitation. On the one hand, it calls us towards a profoundly difficult task: to separate ourselves from the heavy legacy of organized confusion in which revolt has been conflated with its enemies. As “History Drowned in Lethe” astutely analyzes, this confusion was an industry perpetuated by the commissars of the Soviet Union’s departments of propaganda and the ethically and intellectually bankrupt armchair academics who penned various marxist cultural theories that continue to go in and out of fashion. The article suggests, instead and against all this, a project of permanent research, interwoven with all other avenues of struggle, to recover the memory of the rebellions which, wherever and whenever they erupted, left the political charades and armed party cliches behind. On the other hand, the references of “History Drowned in Lethe” itself were thin, and centered — out of a well warranted but perhaps naive enthusiasm — on the intransigent italian anarchist minority in the United States in the early part of the 20th century. There is certainly an incoherence here. Many, many, realities of struggle have contained an incalculable libertarian and informal fringe whether they have taken on the name of anarchism or not, and the article says little to demonstrate in practice how to go about making these inquiries that it argues are completely necessary. In opting for a single example furnished to us in a widely distributed book, Plain Words, the article contravenes the effort which it (rightly) invites all of us to begin making.

But contrary to how the response portrays “History Drowned in Lethe”, at no point does it make the argument that anarchists should not seek to contribute to non-anarchist struggles, whether anti-colonial or otherwise. It’s clear that the text is instead arguing, in light of a widespread tendency to romanticize authoritarian points of reference, that this romanticization doesn’t serve us. To address this obstacle, it proposes making a greater effort …

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Pengarsipan Anarkis: Kritik & Kritik-Diri #1
content:
Belum selesai menghadapi permasalahan ekonomi yang bagai melempar api setitik ke padang ilalang itu, muncul permasalahan baru yang kini menghantui pengarsipan anarkis, permasalahan yang lebih halus dan bahkan tidak dipermasalahkan karena tidak tampak bermasalah di permukaan.

Kata-kata yang dicetak dan diterbitkan (atau bahkan yang tidak diterbitkan sekalipun), seperti buku, pamflet, leaflet, zine mendapat tempat yang signifikan di kalangan anarkis. Karena media tersebut terbukti mampu menyimpan berbagai pengalaman dan pemikiran banyak individu, yang bahkan dalam kasus tertentu, jika terdapat intervensi terhadap media cetak tersebut, eksistensinya akan tetap bertahan—untuk tidak menyebut abadi—lebih lama dari umur para individu yang mengalami pengalaman dan yang mencetuskan pemikiran tersebut. Dan individu-individu yang secara lengkap menyimpan kata-kata yang dicetak serta diterbitkan itu pun kemudian akan mendapatkan suatu manfaat, seperti dapat memiliki akses untuk melihat kembali “praktik untuk mencapai emansipasi” (gerakan dan perjuangan) yang terdahulu.

Itulah mengapa, menurut Baker (2023) ketika meneliti budaya tandingan—atau proses perubahan evolusioner—anarkis Spanyol, banyak perpustakaan anarkis dibangun untuk menyediakan akses terhadap koleksi lengkap kata-kata tercetak yang telah lama tidak diterbitkan kembali. Sayangnya, sejarah pertumbuhan budaya tandingan atau proses perubahan evolusioner anarkis ini tidak terjadi secara mulus atau bahkan macet di Indonesia. Karena Indonesia mengalami periode otoritarianisme—dalam artian paling kerasnya—yang berkepanjangan. Para anarkis tahun 1920-an habis dibuang ke Digul pasca pemberontakan 1926; sedangkan para individu berkecenderungan (anarkis-)sindikalis yang muncul pada tahun 1940-an disingkirkan secara paksa oleh rezim Orde Lama Karno dari pabrik-pabrik yang mereka swa-kelola dan disingkirkan secara perlahan dari arena pemikiran/intelektual oleh PKI; dan menjadi sama sekali tidak terlacak eksisensinya pasca genosida 1965 dan naiknya rezim Orde Bau Harto ke tampuk kekuasaan (Bima, 2018).

Walaupun, periode otoritarianisme berkepanjangan tersebut tidak khas dialami oleh para anarkis di Indonesia saja. Periode otoritarianisme keras yang berkepanjangan, yakni rezim Komunis Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej (1948-1965/17 tahun) dan Nicolae Ceaușescu, menjadikan para anarkis di Rumania dan di Indonesia memiliki—tanpa menafikan perbedaan dampak dari pasca-komunis di Rumania dan pasca-kolonial serta pasca-otoriter-militer di Indonesia yang menciptakan perbedaan yang kompleks—kesamaan dalam hal sejarah perkembangan budaya anarkis mereka. Karena ketika rezim komunis naik ke tampuk kekuasaan para anarkis disingkirkan mulai dari ditekan pergerakannya sampai dibunuh, dan sebagian yang hidup harus pergi mengasingkan diri ke luar negeri atau tetap di Rumania tetapi memilih untuk mengambil sikap tiarap total (Anarhiva, 2021). Situasi ini akhirnya, menurut Tataran (2026), membuat para anarkis yang bermunculan di Rumania pada masa-masa keruntuhan rezim komunis pada 1989 atau setelahnya, yang mayoritas bergerak di skena anarko-punk, hanya memiliki pengetahuan yang secuil atau bahkan tidak memiliki sama sekali pengetahuan tentang para anarkis yang eksis sebelum mereka, sehingga secara otomatis mereka tidak memiliki pengalaman kolektif yang dapat dijadikan rujukan ketika mereka menjalankan praktik anarkis/anti-otoritarian.

Sejalan dengan Adrian Tataran, Ucok (2026) dalam diskusi buku Unfinished Nation yang diselenggarakan di Perpustakaan Bunga di Tembok pun mengatakan hal yang nyaris sama. Menurutnya, sebelum buku Perang yang Tidak Akan Kita Menangkan karya Bima Satria Putra terbit—jauh setelah reformasi—pada tahun 2018, para anarkis yang bermunculan—dan sama seperti di Rumania, yang banyak pula bergerak di skena anarko-punk—saat masa-masa kejatuhan Harto beserta rezim Orde Baunya dan masa setelahnya tidak memiliki pengetahuan tentang gerakan anarkis terdahulu, sehingga sempat terbersit dalam pemikiran mereka kalau diri mereka adalah anarkis generasi pertama di Indonesia. Alhasil, tanpa pengalaman dan memori kolektif yang diwariskan dari para anarkis terdahulu, para anarkis yang hadir kemudian tersebut harus mulai membangun dari awal; berbanding terbalik dengan otoritarianisme yang walaupun dikatakan runtuh, mereka sudah memiliki birokrasi, struktur, militer, yang telah dibangun selama berdekade dan mapan serta siap diwariskan, sehingga bukan hal yang sulit untuk kembali ke tampuk kekuasaan …

author: Unknown
title: Dünya Kobanî Günü: DEM Parti’den ‘demokratik Suriye’ çağrısı
content:
1 Kasım Dünya Kobanî Günü dolayısıyla Türkiye’nin birçok kentinde açıklamalar yapıldı.


1 Kasım, 2014’te Avrupa Birliği Türkiye Yurttaş Komisyonu (EUTCC) ve Peace Camping inisiyatifinin, Kobanî’de IŞİD kuşatmasına karşı süren direnişe destek amacıyla yaptığı “Kobanî ve insanlık için küresel seferberlik” çağrısının ardından Dünya Kobanî Günü olarak anılmaya başlandı.


Mezopotamya Ajansı

’nın aktardığına göre


Adana, Mersin, Urfa Suruç, Konya, İzmir, Van, Erzurum, Bitlis Tatvan, Antalya ve Şırnak’ta düzenlenen açıklamalarda Kobanî’de IŞİD’e karşı verilen mücadele anıldı.


Eylemlerde, Suriye’de eşit yurttaşlık, demokratik çözüm ve birlikte yaşam talepleri öne çıktı.


*Adana


Açıklamalarda konuşan Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi (DEM Parti) temsilcileri, Kobanî’deki mücadelenin farklı halklar ve inançlar açısından ortak yaşam fikrini güçlendirdiğini savundu.


Urfa Suruç’taki etkinlikte konuşan DEM Parti Milletvekili Ferit Şenyaşar, Kobanî direnişinin Kürtlerin dünya kamuoyunda görünürlüğünü artırdığını söyledi. Şenyaşar, “Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci”ne de değinerek devletin somut adımlar atması gerektiğini belirtti.


İzmir’deki eylemde konuşan DEM Parti Milletvekili Burcugül Çubuk, Kobanî’yi Ortadoğu’daki savaş politikalarına karşı barış ve ortak mücadele açısından bir ‘pusula’ olarak tanımladı. Çubuk, farklı halkların birlikte mücadele ederek barışı örgütlemesi gerektiğini söyledi.


*İzmir


Şırnak’taki açıklamada DEM Parti Milletvekili Mehmet Zeki İrmez, Suriye’de demokratik bir sistem kurulması ve bütün halkların haklarının güvence altına alınması gerektiğini söyledi. İrmez, Kürtlerin dil, kültür ve kimlikleriyle Suriye’nin geleceğinde yer alması gerektiğini belirtti.


Antalya’da DEM Parti Milletvekili Saruhan Oluç da Kobanî’de IŞİD’e karşı yürütülen mücadelenin yalnızca Kürtler açısından değil, bölgede yaşayan halklar açısından da önem taşıdığını söyledi.


*Bitlis


“Demokratik bir Suriye inşa edilmeli”


DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tülay Hatimoğulları, 1 Kasım dolayısıyla yaptığı açıklamada Kobanî’yi “kadınların öncülüğünde yükselen, halkların ve inançların ortak yaşam iradesiyle büyüyen” bir mücadele olarak tanımladı.


Hatimoğulları, X sosyal medya hesabından Türkçe, Kürtçe ve Arapça yaptığı paylaşımda Suriye’nin geleceğine ilişkin şu çağrıyı yaptı:


Kobanî’nin tarihsel mirasına yakışır demokratik bir Suriye inşa edilmelidir. Başta yaşam hakkı olmak üzere, Kürt halkının ve Kuzey ve Doğu Suriye’deki tüm halkların kimlikleri, dilleri, siyasi ve kültürel hakları güvence altına alınmalıdır. Demokratik Suriye, eşit ve özgür ortak yaşamın güvencesidir.


DEM Parti Eş Genel Başkanı Tuncer Bakırhan da Kobanî’deki mücadelenin “halkların eşit ve özgür bir yaşam kurma iradesinin simgesi” olduğunu söyledi.


Bakırhan, X sosyal medya hesabından Türkçe, Kürtçe ve Arapça yaptığı paylaşımda Kobanî direnişinin mirasının bugün Suriye’nin geleceği açısından yol gösterici olduğunu belirtti:


Kalıcı barış ve demokratik çözüm; Suriye’de yaşayan tüm halkların kimliklerinin ve siyasi, kültürel ve toplumsal haklarının güvence altına alınmasından geçer.


Suriye’nin bütünlüğü, farklı halkların ve inançların kimliklerini yok saymakla değil, eşit ve özgür bir ortak yaşamla mümkündür. Tüm halkların haklarının tanınması, demokratik entegrasyonun ve kalıcı barışın güvencesidir.


(VC)

author: Stelinsky
title: Η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών αποχαιρετά τον Θόδωρο Μεγαλοοικονόμου
content:
«Ζούμε σε μια πραγματικότητα που βασίζεται στη διαίρεση, σε μια κοινωνική οργάνωση που μας σκοτώνει και μας εξουσιοδοτεί να σκοτώνουμε τους άλλους για να επιζήσουμε. Είναι αυτή η πραγματικότητα που πρέπει ν’ αλλάξει και πρέπει ν’ αγωνιστούμε για να την αλλάξουμε, έτσι ώστε να μπορούμε να βρούμε τις πραγματικές απαντήσεις στις κοινωνικές ανάγκες του άλλου: Σε μια κοινωνία όπου το κοινωνικό σύστημα δεν θα καθορίζεται από αυτόν που το διαχειρίζεται και το ελέγχει, αλλά στο οποίο θα είναι οι ανάγκες όλων που θα καθορίζουν την ποιότητα και τον τρόπο των απαντήσεων».

~Φράνκο Μπαζάλια από την παρέμβασή του σε συνέδριο στο Πανεπιστήμιο της Ρώμης τον Φεβρουάριο του 1975

Ο Θόδωρος Μεγαλοοικονόμου είχε επηρεαστεί βαθιά από το «Πείραμα της Τεργέστης», μια ριζοσπαστική ψυχιατρική μεταρρύθμιση που ξεκίνησε τη δεκαετία του 1970 από τον ψυχίατρο Φράνκο Μπαζάλια, με στόχο την κατάργηση των παραδοσιακών ασύλων και την κοινωνική επανένταξη των ψυχικά ασθενών.

Η Κοινότητα των Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών συναντήθηκε με τον Θόδωρο Μεγαλοοικονόμου και την Πρωτοβουλία Ψ Πρωτοβουλία για ένα Πολύμορφο Κίνημα για την Ψυχική Υγεία σε μια πολύ δύσκολη συγκυρία. Ήταν η αρχή της περιόδου του COVID-19 και η κοινωνία είχε αρχίσει να πιέζεται πολλαπλά, κάτοικοι της γειτονιάς με ψυχικό πόνο βρέθηκαν φοβισμένοι και απομονωμένοι χωρίς πρόσβαση σε δομές υγείας. Η Κοινότητα συναντήθηκε με την Πρωτοβουλία Ψ και τον Θόδωρο Μεγαλοοικονόμου προκειμένου να διαχειριστούμε από κοινού την πολυπλοκότητα της συνθήκης. Θα μπορούσαμε να πούμε πολλά για αυτήν την 6ετή συμπόρευση, αλλά θα σταθούμε σε δύο βασικά σημεία: Το πρώτο είναι το πώς ο Θόδωρος μετέφερε την εμπειρία του στη διαχείριση του ψυχικού πόνου, με αξιοσημείωτη σταθερότητα και φροντίδα στα άτομα και στις ανάγκες τους τόσο από τον ίδιο, όσο και από τα υπόλοιπα μέλη της Πρωτοβουλίας Ψ, και το δεύτερο είναι ότι όλη αυτή η συμπόρευση με τη μεταφορά της γνώσης έγινε σταδιακά βιωμένη εμπειρία για την Κοινότητα, γεγονός που οδήγησε στη δημιουργία της Δομή Υγείας της Κοινότητας των Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών.

Η σοβαρότητα στην κατάσταση της υγείας του Θόδωρου Μεγαλοοικονόμου συνέπεσε με τον μεγάλο κύκλο αγώνα που έδωσε η Κοινότητα με προμετωπίδα την απεργία πείνας των 140 ημερών του Αριστοτέλη Χαντζή και των 55 ημερών της Suzon Doppagne, προκειμένου να επιβιώσει ενάντια στο πλάνο εκκένωσης των Προσφυγικών από την Περιφέρεια Αττικής και τον εντολοδόχο Νίκο Χαρδαλιά. Μέσα στην εκατέρωθεν κρισιμότητα των καταστάσεων ο Θόδωρος δεν έπαψε στιγμή να νοιάζεται, να ενημερώνεται, να αγωνιά και να καταθέτει προτάσεις για την αντιμετώπιση της καταστολής και τη συνέχιση της Κοινότητας. Υπήρξε αξιοσημείωτα συγκινητικό το ενδιαφέρον του και η διαρκής του επικοινωνία με τη Δομή Υγείας της Κοινότητας των Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών όλο αυτό το διάστημα, γεγονός που αποτυπώνει με τον πιο ενδεικτικό τρόπο για το ποιος ήταν ο Θόδωρος Μεγαλοοικονόμου σε όλη τη διάρκεια της πολύπλευρης επιστημονικής και πολιτικής του ζωής.

Εμβληματική μορφή της αποασυλοποίησης, γκρεμίζοντας, όπως ο ίδιος έγραψε, «τον έναν τοίχο μετά τον άλλο», βρέθηκε με την Κοινότητα των Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών σε έναν κοινό βηματισμό, αντιμετωπίζοντας τους ανθρώπους με ψυχικό πόνο όχι ως «πρόβλημα», αλλά ως κάποιους από μας τους τόσο διαφορετικούς μεταξύ μας έτσι κι αλλιώς. Η πεποίθησή του ότι οι κοινότητες αποτελούν από τη φύση τους την απάντηση στα ζητήματα και τις ανάγκες των ανθρώπων, μας οδήγησε στο να γκρεμίσουμε από κοινού αρκετούς τοίχους, άλλοτε διαφωνώντας, άλλοτε συγκλίνοντας, μα πάντα καταλήγοντας στο ότι: Η ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗ ΕΙΝΑΙ ΘΕΡΑΠΕΥΤΙΚΗ.

Τα θερμά μας συλλυπητήρια στη σύντροφο και συνοδοιπόρο του Δώρα Κουτσανέλλου, στα παιδιά του και τους οικείους του.

Θόδωρε Ο ΑΓΩΝΑΣ ΝΙΚΗΣΕ – Ο ΑΓΩΝΑΣ ΣΥΝΕΧΙΖΕΤΑΙ!

Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών

author: Unknown
title: ‘Hangi çocuk şantiyede 6’ncı kata gönderilir?’
content:
Nisa Sude Demirel [email protected]

İstanbul – İşçi Sağlığı ve İş Güvenliği (İSİG) Meclisinin 2026 yılında tespit edebildiği, hayatını kaybeden 71 çocuk işçiden 65’incisi 17 yaşındaki Halil İbrahim Yağız’dı. 28 Eylül’de Antep’in Şehitkamil ilçesindeki filesiz şantiyede baretsiz halde çalıştırılan MESEM’li Halil’in MESEM’deki ilk günüydü. İşin henüz ilk saatinde, inşaatın altıncı katına aşağı tel atması için gönderildi. MESEM’de henüz bir saatini bile tamamlamadan aşağı düşerek hayatını kaybetti. Üstelik Halil’in ölümünden sorumlu Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı ise aileye taziye ziyaretine geldi. Halil’in ölümünü, kendisi de PVC atölyesinde usta olan 20 yaşındaki ağabeyi Eyüp Yağız anlattı.

Halil, 7 çocuklu bir ailenin çocuğu. Mehmet Akif Ersoy Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesinde 11. sınıf öğrencisiydi. Ailenin itirazlarına rağmen ağabeyinin deyimiyle ‘Elinin iş tutması’ hevesiyle bu sene MESEM’e kaydolmuştu, tesisat bölümündeydi.

Evin geçimini büyük oranda sırtlayan Eyüp Yağız’ın, Halil’in MESEM’e yazılmasına ilişkin temel itirazı kardeşinin okumasını istemesiydi: “Yazın kardeşimin canı sıkılınca ‘al yanına’ dedi, ona bile kıyamadım. İşimiz ağır olduğu için ‘İboş çalışmasın okusun, yeter ki okusun’ dedim. Dersleri de iyiydi, bu sene onur belgesiyle takdir belgesi getirdi. Daha çocuk... Bana gelip deseydi ‘Ben inşaata gideceğim’, ben o kapıdan onu göndermezdim. Ama bana tesisatçılık dedi. Benim bildiğim sucular tamirata gider, dükkanda oturur. Nereden bileyim ben koca inşaata gidecek, ustası 6. kata gönderecek, düşecek?”

28 Eylül’de, MESEM’deki ilk iş gününde Halil, saat 07.00’yi geçerken işe gitmek üzere çıkıyor. Ağabeyi Eyüp’ün telefonu kırık olduğundan kendi telefonunu ona veriyor, “Benim telefonuma bir şey olmasın, akşam senden alırım” diyor. Beykent Mahallesi’ndeki şantiyeye doğru yola çıkıyor.

Halil, MESEM kapsamında bir tesisat ustasının yanında çalışıyor. Yani gittikleri şantiyede taşeron. Halil’i altıncı kata tel almaya gönderiyorlar. Eyüp Yağız, Halil’in hayatını kaybettiği anları şöyle anlatıyor: “Çocuk inşaatı bilmiyor, nereden bilsin? Hayatında ilk defa inşaata gidiyor. İşe başlıyorlar, ‘Bismillahirrahmanirrahim’ diyor, hemen çocuğu 6. kata gönderiyor. 6. kattan ‘O teli at’ diyorlar. O telle beraber kardeşim düşüyor.”

Eyüp Yağız’ın anlattığına göre, Halil saat 08.30’da hayatını kaybediyor. Ancak Halil’in babası Mehmet Yağız ancak 11.30’da aranıyor: “Babamı arayıp diyorlar ki ‘Oğlun düştü ama...’ Hayatını kaybettiğini söylemiyorlar. Hastaneye gittiğini söylüyorlar. Ancak ortada hastane filan yok, Halil düştüğü yerde canını veriyor. Biz herhalde ayağı ya da kolu kırıldı dedik. Sonra defalarca ustasını aradık, açmadılar.”

Ardından aile önce Başpınar’daki organize sanayi bölgesindeki hastaneye gidiyor. Saatlerce hastane, karakol geziyorlar. Ancak Halil’i bulamıyorlar. 08.30’da hayatını kaybeden Halil’i, saat 13.30’a doğru adli tıpta buluyorlar: “Ben daha sonra inşaata da gittim, bekçinin yanına. ‘Madem ölmüş niye bize haber vermiyorsunuz?’ dedim. Bekçinin dediğine göre, usta ‘Ben korkuyorum, ailesine haber vermek istemiyorum. Ailesini aradım, düştüğünü söyledim, öldüğünü söyleyemedim’ demiş. Orada biz iki üç saat boyunca hastanede bekledik. Gelen bütün ambulansları, sedyeleri açıyoruz acaba Halil mi diye.”

Halil’in kıyafetleri ortada yok

Ardından baba Mehmet Yağız, kendi imkanlarıyla Halil’in naaşının adli tıpta olduğunu öğreniyor. Ailenin haberi olmadan otopsi yapılıyor. Ancak otopsinin ardından Halil’in kıyafetlerini almak için gittiklerinde bulamıyorlar: “Taziye bitip misafirlerimiz dağıldıktan sonra adli tıbba elbisesini almaya gittik. Elbiseleri cenazeyle beraber gönderdiklerini söylediler. Yıkama yerine gittik, yine böyle bir elbise olmadığını söylediler. Kamera kaydına baktık, elbise yoktu. Belki ayakkabısını değiştirmiş olabilirler, giysisini değiştirmiş olabilirler... Her şey olabilir. Biz şu an elbisesini bulamıyoruz.”

Eyüp Yağız, kardeşini “Hiçbir kötü yönü yoktu. Bu zamanki gençleri anlattıkları gibi değildi. Ne bir kötü huyu vardı ne sigara kullanırdı. Annem ekmek almaya yollamaya bile kıyamazdı” diye anlatıyor. Halil’in ileride ne yapmak istediğini sorduğumuzda ise şöyle diyor: “Çalışmak istiyordu, bir de bizim babamız hayvancıydı önceden. Bizim Siverek’te ahırımız vardı. Ben askere gidecektim bu sene. Geldiğimde birlikte yapacaktık. Allah kısmet etmedi işte.”

Halil’den esas sorumlu olan Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı sadece taziyeye geldi.

Derinleşen yoksulluk çocuk işçiliğini artırırken MESEM’e …

author: Stelinsky
title: Με αφορμή τον θάνατο του Γκιάνα Ασλάν, 16χρονου ποδοσφαιριστή
content:
Για άλλη μια φορά γινόμαστε μάρτυρες ενός άδικου θανάτου ενός αθλητή ερασιτεχνικού αθλητισμού. Για άλλη μια φορά ξεγυμνώνεται η «ασφάλεια» των αθλητικών εγκαταστάσεων όπου αθλούνται μικροί και μεγάλοι καθημερινά σε ολόκληρη τη χώρα. Για τον Άνι, όπως τον λέγανε οι φίλοι του, μια στιγμιαία έλλειψη ισορροπίας αρκούσε για να χτυπήσει το κεφάλι του στο τοιχάκι της κερκίδας, το οποίο βρίσκεται στο 1 μέτρο από το πλάγιο άουτ (αυτό είναι το επίπεδο ασφαλείας πολλών αθλητικών εγκαταστάσεων).

Ως ερασιτεχνικός αθλητικός σύλλογος βλέπουμε και ζούμε εκ των έσω αυτήν την τραγική εγκατάλειψη και υποβάθμιση των αθλητικών εγκαταστάσεων. Χθες ο Δημήτρης Ζαχείλας (παίκτης της ομάδας μας που πέθανε κατά τη διάρκεια προπόνησης στο γήπεδο Μητσιμπόνα Β’ στη Λάρισα), σήμερα ο Γκιάνα Ασλάν, αύριο ίσως ένας φίλος, ένας συναθλητής, το παιδί μας το ίδιο. Θεωρούμε αδιανόητο σε αθλητικά κέντρα όπου παράλληλα αθλούνται πολλά παιδιά και ενήλικες να μην υπάρχει επαγγελματίας υγείας, απινιδωτής και ό,τι άλλο είναι απαραίτητο για να δοθούν οι πρώτες βοήθειες. Θεωρούμε αδιανόητο οι αθλητικές εγκαταστάσεις να μετατρέπονται σε παγίδες θανάτου από την ανεπαρκή συντήρηση και την αδιαφορία των αρμοδίων. Οι κύριοι της πολιτείας έχουν εφεύρει έναν νέο όρο και τον χρησιμοποιούνε ώστε να αποποιούνται των ευθυνών τους: «κοστολόγιο». Όλα είναι κόστος πλέον γι’ αυτούς. Κοστολόγηση κύριοι να κάνετε στις δικές σας ζωές με όποιον τρόπο θέλετε, όχι στις δικές μας. Ο αθλητισμός είναι κοινωνικό αγαθό, τον διεκδικούμε και θα τον διεκδικούμε με κάθε τρόπο. Θα μας βρίσκετε συνεχώς απέναντι στα «κοστολόγιά» σας.

Αυτοοργανωμένος Αθλητικός Σύλλογος Μαρίνος Αντύπας

Σημείωση της εφημερίδας: Ο Άνι ήταν παίχτης του Βύρωνα Καβάλας. Τραυματίστηκε μόλις στο 2ο λεπτό, σε αγώνα που έλαβε χώρα στο γήπεδο της Παναγιάς στη Θάσο στις 27/09/2026. Αυτός ο τραυματισμός οδήγησε στον θάνατό του.
