author: Unknown
title: Iranian security bodies block medical leave for Kurdish political prisoner
content:
Iranian security bodies have blocked medical leave and access to adequate treatment for Fahim Ebadi, a Kurdish political prisoner in Orumiyeh Central Prison who suffers from diabetes, high blood pressure and high blood fat levels, the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported.


Iranian forces arrested Ebadi, who is from Orumiyeh and is serving a 45-month sentence, in the city around two years ago.


After several weeks of interrogation at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility, he was transferred to Orumiyeh Central Prison, where he has remained since.


After several months in detention, a branch of the Islamic Revolutionary Court of Orumiyeh sentenced him to 60 months in prison on charges of “membership of opposition groups” in connection with membership of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).


His sentence was subsequently reduced to 45 months after he waived his right to appeal and requested a sentence reduction.

author: Unknown
title: Resistance against solar power plant project in Kulp on day 91
content:
Resistance against the planned solar power plant project.in the village of Cixsê, in the Kulp district of Amed (Diyarbakır), has continued for three months. For 91 days, residents have maintained a vigil in protest against the project, which threatens grazing lands, water sources, and agricultural livelihoods. An investigation by the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB) has now confirmed significant shortcomings in the environmental impact assessment. The organization is calling for the immediate cancellation of the project.


Representatives of the TMMOB Coordination Council in Amed presented their findings during a protest in Cixsê. The findings are based on a site inspection conducted on October 14, during which experts examined both the proposed construction site and the information contained in the environmental impact assessment documentation.


Grazing lands and water sources at risk


According to Filiz Kaçar, a member of TMMOB’s Energy and Ecology Commission, approximately 30 hectares of land within and around the project area are used as grazing grounds for livestock. The installation of solar panels, fencing of the site, and construction of access roads would fragment continuous grazing areas and significantly restrict their use. The commission is particularly concerned about the potential impact on local water resources. The affected area contains a pond and several streams that are important for supplying water to livestock. The planned construction work could damage these natural resources.


Cixsê is also an important center for silkworm breeding and cocoon production. Alongside livestock farming and crop cultivation, this sector forms a vital foundation of local livelihoods. According to the experts, habitats of migratory birds such as cranes, storks, and swallows would also be affected.


Significant shortcomings in the environmental impact assessment


According to Kaçar, TMMOB’s investigation found that key ecological and economic factors had been inadequately addressed in the project documentation. These include existing bodies of water, the traditional use of grazing lands, biodiversity, natural hazards, and the planned energy storage systems. The organization does not fundamentally oppose the expansion of renewable energy, but rather its implementation at the expense of local residents and their livelihoods. “The transition to renewable energy is necessary. But an energy transition that ignores nature and life is not sustainable. The solar project planned in Cixsê must be stopped immediately,” Kaçar stated.


Fatoş Nujen Ayhan of the TMMOB Coordination Council also criticized the economic interests behind the project: “Cixsê’s energy resources must be used and managed by the local population itself. We cannot allow corporations to exploit our resources and then sell the energy generated from them back to the people at high prices.”


Incorrect photographs previously discovered in environmental report


The new findings have intensified the dispute over the approval of the project. As early as September, it emerged that the environmental impact assessment report contained photographs that had not been taken in the proposed project area. The Amed Bar Association and the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) subsequently filed a criminal complaint against officials of the environmental consultancy Global ÇED and the construction company VBZ İnşaat. However, the public prosecutor’s office in Kulp found insufficient grounds for suspicion of document forgery and closed the investigation. The lawyers appealed the decision. Separately, the decision approving the environmental impact assessment is the subject of administrative court proceedings.


“Our land belongs to us”


The DEM Party also supports the villagers’ resistance. Berivan Turan, a member of the party’s provincial executive board in Amed, warned of the long-term social and ecological consequences during the protest. She stated that the loss of agricultural land and natural resources could exacerbate unemployment, poverty, and migration. “The people do not want a solar power plant on this grazing land. They have been expressing their opposition for months,” Turan said. She placed the resistance in Cixsê within the broader context of local struggles against the economic exploitation of natural resources in Kurdistan, citing the vigil in Arzoxlî as an example.


“We do not want to lose our cemeteries, our culture …

title: Concern for at Least 14 Kurdish prisoners facing death sentences in Iran
content:
30 October has been declared International Day of Political Prisoners. A review of published human rights reports identifies at least 14 Kurdish political prisoners and protesters facing death sentences in Iran.


This list brings together reported cases and includes both initial court rulings and sentences upheld on appeal. Pakhshan Azizi, Hatem Ozdemir, Yousef Ahmadi, Pezhman Touberehrizi, Arman Marefati, Mohammad Faraji, Raouf Sheikh-Maroufi and Mohsen Eslamkhah are eight of these prisoners.


Earlier human rights reports warned that they could face execution. The reports described unfair and secretive proceedings, torture, pressure to obtain forced confessions, and violations of their right to defend themselves.


Hatem Ozdemir is a Kurdish citizen of Turkey imprisoned in Iran. Khosrow Mohammadnia, Masoud Toushmalani, Sirwan Shabani, Borzou Rezaei and Omran Amani are five others on the list. They were sentenced to death in connection with the January 2026 protests. The sentences against the first three were reported on 1 October, and Rezaei’s on 6 October. On 29 October, it was reported that 21-year-old Omran Amani had been formally informed of his death sentence at Great Tehran Penitentiary.


Varisheh Moradi, a Kurdish political activist and member of the East Kurdistan Free Women’s Society, is also among the 14. On 14 October, Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced her to death for a second time. The Supreme Court had overturned her earlier sentence because of an incomplete investigation and problems with the trial process. Her lawyers say the court repeated the death sentence without addressing those problems.


The cases are at different stages of the legal process. The Supreme Court has previously upheld the death sentences against Pakhshan Azizi, Hatem Ozdemir and Yousef Ahmadi. One of Ahmadi’s two death sentences was changed to financial compensation and imprisonment. However, his other death sentence, on a charge of “armed rebellion,” remains in place.


This year’s International Day of Political Prisoners places a strong emphasis on keeping prisoners’ names in public view and supporting their families.


In a joint statement, the 30 October Coalition called for sustained international attention and the immediate, unconditional release of people imprisoned for exercising their basic rights. It also stressed the need to hold those responsible for abuses accountable.

author: Unknown
title: Human rights violations against Kurds continue in Iran
content:
The Iranian regime’s practices of detention, imprisonment and punishment targeting Kurds continue. According to information reported by the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), a request for medical leave by Fehîm Ebadî, a Kurdish prisoner with diabetes held in Urmia Central Prison, has been rejected, preventing him from accessing medical treatment.


Ebadî was detained by Iranian regime forces in Urmia two years ago. He was sentenced to five years in prison on the allegation of being a “member of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).” His sentence was subsequently reduced to 45 months.


Detained without a warrant


Mohammad Reza, who lives in the Malekshahi region of Ilam Province, was detained by Iranian regime forces and taken to an undisclosed location. According to KHRN, Mohammad Reza was detained at his family home in the early hours of the morning on 29 October, without the authorities presenting an arrest warrant. No information has yet emerged regarding the grounds for his detention.


Kurdish cultural activist arrested


Metîn Feremerzpûr, a Kurdish cultural activist and doctoral student in philosophy at the University of Tabriz, was also detained by regime forces on allegations of “propaganda against the state” and taken to Mahabad Prison. According to KHRN, Feremerzpûr was detained on 8 July at Şêx Şaltut Park in Mahabad. After being released, he was summoned to give another statement and was detained again when he appeared.


Prison sentences handed down to two Kurdish political prisoners


KHRN also reported that prison sentences have been handed down to Kurdish political prisoners Mîlad Nasirîran and Afşîn Ezîzî, who were transferred to Urmia Central Prison. Nasirîran was sentenced to 11 months in prison, while Ezîzî received a three-year prison sentence. Mîlad Nasirîran was reportedly detained by Iranian regime forces in Ilam Province three months ago and transferred to Urmia Central Prison a few days ago.

content:
“Η ιδιωτικοποίηση του λιμανιού του Λαυρίου βρίσκεται σε κρίσιμη φάση. Ο διαγωνισμός για την πώληση του 51% του Οργανισμού Λιμένος Λαυρίου οδηγεί στην εκχώρηση μιας στρατηγικής δημόσιας υποδομής σε ιδιωτικά συμφέροντα έως το 2062.

 Σάββατο 31 Οκτωβρίου, στις 12 μ.μ.


 Συγκέντρωση στο Δημαρχείο Λαυρίου και πορεία προς το λιμάνι


Η ιδιωτικοποίηση του λιμανιού του Λαυρίου βρίσκεται σε κρίσιμη φάση. Ο διαγωνισμός για την πώληση του 51% του Οργανισμού Λιμένος Λαυρίου οδηγεί στην εκχώρηση μιας στρατηγικής δημόσιας υποδομής σε ιδιωτικά συμφέροντα έως το 2062.


Σύμφωνα με τις τελευταίες πληροφορίες, στη διεκδίκηση παραμένει η Israel Shipyards Industries, μία από τις σημαντικότερες εταιρείες της ισραηλινής ναυπηγικής και πολεμικής βιομηχανίας. Η εταιρεία κατασκευάζει πυραυλακάτους και ταχύπλοα περιπολικά, συνεργάζεται άμεσα με το ισραηλινό Πολεμικό Ναυτικό και προβάλλει τα προϊόντα της ως «δοκιμασμένα στη μάχη». Με τα σκάφη της οι Ισραηλινοί επιβάλλουν τον παράνομο θαλάσσιο αποκλεισμό της Γάζας και δολοφονούν Παλαιστίνιους ψαράδες.


Η πιθανή απόκτηση του λιμανιού από μια τέτοια εταιρεία μετατρέπει το Λαύριο σε ισραηλινό πολεμικό λιμάνι, με σοβαρές συνέπειες για τους κατοίκους, τους εργαζομένους και την ασφάλεια ολόκληρης της περιοχής. Εντάσσεται στη συνολικότερη διείσδυση της ισραηλινής πολεμικής βιομηχανίας στην Ελλάδα με εξοπλιστικά προγράμματα δισεκατομμυρίων, στρατιωτικές συμφωνίες, κοινές ασκήσεις και εξαγορές ελληνικών αμυντικών επιχειρήσεων.


 Την ίδια στιγμή, αναβιώνει και επεκτείνεται η πολεμική βιομηχανία των Ελληνικών Αμυντικών Συστημάτων στο Λαύριο. Η νέα εταιρεία Ελληνικά Πυρομαχικά Α.Ε. – Hellenic Ammunition ανήκει κατά 51% στα ΕΑΣ και κατά 49% στην MSM, θυγατρική του τσεχικού πολεμικού ομίλου CSG. Στον ιδιώτη έχει παραχωρηθεί η διοικητική και επιχειρησιακή διαχείριση των εγκαταστάσεων για 25 χρόνια.


Προωθείται μεγάλη αύξηση της παραγωγής πυρομαχικών, η κατασκευή βλημάτων πυροβολικού 155 χιλιοστών και πυρομαχικών αρμάτων, καθώς και η επαναλειτουργία της παραγωγής TNT. Η εξέλιξη αυτή σημαίνει αυξημένη αποθήκευση, μεταφορά και διαχείριση εκρηκτικών υλών, εντονότερη βιομηχανική δραστηριότητα και μεγαλύτερους κινδύνους για την υγεία, την ασφάλεια και το περιβάλλον. Οι ανησυχίες γίνονται ακόμη σοβαρότερες εξαιτίας της ήδη καταγεγραμμένης ρύπανσης του εδάφους από TNT και της ανάγκης απορρύπανσης παλαιών εγκαταστάσεων.


Το ενδεχόμενο συνύπαρξης ενός λιμανιού υπό τον έλεγχο ισραηλινού πολεμικού ομίλου με μια πολεμική βιομηχανία παραγωγής πυρομαχικών και εκρηκτικών δημιουργεί ένα νέο, επικίνδυνο τοπίο. Συγκεντρώνει στην ίδια περιοχή λιμενικές υποδομές, αποθήκευση και μεταφορά εκρηκτικών, παραγωγή πολεμικού υλικού και συμφέροντα ξένων πολεμικών ομίλων. Ενισχύει τη στρατιωτικοποίηση του Λαυρίου και αυξάνει την έκθεση της περιοχής στους κινδύνους που συνοδεύουν τη βαθύτερη εμπλοκή της Ελλάδας στους πολέμους και στους γεωπολιτικούς σχεδιασμούς του Ισραήλ και των συμμάχων του.


Το Λαύριο δεν πρέπει να μετατραπεί σε κόμβο παραγωγής, διακίνησης και υποστήριξης πολεμικού υλικού, ούτε σε πιθανό στρατιωτικό στόχο. Οι κάτοικοι και οι εργαζόμενοι δικαιούνται πλήρη ενημέρωση, δημόσιο έλεγχο, ουσιαστικά μέτρα …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: While Americans Paid $148B Extra on Gas Amid War, Big Oil Made $130B in Profits
content:
“All the excess cash we’re accumulating will ultimately be directed toward our owners,” one oil executive bragged.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

As Americans have been forced to shell out an extra $148 billion on gas and diesel in eight months of war on Iran, Big Oil has reaped record profits — with U.S. companies having made over $130 billion in profits, a new analysis finds.

According to The New York Times, these profits were spread across 50 large U.S. oil and gas companies. Many of these companies, like Valero Energy, reported their highest-ever quarterly profits in recent months.

The calculation of oil and gas companies’ collective profits between April and September is conservative, the Times notes, and doesn’t include two months of the war.

Even still, $130 billion is nearly three times more than the industry’s profits this time last year. ExxonMobil more than doubled and Chevron nearly tripled profits in Q3 compared to 2025, and both companies are forecasted to potentially make record profits for the full year.

Meanwhile, prices for consumers have not just hit record highs amid the war, but have also sustained an average price above $4 a gallon for a record amount of time.

According to a tracker set up by Brown University’s Climate Solutions Lab, Americans have paid an extra $147 billion on gas and diesel since the start of the war, amounting to over $1,100 per household. Moody’s Analytics has estimated that, when higher prices for jet fuel are accounted for, the war has cost U.S. households $1,184 more just on these fuel prices alone.

These extra costs compound upon an existing affordability crisis across the country, lining the pockets of oil and gas executives as Americans struggle to afford basic necessities like housing and groceries.

“Over time, all the excess cash we’re accumulating will ultimately be directed toward our owners,” Valero Energy’s chief financial officer Homer Bhullar said in a call with Wall Street analysts last week.

Polling by Gallup finds that the war on Iran and gas prices rank as one of the top issues for voters this midterm election season, following the economy as the top concern.

Despite this, President Donald Trump has not just downplayed the war’s impacts on U.S. households, but has openly bragged about the oil and gas industry’s profits spurred by his aggression. “Because of the price of oil, Texas and Oklahoma and North Dakota and all these places, we’re making a fortune,” Trump said at a rally in Arizona this month.

“I can just see the fake headlines: ‘President Trump is talking about all the money they’re making while people are suffering at the pump.’ But I said, ‘I don’t give a damn. I’m gonna say it. We’re making a freaking fortune,’” Trump told a crowd in Georgia last weekend.

Several states with Republican-controlled legislatures have implemented temporary gas tax holidays ahead of the midterm elections, hoping to take heat off GOP candidates. However, the measures are just a band-aid on a much larger problem: a war that the Trump administration seems desperate to end, but that they only know how to prolong.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Arviat singer-songwriter finds inspiration on the land
content:
For Coral Harbour-based musician Jocelyn Malla, a $9,000 songwriting prize means more than recognition for her music.


“It really helps a lot day to day, living in a very expensive community, along with my children and grandchildren,” Malla said in an interview Thursday.


Malla

won first place

 in the Government of Nunavut’s 2026 Qilaut Inuktut songwriting contest with her song

Tukisivunga

, earning the $8,000 grand prize. She also placed fifth with

Kamatsiaqta

, winning her an additional $1,000.


She previously

took the grand prize

 in 2022,

 and placed fourth and seventh in 2025 in the same competition. 


Tukisivunga

, meaning “I understand,” was inspired by Malla’s experiences spending time on the land with her family from a young age.


“This song really represents who I am, where my ancestors came from and the creation of everything, which is so spectacular,” said Malla. “Going through this song made me realize how much I must appreciate life itself and my surroundings.”


Malla initially considered skipping this year’s competition but said she changed her mind after learning its theme,

Avatiliriniq

, which is focused on respect and care for the land, animals and environment.


She began writing during her summer break this year, starting with a guitar melody before the lyrics came together. She submitted her songs

July 1 and later travelled to Iqaluit to record both entries at Aakuluk Studio this month.


Malla’s interest in music began when she was about eight or nine years old, she said. Growing up in a Christian household in Arviat, she learned from her father, who was also a musician.


She started with keyboard and piano before joining a Christian band as a teenager.


“The passion for music is in me. I really love it and I love sharing my Inuit culture, especially my language. I speak my mother tongue most of the time, and I love to share that,” Malla said.


Her love of music is also shared with students at the Sakku School in Coral Harbour where Malla teaches music and art.


Her classes are currently learning basic guitar chords on the ukulele.


“I try to promote my language but today, [the students] mostly speak English, but I try to speak Inuktitut and it’s kind of hard, encouraging them to speak their language, ” Malla said.


She released her debut solo album,

My Irnik & My Panik

, in October 2024. A second album has been approved, and she hopes to begin recording next year with producer Chris Coleman, who owns Nuvu Music and Sound, a recording studio in Iqaluit.


Malla said the Qilaut competition has given her an opportunity to reflect on her own experiences as an Inuk woman through songwriting.


“Through music, you learn a lot. You pick up words and memorize them, which is really useful. You get the sense of, ‘Yeah, that’s us Inuit. That’s me as an Inuk,’” she said.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Israel Is Creating a “Permanent Architecture of Control” Amid Gaza Genocide
content:
Israel’s flattening, extraction, and reshaping of the rubble in Gaza is a continuation of its crimes, says an expert.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

We speak with Forensic Architecture’s Eyal Weizman about his new book, Ungrounding: The Architecture of Genocide, a meticulous investigation into Israel’s genocide in Gaza, the physical destruction of the territory and its impact on the Palestinian people.

Forensic Architecture was founded in 2010 as an interdisciplinary research group focused on investigating state violence and human rights violations. Since 2023, Forensic Architecture has focused on producing evidence for South Africa’s genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice.

Weizman says “ungrounding” is “a kind of destruction that we have not seen anywhere else,” with Israeli bulldozers “terraforming” the landscape to erase all traces of Palestinian life. With thousands of bodies still unrecovered from under destroyed buildings, Israel’s flattening, extraction and reshaping of the rubble in Gaza is a continuation of its crimes, says Weizman.

“Israel is actively and against court order, against the order of the ICJ, destroying the evidence of the genocide that it has perpetrated,” he says.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: Israel is continuing to commit genocide in Gaza long past the so-called ceasefire agreement. That’s according to a new report out this week from the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. The report also accuses Israeli forces of committing crimes against humanity in the West Bank, including extermination, torture and rape.

The Israeli Mission in Geneva said the latest report was part of a “misinformation campaign to demonize the State of Israel” and to, quote, “destroy the Jewish state,” unquote.

The United Nations-commissioned experts said Israel was, quote, “continuing to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza,” unquote. They found Israeli forces continued using heavy munitions, drones, quadcopters, artillery and sniper fire in densely populated areas during the ceasefire. They also found that the so-called Yellow Line, which was presented as a temporary ceasefire demarcation, is increasingly encroaching into Gaza and becoming a de facto border.

Well, the organization Forensic Architecture, which has been mapping Israel’s military conduct in Gaza since October 2023, details exactly how Israel has used the Yellow Line to expand its territorial control of Gaza. Here’s a clip from the project titled “A Cartography of Genocide.”

NARRATOR: When the ceasefire came into effect, most of the area Israel had depopulated remained under its control. This constituted 54% of Gaza, marked by the Yellow Line. The Yellow Line is meant to mark phase one of Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza. Instead, Israel is using the line to expand its control.

Along the Yellow Line, Israel has placed concrete yellow blocks, signaling areas Palestinians cannot approach. We have mapped the position of more than 100 yellow blocks. Most have been placed well beyond the agreed withdrawal line. Over time, Israel is moving these blocks further into the area where Palestinians are concentrated. With every expansion, the military destroys another neighborhood, preventing Palestinian return.

Israel also imposed an additional boundary, which it called the Orange Line. In some places, this line encroaches more than one kilometer beyond the Yellow Line.

At the same time, Israel has entrenched its military presence. Around every 1.8 kilometers along the Yellow Line, it has built a fortified military base. We have documented 34 active bases. Many bases, like this one in Bani Suheila, have been constructed on the ruins of Palestinian homes.

Israel has also demolished and compacted nearby buildings which remained standing. Building by building, Gaza’s landscape is being permanently reconfigured. This picture shows the neighborhood before it was erased.

AMY GOODMAN: On Tuesday, the U.N. special rapporteur on the Occupied Palestinian Territories, Francesca Albanese, called on the ICC, the International Criminal Court, to investigate incitement to genocide by government officials and media figures in Israel.

author: Jake Johnson
title: UK Bars Entry to Swedish Climate Scholar Who Advocates for Palestinian Rights
content:
Andreas Malm was scheduled to speak at a conference that will also feature a co-founder of Palestine Action.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The United Kingdom’s Labour government has barred Swedish climate scholar and Palestinian rights advocate Andreas Malm from entering the country, without explanation, just days before he was scheduled to speak at a conference that will also feature a co-founder of Palestine Action — an organization banned by the UK government on highly dubious grounds.

Malm, an author and associate professor of human ecology at Sweden’s Lund University, said Friday that he was “dismayed” by the UK Home Office’s decision this week to cancel his Electronic Travel Authorization, noting that he has “been going to the UK for decades — this is where I did my archival research for my PhD dissertation and lectured at dozens of universities and participated in even more conferences.”

Malm said the UK government’s move was “nothing short of scandalous,” and he linked the decision to his scheduled appearance at the conference organized by the socialist magazine Tribune. The event was billed as a discussion of “domination and resistance in the age of [US President Donald] Trump,” featuring Malm and Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori.

“This is a drift toward authoritarianism that didn’t begin with me, and it’s not going to end with me either,” Malm told Al Jazeera. “If I’m now being deemed a threat to the public good because I’m supposed to have a conversation with someone from Palestine Action, this is guilt by association.”

Verso Books, Malm’s publisher — including of his 2025 book The Destruction of Palestine Is the Destruction of the Earth — said in a statement Friday that it is “shocked and disturbed by the Labour government’s decision to ban one of our leading authors.”

“Never in over 55 years of publishing has a British government revoked the right of one of our authors to enter the country,” said Tariq Ali, the chair of Verso’s board of directors. “We can only assume, since no reasons have been given for banning him, that Andreas’ positions on Palestine, no different from the [International Criminal Court] and UN commissions, is the cause.”

“Verso Books condemns the silencing of critical voices and stands in support of writers and scholars who continue to speak out about important issues and contribute to open intellectual discourse,” Ali added. “We urge the government to restore Andreas Malm’s electronic travel authorisation immediately and allow him entry into the country.”

Jeremy Corbyn, the former UK Labour leader who now serves as the Your Party MP for Islington North, joined the chorus denouncing the cancellation of Malm’s travel authorization.

“This is an absurd and outrageous decision,” Corbyn wrote on social media. “What kind of society are we living in where world-renowned authors and campaigners are treated as enemies and threats? The real threat is this government’s assault on freedom of expression.”

“This is not an isolated incident — and the government should know that it is gaining a bad reputation for censorship and repression,” added Corbyn. “We know why the government has taken this decision: because it wants to silence criticism of Israel, as well as its own complicity in genocide. It will not succeed.”

title: Grad Students Strike at Harvard, University With $68 Billion Endowment
content:
“None of us here, despite attending the wealthiest university in the entire world, make a living wage.”

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Harvard graduate student workers walked off the job on Tuesday in their second strike of 2026 — and other Harvard workers are set to follow with additional strikes in the coming weeks, as union activity heats up on campuses in the Boston area.

The Harvard Graduate Students Union-United Auto Workers Local 5118 (HGSU), which represents over 4,000 student workers, began their strike at midnight on Tuesday. The strike comes five months after the union ended a six-week strike in the spring, which ended without a contract.

The union’s demands are “safe work, fair pay, and the right to stay”— meaning stronger grievance processes and the right to third-party arbitration in sexual harassment and discrimination cases; pay equity and wages on par with those for student workers at MIT and Brown University; and protections for non-citizen and disabled workers.

Sarah Johns, a member of HGSU’s bargaining committee, told Truthout that the union called off their first strike this year in May after some progress in contract negotiations with the university. But despite bargaining over the summer, “we were really disappointed in the lack of momentum from Harvard,” she said. As a result, “our membership voted that it was necessary to escalate this fight in order to get a contract.”

In a letter published on Tuesday, HGSU President Denish Jaswal wrote that Harvard had “refused to meaningfully engage” with the union and offered a “regressive contract worse than our last, stripping away millions in previously negotiated benefit funds” and removing protected classes from the contract, while also resorting to “anti-labor tactics.”

“Our benefits have been completely gutted,” Johns told Truthout. “Harvard has cut over $3 million from our benefits funds that we had access to in our last contract. We also no longer have access to health care, dental, vision, and they also cut our parental benefits by 50 percent.”

Harvard grad student workers currently only have access to “emergency funds,” which do not cover costs for people with disabilities and chronic conditions, she said. Though HGSU had brought over a dozen student workers to a negotiating session to testify on the importance of these benefits, Harvard refused to budge on the issue, she added.

A day after HGSU’s last contract expired on June 30, 2025, Harvard “carved out” over 900 student workers from the union, claiming that those covered by stipends could not be considered employees eligible for union protection, weakening the union’s ranks.

In a video taken after the strike’s launch, Jaswal said: “None of us here, despite attending the wealthiest university in the entire world, make a living wage. Right now, I make $26,000, in fact, which qualifies me for SNAP benefits in the state of Massachusetts. Harvard’s offer was to bring me to $29,000 by the year 2029, which still qualifies me for SNAP benefits.”

Harvard has also maintained that they will not bargain on harassment or discrimination policies. The union has asked for third-party grievances and additional protections to be written into their contracts — issues that have been core to the union’s fight since it began organizing in 2018, and which have recently come under the national spotlight with the Cornell rape case.

One in five student workers at Harvard reports experiencing harassment or discrimination while at Harvard, Johns explained. “We have found that many of our students are reluctant to come to Harvard and interact with Title IX processes because they just don’t trust the university and they don’t trust Title IX procedures.”

“We know from notable news stories that Harvard has an interest in not finding itself guilty,” Johns went on, regarding the university’s control over grievance processes. “There are a couple departments that had a number of high profile professors with allegations against them, and Harvard has taken no action against those professors.”

The union is also asking for protections for its non-citizen students, including a policy barring Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents from entering campus without a judicial warrant. While this is Harvard’s current policy, the union is asking for it to be codified into their contract.

author: Daron Letts
title: Cambridge Bay’s runway to be paved
content:
Cambridge Bay’s gravel airport runway is one step closer to being paved, says Nunavut’s transportation minister.


Almost $3.5 million towards planning and design of the project will come from the Department of National Defence’s capital assistance program, George Hickes told Nunatsiaq News Friday in an interview.


The update comes after Cambridge Bay MLA Fred Pedersen pressed Hickes in the legislative assembly Monday during question period about the state of his community’s runway.


“It’s obvious the efficiencies that would be achieved through paving,” Hickes said to Pedersen in response.  “It’s a no-brainer.”


Pedersen had asked

 if the minister agreed with comments made by Buffalo Airways general manager Mikey McBryan, who called on the federal government in September to pave the runway. McBryan made the comments at a House of Commons Indigenous and Northern Affairs Committee meeting in Ottawa on Sept. 24.


The design is expected to be complete by fall 2027, Hickes said in an interview Friday.


As for the paving itself — “the sooner the better after that,” he said.


Cambridge Bay’s airport is located three kilometres southwest of the hamlet. Its

gravel runway is a little more than 5,000 feet long and 150 feet wide.


The gravel limits the size of aircraft that can land in the community.


The airport can accomodate Buffalo Air’s Lockheed Electra and 737-200 aircraft, which burn about 20 per cent more fuel and haul about 10,000 pounds less that the airline’s Boeing 737-300 twin engine jetliner.


But a 737-300 needs to land on a paved runway, McBryan, with Buffalo Air, told federal leaders in September.


“Paving the runway in Cambridge Bay would instantaneously bring the cost of living down the next day,” McBryan said to

 Nunavut MP Lori Idlout, who had asked if paving the territory’s runways could help keep dollars inside the territory.


“I don’t care if it’s military funding, if it’s private funding or if it’s government funding: Pave it. It’ll make everything better,” McBryan said during the committee meeting.


The federal government

announced

 in March a $2.7-billion

plan

 to expand the military’s presence in the Arctic, with upgrades to support military in five Arctic communities, including Cambridge Bay.


The paving project is part of the preparation for Cambridge Bay’s bigger role in the country’s defence network, Hickes said.


Pedersen said he’s “excited” to hear about the funding.


“All airlines will save money and I’m hoping that even passenger airfares will go down,” he said in an interview.


“Having a paved runway and hopefully better airfield lighting and instrument landing systems will help in inclement weather getting things to land.”


Nunatsiaq News asked the Department of National Defence for a comment on the runway paving but did not receive a response Friday morning.

author: Unknown
title: Sciopero generale: l’Italia si blocca
content:
Giornata di sciopero generale: numeri ancor più massicci delle prime manifestazioni dell’autunno scorso. Blocchi in tutta Italia e cortei da decine di migliaia di persone, dalle metropoli alle province.


Contro la guerra, contro il carovita, contro il riarmo voluto dal governo Meloni. E ancora, contro una vita precaria e indignitosa, per dire basta ai sacrifici che il governo italiano, insieme ai governi di tutta Europa, vogliono imporre alla popolazione. La partecipazione è stata impressionante, da Sud a Nord, oltre un milione in tutta Italia. Il Paese che per anni è stato narrato come il bacino dell’indifferenza e che nei migliori dei casi avrebbe voluto “fare come in Francia” in queste settimane, sull’onda del ciclo di movimento iniziato un anno fa a sostegno della Palestina e contro la complicità dei governi con il genocidio, sta dando un segnale chiaro: è giunto il tempo di alzare la testa.


Grazie ai giovani che a fronte del peso di un futuro rubato stanno occupando scuole e università da un mese per affermare la propria esistenza, ai giovani che con rabbia calciano indietro la sfrontatezza dell’ingiustizia, oggi grazie alla chiamata allo sciopero generale indetto dall’Unione Sindacale di Base, si sono uniti i lavoratori e le lavoratrici che non hanno nessuna garanzia di vedere riconosciuto il proprio lavoro. Ma precarietà e sfruttamento non sono più un orizzonte accettato. Gli agricoltori e gli autotrasportatori che al Sud hanno bloccato le merci lo dicono da settimane, insieme a studenti, famiglie e a chiunque individua la causa di questa situazione alle scelte politiche dall’alto, sottomesse ai diktat europei e trumpiani: non c’è più disponibilità.


Il governo Meloni deve fare i conti con il fatto che in piazza c’è il paese che porta avanti l’ingranaggio di questo sistema e che se decide di fermarsi non ci sarà alcuna prova di forza in grado di reggere il confronto. Le briciole di una finanziaria che tenta di mascherare in ogni modo che l’unico interesse governativo è trovare i soldi per il riarmo non hanno alcuna possibilità di convincere la popolazione.


A Bologna, Pisa, Livorno, Roma, Torino, Treviso, Milano, Reggio Calabria, Palermo, Bari, Trieste, Pavia, Vicenza, Modena, Padova, Mestre, Cosenza, Napoli, Genova sono state bloccate le arterie principali delle città, gli snodi delle tangenziali e i porti.


Livorno: la mattinata parte con il blocco del porto, prosegue poi con un corteo di oltre 20 mila persone e continua con il blocco della circolazione al varco Zara.


Bologna: 50 mila persone nonostante i blocchi della polizia aprono un varco e arrivano a inondare l’autostrada.


Modena: giovani e famiglie in corteo contro guerra e carovita.


Torino: un corteo diramato in tutta la città, dal centro alla tangenziale, raggiunge quota 100 mila persone, viene rilanciato l’appuntamento alle 18 per un altro corteo cittadino.


Cosenza: corteo di massa di 7mila persone ha invaso le strade della città e bloccato autostrada e superstrada.


Pisa: un corteo di 20 mila persone si conclude con l’occupazione del Palazzo della Sapienza, nel pomeriggio appuntamento per una grande assemblea.


Brescia: 10 mila persone in corteo hanno tentato di raggiungere l’autostrada, cariche della polizia.


Milano: 80 mila persone raggiungono la tangenziale.


Pavia: grande manifestazione contro guerra e carovita.

author: Aldrey Olegario
title: ‘Primavera Brasileira’: como ato de estudantes virou onda global contra extrema direita
content:
Na noite de 4 de outubro, quando Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) terminou à frente de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no 1.º turno das eleições, a seguinte mensagem chegou num grupo de WhatsApp de alunos da Universidade Federal Fluminense (UFF): “O momento pede ação”. Na noite seguinte, 5 de outubro, o Brasil assistiu ao primeiro ato dos jovens.


“Nós vimos a vitória do Flávio de uma forma muito acachapante. Ninguém estava esperando. Aquilo gerou um sentimento de descrença muito forte no campo progressista. Mas na Faculdade de Direito da UFF, pela nossa história, enxergamos de forma contrária: com esperança e com vontade de ir à luta”, diz Kayky Moraes, aluno do curso de direito da UFF que participou do primeiro levante.


Realizada em Niterói, na região metropolitana do Rio de Janeiro, a marcha dos estudantes saiu do prédio da Faculdade de Direito rumo à reitoria da universidade.

As imagens tomaram as redes e iniciaram um efeito dominó que impulsionou mobilizações estudantis nos cinco cantos do país. “Ali a gente sentiu que dava para brigar.”


Neste momento manifestação contra Bolsonaro pelos estudantes nas ruas Niterói

October 5, 2026


O resultado desse “efeito borboleta” veio no dia 25 de outubro, três semanas depois. Um feito histórico: Lula virou o jogo e

venceu as eleições

 por uma vantagem de 4,4 milhões de votos, algo que nenhum candidato a presidente que terminou como segundo colocado no 1º turno havia conseguido fazer antes. Os eleitores de Lula e os estrategistas de campanha do PT tiveram apenas três semanas para mudar a rota. “Essa foi a campanha menos organizada que participei desde 1989”, chegou a dizer o presidente Lula em uma reunião com parlamentares em Brasília.


“Os jovens tomaram as ruas de forma orgânica e organizada para defender um projeto de país, mas também um projeto de ser humano. Quando Lula disse aquela frase para a gente ser ele amanhã, porque ele já foi a gente ontem e para a juventude botar a cara a tapa, acho que é isso mesmo”, diz Kayky, em referência a um trecho da entrevista de Lula para o podcast Flow.

“Estamos fadados a viver o futuro e a gente tem que construir o futuro que a gente quer.”


A “primavera brasileira”, como começou a ser apelidada a vitória eleitoral frente à extrema direita, também pode ser vista por como uma posição do Brasil

como símbolo de resistência aos interesses dos Estados Unidos, defende Mayra Goulart, doutora em ciência política pela UERJ.


“O Brasil será um pólo da resistência à relação imperial que os Estados Unidos tentam restabelecer. Na última assembleia geral da ONU, Lula disse que o Brasil não iria ser o quintal de ninguém. O presidente Lula recupera a tradição de não alinhamento automático da diplomacia brasileira a potências estrangeiras e a adoção de um caminho próprio e soberanista. Isso é entendido muitas vezes como um caminho que vem a liderar outros países periféricos”, diz.


A “Primavera Brasileira” vista do exterior


No México e na Espanha, a virada eleitoral brasileira foi recebida não apenas com alívio geopolítico, mas como um estudo de caso sobre como conter a ascensão da extrema direita.


Para Homero Campa Butrón, cientista político e professor da Universidade Nacional Autônoma do México (UNAM), a manutenção do governo progressista no Brasil evita o isolamento regional no continente. “Brasil e México representam 55% da população da América Latina e 60% da economia da região. O resultado no Brasil foi vital para o governo mexicano, pois evita o isolamento diante da onda de vitórias da direita na região nos últimos meses”, analisa Campa, destacando que a comunicação entre a presidenta mexicana Claudia Sheinbaum e Lula é direta e estratégica.


O impacto também ressoa na Europa. “Se o Brasil conseguiu, a Espanha também consegue”, disse o primeiro-ministro da Espanha Pedro Sánchez

, em um comício em Gijón, na região de Astúrias, realizado na segunda-feira, 26 de outubro. “Vamos fazer o mesmo que Lula fez no Brasil. O mundo está olhando para nós”, completou.


Com eleições gerais agendadas para o próximo mês na Espanha, onde as pesquisas têm indicado a predileção do eleitorado à direita, o desfecho brasileiro renovou o ânimo das forças de esquerda. “Certamente, no México e na Espanha, percebe-se um enorme interesse no modelo de mobilização social promovido por meio das redes sociais, coordenado pelo deputado André Janones. author: rimsha syed
title: Houston Activists Are Working to Disrupt the Flow of Weapons to Israel
content:
Organizers and workers around the world are highlighting the invisible complicity of logistics companies in genocide.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

On October 30, port workers in over 100 locations across the world stood in principled resistance to Israel’s ongoing genocide through an international strike meant to constrict the arms trade and physically halt munitions destined to be used in Palestine. From coast to coast, linking arms in the struggle against maritime transport has been a historic strategy to intervene in the material transport of weapons, ammunition, and military equipment, through coordinated direct action by the working class.

Three years into Israel’s livestreamed genocide, actions of international magnitude underscore the immediate and collective need to stop the flow of artillery into Gaza. Following the repeated demands of the Palestinian General Federation of Trade Unions to “urgently halt the arms trade with Israel” and “take action against complicit companies involved in implementing Israel’s brutal and illegal siege,” several grassroots arms embargo campaigns in port cities across the United States — including New York City, Oakland, and Houston — have been mobilizing alongside dockworkers, transportation crews, and unions.

In New York, the “Break the Chain” campaign is fighting to halt explosives and F-35 bomber components from reaching Gaza through the JFK Airport. In Oakland, the People’s Arms Embargo gathered hundreds outside FedEx’s massive Air Freight Center in East Oakland to protest the company’s complicity in shipping arms to Israel. Last year, the Palestinian Youth Movement shared a report stating that in 2025, at least 280 military cargo shipments, including parts for one of the world’s most lethal fighter jets, reached Gaza via Oakland’s airport. Now, the Houston arms embargo campaign is calling on Texans to join their week of action to confront logistics executives complicit in unfathomable violence and destruction at the 2026 Houston International Maritime Conference.

In the sweltering September Houston heat, at a cafe with “ICE not welcome” signs plastered on every door and window, arms embargo organizers hosted a teach-in about the city’s port — a key transportation hub for the global weapons supply chain. Elsewhere in the cafe, others hand-crafted banners with calls that read “A Future Without Genocide, A Port for the People” as a response to the conference’s slogan “Lessons from the Past, Strategies for the Future.”

The fifth annual maritime conference, hosted from November 2-5, presents a unique opportunity to directly confront executives from logistics companies responsible for supplying the Israeli military with weapons. Roshni Ahmed, a member of the outreach working group, said that the arms embargo demands aren’t new: “Many people in the past three years have felt a deep sense of hopelessness and heartbreak watching the genocide unfold.” In May 2024, the Palestinian Youth Movement launched the #MaskOffMaersk campaign, in which Houston has played a critical role through a myriad of ongoing organizing strategies.

“Through coordinated pressure, boycotts, and refusal to handle military cargo, the world can make these genocidal supply chains politically untenable.”

“Arms embargo campaigns, such as this one in Houston, give people a very tangible way to stop the genocide by cutting off the very weapons that are used to kill Palestinians,” said Ahmed. The movement against the blood-soaked military industrial complex in Houston centers on Lockheed Martin’s massive aeronautics production plant in nearby Fort Worth, where the F-35 fighter jet is assembled from components transported on Maersk container ships before being flown directly to the Nevatim Airbase and used to bomb the besieged population in Palestine. “From 2020 to 2025, Houston’s port processed 85 percent of all Israeli shipments of F-35 fighter jet parts,” said Ahmed, noting how logistics companies like Maersk directly facilitate U.S. and Israeli wars.

Logistics companies like Maersk “are integral to the arms pipeline sustaining Israel’s genocidal assault in Gaza and its brutal military occupation of the West Bank,” said Dr. Jake Alimahomed-Wilson, a professor of sociology at California State University. author: David Swanson
title: The 10 Worst Congressional Excuses for Voting for More Military Spending
content:
Economic Cost, Immorality, Law, Myth of Necessity, North America, What to do

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 30, 2026

Every year for many years now, the bitterly divided, grid-locked, virtually civil-war-waging United States Congress (as it’s commonly depicted) has harmoniously voted for vastly more money in war spending than it had done the year before. Our lords and misrepresentatives are threatening the same again right now.

It’s a heartwarming story of cooperation and understanding, no doubt, but how can you, as an elected official, explain to constituents living third-world lives in a wealthy nation that, not only can you not tax the rich or the corporations, but you also cannot afford to fund education, energy, environment, transportation, retirement, healthcare, or housing because the weapons dealers just want more and more?

The trick, of course, in most cases is to keep your head down and your mouth shut until a bigger military spending bill than last year’s is guaranteed to pass no matter how you vote, and then vote No. You’ll be untouchable. It’s golden. You won’t have publicly organized your colleagues or used various available procedures to actually try to reduce the war spending, but you’ll have an “I voted No” shield, and that’s all you’ll need. Constituents will fall for it without fooling any weapons dealers.

But what if it’s your turn? What if you’ve drawn the short string this year? What if you can either vote Yes or anger your party’s “leader”?

Never fear! That’s what this handy guide is for! Here are 10 popular categories of excuses that have proven effective through the past quarter-century.

You can easily depict an increase to military spending as a decrease if it’s a smaller increase than someone — ideally the president — had initially proposed. This one is in the works right now and may prove very successful. A variation on this is to claim that the bad political party (the one you’re not in) would have gotten a larger increase if you hadn’t hurried or stalled, depending on which party is gaining or losing a majority.

Almost foolproof is the oft-used explanation that you focused your efforts on doing exactly what the peace activists wanted by removing some nasty section from the bill. “You didn’t want the U.S. and Israeli militaries to merge. You said to only vote for the bill if that was removed. We got it removed on condition that we vote for the bill. This is how things work in the real world.” This excuse gets a 5 out of 5 on Yelp. Anyone who objects is a silly dreamer, so you need not address their concerns.

Almost matching the batting record of #2 (removing something) is adding something. It hardly matters how absurd the thing or how out of place in an institution of mass-murder and destruction, as long as it’s humanitarian. Create an agency of environmentally sustainable carpet bombing, or eliminate discrimination against transgendered pilots, or establish a proactive contracting program to minority-owned surveillance companies. Whatever. Anyone who objects will be objecting to that thing you voted for. You should be clear that it is only that thing for which you voted; nothing else exists.

If you cannot use the top three steaming turds of the coming apocalypse, or don’t have time to come up with anything concrete, just fall back on troopism. You voted to fund the troops. Anyone objecting hates the troops, wants the troops left in the wars but their armor and weaponry carefully collected and brought home without them. If you can, grab an actual troop or three to stand in front of and ask one of them to slap you in the face really quickly until there are tears visible in your eyes before the cameras are ready.

Numerous other excuses can work beautifully, depending on the circumstances. There’s always a most-unpopular war among the current wars. Right now, for example, some people are more upset about the crumbs going to the war on Iran than about the mountain of loafs going to the Pentagon in its entirety. So, here’s what you do. You make getting a war powers resolution on Iran vetoed part of a grand bargain in which you vote for the money to create 10 more similar wars. Or you join in a lawsuit against the war on Iran. Or you actually include in the spending bill or elsewhere a ban on spending money on that particular crime — but make clear to everyone that it’s part of a grand bargain on a 4-D chessboard. You voted for increased war money FOR PEACE and so that …

author: daniel
title: Der lange Atem zählt
content:
Rückblick: Geschichte der UAA Gronau

Seit 1985 wird in der bundesweit einzigen Urananreicherungsanlage Uran angereichert. Nach mehreren Erweiterungen kann inzwischen in der Anlage jährlich nuklearer Uran-Brennstoff für den Betrieb von ca. 30 Atomkraftwerken in aller Welt produziert werden. Betrieben wird die UAA Gronau vom Urenco-Konzern, der international verschachtelt ist. Urenco betreibt u. a. auch die niederländische Schwesteranlage in Almelo. Der deutsche Zweig des Urenco-Konzerns ist jeweils zu 50 % im Besitz der Energiekonzerne E.ON und RWE.

Während am Standort Gronau, neben der Produktion von angereichertem Uran, inzwischen auch an neuen „Brennstoffen“ für neue AKW-Typen geforscht wird, erfolgt am Urenco-Standort Jülich (auch in NRW) über die Enrichment Technology Company (ETC) die für die Urananreicherung erforderliche Zentrifugenforschung bzw. Zentrifugenproduktion.

Gegen den Bau der UAA Gronau wurden Ende der 1970er Jahre rund 7000 Einsprüche gesammelt und eingereicht. Im Mai 1981 fand in Gronau der Erörterungstermin für die erste Ausbaustufe statt und Silvester 1981 wurde die erste Genehmigung zum Bau einer Anlage mit 1000 Tonnen Urantrennarbeit pro Jahr (UTA/a) erteilt. Es folgten weitere Genehmigungsverfahren und jetzt sind 4500t UTA/a genehmigt.

Nach dem Baubeginn 1982 begann im ersten Teil der UAA Gronau am 15. August 1985 erstmals die Produktion von angereichertem Uran, das nach der Weiterverarbeitung in Brennelementefabriken (z. B. in Lingen oder in Schweden) die Grundlage für den Betrieb zahlreicher Atomkraftwerke in aller Welt ist. Die offizielle Einweihung der Anlage erfolgte Monate später unter Protest am 12. Juni 1986, wenige Wochen nach dem Super-GAU in Tschernobyl. Vor der Anlage demonstrierten rund 300 Bürger*innen gegen die UAA und die mit ihr verbundenen Gefahren.

Anlässlich des 40. Jahrestages der offiziellen Inbetriebnahme der UAA (12. Juni 1986 / 2026) bekräftigten Umweltverbände und Bürgerinitiativen (darunter der BBU und der AKU Gronau) ihre Forderung nach Aufhebung der UAA-Betriebsgenehmigungen und nach der sofortigen Stilllegung der bundesweit einzigen Urananreicherungsanlage.

Gefahren der Urananreicherung, der Urantransporte und der atomwaffentauglichen Zentrifugentechnik

Umstritten ist die Gronauer Atomfabrik wegen zahlreicher Gefahren, aber auch, weil die in ihr genutzte Zentrifugentechnik nach Umbauarbeiten auch zur Produktion von Uran für Atomwaffen genutzt werden könnte. Die Anlage in Gronau ist weder gegen Flugzeugabstürze noch gegen militärische Angriffe oder Drohnenbeschuss gesichert.

Wiederholt gab es in der UAA Störfälle. 2010 wurde ein Arbeiter in der Anlage verstrahlt. Erhebliche Gefahren gehen auch von den zahlreichen Urantransporten mit LKW und Sonderzügen von und zur Urananreicherungsanlage aus, die ganz NRW, aber auch weitere Bundesländer, durchqueren. Oft werden sie auch international durchgeführt. Hilfs- und Rettungskräfte an den Transportstrecken werden im Vorfeld nicht über die gefährlichen Transporte informiert. Bei einem Transportunfall könnte es zu weitreichenden Verseuchungen kommen. Wissen muss man dabei, dass in der UAA Uranhexafluorid (UF6) verarbeitet wird, und dieser Stoff wird auch in verschiedenen Isotopenzusammensetzungen transportiert. UF6 ist radioaktiv und reagiert bei Freisetzungen u. a. zur aggressiven Flusssäure. Wiederholt gab es Proteste gegen diese Transporte sowie Schienenblockaden. Schwachaktiver Atommüll aus Gronau wurde auch bereits in das Fasslager in Gorleben gebracht.

Auch aus den Reihen der Friedensbewegung wird immer wieder die Stilllegung der Gronauer Urananreicherungsanlage gefordert. Die UAA Gronau könnte im Konfliktfall ein militärisch wichtiges Angriffsziel sein, denn die Zentrifugentechnik, die in der Anlage zum Einsatz kommt, kann auch zur Produktion von Uran für Atomwaffen genutzt werden. Dieser Umstand diente dem Trump-Regime als Vorwand, um die Urananreicherungsstandorte im Iran zu bombardieren.

Um auf die militärische Brisanz der Urananreicherung hinzuweisen, fanden und finden immer wieder Ostermärsche zur Gronauer Urananreicherungsanlage statt. An dem bisher größten Ostermarsch in Gronau beteiligten sich 2011, kurz nach der Atomkatastrophe in Fukushima, rund 15.000 Menschen.

Aktuelle Militarisierung der Urananreicherung und des Urenco-Konzerns

author: daniel
title: Der rechte Durchmarsch kann gestoppt werden
content:
die Graswurzelrevolution setzt seit 1972 auf die emanzipatorischen sozialen Bewegungen. Die letzten Wochen haben gezeigt, dass diese Bewegungen, allen Rückschlägen zum Trotz, weltweit den gesellschaftlichen Wandel hin zu einer besseren Gesellschaft vorantreiben. Wer hätte gedacht, dass die studentische Bewegung in Serbien den seit neun Jahren regierenden Autokratie- und Putin-Fan Aleksandar Vučić hinwegfegen würde? Diese Protestbewegung erreichte bei der Wahl am 25. Oktober mit einer eigenen Liste die absolute Mehrheit: 52 Prozent der abgegebenen Stimmen. Bei der Wahl in Brasilien wurde der rechtsextremistische Kandidat Bolsonaro junior massiv vom Trump-Regime, den Techmilliardären Musk und Zuckerberg und ihren Propagandamaschinen X, Facebook, instagram, Whatsapp und Co. unterstützt. Trotzdem gewann am 25. Oktober der von großen Teilen der emanzipatorischen Bewegungen des Landes unterstützte Sozialist Lula die Wahl im größten Land Lateinamerikas. Eine gute Nachricht für den Amazonas und die Überlebenschancen zukünftiger Generationen. Als Anarchist bin ich grundsätzlich kein Freund von Regierungen. Aber ich weiß, dass es einen Unterschied macht, ob es eine linke Regierung gibt, die die Verfeuerung des Regenwalds eindämmt oder eine faschistische Lügenbaron-Mafia, die die Lebensgrundlagen der Menschheit und alles, wofür wir kämpfen, für einen profitorientierten, menschenfeindlichen Turbokapitalismus zerstört. Auf dem Weg zu einer solidarischen, gewaltfreien und herrschaftslosen Gesellschaft, können wir nicht zulassen, dass soziale Errungenschaften getilgt und Menschenrechte mit Füßen getreten werden. Die Ereignisse in Serbien und Brasilien zeigen, dass der rechte Durchmarsch gestoppt werden kann, wenn die antifaschistischen Menschen sich unterhaken. Alle Despoten werden fallen, wenn wir sie vom Pferd ziehen. Seit Wochen sind in Europa Hunderttausende auf der Straße, um sich gegen die Sozialkahlschlagspolitik zu wehren, mit der die Regierungen ihre massive militärische Aufrüstung finanzieren. An den überwiegend gewaltfreien Massenprotesten in Frankreich (siehe Artikel auf Seite 3) beteiligten sich allein am 24. Oktober über 500.000 Schüler*innen und Student*innen, der Polizeigewalt und Hetze von rechten Politiker*innen und Medien zum Trotz. Wunderbar! Mit der GWR 512 konnten wir ein bisschen zur Mobilisierung für die Konzertkundgebung „UNZWINGBAR – Kein Bock auf Krieg und Wehrpflicht“ in Berlin beitragen. Am 2. Oktober zeigten über 20.000 überwiegend junge Menschen vor dem Brandenburger Tor, dass der Antimilitarismus lebt. Zusammen mit Musiker*innen u.a. von Dritte Wahl und K.I.Z. setzten sie ein Ausrufezeichen gegen Aufrüstung und Militarisierung.

Die GWR ist ein Sprachrohr u.a. des Antimilitarismus. Auch diese Ausgabe hat wieder einen antimilitaristischen Schwerpunkt (S. 1, 8-11, 18). Wie erfolgreich eine soziale Bewegung auch hierzulande sein kann, das hat die Anti-Atomkraft-Bewegung gezeigt. Nach jahrzehntelangem Kampf wurden am 15. April 2023 mit Lingen 2, Isar 2 und Neckarwestheim endlich die letzten von 37 AKWs des Landes stillgelegt. Der Atomausstieg ist aber auch in Deutschland noch nicht verwirklicht. Das zeigen der deutsch-französische Atomdeal mit dem Putin-Konzern Rosatom (siehe GWR 512) und der Betrieb der Urananreicherungsanlage (UAA) in Gronau (S. 1, 19). In dieser GWR geht es auch um Repression gegen soziale Bewegungsaktivist*innen in der Türkei (S. 6), in Griechenland (S. 4), in Ungarn (S. 7) und in den USA (S. 5). Wie sehr eine mediale Hetzkampagne ins Leere laufen kann, zeigt die seit dem Wahlsieg der Linken in Berlin andauernde Schmutzkampagne von CDU/CSU und AfD gegen die Rote Hilfe (S. 7). Die Mitgliederzahl der linken Hilfsorganisation geht seitdem durch die Decke. Da möchte ich Heinrich Mann zitieren, der 1913 mit „Der Untertan“ eines der wichtigsten Bücher des 20. Jahrhunderts geschrieben und 1926 klar gestellt hat: „Die Rote Hilfe ist vor allem ein zivilisatorisches Werk, sie wirkt der uns bedrohenden Barbarei entgegen.“ Wir brauchen einen langen Atem und Utopien, die uns Kraft spenden „für den Kampf ums Paradies“ (Ton Steine Scherben). Dazu empfehle ich Euch die Beiträge unter der Rubrik „Jetzt oder nie – Utopie“ (S. 13 f.), die Texte über die Anarchistinnen Erna Paul (S. 16) und Kati Horna (S. 17). Außerdem die Film- und Buchrezensionen, die ihr im „Feuilleton“ (S. 20 ff.) findet. Anarchie und Glück, Bernd Drücke (GWR-Red.)

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Starlink Reportedly Tried to Upsell Ukraine on New Plan After Throttling Service
content:
Ukraine is highly dependent on Starlink connectivity as the company has a relative monopoly in the industry.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

After Elon Musk ordered his company SpaceX to throttle Ukraine’s satellite internet service amid disagreements over its military operations earlier this month, the company suggested that Ukraine’s government upgrade its plan to avoid service interruptions, new reporting finds.

The upsell was reported in The Atlantic, which found that SpaceX, which operates Starlink, advised that Ukraine switch to a more expensive plan to avoid service interruptions when asked about the outage.

“If anything can yet restrain Musk from abandoning Ukraine, it may be his own financial interests,” The Atlantic reported this week. “Earlier this month, when U.S. military officials asked SpaceX about the outages in Ukraine, the company advised switching to an upgraded contract to restore Ukraine’s access, U.S. officials told us.”

The incident came just four months after SpaceX’s IPO this June. Reports have suggested that Starlink has already made hundreds of millions of dollars providing Ukraine and its military with internet service since the start of Russia’s invasion.

Early in the war, Musk supposedly “donated” thousands of Starlink satellite kits to the country, making much of Ukraine dependent on the service that holds a relative monopoly over satellite network systems and Ukraine’s ability to conduct critical military operations, such as drone piloting.

The New York Times reported in 2023 that the company is charging $2,500 per terminal per month, with over 42,000 Starlink terminals in use across the country. The co-founder of the Ukraine Defense Fund, which has helped secure Starlink access for the Ukrainian military, told The Atlantic that he estimates there are now over 250,000 Starlink terminals in use across the war zone.

Musk’s capping of service was met with outrage earlier this month, sparking panic within both the Ukrainian and U.S. governments as a large swath of the country’s military was effectively out of service. On Saturday, Musk admitted that he was behind the decision and accused the military of violating Skylink’s terms of service, which Ukraine has denied.

“Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact,” Musk said. “That said, I have nothing but UTTER CONTEMPT for the virtue-signaling evil warmongers who push for endless slaughter and offer no realistic solution to the conflict. May you burn in hell.”

Musk’s seeming turn on Ukraine comes as the Trump administration is increasingly embracing Russia and cutting funding to Ukraine.

The incident has shined a spotlight on Musk’s vast ability to control world events and swing the favor of an entire war toward one side if he so chooses — an enormous amount of power left to one man who represents nothing but his own whims and profits.

Despite this, the Pentagon’s inspector general is effectively refusing to investigate Musk’s interruptions to the service, it told Congress this week.

Critics have already raised concerns about the enormous control that Starlink has over space in low orbit, while its services are the only option in many places that otherwise lack connectivity. Starlink has already faced scrutiny for monopolizing internet services in rural areas of the U.S., and then raising prices dramatically after getting communities hooked.

As Trump cracks down on political speech, independent media is increasingly necessary.

author: Clare Hymer
title: ‘Major Opportunity’ for UK Unions to Recruit Workers As New Rules Take Effect
content:
Trade unions could see a boost in membership due to

new workplace rights

 that come into force today.


As of 30 October, union representatives have the right to request in-person or digital access to workplaces where at least 21 people are employed – even if the union isn’t recognised by the employer or it has no members there.


This will make it easier for organisers to reach workers shut out of collective representation in order to speak to them about demanding better pay and conditions.


Until today, bosses could keep unions out of many workplaces by simply refusing access. Now, if talks to negotiate an access agreement fail, the Central Arbitration Committee – an independent government body – can force employers to agree, with penalties for breaches reaching £500,000.

 


Andrea Egan, general secretary of Unison – Britain’s largest trade union – said the new laws presented “a major organising opportunity”.


“For decades, employers have used every trick in the book to prevent unions getting into workplaces,”

she wrote in a blog post

 earlier this month. “They know organised workplaces shift the power dynamic so that workers have a real voice through recognition and collective bargaining and they don’t want that to spread. 


“The new access rights provide a significant reset of industrial relations.”


After peaking at 13.2 million in 1979, union membership in the UK plummeted as a result of deindustrialisation and anti-union legislation introduced by Margaret Thatcher’s government.


The new rules, which form part of Labour’s Employment Rights Act 2025, could be particularly helpful for unions wanting to reach workers in the private sector, where

just 12% of employees

 are unionised.


Other reforms taking effect today strengthen protections for workers taking part in industrial action. 


A separate requirement for bosses to inform staff of their right to join a union is due to come into force on 1 January 2027.

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Cuidar la vida en el territorio: la deuda pendiente con las mujeres del campo
content:
OPINIÓN


Por Carolina Llorens*


Las tareas de cuidados recaen de manera desproporcionada sobre las mujeres y disidencias y en el ámbito rural la realidad es aún más compleja. Según datos del Movimiento Nacional Campesino Indígena Somos Tierra (MNCI ST),

 en Argentina el 60 por ciento de las mujeres rurales vive una triple jornada simultánea: producen alimentos, sostienen el hogar y cuidan del territorio

. En promedio, trabajan más de 14 horas al día, lo que les deja apenas 1,6 horas diarias para el descanso o el autocuidado. Cada 29 de octubre se conmemora el Día Internacional del Cuidado y el Apoyo. Esta fecha, propuesta por las Naciones Unidas en 2023, invita a reflexionar sobre estas tareas que hacen posible la vida, pero que rara vez son reconocidas


Lejos de ser una vocación natural, el cuidado en el campo es un acto político.

Para las comunidades campesinas e indígenas, el cuidado es integral: abarca la tierra, el agua, las semillas criollas, la biodiversidad, los animales y los saberes ancestrales.

Sin embargo, esta labor se desarrolla en un contexto de abandono estatal y crisis climática, donde las mujeres rurales actúan como el "amortiguador" que sostiene la vida en los territorios. El impacto en la salud es alarmante: el 85 por ciento de ellas sufre estrés constante y casi la mitad no acude al médico por falta de tiempo.


Un diagnóstico de desfinanciamiento


Esta realidad rural se enmarca en un escenario nacional crítico. El conjunto de organizaciones que impulsan el

Acuerdo Nacional por los Cuidados

 advierten que en los últimos años se destruyeron 48 de 50 políticas de cuidado, lo que profundizó el abandono y trasladó la carga de manera desproporcionada hacia los hogares y, especialmente, hacia las mujeres. "Hoy la organización social del cuidado está en emergencia", señalan. Mientras el costo de vida aumenta y el hambre crece,

las redes comunitarias intentan cubrir las necesidades básicas

, pero no pueden reemplazar la responsabilidad del Estado.


Para las familias rurales, esta ausencia estatal es doblemente grave. La falta de acceso a salud integral, infraestructuras y servicios básicos, sumada a la falta de regulación de la propiedad comunitaria y a las políticas de adaptación al cambio climático, coloca a las mujeres del campo en una situación de extrema vulnerabilidad. La sobrecarga de trabajo no solo limita su autonomía, sino que también se constituye como una forma de violencia estructural.


Foto: MNCI ST


Hacia un Acuerdo Nacional por los Cuidados


El Acuerdo Nacional por los Cuidados, respaldado por una amplia diversidad de organizaciones sociales, sindicatos y académicos, plantea la necesidad de reconstruir una organización social del cuidado basada en la corresponsabilidad. Esto implica que el Estado, las familias, las comunidades, los sindicatos y el sector privado asuman responsabilidades concretas.


La propuesta no se limita a un conjunto de políticas aisladas, sino que busca ser un proyecto de país que ponga la sostenibilidad de la vida en el centro de la agenda pública.


Desde el sector rural se impulsa a que este acuerdo nacional tenga una perspectiva campesina, indígena y territorial. Para las mujeres rurales, esto se traduce en exigencias urgentes: acceso a la salud, servicios básicos, regulación de la propiedad comunitaria, reconocimiento del cuidado comunitario rural como un trabajo y políticas de adaptación al cambio climático que garanticen agua, alimentos y condiciones dignas para vivir y producir.


La urgencia de esta demanda radica en que el cuidado no puede seguir siendo una responsabilidad individual ni recaer siempre sobre las mujeres y diversidades.

 Construir un sistema integral de cuidados es una inversión estratégica que no solo mejora la calidad de vida de quienes cuidan, sino que también dinamiza la economía y reduce las desigualdades. En el campo, donde las mujeres sostienen la producción de alimentos y la biodiversidad, garantizar el derecho al cuidado es garantizar la soberanía alimentaria y el arraigo.


Porque cuidar debe ser un proyecto de país, en el Día Internacional de los Cuidados, la voz de las mujeres y diversidades rurales se alza para exigir que el Estado deje de mirar para otro lado y reconozca que, sin cuidados, no hay vida posible en los territorios.


*Coordinadora del Equipo de Feminismo y Diversidades del Movimiento Nacional Campesino Indígena - Somos Tierra

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Ottawa police ask residents to check sheds, garages in search for missing Inuk teen
content:
Ottawa police are asking residents in the 1000 block of Gladstone Avenue to check their properties and surveillance cameras as they continue searching for a missing 14-year-old girl.


Lydia Oyukuluk was last seen Wednesday, Oct. 28, at about 6 p.m. in the area, police said in a news release Thursday.


On Friday, police asked people in the area, including along Spadina Avenue and surrounding streets, to check backyards, sheds, garages and other places where Oyukuluk might have sought shelter.


They are also asking residents to review doorbell camera and surveillance footage from Wednesday evening onward for possible sightings.


Temperatures in Ottawa dropped to 8 C early Friday morning, according to Environment Canada online weather reports.


OPS media spokesperson

Julie

 Kavanagh confirmed Friday that Oyukuluk is Inuk.


She is described as four-foot-nine with a petite build and long black hair partially dyed red at the back.


She was last seen wearing baggy black sweatpants, a black camouflage hoodie and socks. She was not wearing shoes.


Anyone who sees Oyukuluk is asked to call 911 so she can receive immediate assistance, an updated release said. Anyone with information about her whereabouts can contact Ottawa police at 613-236-1222.

title: “No vendan el Estatuto”: el gremio de prensa reclamó al Senado que trate en comisión los proyectos para proteger el periodismo
content:
Sindicatos de prensa de todo el país, representantes de las carreras de comunicación y organizaciones de la sociedad civil se movilizaron este jueves 29 al Congreso de la Nación para reclamar que traten los diversos proyectos legislativos para actualizar o prorrogar el Estatuto del Periodista Profesional (Ley 12.908), cuya derogación fue establecida por la regresiva Reforma Laboral del gobierno nacional de ultraderecha a partir del 1 de enero de 2027.


“Senadores, diputados: NO VENDAN EL ESTATUTO DEL PERIODISTA, la libertad de expresión y el derecho a la información”, pidieron dirigentes gremiales, periodistas y trabajadores y trabajadoras de prensa en la bandera que desplegaron en la puerta del Congreso Nacional. La acción de visibilización fue impulsada por el Sindicato de Prensa de Buenos Aires (SiPreBa) y la Federación Argentina de Trabajadores de Prensa (FATPREN).


Presentamos una solicitud formal a su presidenta, @carmenAlvarezR , y al resto de los legisladores para exigir que cumplan su compromiso y traten los proyectos de actualización y prórroga del Estatuto.


No vamos a permitir que el silencio parlamentario y los intereses de las empresas de medios destruyan nuestros derechos ante un contexto de ataques a la prensa y grave precarización laboral.


#SiPreBA2026


— SiPreBA – Sindicato de Prensa de Buenos Aires (@sipreba)

October 30, 2026


En el marco de la protesta, se presentó una solicitud formal dirigida a la senadora Carmen Álvarez Rivero, presidenta de la Comisión de Trabajo y Previsión Social del Senado, y a los legisladores que la integran. El documento exige la inmediata convocatoria a reunión de comisión para evitar que la inacción parlamentaria decante en un vacío legal, que termine exponiendo al periodismo en una situación de vulnerabilidad mayor a las presiones políticas, económicas y judiciales.


La nota convoca a todos los miembros de la comisión a tratar los proyectos, pero puntualmente a los legisladores que se comprometieron a discutir una actualización de la Ley 12.908 en el marco de la prórroga, como los senadores Carolina Losada, Eduardo Vischi, Sonia Rojas Decut, José Carambia, Flavia Gabriela Royón y Carolina Moises, entre otros.


“Desde la sanción de la reforma laboral, la Comisión de Legislación del Trabajo del Senado no se volvió a reunir ni una sola vez. Las y los senadores que muchas veces hablan de la regulación laboral no están haciendo su laburo”, sostuvo Agustín Lecchi, secretario general de SiPreBA.


“En un contexto de gran ataque a la libertad de expresión, donde el Presidente de la Nación dice que nos quiere quemar en la hoguera, los empresarios de medios aprovechan la política laboral de este gobierno para derogar una ley que nos protege y resguarda la libertad de expresión”, agregó Lecchi.


 NI UN DÍA SIN ESTATUTO DEL PERIODISTA


Mariano Recalde @marianorecalde , senador de Unión por la Patria, realizó un pedido de preferencia para que se trate de manera urgente los proyectos para sostener la vigencia y actualización del Estatuto del Periodista Profesional.


Exigimos a la senadora @carmenAlvarezR que sesione la Comisión de Trabajo y Previsión. Denunciamos que desde la Reforma Laboral no se juntó ni una sola vez, bloqueando cualquier tipo de debate democrático.

October 30, 2026


Durante el acto expresaron su apoyo los senadores Mariano Recalde, Marcelo Lewandowski, Jimena López, Ana Inés Marks y María Teresa González, junto al diputado Esteban Paulon y el legislador porteño Gabriel Solano.


Los senadores no están haciendo su trabajo y tienen que tratar el Estatuto del Periodista.


Nuestro secretario general, @AguLecchi estuvo en @radioconvos899 en el programa de @aleberco donde comentó que desde la sanción de la reforma laboral, la Comisión de Legislación del Trabajo del Senado no se volvió a reunir ni una sola vez y convocó mañana a las 12 frente al Senado para exigir a la comisión laboral que trate el proyecto de actualización del Estatuto del Periodista Profesional y del Personal Administrativo presentado en junio pasado.
